signals.bank_theme: Albania — POS acceptance mandate + deposit-ATM growth
signals.signal: This cycle the acceptance estate is measured at the central bank rather than at the trade association. The Bank of Albania's own terminal series puts POS at **38,662 at end-Q2-2026**, made up of 38,615 EFTPOS plus 47 cash-advance. That is up from 32,224 at end-Q1-2026. The comparable earlier figures are 31,263 at end-2025 and 24,481 at end-2024. The rise is 23.7% in six months and 57.9% over eighteen months. Roughly 10,700 terminals were added in twelve months, and virtual POS stands at 389 (A4, A6). H1-2026 card payments at POS were 16,006,404 transactions worth ALL 58.3bn. Card payments at POS have now firmly overtaken ATM cash withdrawals, at about 56 of every 100 card operations (A4, A6). The driver is legal rather than commercial. The Law on Tax Procedures, as amended by Parliament at end-2025, obliges businesses to hold a terminal during 2026. Accommodation, transport and public enterprises are bound from end-May 2026. The rest are bound by 31/12/2026, inside a national cashless-by-2030 goal (A6). Alongside it runs the POSi National Electronic Payments Acceleration Programme. This is a government, Albanian Association of Banks and Mastercard scheme launched on 27/03/2025, not a Mastercard-only offer. It now has five confirmed acquirers: Raiffeisen, Union Bank, BKT, Credins and OTP Albania. It gives a free terminal and 0% commission for twelve months, up to EUR 20,000 a year. It is valid until 31/12/2026, or until all terminals are distributed (A1). One caution carries over from the source. The 38,662 terminals are about 28% of Albania's ~138,000 active enterprises. Many terminals sit inside chains, so this is not 28% of businesses (A6). Two acquirers are actively replacing hardware with software. Raiffeisen offers RaiPOS softPOS plus a free NFC smartphone as an alternative to a terminal (A1).

sources.text: Bank of Albania — F6 terminal series, end-Q2-2026

signals.date: 13/08/2026 — Bank of Albania publishes Q2-2026 terminals: POS 38,662; 31/12/2026 all remaining businesses must hold a terminal and the POSi free-terminal wave ends; phase-1 sectors bound since end-05/2026
signals.implies: This is a legally required terminal rollout that continues through 2026, whatever merchants want. Acquirers adding thousands of terminals in months need terminal management, remote key injection, monitoring and deployment logistics more than they need another box. The lasting revenue is therefore estate management rather than hardware. Printec's own Albania page claims only **150 POS terminals in the field, against a national estate of 38,662**. That is roughly 0.4% share in the market where it leads on ATMs. It is the clearest measured gap in the country.
signals.likelihood: Very high — the deadline is statutory and the phase-1 step has already produced the measured jump
signals.follow_up: Go to the five POSi acquirers now, before the 31/12/2026 cap is reached. Offer terminal supply plus POS monitoring, a merchant portal, key injection and point-to-point encryption. Find out which vendors supplied the roughly 10,700 net new terminals. Build a softPOS answer for the small-merchant tail that Raiffeisen and OTP are taking with free software.
signals.product_review_why: A legal terminal mandate drives demand for POS supply, terminal management and key injection, while the ATM figures are only backdrop.

signals.bank_theme: Albania — TIPS Clone instant-payment rail, November 2026 go-live
signals.signal: This is the only dated event in this market. Banca d'Italia announced on **20/07/2026** that its TIPS Clone instant-payment settlement platform went live for the Western Balkans. Bosnia and Montenegro joined first. **A second onboarding window is scheduled for November 2026, when the central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected to join** (A3, primary). · Governor Gent Sejko then spoke at the 05/08/2026 monetary-policy briefing. He said the project is in its final implementation phase, and that the system should be fully operational **within November 2026, at the latest by end-November**. He put the savings at up to ALL 35bn a year for the financial system and ALL 38bn for the economy (A3 and A5, multi-outlet). Bank of Albania's own National Payment System Committee minutes of 16/12/2025 confirm the programme and record Banca d'Italia's original **July 2026** target. The November date is therefore a delay (A4, primary). · Two design features matter commercially. Transfers are addressed by **mobile phone number instead of IBAN**. A **Verification-of-Payee check** confirms that the account belongs to the named payee before the payer confirms (A4). The platform settles in local currency in central-bank money and in euro in commercial-bank money, which are two separately screened flows (A3). · Context volumes: SEPA credit transfers went live 07/10/2025, and AIPS-EURO customer payments rose from 31,545 in January to 49,005 in July 2026. The AECH retail clearing house reached a record 237,974 transactions in July alone, up 46.2% in seven months (A4). AIPS, AIPS-EURO and AECH were all moved to ISO 20022 during 2025 (A4). · One caveat applies. There is no Bank of Albania press release, no day-level date, and **no published list of participating commercial banks or bank-side legal deadline**. The urgency comes from the Governor, not from a legal duty on banks (A3, A5).

sources.text: Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone goes live, second window November 2026

signals.date: 20/07/2026 — platform live, Albania named for the November 2026 onboarding window; restated by the Governor 05/08/2026; original July-2026 target slipped
signals.implies: Every Albanian bank has to fund a long list of changes inside one quarter. The list includes 24/7 payment operations, and sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening at instant speed. It also includes real-time fraud and transaction monitoring, and hardware security module capacity for the new rail. Hardware security modules are secure devices used to store payment encryption keys. The last item is a phone-number-to-account lookup with payee verification. · Budget not committed by around September 2026 becomes a 2027 fix. The delay from July to November is therefore the selling window, because banks are behind and are buying integration capacity now. Printec reference accounts OTP Albania and Raiffeisen Albania are both in the wave.
signals.likelihood: High that the central bank goes live in the window; commercial-bank readiness is entirely unevidenced
signals.follow_up: Get the exact November date and the participant-bank list from Bank of Albania and the 12th National Payment System Committee papers. Obtain the TIPS Clone message specification. The ISO 20022 assumption has no source and must not be presented to a customer as fact. Identify which Albanian banks have no real-time fraud engine. Sell integration, screening and managed monitoring against a Q4 date, without presenting November as a legal duty on the bank.
signals.product_review_why: Banks joining a new instant rail need integration, payee verification, real-time fraud screening and HSM capacity by a fixed date.

signals.bank_theme: Printec Albania / Bank of Albania banknote-machine certification — the fitness gate
signals.signal: Bank of Albania's official list of **customer-operated** banknote-handling machines tested for the lek has only **two entries, and Printec Albania Ltd is the named distributor for both**. They are the NCR SelfServ 6682/6684/6632/6634 family (tested 20/02/2026) and the LIVIX 7 from Vivex Group Belgrade (tested 30/01/2026). Both are marked "no" in the column for sorting notes **by fitness**. · Fitness checking means sorting out worn or damaged notes. It is the rule a machine must meet before deposited lek can go back into circulation. So as of mid-2026 **no customer-operated machine in Albania is certified to recycle notes**, and every deposit must be sorted again on a staff-operated machine. · The staff-operated list is almost entirely fitness-capable. It is made up of Giesecke+Devrient, Cima and Italdes units sold by **Mellon Albania and Pelikani Security. Printec appears nowhere on it** (A4, list dated 10/07/2026). · Printec's channel position is strong in another way. NCR Atleos named Printec Group its **Global Partner of the Year on 11/05/2026** (the 2025 awards). BKT's own annual report names CxBanking software on its Smart ATMs, which is the same NCR Atleos software Printec resells (A1). Printec's own country page claims 1,270 ATMs in the field, 90 Qmatic queueing branches and 340 electronic safe locks. But 1,270 is more than the whole national ATM count, so it cannot be a live Albanian installed base (A1).

signals.bank_theme: Albania — third-party ATM partnership operators forming an independent deployer layer
signals.signal: Bank of Albania statistics reported 29/07/2026 show automated cash deposits at ATMs reached 676,000 in Q1-2026. That is up 125% year on year, and worth ALL 33.4bn, up 146%. This follows nearly 2.2m deposits worth ALL 104.8bn in full-year 2025. The structural detail that matters is who is installing the new machines. Recent ATM growth has come especially from units placed in **tourist areas**. **These are typically not operated by the banks but under a partnership model with third-party businesses, which the source says are usually the companies that sell ATM equipment**. In that split the bank supplies the payments infrastructure, accounting and cash. The partner supplies the machine and handles transport, replenishment, cash insurance and the site-rental relationships. Revenue is shared by cost (A6). Separately, **ABI Bank presents its customer ATM access through a dedicated "ATM Euronet" menu item** alongside its own branch-and-ATM page. That is a visible self-service relationship with an ATM-as-a-service operator at a mid-sized Albanian bank (A5).

signals.bank_theme: Albania — branch counter cash and paper payments, the teller-automation case
signals.signal: Bank of Albania's own forms show how much cash and paper still crosses the counter. **Over-the-counter cash transactions in H1-2026 were 3,357,815 items worth ALL 1,170.8bn**. Of these, counter cash **deposits alone were 2,279,914 items worth ALL 783.7bn**. ATM deposits over the same half-year were 1,378,900 items worth ALL 68.6bn. So **the branch counter absorbs 11.4 times the cash-deposit value the entire ATM estate does**, and businesses are 73% of counter deposit value (A4). Paper-based credit transfers are still large as well. They ran at **3,250,200 items worth ALL 2,477.9bn in H1-2026, which is 33.1% of customer transfers by count but 62.1% by value**. Business paper transfers alone were worth ALL 1,612.1bn (A4). The branch estate this lands on is growing, not shrinking. There were **408 bank branches at end-2025, up from 400, the highest since 2021, with about 46% in Tirana** (A4, press reporting of central-bank data). Cash outside banks reached ALL 505.7bn at June-2026, up 4.6% in six months and up 14.4% year on year on the central bank's own annual-change line. Note volume is therefore rising in absolute terms, even as card acceptance grows fast (A4). ProCredit Albania states the underlying economics plainly to its own customers. Staffed counters open roughly 30 hours a week, against 24/7 self-service zones. Deposits are credited in under five minutes, and there is a night-safe tier for businesses depositing over ALL 1,000,000 a day (A1).

sources.text: Bank of Albania — Form 3 teller cash transactions, Jan-Jun 2026

signals.date: 14/08/2026 — Bank of Albania publishes H1-2026 teller-cash data; paper-transfer form published 13/08/2026; branch count 408 at end-2025 reported 30/07/2026
signals.implies: This is the strongest branch-transformation case in the market, and it rests on regulator primary data rather than inference. Teller cash recyclers are machines at the counter that accept, check, store and re-dispense the same notes, instead of sending them away and back by courier. Together with assisted-service kiosks, they address ALL 783.7bn of manual deposits per half-year, concentrated in business branches. The paper-transfer number is the second half of the same brief. Two-thirds of transfer value still crosses a counter on paper, which self-service kiosks and qualified electronic signature can make digital. Because branches are still being opened, this is fit-out demand, not decommissioning. Tirana's 46% concentration makes a single-city pilot cheap.
signals.likelihood: High as a standing demand case; no dated procurement trigger exists
signals.follow_up: Identify the three or four banks with the largest business cash-deposit share (BKT, Credins, OTP Albania, Raiffeisen Albania). Pitch teller-recycler branch pilots ahead of the November instant-payments launch, when the cash-cycle cost argument peaks. Find out which banks still require wet-ink mandates, the natural e-signature entry point. Bank-level splits are not published, so this needs direct bank enquiry.
signals.product_review_why: Heavy counter cash calls for teller recyclers and assisted kiosks, and paper transfers call for qualified e-signature.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: Raiffeisen Bank Albania — self-service zone conversion and an open digital-signature gap
signals.signal: Raiffeisen's Albanian-language annual report says its ATM network grew to 197 units during 2025, with 14 machines added. It says its 74 branches are the largest network in Albania, and that they include 30 self-service zones with cash-deposit and dual-currency lek/euro ATMs. Hybrid branches are 28% of the network, with reduced cash hours. In its own words, the bank "will continue to invest in modernising the fleet and in expanding self-service centres in urban areas". Branch payments fell 16% year on year (A1). RBI group's H1-2026 deck separately puts Albania at 74 business outlets at 30/06/2026, down from 76. The bank's own published map returns 77 branches and shows no ATM layer at all (A1). The near-term opening is narrower and more urgent. Raiffeisen says it is the first bank to offer digital registration for individuals, but the process still ends with a contract signed in the branch. It says "work is under way on integrating a digital signature provider" to make the process fully paperless. It already uses SMS one-time-password signing for credit documents, so what it needs is a qualified eIDAS-grade signature for account opening (A1). On competitive context, the Albanian Association of Banks gave Blinking a platform on 11/12/2025 at a Tirana workshop on digital onboarding and compliance. The audience was the alternative-channels, compliance and anti-money-laundering units of every member bank, which is the exact buying group for this gap (A1). Raiffeisen is also pushing RaiPOS softPOS, with POS transactions up 29% and e-commerce up 79% (A1).
signals.date: 27/08/2026 — RBI group and locator data re-pulled, Albania 74 outlets at 30/06/2026; the annual report describing the open digital-signature integration is dated Dec-2025 and the work was already under way then
signals.implies: The largest branch estate in the country is being turned into self-service with dual-currency deposit machines, while cash hours shrink. The bank has also publicly promised further fleet modernisation. That creates clear demand for recyclers, queueing systems and managed services against a 197-unit estate. The digital-signature gap is the most actionable near-term bid in Albania, because the bank has named the missing part itself. It is also time-critical and contested. Integration was already under way at end-2025, and Blinking has been in front of the decision-makers.
signals.likelihood: High that a signature provider is chosen in 2026; the decision window may already have closed
signals.follow_up: Find out at once whether the digital-signature provider has already been chosen. Get the share of the 197 machines that take deposits, and the make of the dual lek/euro units, as neither is published. Find out whether Blinking has won any Albanian bank. Also identify who supplies BKT's already-live qualified signature stack, because that vendor is the incumbent competitor here.
signals.product_review_why: Branches are being converted to self-service zones with deposit machines, and the bank has named a qualified e-signature gap.

signals.bank_theme: BKT — branch rebuild, an eight-year-old ATM fleet and post-office cash-in
signals.signal: BKT is the largest bank in Albania, with 24% market share, total assets of EUR 7,196m (+9.3%) and return on equity of 27.5% at 31/12/2025. Its annual report records 164 installed ATMs across 2025, including 30 new off-site locations. It states that ATM cash deposits are now four-fifths of all its cash-deposit transactions, with branch deposits down to 21%. It claims BKT captures "nearly half of the country's ATM deposits" through tablet-like interfaces (A1). A date correction is carried this cycle. The milestone timeline shows the ATM network was fully renewed in 2018, not 2016, with the CxBanking software upgrade in 2022. The fleet is therefore eight years old. That puts it in the normal 2026-2028 replacement window rather than making it overdue (A1). The Project EASY branch transformation has completed 35 branches across 2024-2025, with more scheduled. BKT's stated 2026 aim is to remove routine cash transactions from branches (A1). Its POS Network Optimization programme raised terminal activity from 85% to 88.7%. That leaves roughly 11% of a reported estate of about 10,000 terminals idle, a target the board can see (A1). BKT also states an agreement with Posta Shqiptare, the state postal operator. It lets customers make cash deposits in rural areas without a branch (A1). One area is already closed. BKT runs live digital onboarding at 15% of new retail acquisitions. It also has a qualified electronic signature stack that complies with Albanian law and eIDAS, with around 3,000 cases completed by 31/12/2025. Do not pitch digital onboarding here (A1).

It also has a funded multi-year branch rebuild, which is the entry point for teller recyclers, signage and queueing. Its own stated 2026 goal is to remove routine cash from branches. That amounts to a cash-automation brief written by the customer. The Posta Shqiptare arrangement is a second route. The post office is state-owned, so a device rollout there would be a public procurement that Printec can bid for in its own name.

signals.bank_theme: Albania — eIDAS2 electronic identification and digital identity wallet law adopted
signals.signal: The Albanian Parliament adopted the law "On electronic identification, trusted services and the digital identity wallet" on **07/05/2026**, after committee review on 4-5 May. The law is stated to be fully aligned with the EU eIDAS and eIDAS2 regulations. It creates a digital identity wallet, provided free to citizens. The wallet can store and prove identity data and electronic attestations of attributes. It can also sign and seal documents electronically, log every digital interaction, and work offline and across borders. The law widens the range of qualified and non-qualified trust services. It also tightens supervision of eID schemes, wallets and trust-service providers (A4, national cyber-security authority announcement 14/05/2026). This closes a gap the European Commission had flagged. Its Albania Report of 04/11/2025 stated word for word that Albania should adopt such a law to align with the European Digital Identity regulation. That confirms that no eIDAS-aligned law existed as of late 2025 (A3). Implementing acts are still pending. The accreditation route for qualified trust-service providers is not yet published (A4).

sources.text: AKSK — law on electronic identification, trusted services and the digital identity wallet adopted

signals.date: 07/05/2026 — law adopted by Parliament, announced 14/05/2026; implementing acts and the trust-service accreditation route still pending

That unblocks an 18-month bank integration cycle: remote enrolment, qualified signature, wallet-based authentication for the November instant rail, and the trust-service infrastructure behind it. It is also the mechanism that replaces the 3.25m paper credit transfers per half-year still crossing branch counters. In concrete terms, it turns Raiffeisen's open digital-signature integration and Credins' 2026 loan-origination build into buildable, legally supported projects rather than aspirations.
signals.likelihood: High that implementing acts follow within 12 months, given this is an explicit EU accession recommendation
signals.follow_up: Track the national cyber-security authority's secondary legislation and the accreditation route for qualified trust-service providers. Check whether an existing EU qualified provider can passport onto Albania's national trust list. That is the fastest route to a compliant offer at Raiffeisen and Credins.

First, a full read of the CBBiH rulebook found Article 7(2), a rolling trigger the master row missed. signals.bank_theme: Bosnia & Herzegovina — SEPA accession + ISO 20022 structured-address remediation
signals.signal: The application is now actually filed. On **06/08/2026 CBBiH formally submitted BiH's application to join the Single Euro Payments Area**. This closes a two-year programme run through the SEPA Accession Coordination Board. CBBiH chairs that board alongside both entity finance ministries, both banking agencies and the BiH Banking Association. A draft had been lodged 12/12/2025. The last precondition fell on 28/07/2026, when the FBiH House of Representatives adopted the harmonised financial laws that the Republika Srpska National Assembly had already passed (A1, A4). The European Payments Council is now reviewing the file. CBBiH says clearly that commercial banks must align their IT and business systems with SEPA standards and join the relevant European payment schemes. It also says that a significant part of that work can only be done after formal admission. It expects the first SEPA transactions at the earliest six months after admission. The sales trigger is therefore the six-month post-admission clock, not the application (A1, A4). The World Bank estimates BiH fee savings of around EUR 100m, and CBBiH notes BiH does over 80% of its foreign trade with SEPA countries (A4). Two domestic message-format facts were confirmed this cycle from primary gazette and central-bank text. CBBiH's giro-clearing system already uses the SEPA message format conforming to ISO 20022. It also conforms to whichever European Payments Council rulebook version the central bank designates as current. The 14-15/11/2026 SWIFT SR2026 removal of unstructured postal addresses therefore reaches BiH retail clearing the moment that designation carries it, and that designation is not publicly dated (A3). Meanwhile BiH high-value RTGS is still legally fixed to SWIFT MT formats: MT102, MT103, MT202 and MT205, with mandatory service code BAP. The Governor can set the switch to ISO 20022 pacs.008 and pacs.009 on only fifteen days' written notice once all participants are ready. That is the shortest lead time to a live cutover anywhere in the footprint (A3).

signals.bank_theme: FBiH Banking Agency — binding ICT-risk decision with an annual external ICT audit due 31/03/2027
signals.signal: BiH banks are regulated even where the wider economy is not, and the rulebook now has a hard filing date. FBA's binding "Odluka o upravljanju informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom i IKT rizikom u banci" was adopted 25/02/2025 and has been in application since 31/12/2025. It is BiH's equivalent of the EU's operational-resilience regime. It requires measures to protect the cryptographic keys that encrypt data at rest and in transit. It also requires ICT incident and cyber-threat reporting to FBA, resilience testing, oversight of third parties, and both internal and external ICT audit. The external ICT-system audit report is a standalone report that every bank must deliver to FBA no later than 31 March of each year. **The next one is due 31/03/2027 and applies to all 13 FBiH banks** (A4). On top of that, FBA published its supervisory expectations for 2026 on 20/02/2026. They require penetration testing and red-team exercises, layered security controls, data encryption, network segmentation, continuous monitoring and automated attack response. They also require continuity plans covering rebuilding systems from zero, and a full register of every outsourced activity with direct board accountability. They further require transaction-monitoring systems tuned to actual BiH client behaviour, including cash flows, diaspora remittances and cross-border payments (A1, A4). Banks are already acting. Three of the largest FBiH banks resolved at their spring-2026 AGMs to commission external audits. UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar appointed KPMG for a financial-statement audit including an assessment of AML obligations, plus a separate information-system audit. ASA Banka resolved to select an external ICT auditor. NLB Banka d.d. Sarajevo appointed an auditor across three separate scopes covering financial statements, the AML segment and the ICT system. Those three banks hold 447 of the Federation's 1,400 ATMs and 15,085 of its 28,834 POS terminals (A1).

signals.bank_theme: Seven FBiH banks with zero own POS estate — greenfield card acceptance
signals.signal: The regulator's own bank-level table shows a clean structural gap. At 30/06/2026, **seven of the thirteen FBiH-headquartered banks report zero POS terminals of their own**. They are Sparkasse (123 ATMs), BBI (91), Addiko Sarajevo (75), ProCredit (35), Privredna banka Sarajevo (32), Union banka (32) and KIB Velika Kladuša (6). They issue cards but do not acquire, meaning they do not process card payments for merchants. Merchant acceptance is therefore either outsourced or absent. That makes any terminal, terminal-management or software-POS pitch a fresh build rather than a displacement fight (A1, A4). Sparkasse is the most interesting of the seven. Its 123 ATMs against only 46 branches and sub-branches make it comparatively self-service-heavy. It is one of only three IPS BiH launch banks, which signals real appetite for payments investment. Its ATM fleet was migrated to Diebold Nixdorf by Payten in 2018-19 (A1, A4). Demand is moving fast underneath these banks. Card acceptance is growing far faster than the ATM count across BiH, with POS up 3,079 units in six months against 30 more ATMs. Republika Srpska POS grew 23.5% year on year, against 4.5% in the Federation (A1, A4). BiH-wide there were 37,895 POS terminals at end-2025 and 215 million card transactions in 2025, at an average of KM 98. Contactless already accounts for 70% of card transactions (A4).

signals.bank_theme: BAMCARD d.d. Sarajevo — the domestic processor, and an unresolved partner-or-compete question
signals.signal: BAMCARD is BiH's domestic card processor, and ASA Banka owns a stake above 10%. It markets an "Instant payment and White Label solution", which its own site describes as the first instant mobile payment platform in BiH. It supports QR-code payments in store, in app and online, plus person-to-person transfers, top-ups and donations. It is available standalone or white-labelled, that is sold under another brand, to banks, fintechs, insurers, microcredit organisations and merchants (A1). BAMCARD has also launched a cardless ATM withdrawal service for microcredit payouts with Partner MKF and ASA Banka, and a dynamic currency conversion service certified by Visa and Mastercard. Two points are unresolved and matter. First, BAMCARD makes no public claim to be involved in IPS BiH or in CBBiH's planned QR scheme. So it is not known whether it builds the participant-side gateways for joining banks. That leaves it unclear whether it is the partner or the competitor on the largest opportunity in this market. Second, a "Notice of Acquisition of the Company's Shares" dated 23/09/2025, under the FBiH Takeover Law, sits unexplained on its news page. So it is not known whether control has changed. CBBiH data separately show that BAMCARD-branded cards are accepted at only **four banks' ATMs and one bank's POS**, so its own acceptance footprint is narrow (A1). Its careers page returned a 404 on 31/08/2026, so no hiring signal could be read (A5).

sources.text: BAMCARD d.d. Sarajevo — Instant payment and White Label solution

signals.date: STANDING: 28/01/2026 — latest dated corporate event is the tariff of fees adopted by the Supervisory Board on 27/01/2026 and published 28/01/2026; the takeover notice dates from 23/09/2025

Its white-label instant and QR product competes directly with the mobile-initiation requirement that the central bank's rulebook places on every joining bank. signals.bank_theme: Bosnia & Herzegovina — no electronic-identity or trust-services law, remote onboarding legally blocked
signals.signal: The European Commission's BiH 2025 Report says, in the financial-services section, that "There is no legal and regulatory framework for digital identity, and banks can only offer hybrid solutions". The digital chapter says that "No progress was made in adopting a Law on electronic identity and trust services for electronic transactions in line with the EU acquis". It also says the recommendation to set up a single countrywide supervisory body still stands. It adds that there was no progress on interoperability of electronic signature across the country (A3, A4). Both quotations were confirmed word for word this cycle. The state-level draft law is still with the Council of Ministers and has not been adopted. A set of press-tier claims could not be verified this cycle, and they must not be presented as fact. The first is a Republika Srpska entity law on electronic identification, said to have been adopted in June 2026. The others are a March 2026 Constitutional Court finding and a June 2026 letter from the IDDEEA director (A3). The Commission separately told BiH to set up a countrywide beneficial-ownership register, which is a list of who really owns each company. That is still not done and is a named FATF action-plan item. The Commission also told BiH to align with the payment-services and e-money directives and the SEPA regulation, which is now done in both entities (A4).

sources.text: European Commission — Bosnia and Herzegovina 2025 Report, SWD(2025) 751 final

signals.date: STANDING: 04/11/2025 — EC BiH 2025 Report confirms no e-identity or trust-services law; the EC's 2026 enlargement package, expected around October or November 2026, will re-score it
signals.implies: This answers the remote-identity question with a clear no, on a primary source, and it cuts both ways. A fully remote, identity-only onboarding product cannot be sold as compliant in BiH this cycle, and it should not go on a roadmap. Because identity cannot be proven remotely, the physical channel stays essential. That is good for branch and self-service lines: assisted-onboarding stations, cash-accepting and recycling ATMs, and electronic signature used in an attended rather than unattended set-up. Alongside this, BiH still has no network-and-information-security law at all, while FBA has already put resilience rules on banks, so banks are regulated ahead of the country. The beneficial-ownership register, a FATF action-plan item, is a separate opening in data quality.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the law has been recommended repeatedly and not adopted; SEPA and FATF pressure is the new forcing function
signals.follow_up: Watch for the EC's 2026 BiH report around October or November 2026, and for any draft state law on electronic identity and trust services. Find the claimed June-2026 Republika Srpska entity law in the RS official gazette, and the March-2026 Constitutional Court decision, before either is used commercially. Ask CBBiH and both banking agencies which identification method they will accept for remote account opening.
signals.product_review_why: Remote identity is legally blocked, so onboarding stays attended and shifts demand to branch and assisted self-service.

cited.label: European Commission — Bosnia and Herzegovina 2025 Report, SWD(2025) 751 final

signals.bank_theme: Bulgaria — post-euro changeover consolidation
signals.signal: The regulator has now formally closed the changeover, and every date is known. BNB Governor Dimitar Radev published a seven-month look-back on 21/08/2026 saying "the technical transition is complete, the real work continues". He confirmed that Bulgarian banks now draw Eurosystem liquidity on common terms (A3). The legal dual lev-euro price display ended on 08/08/2026 under ZVERB Art.15(2) as amended. Three banks have already switched their channels over. UniCredit Bulbank switched from 09/08/2026. UBB and the KBC companies switched in stages from 12/08/2026. Postbank switched from 14/08/2026 (A1, A5). For the device estate, ZVERB Art.21(2) item 3 required dual-currency amounts on ATM cash-withdrawal screens only during that display period. That duty ended on 09/08/2026. So every Bulgarian ATM and kiosk estate now needs a screen and receipt reversion release, which is a software update back to single-currency screens (A3). The remaining lev tail is measured. BGN 29.4bn was exchanged and 94.48% of lev cash withdrawn by 30/06/2026, with **BGN 1.7bn still outside BNB vaults**, against EUR 8.8bn of euro cash in circulation. Free exchange at banks ended on 30/06/2026, but UBB and UniCredit Bulbank both extended it voluntarily to 30/09/2026. Banks may not refuse the service until 31/12/2026. They may stop it only from 01/01/2027, after telling BNB in advance under Ordinance No.47 Art.2(4) (A1, A3). Consumer-protection enforcement did not stop; it changed legal basis. KZP and the revenue agency ran 37,955 euro-related inspections to 13/08/2026, with EUR 3.26m of penalties. The ban on unjustified price rises continues under the Consumer Protection Act to 09/08/2027 (A3).

sources.text: evroto.bg — BNB Governor Radev, seven-month assessment (BG)

signals.date: 21/08/2026 — BNB Governor declares the technical changeover complete; dual display ended 08/08/2026 and the ATM-screen dual-display duty fell away 09/08/2026; free exchange ends at UBB and UniCredit Bulbank 30/09/2026; statutory duty to exchange ends 31/12/2026
signals.implies: The budget freeze is over. Bulgarian bank IT and cash budgets were locked on changeover delivery through H1-2026, and they are now released into the 2027 planning round. That round is being set right now, from September to November 2026. Three concrete pieces of paid work follow from these dates. First, a screen and receipt reversion release across every ATM and self-service estate, now that dual display is no longer needed. Second, retiring lev validator profiles, firmware and cash-forecasting parameters once the exchange duty ends on 31/12/2026. Third, a single-currency re-baselining of cash forecasting and cash-in-transit routing, on a fleet that has never run a full euro year. Present this as post-changeover optimisation rather than changeover support.
signals.likelihood: High — every date is statutory and fixed, and the 2027 budget round is open now
signals.follow_up: Open the Q4-2026 conversation at DSK, UBB, Postbank, UniCredit Bulbank and Fibank on two bundled items. These are the ATM and kiosk screen reversion release after 08/08/2026, and lev decommissioning plus single-currency cash-forecast re-baselining. Ask BNB's Issue Department for the Ordinance 47 list of banks that have notified an exchange fee or a discontinuation date. Those banks are furthest through the wind-down and will need re-optimisation first.

signals.bank_theme: Bulgaria — big-four ATM estate: deposit-capability white space quantified
signals.signal: The white space has been re-measured on a single synchronised date, 27/08/2026, from each bank's own live locator feed. It has barely moved in a month. UBB shows 737 ATM pins, 244 with the cash-deposit feature, so 493 are dispense-only, or 33% deposit-capable. That compares with 738 and 246 on 30/07/2026, so the position is flat. Postbank shows 668 location records, 501 tagged as ATMs and 226 deposit-capable, so 275 are dispense-only. The estate grew by three ATM sites in four weeks and the deposit-capable share did not move, from 45.2% to 45.1%. That means new machines are still going in dispense-only, which is the strongest available evidence that no recycler decision has been taken. DSK shows 724 ATM-bearing sites out of 777 records. Only 214 carry either deposit tag and just 133 carry the explicit deposit-ATM tag, so roughly 510 to 620 sites are cash-out-only. In 169 of 285 localities, not one site takes a deposit. UniCredit Bulbank shows 761 ATM records and only 197 deposit-capable, so 564 machines, or 74.1%, are cash-out only (A1). Two new cross-checks sharpen the sizing. OTP's H1-2026 statutory report puts DSK at 952 ATMs at 30/06/2026, against 724 ATM-bearing sites. So at least 228 machines sit above one per site: pins are locations, not terminals (A1). BNB payment statistics, updated 22/07/2026, show the national fleet falling to **5,031 ATMs** at end-2025, from a 5,751 peak in 2016. ATM deposits rose to 12.53m transactions worth EUR 7.2bn across 2025, up 50% by value. Over-the-counter branch deposits jumped 70% by volume, to 9.7m transactions worth EUR 16.4bn in H2-2025 (A5).

signals.bank_theme: Bulgaria — Verification of Payee cliff at 01/01/2027 (legal basis contested)
signals.signal: The contested legal basis is now resolved, and the ATM estate is explicitly in scope. The open verification debt was closed this cycle against the Official Journal text itself. Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Article 16(9), inserted by Article 1(5) of the Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886, covers Member States that adopt the euro before 09/04/2027. Their payment service providers must comply with Articles 5a, 5b and 5c within one year of euro introduction. Bulgaria adopted the euro on 01/01/2026, so the duty applies from **01/01/2027**. This is directly applicable EU law, not a regulator's claim, and the previously feared 09/01/2027 non-euro date does not apply here (A3). BNB's own SEPA FAQ, re-read 27/08/2026, gives the same date for instant euro sending and for Verification of Payee (VoP). VoP is the check that the payee name matches the account, and it applies at every PSP licensed in Bulgaria (A3). The decisive new detail for Printec sits in recital 11 of Regulation 2024/886. It names the initiation channels expressly: "online banking, a mobile application, an automated teller machine, a self-service terminal, in a branch or by phone". It requires no difference between instant and other credit transfers across channels. ZVERB paragraph 1 item 16 defines a Bulgarian ATM as a device that also executes transfers between payment accounts. So the ATM and kiosk estate is inside VoP scope as a matter of primary EU text, not inference (A3). UBB went live with VoP on 15/07/2026 with four match outcomes, 24/7, stating the same 01/01/2027 market obligation (A1). BORICA's VoP service has run live since October 2025 and is certified by the European Payments Council as a Qualified Routing and Verification Mechanism (A2, A6).
signals.date: 01/01/2027 — every PSP licensed in Bulgaria must offer instant euro sending, price parity and full Verification of Payee on every initiation channel; legal basis confirmed at the OJ text on 27/08/2026, UBB live since 15/07/2026
signals.implies: The remaining lead time is four months, not seventeen. The material change this cycle is that ATMs and self-service terminals are named in the primary text. That turns a payments-department compliance item into a device-estate item, so any bank that scoped VoP to online and mobile only has a gap on its machines. The sale is VoP and name-matching integration into multivendor ATM software and bank kiosks, so a transfer started at the machine carries the mandatory payee check. Add instant-speed sanctions screening with re-screening, real-time transaction monitoring, and hardware security module (HSM) key capacity for 24/7 volumes. UBB and BORICA are reference points, not prospects. A 01/01/2027 go-live had to be funded in H1-2026, so unfunded work now prices as late-stage remediation.
signals.likelihood: High — a directly applicable EU regulation with a fixed date, confirmed by the regulator and already being worked to by the market
signals.follow_up: Ask BNB Payment Supervision which Bulgarian PSPs have declared VoP readiness on non-online channels specifically, and approach those with an ATM or kiosk gap first. Get BORICA's BISERA scheme rules for the Bulgarian VoP routing mechanism. One legal point remains for Printec Legal before any date goes into a contract. It is what "within one year of" 01/01/2026 means. The answer is either 31/12/2026 or 01/01/2027.
signals.product_review_why: Verification of Payee must now reach ATM and kiosk transfers, with instant-speed screening behind it.

signals.bank_theme: UniCredit Bulbank — bank-named "ATM obsolescence" inside a Group renewal plan to 2027
signals.signal: The 2025 Annual Report wording is now confirmed at the page. "ICT and ICT Security Risks — ATM obsolescence" is named as a non-financial risk driver the bank will focus on and closely monitor in 2026 (page 111, published 14/05/2026). The Group section bound into the same document commits to "replacing more than half of our machines with latest-generation models by 2027". BancoSmart 2.0 moves from withdrawal-only to deposit-capable ATMs, with no Bulgarian allocation disclosed anywhere (A1). The 27/08/2026 locator re-pull shows 761 ATM records and only 197 deposit-capable. Roughly 443 machines sit off-site at retail hosts, including Kaufland 108 and Fantastiko 45. The bank actively grows this estate by offering corporate customers ATM installation inside their outlets (A1). Three new points sharpen the read this cycle. First, the cashless-branch programme is a measurable rolling conversion. On 27/08/2026, 32 of 162 branch records carried the "Cashless service" flag, up from 31 on 30/07/2026, spread across 26 towns. That is roughly one conversion per month. Geo-matching the two feeds shows that **30 of those 32 already have a deposit-capable ATM within 500 m**. So conversion turns close to one-for-one into deposit-ATM demand, and 130 unconverted records remain (A1). Second, the bank claims the number-one national position in ATM-deposited amounts, up about 20% year on year, on a fleet where only 26% of machines take deposits. That is a capacity argument, although the 20% is a one-off changeover effect. Third, the procurement chapter states that "all necessary activities for the upgrade of ATM and POS devices were duly contracted" for the euro programme in 2025. It says DORA third-party obligations were addressed, and it names no supplier (A1). Free lev exchange including coin runs to 30/09/2026. SEPA Instant was announced for 20/08/2026, but no go-live confirmation had appeared by 27/08/2026 (A1).

sources.text: UniCredit Bulbank 2025 Annual Report, Risk Management "2026 Outlook" p.111 and Group Channels p.51

signals.implies: The bank has written the trigger itself, and the conversion rate can now be measured at about one branch a month. Two hard limits remain, and both must be respected in any proposal. signals.bank_theme: Postbank (Eurobank Bulgaria) — "Postbank NEXT" branch-format rebuild
signals.signal: The NEXT format now has a published device specification and a confirmed plan to expand. Postbank's own product page defines exactly two Express Banking device types. A cash device withdraws, deposits and performs cashless operations. A kiosk device is cashless only, covering statements, transfers, utility bills to over 250 billers, municipal taxes, and an e-receipt after every operation. Users log in by card and PIN, with no internet-banking registration needed. It is switched on automatically for all retail customers, and non-Postbank cardholders get withdrawal and bill payment (A1). The 35th-anniversary rebrand release calls NEXT a network of next-generation offices, and lists "expansion of the office network" among the coming months' initiatives. Already delivered are a new front-office system, a new card platform, over 100 deployed AI solutions and completed euro migration (A1). The 27/08/2026 locator re-scrape gives 154 of 167 branch records with a self-service zone, 137 of them 24/7. It also gives 501 ATM sites, of which **275 remain dispense-only**, with the estate growing (A1). There are two new corporate developments. Eurobank's 1H2026 interim statements disclose an agreement entered in February 2026. It is to acquire a controlling interest in a Bulgarian software company for about EUR 18m upfront plus an earn-out, and completion is expected in Q3-2026 (A1). Postbank is also setting up a whole IT service and security operations department, with six roles including the department head all posted in August 2026 (A5). The named current AI and integration stack in the back office is IBM watsonX with local integrator IBS, on a hybrid cloud-to-core middleware architecture (A1). Mellon Bulgaria was an official partner of Postbank's 35th-anniversary gala on 29/06/2026, with no scope disclosed (A6).
signals.date: 27/08/2026 — locator re-scrape with the estate still growing dispense-only; software-company acquisition completes Q3-2026; IT security operations department posted August 2026
signals.implies: This is the one Bulgarian bank expanding rather than shrinking its physical network, and it has published the requirements list itself. That list is a two-model self-service fleet, split between cash-capable devices and cashless kiosk devices. They can be dropped into 137 sites that already have 24/7 self-service zones and need no building work. The 275 dispense-only ATM sites are the parallel device slice, and new sites are still going in dispense-only, so the recycler decision is genuinely unmade. Two limits apply. A named rival already has warm access to this account, and the software purchase narrows the software scope on offer, while leaving hardware, cash automation and managed services untouched. The security operations build-out is an open window for service-desk and managed-services capacity while the team is being put together.

signals.bank_theme: BORICA / OpenWay Way4 — the national switch layer under every Bulgarian ATM bid
signals.signal: There is independent confirmation this cycle that BORICA's reach extends from the switch into the device layer and into state acquiring. The award release of 23/07/2026 states that OpenWay's Way4 platform provides the technological foundation of the national card infrastructure. That covers authorisation, card issuing, merchant servicing, card switching, ATM and POS device management, fraud prevention and transaction processing, across a programme of more than 35 participants. It handled over 930,000 card and ATM transactions worth close to EUR 42m in the first 48 hours of euro operation, with no unplanned outage. The two firms have worked together for more than seven years (A1, A6). Procurement records add the commercial side. BORICA holds the state card-acquiring rail. The National Revenue Agency contract is worth **EUR 9,381,606.79** and runs to 01/11/2028. The Road Infrastructure Agency contract is worth EUR 2,556,459.41 and includes host-to-host interface maintenance. Both explicitly cover physical POS terminals as well as virtual POS. The Ministry of e-Government contract was extended on 01/07/2026 by term only, to 29/05/2027. It was originally awarded by negotiated procedure without prior publication, on the stated ground of BORICA's exclusive rights, which is a formally declared sole-source incumbency (A2). A6 flags that OpenWay is absent from Printec's 164-name competitor roster, despite sitting inside national ATM and POS device management (A6).

signals.bank_theme: DSK Bank (OTP) — disclosed IT cost cycle, card-systems build-out and a greenfield kiosk layer
signals.signal: Bulgaria's largest retail bank has put a technology spend cycle on the record and is hiring for it. On the 1H-2026 results call of 05/08/2026, OTP said that in Bulgaria "normalized operating expenses increased by 22% year on year on an FX-adjusted basis". It gave the drivers as "several years of double-digit wage inflation as well as rising IT costs". It said euro-area entry cut the mandatory reserve ratio from 12% to 1%, and released almost **EUR 2bn** of previously non-interest-bearing liquidity at DSK. It also said revenue fell on lost FX-conversion income (A1). So the bank has both a named cost problem and balance-sheet room to fund capital spending. On the estate, OTP's statutory H1-2026 report gives DSK 952 ATMs at 30/06/2026 against 271 branches, so the machine count is up year on year while branches shrink. The 27/08/2026 locator shows the shrinkage is on the branch side, with ATM-bearing sites flat at 724 (A1). The self-service layer beyond the ATM is effectively greenfield, meaning untouched. Exactly one site in 777 carries a kiosk device, and 129 have a 24-hour self-service zone. Coin deposit is 100% manual at the counter, pre-sorted by denomination and explicitly excluded from the ATM deposit campaign (A1). Hiring supports this, with 38 live technology roles on dev.bg at 31/08/2026. They include two concurrent Functional Support Card Systems Expert postings, dated 04/08 and 14/08/2026. They also include an Enterprise Architect posted 27/08/2026, a Cloud Infrastructure Product Owner, and a Senior Governance Expert for an Innovation and AI Office (A5). Two limits apply. BPC's SmartVista is the entrenched card switch and ATM driving layer. It completed the BGN-to-EUR migration of 2.6m debit and 300k credit card accounts, and has a decade-long footprint spanning fraud management, merchant management and acquiring. A cluster of DSK Mobile and card-payment outages also ran through July 2026, with no ATM or branch fallback offered (A1).

signals.bank_theme: BORICA — centralised national anti-fraud model with SIBS, rules by end-2026 and market implementation from 2027
signals.signal: At a BORICA business event on 09/07/2026 on the PSD3 and PSR package, BORICA set out a centralised national fraud-prevention model for Bulgaria. It is built in partnership with the Portuguese processor SIBS. The national concept and rules are to be agreed by end-2026, with market implementation starting in 2027. The scheme's existing stack was confirmed at the same event. A Verification of Payee service has been live since October 2025 and is certified by the European Payments Council as a Qualified Routing and Verification Mechanism. A pre-transaction risk-assessment platform is built on IBM Safer Payments, using device fingerprinting, behavioural models and remote-access indicators. CEO Miroslav Vichev said individual institutional defences are no longer enough. The figures presented include EEA payment-fraud losses of EUR 4.2bn, up 17% year on year, of which credit-transfer fraud was EUR 2.5bn. Bulgarian credit-transfer fraud was about **EUR 7.9m**, roughly 70% of national losses, and IBAN-substitution fraud was EUR 13m in 2025. Instant transfers rose 87% to EUR 35bn, and there were 24,755 registered card-fraud cases. PSD3 and PSR final texts are expected around end-2026, with a 21-month compliance window. The agreed PSD3 text gives existing payment and e-money institutions until entry-into-force plus 27 months to re-authorise (A2, A5, A6). BORICA is a bank-owned private joint-stock company, so this will never appear as a public procurement notice. It is a direct commercial purchase (A2).

signals.bank_theme: Bulgaria — coin handling, the unautomated tail of the changeover
signals.signal: Coin is the one part of the euro cash cycle that Bulgarian banks are still handling by hand. BNB's own procurement has just sized the volume about to reach the system. UBB received over BGN 33m of coin by end-May 2026, roughly 370 tonnes, BGN 21.5m of it in January alone. signals.bank_theme: ProCredit Bank Bulgaria — a euro fee-income hole and a bank staffing up to run its own ATM estate
signals.signal: ProCredit Holding's Q2-2026 results presentation of 13/08/2026 flags euro introduction in Bulgaria as an FY-2026 extraordinary development with a measured negative. It reports "reduced fee income potential due to decrease in number of FX transactions" of a mid single-digit EUR million amount, against long-term benefits. It says that without the extraordinary items, group return on equity and cost-income would already have improved visibly. Bulgaria is at the same time the group's largest single-bank profit contributor, at **EUR 16.9m** of H1-2026 profit on a EUR 2,047m loan portfolio (A1). The estate is deliberately tiny and self-service-led. There are 18 sites: 17 offices plus one standalone 24/7 zone. Of the 17 offices, 14 carry an attached 24/7 self-service area, so 15 of the 18 sites have one. Staffed hours are only 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays. The bank publishes a four-tier cash stack. First, ATMs taking all seven euro note denominations, up to 50 notes per operation, and dispensing to any issuer's card. Second, a separate EUR and BGN deposit machine, up to EUR 10,000 per transaction. Third, a bulk envelope deposit safe up to EUR 25,000 under prior contract, using barcode-scanned envelopes with the slip booked afterwards in internet banking. Fourth, a contracted cash-in-transit service (A1). Separately, a live "Expert Cash Management" posting in Sofia dated 24/08/2026 turns out on inspection to be an ATM and self-service operations role, not treasury. It covers monitoring 24/7 ATM self-service zones, handling cash-machine customer requests, working with external suppliers, evaluating ATM performance, and maintaining documentation and regulatory compliance (A5). Identity and signing are bought from local qualified providers, Evrotrust and B-Trust Mobile, while the mobile app is built in-house by the group's own IT subsidiary Quipu (A1).

The scope needs a correction: the release is tagged Germany and was issued in German. So it is a DACH go-to-market move, not a Bulgarian bank win. Even so, Evrotrust raised EUR 6.6m in November 2025 specifically to deploy the EU Digital Identity Wallet in Bulgaria. Its published Bulgarian bank reference is **UniCredit Bulbank**, which uses it for mobile-banking onboarding (A6). Independently, ProCredit Bulgaria's own site navigation names Evrotrust for signing and identification, and B-Trust Mobile for confirmation. This confirms that the identity and e-signature layer in Bulgaria is bought from local qualified providers in each market. It comes up for renewal on its own cycle, while the banking app itself is built in-house (A1). Separately again, on 18/06/2026 the listed Bulgarian integrator Sirma Group became a Temenos Referral Partner, initially in Bulgaria and Albania. The aim is to introduce qualified core-banking opportunities. The two have worked together for years, and Sirma's cloud-migration service is listed on Temenos Exchange (A6).
signals.date: 04/08/2026 — Evrotrust launches its combined eKYC and qualified-signature workflow; Sirma becomes a Temenos Referral Partner for Bulgaria and Albania 18/06/2026
signals.implies: Two areas are getting harder to compete in at the same time. On identity, a domestic qualified trust service provider that already holds the UniCredit Bulbank reference is assembling a complete electronic know-your-customer (eKYC) and qualified-signature stack. Bidding identity capture alone against it is not defensible. The workable position is to bundle onboarding with AML and sanctions screening, and with branch and self-service capture. The argument to make is that banks need an orchestration layer across channels, rather than a single signature supplier. On core banking, a Bulgarian integrator now has a formal channel into Bulgarian and Albanian core modernisation. Core replacement is exactly the moment when ATM middleware, kiosk and onboarding stacks get re-tendered alongside the core. So the sensible posture is to sub-contract scope under Sirma rather than fight for the prime slot. The Albanian half of that partnership may matter more than the Bulgarian half.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the Evrotrust launch market is Germany rather than Bulgaria, and Sirma has no named bank programme yet, so both are capability-building rather than live displacement
signals.follow_up: Watch for a Bulgarian-language version of the Evrotrust, Shufti and sproof announcement. That would signal the workflow being sold into Bulgarian banks. Check whether any bank beyond UniCredit Bulbank adopts it. Watch for the first named Bulgarian or Albanian Temenos programme referred by Sirma. Find out whether Sirma bids ATM and self-service scope itself, or sub-contracts it.
signals.product_review_why: A local trust provider is closing the eKYC and signature lane, so onboarding must be bundled with AML screening, while a core-banking channel opens through Sirma.

signals.bank_theme: Bulgaria — European Accessibility Act market surveillance now bites on ATMs and payment terminals
signals.signal: Bulgaria has transposed the European Accessibility Act as the Law on Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services. It was published in State Gazette issue 31 of 11/04/2025 and came into force on 28/06/2025. The gazette text has been read, and it covers the device estate explicitly. Article 2 names **payment terminals and ATM terminal devices** alongside ticketing and information terminals, and it covers consumer banking services. Article 34(1) makes the Chairman of DAMTN, the metrology and technical surveillance agency, the market-surveillance authority for those products under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Article 39 lets him order temporary suspension of supply. He may also prohibit making a product available or putting it into service, or order withdrawal of the product from the market. Article 54(1)(8) makes BNB the control body for consumer banking services. The dated change is in the penalties. A transitional provision halved all Chapter Six penalties for infringements committed up to 01/06/2026. Full rates have applied since that date: BGN 1,000 to 5,000 on individuals, or BGN 5,000 to 25,000 on undertakings, doubling on repeat breach. Transitional rules also cover the installed estate. Self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life, but no more than 20 years from entry into use. The general service-provider transition ends 28/06/2030. One correction was recorded this cycle. The previously carried 28/06/2027 supervisory milestone applies to emergency-call provisions, not to ATMs or payment terminals. No DAMTN or BNB enforcement action against an ATM or payment terminal had been published as at 27/08/2026 (A3).

sources.text: Държавен вестник issue 31 of 11/04/2025 — Law on Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services (BG)

signals.date: 01/06/2026 — full-rate penalties in force since the transitional discount expired; general service-provider compliance deadline 28/06/2030 and a 20-year economic-life backstop on terminals in use before 28/06/2025
signals.implies: There are two distinct levers here, and the fines are the less important one. On the supply side, DAMTN can ban or withdraw a non-compliant ATM or payment-terminal model from the Bulgarian market. So every machine sold there needs a current EU Declaration of Conformity and EN 301 549 accessibility evidence. That is a competitive advantage against older or grey-import terminal stock, rather than a cost. On the demand side, BNB supervises the accessibility of consumer banking services. This reaches the same banks at the same moment as the post-euro recycler and cash-automation programme. One engagement can therefore carry both euro-ready cash handling and an accessible interface. With penalties capped around BGN 50,000, sell the market-withdrawal risk and the bundling, not fine avoidance.
signals.likelihood: Medium — in force with full-rate penalties, but no enforcement action against a terminal has yet been published and the substantive compliance deadline is 2030
signals.follow_up: Monitor DAMTN's market-surveillance register and BNB supervisory announcements for the first accessibility action against a payment terminal or ATM. Confirm whether DAMTN has published a sectoral inspection plan covering self-service terminals. Make sure conformity and EN 301 549 evidence is ready for every ATM and PIN-entry device model offered in Bulgaria, before it is asked for.
signals.product_review_why: Accessibility compliance now applies to every ATM and payment terminal sold in Bulgaria and can be bundled with the cash-automation refresh.

signals.bank_theme: Croatia — national shared ATM network (HUB / Ministry of Finance / HNB)
signals.signal: The legal basis is now fully sourced, and the decision on the operating model is close. The obligation comes from the amendments to the payment-account comparability and basic-account law, Narodne novine 105/2025 of 23/07/2025. Banks have a transition period to 01/01/2027 to set up a national shared ATM network. If they do not, every bank must let any consumer who is not its own client withdraw cash free of charge twice a month (A5, A2). The Government has confirmed that a Memorandum of Cooperation between the Ministry of Finance, the central bank and the banks would remove that provision from the law. The banking association HUB commissioned an Ernst & Young study that produced three candidate operating models. The study is not public, and a decision was reported as weeks away as at 27/04/2026 (A2). Market scale is reported as 3,816 active ATMs, with over 4,700 at the summer 2026 peak. The shared MBnet infrastructure covers roughly 1,000 machines across 12 member banks. There are 106 million ATM withdrawals a year, worth EUR 19.24 billion. The central bank had earlier proposed the state Financial Agency FINA as operator, then left implementation to direct agreement between the banks. Confirmed again this cycle: nothing about this will ever appear on the national e-procurement portal or on TED. A full TED sweep of Croatian ATM and cash procurement classes returns zero commercial-bank notices (A2).

sources.text: Vlada RH statement on ATM withdrawal fees

signals.date: 01/01/2027 — the interbank shared-network deadline, after which free twice-monthly cross-bank withdrawals become compulsory · 27/04/2026 — three Ernst & Young operating models on the table, decision reported as weeks away
signals.implies: This is still the largest structural ATM opening in Croatia, and less than eighteen months remain. Whichever operating model is chosen, a pooled network needs multivendor ATM software, so one set of screens can drive machines from different manufacturers. It also needs device monitoring, cash-cycle optimisation and managed field services. A refresh toward recyclers is very likely. Recyclers are ATMs that re-dispense the notes customers have deposited. Because the work is bought privately through the banking association, there is no notice to respond to. The only route in is pre-tender positioning with HUB and the largest member banks. Printec's independently operated off-site ATM estate in Greece is the reference to lead with.

signals.follow_up: Approach HUB and the biggest member banks now, using the independent-ATM-operator model as the reference case. Ask the central bank's payment-systems area which of the three models it could supervise most easily. Try to get the Ernst & Young model summary through a member bank. Do not wait for a procurement notice, because there will not be one.

signals.bank_theme: Croatian banks — measurable per-bank ATM deposit gap now public from the central-bank cash-point registry (ZABA, PBZ, RBA)
signals.signal: The Croatian National Bank runs a public national registry of cash access points that computers can read. We downloaded it in full on 27/08/2026. It returns 6,852 records from 26 reporting providers. These are 3,841 cash-out-only ATMs, 901 machines that take deposits and give cash, 85 cash-in-only machines, 126 coin deposit machines, 1,860 branches and 39 cashless branches. Each record carries the provider name, tax number, address and coordinates (A1). The split by provider is the finding. Zagrebačka banka has the largest fleet in the country, with 562 cash-out-only ATMs against 137 that take deposits. That is a 19.6% deposit share, the worst of the big four. It also has 95 branches, of which 5 are cashless. Privredna banka Zagreb has 429 cash-out-only machines against 239 that take deposits, a 35.8% share and the best of the big four, plus 128 branches. But its own 2025 annual report admits to just 22 coin-payment devices, and only five machines that take both banknotes and coins. Raiffeisenbank Austria has 286 cash-out-only against 150 that take deposits, a 34.4% share, and 17 cashless branches, the most in the market. This shows the cashless-branch model is already growing. Roughly 2,400 cash-out-only machines sit in the six largest bank-owned fleets. Hiring confirms where the money is moving (A5). PBZ has 52 live Croatian vacancies, including a Chief Manager for the Payment Instrument Acquiring Directorate and a rebuild of branch counters across two dozen small towns. RBA has 21 vacancies, mostly in IT risk, resilience and governance. Zagrebačka banka, by contrast, has ten vacancies and none at all in ATMs, self-service, payments, cards or channels.
signals.date: 27/08/2026 — first full pull of the central bank's per-device cash-point registry, giving a per-bank deposit-capability map · bank careers boards re-enumerated 31/08/2026
signals.implies: Printec now has a free map from the regulator that can be refreshed at any time. It shows exactly which Croatian bank is short of deposit machines and where, down to the coordinates of each machine. A target list like this normally takes months of fieldwork. Read together with the free-withdrawal and free-deposit duties that start on 01/01/2027, it shows Zagrebačka banka as the biggest single conversion group in the country. It also shows that PBZ has almost no coin or mixed banknote-and-coin automation at all. RBA's 17 cashless branches are the clearest sign that a branch-conversion programme is already running. Each converted site needs at least one machine that takes deposits. The hiring pattern shows where to knock. PBZ and RBA are staffing up locally. Zagrebačka banka's technology demand plainly runs through UniCredit group hubs, so it must be approached through group vendor management rather than the Zagreb board.
signals.likelihood: High that at least one of the three commits to deposit-capability investment within twelve months; no tender or programme is published by any of them
signals.follow_up: Build a target list for each bank from the registry's coordinate records. Refresh it monthly and compare the counts of deposit-capable machines, because a jump is the buying signal. Approach PBZ through the acquiring directorate hire, and RBA through the cashless-branch programme. Go to Zagrebačka banka via UniCredit group procurement. Separately, ask the central bank which legal instrument obliges providers to submit the data, since the registry note names none.
signals.product_review_why: The registry maps which banks lack deposit-capable machines, and cashless branch conversion adds self-service demand.

signals.bank_theme: Erste & Steiermärkische Bank (Erste Croatia) — 467 withdrawal-only ATMs
signals.signal: We checked this again from two independent angles, and the gap has not closed. Erste Croatia's own locator, retrieved 27/08/2026, returns 665 ATMs. Of these, 199 accept deposits (29.9%) and 466 are withdrawal-only, with 161 inside branches. The central bank's registry independently gives 468 cash-out plus 198 cash-in-and-out = 666 machines. It also lists 66 cash-in-only devices and 66 coin machines. The branch picture is worse than the master row recorded. Of 106 branches, 100 still run a staffed cash desk and only 6 are cashless, not 97 and 9 (A1). Even so, the conversion programme is live and dated. A fully cashless branch opened in Kastav on 12/01/2026 with a 24-hour self-service zone. It holds a deposit-and-withdrawal ATM plus a device the bank brands "Erste Smart Cash". From 01/04/2026 a list of branches moved to opening hours where part of the day is kept for advice and cashless business only. Customers are sent to self-service devices for cash. On the commercial side, the bank has just left card issuing and acquiring, which is handling card payments for shops. The sale of Erste Card Club d.o.o. to Global Payments s.r.o. of Czechia closed in January 2026. It booked a EUR 116m gain and cut Croatian fee income by 13.2%. So its fee income now leans harder on account and cash services. H1-2026 net profit was EUR 234m against EUR 135m a year earlier. The cost-to-income ratio improved to 49.1%. Erste is also hiring a Senior Cyber Fraud Specialist in Zagreb, posted 25/08/2026 with a 04/09/2026 deadline (A5).

That gives two openings at once. The first is recyclers, which are ATMs that re-use deposited notes, to take cash-in off 100 staffed counters. The second is managed services to run an unattended estate. The card sale matters twice over. Get the branch list attached to the 29/01/2026 opening-hours notice, and count how many sites need a deposit device. Find out which hardware sits behind "Erste Smart Cash". Find the manufacturer of the 665 machines, and check whether an Erste group ATM framework would block a local sale. Separately, track Global Payments' Croatian terminal count and its plan to move to a new platform.

signals.bank_theme: OTP banka Hrvatska — 353 withdrawal-only ATMs plus a funded branch-reformatting programme
signals.signal: Three independent sources now agree within five machines. OTP's own locator feed on 27/08/2026 lists 459 ATMs with 459 unique terminal identifiers. Only 109 take deposits and give cash, and 350 are cash-out only, a 23.7% deposit share. Of the fleet, 113 are inside branches and 346 are off-premise, against 95 branches. The central bank registry gives 350 plus 110 = 460. OTP Group's own Q2-2026 analyst tables report the Croatian unit at 455 ATMs and 99 branches at 30/06/2026. signals.bank_theme: Hrvatska poštanska banka (HPB) — declared card-ecosystem change programme, a won toll-road acquiring contract and the country's worst deposit ratio
signals.signal: Three independent strands point to the same bank in the same cycle. First, HPB has a live vacancy for a Senior Specialist in Card Business Development, confirmed live on 31/08/2026. Its text says the bank has "defined a clear vision and strategy that will position us among leading banks in the card segment". It adds that this "also requires implementing changes in our card ecosystem". The role covers both issuing and acquiring. That is close to platform-replacement language at Croatia's largest domestically-owned bank (A5). Second, HPB won the largest Croatian open-loop card-acceptance tender of 2026. Hrvatske autoceste, the motorway operator, awarded acceptance of Visa, Mastercard and Maestro across its e-commerce and toll-plaza terminal channels at EUR 1,141,358, against an estimate of EUR 1,600,000. The contract is dated 07/04/2026, and the award notice was published 07/08/2026, with five bidders (A2). So HPB has to deploy and manage a fleet of EFTPOS (card payment) terminals on the motorway network. Third, the central-bank registry puts HPB at 288 cash-out-only ATMs against just 41 that take deposits. That is a 12.5% deposit share, the worst gap-to-fleet ratio of any large Croatian bank. It also has 65 branches with no cashless branches, plus a partner network of 219 ATMs run by Cashere and 973 Hrvatska pošta counter locations (A1).
signals.date: 31/08/2026 — card-strategy vacancy confirmed live, bank states its card ecosystem must change · 07/08/2026 — HAC acquiring award to HPB published, contract dated 07/04/2026
signals.implies: This bank has publicly said its card platform must change. It has just won an acquiring contract that requires it to field a new unattended terminal estate on toll plazas. It also has the weakest deposit-capable ATM ratio in the country. Together, those three facts make it the best-qualified Croatian buying centre this cycle. The scope touches card issuing and acquiring software, POS and unattended terminal supply with terminal management, key-management hardware, deposit-capable ATMs and managed services, all at once. Unlike the foreign-owned banks, HPB takes the decision in Zagreb rather than at a group hub.

signals.follow_up: Find out who HPB's current card processor is, and whether a formal tender is planned. Approach through the payments and direct-channels divisions. Separately, open a conversation now on supplying terminals, terminal management and unattended POS for the HAC contract, rather than waiting for the next cycle. Put the 288 cash-out-only machines on the table in the same meeting.
signals.product_review_why: The bank says its card platform must change, must field unattended toll-plaza terminals, and has the weakest deposit-capable ATM share in Croatia.

signals.bank_theme: Hrvatska poštanska banka — crypto-asset authorisation supervised by the central bank
signals.signal: The Croatian route for banks is now clear, and it is not a licence application. HANFA, the financial-services supervisor, published on 03/07/2026 that from 01/07/2026 firms providing crypto services need a licence and registration. It also said that five Croatian crypto licences have been granted. Bitblock, Digital Assets, Electrocoin and White Tech are already in the register, and IN Kapital is awaiting court registration. The key point is the route for banks. HANFA states that financial institutions already supervised by HANFA or by the Croatian National Bank go through a notification procedure under Article 60 of the EU crypto-asset regulation. They do not need a full licence application (A3). That is the mechanism behind HPB's existing authorisation. The European securities regulator's interim register records it with competent authority "Croatian National Bank" and notification date 16/06/2026. It is still the only entry in Printec's whole footprint whose crypto supervisor is a central bank. HANFA keeps two separate lists: its own register of licensed providers, and a list of firms notified from other member states.

Zagrebačka banka, PBZ, Erste Croatia and OTP Croatia are the follow-on. If none of them has yet filed a notification, that is a sales opening rather than a closed door.

signals.bank_theme: Croatia — the 22% H1-2026 ATM build-out is coastal, low-specification and third-party, not a bank recycler wave
signals.signal: Central-bank infrastructure tables published 25/08/2026 show installed ATMs rising from 3,787 at 31/01/2026 to 4,633 at 30/06/2026. That is 846 machines, or 22.3%, in five months. Card terminals rose from 156,053 to 166,677, and bank branches fell from 781 to 777. Three further cuts of the data show what the growth actually is (A1). By county, seven coastal counties account for +859 machines, more than the whole national increase. They are Split-Dalmatia +313, Istria +153, Dubrovnik-Neretva +109 and Zadar +89. The other three are Primorje-Gorski kotar +80, Šibenik-Knin +66 and Lika-Senj +49. The City of Zagreb fell from 753 to 744, and every inland county was flat or down. By feature, the growth is almost all contact-only machines with no tap capability, up 809 to 2,502. Contactless-capable ATMs barely moved, up 42 to 2,131. By operator, the registry identifies four non-bank or partner deployers running 1,094 machines in Croatia. Every one of them is cash-out only with zero deposit capability: Euronet with RBA 685, Cashere as an HPB partner 219, Monestiq 119 and MoneyGet 71. MoneyGet is the independent-deployer brand of Printec's nearest regional rival Payten. Payten's own H1-2026 report separately admits that its ATM equipment deliveries fell in Croatia (A6). Meanwhile day and night deposit boxes fell from 367 to 362, and coin machines rose only from 40 to 45.
signals.date: 25/08/2026 — central bank publishes the H1-2026 infrastructure tables · registry and provider pull 27/08/2026 · re-test at the October and December updates
signals.implies: Reading the headline 22% as lasting demand would badly overstate it. Much of the fleet is seasonal capacity on the tourist coast that may come out after the season. That makes it a managed-service and short-term-deployment market rather than a capital-equipment one. The structural signals point the other way. Manual cash-in is being retired, because deposit boxes are disappearing with no automated replacement. Zagreb's fleet is shrinking, and there are only 45 coin machines in the whole country. Two commercial consequences follow. First, the independent deployers are themselves a buyer of scale, with 1,094 machines needing hardware, monitoring and field service. Second, because none of them accepts deposits, deposit capability still falls back on the banks, which protects the recycler opportunity. The low-specification contact-only fleet also creates a later wave of contactless and deposit upgrades.
signals.likelihood: High that a share of the coastal machines is withdrawn after the season — measurable in the Q4 files; the independent fleet is already installed
signals.follow_up: Pull the county table again after the October and December updates. The size of the post-season drop measures how much of the fleet is seasonal, and therefore service rather than capital. Check Monestiq and MoneyGet in the company register, and find out who supplies and services their machines. Confirm how the 685 Euronet-with-RBA units split between the two before sizing. Pitch seasonal and managed-service ATM models on the coast, and recycler replacement of the declining deposit-box estate inland.
