signals.bank_theme: Croatia — free-basic-services package: deposit-migration driver with a coin carve-out
signals.signal: The legal basis is now confirmed, which closes the master row's open question. The instrument is the Act amending the law on comparability of fees, payment-account switching and access to a basic account. It was published in the official gazette Narodne novine 105/2025 on 23/07/2025 (A5). From 01/01/2026 any consumer receiving regular income into a payment account may request a free basic package. It covers account opening and maintenance, and internet or mobile banking at the bank's choice. It also covers cash deposits at counters or ATMs, excluding coin processing, and cash withdrawals at the account bank's own counters or ATMs. Incoming transfers are included, as are the issue and use of a debit card at physical points of sale. From 01/01/2027 package holders and vulnerable basic-account holders may also withdraw cash twice a month free of charge at any other Croatian bank's ATMs. The Ministry of Finance question-and-answer document of 04/02/2026 confirms the coin carve-out word for word. The bank's response deadline fell from 30 days to 10 working days on 02/07/2026. Take-up remains small, at 108,171 packages against 5.9m consumer accounts, or 1.6%. Nationally there are only 45 coin-deposit machines (A1). A contradiction is also resolved. One A1 row this cycle warned that the 01/01/2027 cash-access right could not be substantiated. It is substantiated, by the gazette citation, the Ministry press release and the Government's own statement (A2).

sources.text: Ministarstvo financija — free basic services package

signals.date: 01/01/2027 — two free monthly withdrawals at any other bank's ATMs begin · 23/07/2025 statute published as NN 105/2025 · 04/02/2026 Ministry confirms the coin carve-out · 02/07/2026 response deadline cut to 10 working days
signals.implies: The law does not force banks to offer ATM deposits, because a bank can comply with tellers alone. But complying free of charge at the counter is the expensive way to do it. That pushes banks to steer free deposits onto recyclers and deposit ATMs, and to improve their cash cycle. From 01/01/2027 banks also absorb much more foreign-card withdrawal traffic, meaning cards from other banks, with no fee recovery. That is precisely what makes a pooled or outsourced ATM operating model attractive. The strongest commercial point is still the coin carve-out. Coin handling can still be charged for, so coin automation is a revenue product to sell rather than a compliance cost, in a market with 45 machines installed nationally. Size the near-term deposit-migration case on the actual 1.6% take-up, not on the whole retail base.
signals.likelihood: Certain in law — the 02/07/2026 milestone has passed and 01/01/2027 is fixed; commercial volume is gated by package take-up
signals.follow_up: Model the shift in cross-bank withdrawals, and the shift in deposits from counter to ATM, bank by bank. Take it to each of the big six before 01/01/2027, paired with an ATM-as-a-service or pooled-estate offer. Track package take-up every quarter. If it stays near 1.6%, the deposit-migration business case is far weaker than the headline. Pitch coin automation separately as a chargeable add-on.
signals.product_review_why: Free counter deposits push banks toward deposit ATMs, recyclers and coin machines, and the 2027 cross-bank withdrawal rule favours a pooled or outsourced estate.

signals.bank_theme: Croatia — European Accessibility Act (NN 89/2025): the harshest fines in the footprint, with the central bank as supervisor of bank services
signals.signal: Croatia's transposition of the European Accessibility Act, its version of the EU law in national law, was adopted on 06/06/2025. It was published in the official gazette Narodne novine 89/2025 on 13/06/2025, and entered into force on 28/06/2025. The gazette text has been verified (A3). It covers self-service terminals, including ATMs, payment terminals, ticketing machines and interactive information terminals. Market surveillance of those products sits with the State Inspectorate. Surveillance of consumer banking services sits with the Croatian National Bank and the financial-services supervisor, each within its own remit. The penalties are the highest of the five transpositions checked this cycle. A manufacturer that is a legal person faces EUR 6,630 to EUR 132,720 for placing on the market a product not designed to the accessibility requirements. The same band applies to a service provider that fails to make its service accessible. That is an order of magnitude, about ten times, above Cyprus, Romania and Bulgaria. Service providers have until 28/06/2030. Self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life, but no more than twenty years from entry into use. An annex example literally requires "fitting a socket and installing software on the ATM to allow headphones to be connected so that on-screen text is reproduced as sound". It also requires text-to-speech, time-out warnings in more than one sense, time extension, contrast, keys that can be told apart by touch, and no need for high force. No enforcement decision against any bank or terminal had been published as at 27/08/2026.

sources.text: Narodne novine 89/2025, item 1231 — Zakon o zahtjevima za pristupačnost proizvoda i usluga

signals.date: STANDING: 13/06/2025 — Act published in the official gazette, in force 28/06/2025 · service-provider transition ends 28/06/2030 · no enforcement action published as at 27/08/2026
signals.implies: Croatia carries the sharpest accessibility enforcement risk in the region. Uniquely, the prudential supervisor of these same banks is also their accessibility supervisor for consumer services. That makes it a board-level issue rather than a facilities one. Named exposure covers every large Croatian bank. The work it creates is specific. It includes ATMs with the audio socket and screen-reader stack the annex literally describes, and accessibility retrofits where the chassis allows. It includes multivendor ATM software, so one compliant accessible interface can run across machines from different manufacturers. It also includes accessible PIN pads with remote software push to merchant estates. Above all it includes an estate audit that sets each machine's twenty-year clock. Budgets are committed in 2028-2029 for a 2030 estate, so the audit and roadmap are what sell now. No enforcement action has been taken so far, and that is the pre-enforcement period in which readiness sells.
signals.likelihood: In force and unenforced — the estate deadline is 28/06/2030, beyond the twelve-month horizon, so this is a standing driver rather than a live trigger
signals.follow_up: Sell an estate accessibility audit and roadmap now, to establish each machine's remaining economic life against the twenty-year cap. Monitor the State Inspectorate's published inspection results and central-bank supervisory notices for the first accessibility action. Ask the central bank whether it intends to issue a supervisory expectation on accessibility of consumer banking services, as the Hungarian regulator has.
signals.product_review_why: This is an accessibility compliance deadline that drives ATM audits and retrofits plus accessible PIN pads.

signals.bank_theme: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) — Hellenic Bank merger: ~156-ATM harmonisation and an April-2027 core cutover
signals.signal: The 156-ATM figure no longer comes from press coverage. We read the Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Review 2025-2026 directly. It gives Eurobank Limited 156 ATMs, 59 branches and 2,450 staff. That is the largest ATM estate on the island, and 49% of the 321 machines run by the eight member banks (A1). · The bank's own channel data, released 06/08/2026, is a stronger anchor. ATMs now handle 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits, rather than a counter. The branch share of all transactions fell from 4.7% in 2024 to 3.5%. Card payments at shop terminals (card-at-POS) are 68.5% of transactions. · The 1H-2026 disclosures (30/07/2026) show 67 outlets and 2,716 staff. The 67 outlets are 52 retail branches plus 15 business and private-banking centres. In Q2-2026 alone the bank cut 139 staff and 6 business centres, while 2 retail branches were added. · The directors repeat that the operational merger is under way "to provide unified platforms". A voluntary exit of about 200 staff finished in April 2026. It cost EUR 35m one-off and saves about EUR 14m a year. Cyprus adjusted net profit fell 7.7% year on year to EUR 231m, even though the group grew. · The FY-2025 deck puts Cyprus merger synergies at EUR 140m, fully in place by 2027, with EUR 85m still to capture. Only about EUR 25m of that is operating cost. Eurobank's group technology programme "Banking Forward", announced 29/06/2026, is worth about EUR 1bn for 2025-2028. It names Cyprus in scope but publishes no Cyprus allocation. · On vendors, the much smaller ex-Eurobank Cyprus side went live on Temenos core, digital and financial-crime software in June 2024. AML (anti-money-laundering) software is therefore contested. ATM hardware, ATM driving software, recyclers and managed services sit outside that scope. The bank has itself named ATMs among the infrastructure it must update to the new corporate image (A5).
signals.date: 06/08/2026 — the bank discloses that almost 90% of deposits and 95% of withdrawals now go through machines, not branches · 30/07/2026 1H-2026 results, 67 outlets and 2,716 staff · 18/06/2026 the banking association's own annual review confirms the 156-ATM fleet · core cutover targeted April 2027
signals.implies: Nine in ten deposits already come through the machines, so those machines are doing the teller's job. To keep doing it they must accept deposits and recycle cash. A recycler is an ATM or counter machine that re-dispenses the notes customers have just paid in. · Two legacy estates must be moved onto one driver, one hardware and software generation and one service contract before the April-2027 cutover. The staffed branch network is shrinking around them. · Printec is not a named incumbent at this bank. ATM and self-service consolidation, cash-cycle and cash-in-transit optimisation, and the branch-and-ATM re-imaging work are therefore all open to win. Do not size the opportunity from the EUR 1bn group headline, because no Cyprus allocation is published.
signals.likelihood: High — specification and vendor choices must run through H2-2026 to hit an April-2027 cutover
signals.follow_up: Get in front of the Cyprus integration programme office before the specifications are frozen. Ask how many of the 156 machines actually accept deposits today, because that gap is the sale. Find out which of the two legacy cores and which ATM switch survive. Establish who the ATM OEM (original maker) inherited from Hellenic Bank is. Ask investor relations for the Cyprus integration capex and synergy schedule, and for a date to retire the remaining branch-in-branch sites.

signals.bank_theme: Cyprus — payment-fraud surge against a hard Verification-of-Payee cut-over
signals.signal: The master row's figures are out of date. The Central Bank of Cyprus published Payment Fraud Statistics for the second half of 2025 on 25/08/2026. Total fraud value was EUR 3.7m, up 16% year on year, on about 14,000 incidents, down 5%. Value is rising while volume falls, which differs from the increase in both recorded in the H1-2025 release. · Credit transfers account for EUR 2m or 56% of fraud value. The average fraudulent credit transfer in Cyprus is EUR 6,300, against EUR 1,800 across the euro area. On the regulator's own statement, that is the highest average value in the euro area. · Manipulation of the payer, that is authorised push-payment fraud where the victim is tricked into sending the money, is 70% of credit-transfer fraud cases. Payment-service users bear about 95% of credit-transfer fraud losses. Cards are 93% of fraudulent transactions. Online is 96% of card-fraud cases and 94% of value, despite being roughly 30% of card volume (A1, A5). · A regulatory caveat must travel with this row. The 20/09/2026 03:30 CET Verification-of-Payee rulebook v1.1 cut-over carried in the master row is unverified. The European Payments Council site returned a Cloudflare block on every route tried, so nobody has opened the primary document. The date must not go in a client paper (A3). · What is confirmed comes from the banking association's own Greek-language announcement. Cyprus went live with instant payments and Verification of Payee, which checks the payee's name against the IBAN, from 09/10/2025 under the Instant Payments Regulation. At that point Cypriot banks were still only at study stage on a voluntary common mobile-alias platform. It would allow payment by phone number or email instead of IBAN, and was expected to operate within 2026 (A3).

signals.date: 25/08/2026 — the central bank publishes H2-2025 fraud statistics showing the euro area's highest average fraudulent credit transfer at EUR 6,300 · the 20/09/2026 Verification-of-Payee v1.1 cut-over remains unverified at primary source
signals.implies: This is a regulator-owned, measured and very recent problem. The average loss is EUR 6,300, three and a half times the euro-area average. Social engineering causes 70% of it, and 95% of the loss lands on the customer rather than the bank. · That reputational exposure moves budget. It is the case for behavioural and authorised-push-payment analytics, real-time transaction monitoring, name-matching tuning and stronger authentication, sold as a fix rather than a new build. · Bank of Cyprus as the largest issuer and JCC as the acquirer are the two doors. Alpha Bank Cyprus is at its highest-risk moment while it merges two customer bases. The mobile-alias platform, if it went ahead, is a real build needing an alias directory, instant screening and key management. Chase it with the association directly.

signals.bank_theme: Cyprus — a direct-sales market, not a tender market, with the Housing Finance Corporation the one public bank buyer
signals.signal: This is a documented zero, and it is a coverage finding as much as a commercial one. Across this cycle there is no open or awarded Cypriot public notice in any of our product areas. That covers ATMs and ATM software, recyclers, self-service and branch kiosks, POS terminals and terminal management, and softPOS. It also covers instant payments, transaction-monitoring and fraud systems, key-management hardware and ATM physical security. · The reason is structural. The commercial banks are private companies, so they are not contracting authorities, and their buying never reaches the portal or the EU journal. The Central Bank of Cyprus buys entirely outside the national portal under its own directives. It publishes in the Official Gazette and on its own site, and reaches the EU journal only above threshold. It then deletes closed notices, so its sub-threshold pipeline is invisible after the fact (A2). · The exception is the state-owned Housing Finance Corporation, the only Cypriot bank that is a contracting authority. It awarded project-management services to Deloitte Limited at EUR 648,520, against a EUR 650,000 estimate. That was a single bid, award date 10/07/2026, after the notice had to be published four times. It also paid Pansophic Software EUR 13,800, unopposed and without a prior call for competition, to move its property valuation system out of KEDIPES' data centres. · Those awards show two things. The run-off vehicle for the former co-operative bank book is being wound down and its shared IT moved elsewhere. And a credible bidder can win at this buyer with no competition at all (A2, A6). · Adjacent public cash-handling demand exists outside the banks. The Electricity Authority's banknote-counter tender, at a EUR 55,000 estimate, drew four bids. They were TH.K. Office Supplies at EUR 31,400 and Mastertype C.P. Services at EUR 33,000. A. Finiris bid EUR 43,600 and Brink's Cyprus EUR 59,050. That tender has sat under evaluation for ten and a half months. The central bank's SWIFT gateway administration contract went to Allied Engineering Group (Cyprus) at EUR 415,000 on a single bid.

signals.bank_theme: Cyprus accessibility law — a 28/06/2030 replacement cliff for every ATM and payment terminal
signals.signal: Cyprus brought the European Accessibility Act into national law through the Accessibility of Products and Services Law N.57(I)/2024, gazetted on 02/05/2024. We read the primary Greek legal text directly this cycle to close a verification gap carried from before. · It applies to products placed on the market from 28/06/2025. It expressly names self-service terminals, including payment terminals and ATMs, ticketing machines, check-in machines and interactive information terminals. · Section 45 gives a transitional period ending 28/06/2030. During it a service provider may keep using products it lawfully used before that date. Service contracts signed before 28/06/2025 may run to expiry, but never beyond five years. That sets a firm replacement deadline for the installed estate. · The competent authority is the Deputy Minister of Social Welfare, not the central bank and not the consumer-protection service. The Council of Ministers has still not published the decision naming the accessibility surveillance authorities, so enforcement remains a live gap. · Administrative fines are low, at EUR 10,000, or EUR 20,000 for a repeat breach. The criminal provision runs to two years' imprisonment on a first conviction and three on a second (A3).

signals.bank_theme: Cyprus acceptance market — softPOS erodes terminal supply while Mellon takes full local control

signals.bank_theme: Czech banks — instant euro payments and Verification of Payee, on a fixed 2027 clock
signals.signal: The Czech National Bank confirms on its own instant-payments page, re-read 27/08/2026, that from January 2027 Czech banks must be able to receive instant euro payments. The CNB states, in its own words, that the system for instant euro payments is not operated by the CNB. It adds that the system has nothing to do with participation in CERTIS. Every Czech bank must therefore buy its own euro instant reachability and stack (A3). · We re-read the underlying legal text and reversed an earlier wrong date. Under Regulation (EU) 2024/886 the calendar for non-euro member states is as follows. From 09/01/2027 banks must receive instant euro transfers and meet the charges-parity rule. From 09/04/2027 e-money and payment institutions must receive. From 09/07/2027 all providers must send, and must offer Verification of Payee, the payee-name-against-IBAN match, free of charge (A3). · Domestic koruna instant payments are already mainstream. CERTIS carried nearly 43.6 million payments in June 2026. They were about 46.4% of all interbank transfers in April 2026, against 21% in mid-2022. Bulk payments and standing orders are excluded today. The CNB is working to add bulk instant payments in 2026, which is a separate second integration (A3). · Supporting build activity is visible too. The CNB is itself hiring an IT analyst specifically for CERTIS and a payment-systems methodologist, both posted in the last week of August 2026. Komerční banka has already made structured payment-address fields live for SEPA and foreign payments from 20/06/2026 (A5).

signals.bank_theme: Czechia — EET 2.0 nationwide fiscal sales-recording mandate from 01/01/2027
signals.signal: The Czech Chamber of Deputies approved the government's sales-recording bill, known as EET 2.0, in third reading on 15/07/2026. It then went to the Senate. The tax administration published technical documents for developers and suppliers of cash-register systems on 05/06/2026, and launched a dedicated portal. It has a firm published timetable. Technical documentation appeared on 05/06/2026. A developer seminar was held in Prague on 23/06/2026. A test environment opened on 01/07/2026. EET 2.0 functions, including creation of cash-register certificates in the tax mailbox, follow from 01/11/2026. A free state app for small traders follows from 01/12/2026. The scheme records only contact payments at the point of sale (cash, cards and QR), and leaves out bank transfers and invoices. Importantly, the Finance Ministry says in its own words that the law brings in no compulsory receipt printing and does not require the purchase of new cash-register equipment. The state will give the smallest traders a free web application. The ministry expects CZK 14.4bn a year in extra revenue. Vendors are already selling against the deadline anyway. signals.bank_theme: Czechia — DORA and the new Cybersecurity Act create a dual compliance surface, with a hard December 2026 data date
signals.signal: The supervisor (A1): the CNB's 2025 supervision report covers its first year of supervising the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). DORA sets common rules for banks' IT risk management, incident reporting and resilience testing, and has been in force since 17/01/2025. In 2025 the banking sector reported 26 major technology incidents, insurers 2 and other supervised firms 8. None was caused by a cyberattack. Most were technology or process failures at the institutions or at their ICT providers. The CNB piloted a cyber-maturity self-assessment questionnaire of more than 400 questions with 16 firms, and says it will be sent to obliged entities during 2026. Advanced red-team penetration testing, meaning simulated attacks against live systems, began at one significant institution in 2025. The stated goal is to test each significant institution once every three years. Third-party ICT risk, and the contract renegotiations it forced, are named among the biggest challenges for institutions. Separately, the CNB and the national cyber-security authority issued a joint statement on 24/06/2026, dividing supervision between them under the new Czech Cybersecurity Act. They agreed to cooperate as far as joint inspections and shared inspection results. The data date (A3): the DORA register of ICT contracts must be compiled as at 31/12/2026 as its reference date. Each bank submits it to the CNB on the CNB's own earlier cut-off, typically February or March 2027. It is then forwarded to the European supervisory authorities by 31/03/2027.

On the exposure side, every bank must describe each ICT contract supporting a critical function, by legal identifier and by function, together with the subcontractors beneath it. Banks will ask their ATM, terminal and managed-service suppliers for that data in Q4-2026 and Q1-2027. Supplying a clean, pre-formatted pack is a cheap way to protect a renewal. Failing to supply it is a common reason for putting a service back out to tender.

signals.bank_theme: Czechia — euro deferred: no ERM II, no CERTIS ISO 20022 migration, no digital koruna
signals.signal: What moved: a hard new primary date takes Czechia out of the euro pipeline for the rest of the decade. The CNB's own euro-adoption page states this word for word. The next update of the joint Finance Ministry and CNB Assessment is to be submitted to the Czech government by the end of March 2030. That Assessment is the document in which a target date for joining the euro could be set. The last edition, April 2025, advised the government not to set a target date, noting that Czechia met only two of the four required criteria in 2024. Around that, the European Central Bank and Commission Convergence Reports of 24/06/2026 confirm two findings. None of the five reviewed currencies is in the exchange-rate mechanism, and none of the five countries is legally compatible. The next scheduled assessment is in 2028. Czechia passes on price stability and long-term interest rates, but fails on exchange rate and legal convergence. The CERTIS negative was re-tested by a full-text scan of the CNB's official system description on 27/08/2026. It returned zero occurrences of ISO 20022, confirming there is no published migration. The CNB's Czech-language page also still states word for word that its Bank Board has taken no decision on a Czech central bank digital currency. Existing law does not permit issuance at all.

That lifted the segment margin from 16.6% to 18.7% on only 2% organic revenue growth, which is a deliberate shift out of cash-in-transit into ATM outsourcing. Brink's also disclosed, without naming it, a new European bank consortium full ATM outsourcing win going live in H2-2026 (A6). signals.bank_theme: Greece — IRIS instant payments as a mandated card alternative
signals.signal: The cross-border phase of IRIS Payments is now live, and it shows a named competitive gap that the master row did not record. On 30/06/2026 the first phase of the European link-up went live for person-to-person transfers. It covers 57.3 million citizens in five countries. It was delivered by the Greek clearing operator DIAS joining the EuroPA alliance. That alliance links the Greek, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian account-to-account schemes, so users send money by mobile number with no account number. · Reach is expected to grow to more than 176 million citizens in 18 European countries by end-2026. From 2027 the plan is to extend this to payments at online and physical stores. The key detail is that the service is at first available only through Eurobank, Piraeus and Viva.com. Alpha Bank and NBG are the named gap. The other Greek banks are expected to join in the period ahead (A3). · Volume context comes from the clearing operator's own 2025 statistics. Instant payments reached 122.1m transactions, up 72.8%, and 27% of all credit transfers. Person-to-person IRIS reached 111.4m transactions, up 90%, with 4.3m registered users. Professional IRIS rose 197% across 583,445 registered professionals, and commerce IRIS rose 70.8%. · Interbank ATM transactions also rose 27.7% in 2025. That figure covers under five months of the zero-fee withdrawal regime, so 2026 will be the first full year (A1). DIAS is separately working to bring commerce IRIS into physical stores through a per-transaction QR code shown on the terminal (A1). Cardlink and Worldline dominate Greek public-sector card acceptance. So the acquirer, the bank that processes card payments for the shop, decides which terminal is used, not the buyer (A2, A6).
signals.date: 30/06/2026 — IRIS goes live cross-border through the EuroPA alliance with only Eurobank, Piraeus and Viva participating; expansion to 18 countries expected by end-2026; merchant and retail interoperability slated for 2027
signals.implies: There are two clearer angles than before. First, Alpha and NBG are confirmed as not being on the cross-border scheme, while three rivals are. It also means terminal-management changes and merchant onboarding. This is a software and management refresh across an installed base, not a driver of new terminal sales. It also brings rising demand for real-time fraud monitoring on a payment rail that bypasses cards entirely. · Meanwhile interbank ATM use is growing quickly. That points the other way, and supports the case for cash automation and ATM managed services.
signals.likelihood: High for the end-2026 expansion; Medium for the 2027 merchant leg, which is press-only
signals.follow_up: Approach Alpha and NBG now on their cross-border onboarding timelines, while they are the named laggards. signals.bank_theme: Greece — cash access policy: merchant cash-out and the EU legal-tender file
signals.signal: Two policy developments moved this cycle, and they pull Greek cash infrastructure in opposite directions. · First, a written answer was given to a parliamentary question tabled 15/06/2026 about the removal of the only ATM in the village of Delvinaki. In it the Secretary General for the Financial Sector confirmed a change under the revised EU payment-services framework that Greece negotiated. Retail merchants will be able to provide cash withdrawals from their shops on a voluntary basis, even without a prior purchase. This is aimed at areas with limited ATM or branch access, and merchants earn a small commission. Several outlets report a €50 cap per purchase-free withdrawal. The same answer repeats that where branches and ATMs are placed remains a commercial decision of the banks. The MP who raised it argued instead for a legal duty to keep an ATM in specified outlying areas (A1, A5). No Greek bill was tabled as at 31/08/2026 (A5). · Second, and pulling the other way, the European Parliament confirmed by plenary on 08/07/2026 its negotiating mandate on the regulation on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins. Member states would name authorities to oversee cash acceptance and access. They would also file a yearly assessment against common indicators, to be set by an implementing act. The named indicators include density of cash access points relative to population. · Where an assessment is negative, the state must adopt remedies, including geographical access requirements. If it fails to act, the Commission may impose country-specific measures. The Council position also bans refusal of cash except in narrow cases. It requires resilience measures to keep cash payments working during major electronic outages. Whether the density indicator survives into the final text is unverified (A3).

sources.text: Dimokratiki tis Rodou — reporting the Ministry's written answer, 21/08/2026

signals.date: 21/08/2026 — the Ministry's written answer confirming purchase-free merchant cash withdrawals is reported; 08/07/2026 European Parliament plenary confirms the negotiating mandate on the euro legal-tender regulation
signals.implies: There are two opposite futures for Greek cash access, and only one of them is a hardware opportunity. · Purchase-free cash at retail creates a new product surface. That means cash-out-enabled terminals, merchant reconciliation and float management, and small-safe tooling rather than full cash-in-transit. At the same time it caps rural ATM demand, which matters most for the banks with the largest rural fleets. · A surviving cash-access-density obligation would do the reverse. It would force extra machines in thin areas, plus recyclers, which are ATMs that re-use deposited notes, to make marginal sites pay. It would also require monitoring to prove uptime, and offline-capable dispensing under the resilience clause. · Neither is law yet. A density gap analysis can therefore be sold today only as scenario planning, never as compliance.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the Greek debate is live but no bill is tabled; the EU file plausibly reaches political agreement around end-2026 with the density indicator unconfirmed
signals.follow_up: Retrieve the actual written parliamentary answer from the Hellenic Parliament register, to confirm the €50 cap and the exact wording before quoting it. · Obtain the consolidated parliamentary report on the legal-tender file. Confirm whether the density indicator and the Commission backstop survive in the mandate's articles, not only in a pre-vote summary. · Track both branches of the Greek debate, because a rural ATM obligation and a merchant cash-out regime lead to completely different propositions.
signals.product_review_why: Both policy paths change ATM and recycler demand, and merchant cash-out adds a cash-out terminal product surface.

signals.bank_theme: Hungary — Act XVIII rural ATM rollout + MNB validation/uptime mandate
signals.signal: WHAT MOVED: two agents independently read Annex 1 of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.) line by line and produced the same allocation — 80 settlement packages covering 1,039 named settlements, each package assigned to ONE obligated bank: OTP Bank 428 settlements in 33 packages, MBH 195 in 15, K&H 117 in 9, Erste Bank Hungary 104 in 8, Raiffeisen 65 in 5, CIB 52 in 4, UniCredit Hungary 52 in 4, Gránit 13 in 1, MagNet 13 in 1 (A2, A3). Both decrees were re-read from the consolidated texts this cycle and are still in force with no changes. The package-swap deadline of 28/02/2026 has passed, so the bank-by-settlement map is now fixed for 2026. A hand-over of operation cannot be contracted for less than five years — whoever equips a package holds it for years. Every one of the 1,039 machines must be barrier-free under NGM decree 16/2025 §2. Because all enter service after June 2025, none can use the accessibility legacy exemption. MNB Recommendation 6/2025 separately expects each bank to list and publish per-machine accessibility features down to settlement level, including speech support or push-button entry where a PIN is typed on a touchscreen (A3). The fine ladder is HUF 2m–200m at first, then HUF 5m at three months of continued non-compliance, rising step by step to HUF 200m at thirty months. OTP, joined by Erste and Raiffeisen, filed a constitutional complaint on 10/11/2025, and no Constitutional Court decision could be found (A2, A5). NEWLY CLOSED THIS CYCLE: the rollout generates ZERO procurement notices. A full CSV sweep of the Hungarian public-procurement register (EKR) returned no ATM supply procedure of any kind in 2026. This is because the nine obliged institutions are private banks and are not contracting authorities for this spend (A2).
signals.date: 31/12/2026 — statutory phase-2 deadline, ATM cash withdrawal must be available in every settlement above 500 inhabitants · 28/02/2026 swap deadline passed, so the per-bank allocation is now frozen · constitutional complaint of 10/11/2025 still undecided

It also covers vendor-neutral ATM software, so a bank does not lock 400 rural sites to one manufacturer. Physical security for unattended sites and rural service-level field support complete the list. · The five-year minimum on hand-over contracts and the three-yearly re-allocation both argue for a software layer that survives a site changing hands.

signals.follow_up: Go straight to OTP, MBH and K&H procurement on rural low-footfall hardware, monitoring and field service, because they carry 57 of the 80 packages. · Ask MNB or the ERA notification system how many of the 1,039 sites are actually live, and which packages were swapped after 28/02/2026. Track the Constitutional Court docket for any suspension. Do not staff a Hungarian tender watch for this, because it will not appear on EKR or TED.

signals.bank_theme: Hungary — Act XIV of 2026 ATM decommissioning and relocation freeze
signals.signal: Act XIV of 2026 §96(1)-(2) rewrote section 3 of the ATM Act with effect from 14/05/2026. Two agents re-read the consolidated statute word for word this cycle (A3, A5). A credit institution may no longer stop operating any ATM that existed when the Act came into force. The same no-closure rule now covers a branch's cash-payout service. Replacement of the machine is expressly carved out ("ide nem értve az ATM cseréjét"). · A relocation is allowed only in a justified case, and only if an ATM keeps operating in the same settlement or Budapest district. The justified cases listed are moving into a settlement with no ATM at all, evidence from average cash-withdrawal volume data, or the landlord ending the site lease. · Subsection (1b) expects that a like-for-like swap may be impossible at a site. The reason given is "for purely technological or technical reasons — in particular the dimensions of the new ATM and its security requirements". In that case the replacement machine may be installed elsewhere in the same settlement. Breach carries an MNB fine of HUF 2m–200m. A1 records the same amendment from OTP's side, and notes that OTP still cut its Hungarian estate by 58 machines in H1-2026.

sources.text: Act XVIII of 2025, consolidated text in force from 14/05/2026

signals.date: 14/05/2026 — the decommissioning and relocation freeze enters into force, and every Hungarian ATM refresh decision from that date runs through these rules
signals.implies: Hungary has legislated its ATM estate into a guaranteed replacement market. Roughly 5,700 machines nationally can only be swapped, never retired. That total is commonly cited, but the independent validator notes it is not reconciled to any per-bank census in this cycle's evidence. · The statute itself expects the replacement machine may be physically bigger and carry higher security requirements than the one it replaces. That is exactly what happens when an old through-the-wall dispenser is swapped for a deeper deposit or recycling machine, or one with accessibility hardware. A shrinking fleet therefore becomes a multi-year refresh pipeline. · It also adds two attached sales. The first is a chargeable site-survey and fit study for machines that will not fit their old holes. The second is withdrawal-volume telemetry, because a bank now needs volume evidence to justify any move.
signals.likelihood: High — the law is in force and binds every refresh decision already being taken
signals.follow_up: Take the replacement pipeline to each of the nine banks separately from the 1,039 rural sites. Lead with recycler-class upgrades plus a paid site-survey and fit study against subsection (1b). Attach withdrawal-volume telemetry as the evidence a bank needs to justify a relocation. · Obtain Act XIV §96 from the Magyar Közlöny, together with its explanatory memorandum. Ask MNB whether a replacement that fails the (1b) test needs prior notification.
signals.product_review_why: The no-closure rule turns the whole estate into a replacement pipeline with site surveys and withdrawal telemetry attached.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: MBH Bank — 115-location 2026 ATM programme plus a ~500-unit replacement cycle
signals.signal: MBH's own branch-and-ATM locator API was pulled on 27/08/2026 and gives the clearest estate picture yet (A1). It returns 1,285 fixed ATMs across 779 settlements. Only 256 (19.9%) accept cash in, and 1,029 are cash-out only. It also lists 398 fixed branches in 323 settlements, 132 mobile-branch stops and 8 university digital zones. Of 538 branch-type points, 525 still run a staffed cash desk. · The API tags every machine by predecessor brand: 803 are legacy Takarékbank, 383 legacy MKB and 99 legacy Budapest Bank. The same feed shows four different quick-withdrawal preset configurations across one bank. The ATM software and configuration estate is therefore clearly not yet harmonised. · There is also new vendor information on the point A1 had called this market's highest-value unknown. An MBH job advert posted 17/08/2026 for an "Arksys rendszerszervező" confirms the platform. MBH's card and ATM transaction switching runs on Arksys, the Euronet-owned platform, with Oracle FLEXCUBE as the core (A5). MBH is also allocated 195 of the 1,039 mandated settlements. · On leadership, Dr. Ákos Tamás took office on 01/08/2026 as deputy CEO for standard customer service. signals.bank_theme: OTP Bank Hungary and Erste Bank Hungary — cash-in white space against a shrinking OTP estate
signals.signal: OTP's H1-2026 statutory report of 05/08/2026 puts OTP Core Hungary at 299 branches, 1,929 ATMs and 149,868 POS terminals at 30/06/2026. The comparable figures at 31/12/2025 were 301, 1,987 and 150,158. That is a net loss of 58 ATMs, or 2.9%, in six months, and 69 fewer than at 31/03/2026 (A1). · This runs directly against the standstill in force since 14/05/2026. It also runs against OTP's own 2025 annual report. It states, on the MNB decree: "in the case of OTP this means the installation of 195 new or relocated ATMs across Hungary in 2025 and further 233 in 2026". · OTP's own locator API, pulled 27/08/2026, returns 1,844 points across 764 settlements. Only 624 (33.8%) take cash in, and 1,220 are cash-out only. 376 sites are hosted in municipal or other public premises, which is exactly the Act XVIII delivery model. · Erste Bank Hungary's locator returns 505 ATMs across 276 settlements. 268 of them (53.1%) are deposit-capable, leaving 237 cash-out only. That sits on a very thin base of 97 branches in 72 settlements, so the ATM network is effectively the branch estate. · Cross-matching the OTP, MBH and Erste feeds shows their estates together touch 1,217 distinct settlements out of roughly 3,150 in Hungary. Only 195 settlements have all three present. OTP's H1 report never mentions Act XVIII at all.

sources.text: OTP Bank Nyrt. Féléves jelentés 2026, network table p.42

signals.date: 05/08/2026 — OTP half-year report shows 58 Hungarian ATMs removed in H1-2026 while a legal standstill and a 233-machine 2026 obligation both run · 27/08/2026 locator pulls quantify 1,220 OTP and 237 Erste cash-out-only machines
signals.implies: There are two possible readings. Either the mandated rural machines sit outside OTP's reported estate, installed jointly or assigned to another designated provider, or a compliance catch-up is due in H2-2026. Both readings are commercially live: a jointly installed pool is one large supply-and-install job, and a catch-up is the same job with a tight deadline. · Meanwhile roughly 1,450 OTP and Erste machines have no cash-in path at all. That is the single largest recycler retrofit pool in the country. · Rural Hungary is overwhelmingly a one-bank-per-village market, which is why the legislator wrote a cost-sharing decree. The remaining settlements will be served by one shared machine, not four. A shared fleet is normally run by one operator under one contract.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — the obligation is dated and the gap is measurable, but OTP has disclosed no compliance capex programme
signals.follow_up: Ask OTP investor relations directly whether an Act XVIII capex programme exists and is simply not disclosed. Also ask whether the 58 removed machines are permitted relocations or reportable removals. Establish whether Erste Hungary's 505 machines are self-operated or already outsourced. · Subtract the three-bank settlement union from the KSH settlement register to build the definitive list of uncovered settlements. Nobody outside MNB appears to hold that list, and it is the sales target.

signals.bank_theme: K&H Bank — MNB-ordered branch teller capacity, queue analytics and appointment booking
signals.signal: The binding MNB order is unchanged and still running. **Note on provenance, added after this cycle's independent validation: the decision number and the fine do not appear in any of this cycle's findings files. They trace to the previous cycle's disclosure file, [A1 2026-07-30](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-07-30.md), where the decision is recorded as *partially confirmed*.** · On that basis: decision H-KPL-I-4/2025 of 17/12/2025 fined K&H HUF 60,000,000. From 01/03/2026 it re-imposed three duties. K&H must add staffed teller positions in named branches. It must extend online appointment booking for cash transactions to every branch with a teller, including the lunchtime and closing windows. It must also file a monthly waiting-time monitoring report. The March–May 2026 per-branch waiting-time data was filed with the MNB by 15/06/2026 and is still under assessment. · What moved this cycle is the cost picture behind the order. KBC's 2Q2026 disclosures of 06/08/2026 put K&H at 188 branches, down from 189 at 31/03/2026, 191 at 31/12/2025 and 193 a year earlier. That is the fastest-shrinking network in KBC's International Markets business unit, on a flat 1.7m clients, EUR 9bn of loans and EUR 12bn of deposits (A1). · KBC also booked a EUR 42m lifetime modification loss at K&H in the quarter. The reason is that the Hungarian mortgage interest-cap legislation "no longer contained an expiry date" at 30/06/2026. That makes the margin squeeze permanent rather than temporary. It came on top of a EUR 134m windfall and deposit-guarantee tax charge in 1Q26. · K&H is separately allocated 117 of the 1,039 mandated settlements (A3). Its payments arm holds the state student-loan agency's card-acceptance contract, re-tendered on 13/07/2026 with the award still pending (A2). K&H's own ATM count remains unmeasured, because kh.hu was re-tested this cycle and still returns HTTP 403 to automated access.
signals.date: 06/08/2026 — KBC confirms the Hungarian interest cap is now open-ended and books a EUR 42m loss, making K&H cost-out structural · waiting-time evidence filed 15/06/2026 and still under MNB assessment · obligations running since 01/03/2026
signals.implies: A regulator has ordered this bank to add physical cash-handling capacity, and to prove branch queue performance with statistics. At the same time its owner faces open-ended regulated margin pressure, and is cutting branches faster than anywhere else in its group. · Those two forces point at the same purchase. That is teller cash recyclers and branch cash automation, which add capacity without adding staff. It also includes queue management, appointment booking and waiting-time analytics good enough to satisfy a supervisor. K&H has already been fined once for missing these same deadlines, so a third decision is plausible.
signals.likelihood: High — a binding repeat order with obligations live, evidence filed and awaiting assessment
signals.follow_up: Approach K&H branch operations before the MNB rules on the 15/06/2026 submission. Lead with teller recyclers, queue management, appointment booking and statistically sound waiting-time analytics. · Obtain the ATM and deposit-ATM counts directly from the bank or from MNB payment statistics. kh.hu is blocked to automated access, and this is now the second cycle in a row it has failed.
signals.product_review_why: The regulator's order drives teller cash recyclers plus queue management, appointment booking and waiting-time analytics.

signals.bank_theme: Raiffeisen Bank Hungary — twin MNB AML fines mandating automated due diligence and beneficial-owner remediation
signals.signal: The two 2026 MNB anti-money-laundering decisions carried from the master still apply, and their deadlines are still ahead. Decision H-PM-I-B-13/2026 of 04/06/2026 requires internal-audit testing of beneficial-owner identification by 30/09/2026. By 31/10/2026 the bank must deliver the audit reports to the MNB. It must also deliver a register of every client whose ownership and control structure is not yet established to the required standard. · The earlier decision H-PM-I-B-8/2026 of 13/02/2026 had already ordered an IT-supported control environment able to test low-risk classifications. It also ordered a retrospective review of alert pre-screening quality performed by the bank's outsourced provider. No agent refiled the underlying MNB decisions this cycle, so that evidence is carried forward from the master rather than re-verified. · What is new is that the Hungarian board changed. Kamila Makhmudova and Roman Ermantraut were appointed to the Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. board effective 28/07/2026. Sabine Abfalter's mandate ended the same day, and Daniel Rath had resigned effective 31/12/2025. All this was disclosed through a Budapest Stock Exchange filing (A5). · At group level, Michael Höllerer became RBI chief executive on 01/07/2026. Curt Chadha takes over group Retail Banking from 01/09/2026, with an explicit digital-transformation and group-cooperation remit (A5). · On the regime side, the EU anti-money-laundering authority has now missed its own statutory 10/07/2026 delivery date on the customer-due-diligence technical standards. The AML Regulation still applies from 10/07/2027, so banks are scoping remediation against drafts (A3). Raiffeisen also carries 65 of the 1,039 mandated ATM settlements, and was one of the three banks that filed the constitutional complaint.
signals.date: 30/09/2026 — internal-audit testing of beneficial-owner identification due · 31/10/2026 audit reports plus the unresolved-ownership client register due to the MNB · 28/07/2026 Hungarian board changes · 01/09/2026 new RBI group retail head takes office
signals.implies: The regulator has written the compliance shopping list into a binding order. It covers automated customer risk scoring, IT-supported control testing, beneficial-owner screening to a named standard, and due-diligence remediation across a defined client population. Two deadlines are still ahead. · Because the named weakness sits with an outsourced alert pre-screening provider, this is a chance to displace an incumbent as well as to build something new. A new Hungarian board and a new group retail head arriving in the same quarter mean the vendor decisions are being made again now. The EU-level standards being late argues for a configurable rules layer rather than a hard-coded flow.
signals.likelihood: High — a binding order with two deadlines inside the next two months
signals.follow_up: Time the customer-due-diligence and beneficial-owner pitch to the 30/09/2026 and 31/10/2026 dates. Get in front of the new group retail head after 01/09/2026, as well as the local board. · Establish whether the incumbent pre-screening provider is being kept or replaced. Re-verify both MNB decisions from the MNB register next cycle, because this row now rests on carried evidence.
signals.product_review_why: Binding AML orders call for automated risk scoring, beneficial-owner screening and alert pre-screening, a compliance suite sale first.

signals.bank_theme: Hungary — cyber-audit remediation wave after the 30/06/2026 NIS2 deadline
signals.signal: Re-checked this cycle and unchanged. Under Act LXIX of 2024 on Hungary's cybersecurity, entities operating before 01/01/2025 had to contract an auditor by 31/08/2025. They then had to complete their first cybersecurity audit by 30/06/2026. That date has now passed, and the Hungarian supervisor's published regime has moved from build to enforcement. · Continuing duties are registration within 30 days of falling in scope, and classification of electronic information systems by security level. They also include supervisory fees, use of registered auditors, and protective measures matching the assigned security class. · A3 independently re-confirmed that no new 2026 or 2027 deadline appears anywhere on the supervisor's cybersecurity pages as at 27/08/2026. It also confirmed that no enforcement decision or fine has been found since 30/06/2026. The first enforcement action would be the real spend trigger, and it has not happened. The master's audit-round statistics of 10/07/2026 were not re-filed this cycle.
signals.date: 30/06/2026 — first mandatory cybersecurity audit deadline passed, enforcement phase now running · no further statutory deadline published as at 27/08/2026
signals.implies: The Hungarian window has shifted from getting audited to fixing what the audit found. That is where hardware and software spend actually lands: asset inventory, network segmentation, logging and retention, patching and supplier management. All of these reach the ATM, self-service and POS estates. · In practice that means device telemetry and monitoring to produce evidence, and multivendor ATM software to retire unsupported systems flagged by auditors. It also means terminal management for auditable firmware and parameter changes, and managed services with documented patch controls. · It runs alongside the 31/12/2026 rural-ATM obligation on the same nine banks, so one Hungarian sales approach can carry both. Budgets are forming now against no fixed statutory date, which limits urgency.
signals.likelihood: High that remediation spend follows the completed audits, but this is commercial inference — no source states it and no enforcement action has yet been taken
signals.follow_up: Obtain the supervisor's register of in-scope entities, and check which Hungarian banks and which of their ICT suppliers appear. Hunt specifically for the first enforcement decision published after 30/06/2026, because that is the event that turns remediation talk into budget. Cross-link to the EU compliance-wave row, so this spend is not counted twice.
signals.product_review_why: Post-audit remediation lands on resilience tooling, monitored managed services and multivendor ATM software across the device estates.

signals.bank_theme: Magyar Nemzeti Bank — Entrust nShield HSM tender (live)
signals.signal: Status changed: the tender is closed and can no longer be bid. MNB's EU-threshold supply procedure "Hálózati kulcstároló eszközök és gyártói támogatás" (network key-storage devices and manufacturer support) is procedure EKR001466692026 and TED 511411-2026, published 23/07/2026. It took bids until 24/08/2026 10:00. As at 27/08/2026 there was no result notice, corrigendum or cancellation. The winner is therefore unknown, and an award notice is expected September–November 2026 (A2). · The scope is brand-specified down to part numbers. It covers three Entrust nShield Connect 5c Mid eIDAS/CC units (NH2096-M-CC), three years of premium manufacturer support, rail kits, 36 extra soft-client licences and Security World software. The term is 36 months, with no estimated value published. A6 re-read the same notice independently. It confirms the Entrust specification and the HUF 41,000,000 minimum liability-insurance requirement on the winner. · Separately, A2 records a second, distinct MNB procedure, EKR001193282026, with result notice KÉ 14192/2026 published 16/08/2026. It awards operational support for MNB's PKI signing platform, and consultancy for the HSMs behind it, to Noreg Információvédelmi Kft., a Budapest infosec SME. signals.date: 24/08/2026 — bids closed on the MNB nShield procedure, award pending and the tender no longer biddable · 16/08/2026 result notice publishing the Noreg award on the adjacent PKI and HSM support contract, 36 months
signals.implies: The only Hungarian public tender in core scope that could genuinely be bid this cycle has now closed unbid, and its value was never in the three boxes. The lasting finding is the standard that has been set. The Hungarian central bank has written Entrust nShield into its specification down to part number for general-purpose key storage. It has also put a small Hungarian infosec integrator into the seat behind it for three years. · That closes the general-purpose key-storage door at MNB for this cycle. It does not touch the payments-HSM and PCI-PIN layer, which covers PIN translation, card-key management and remote key injection. The specification does not reach that layer, and that is where the Hungarian commercial banks buy. Resolve the Noreg question by pulling KÉ 14192/2026 directly.

signals.bank_theme: Budapest BKK — open-loop cEMV transit programme and the 317-unit ticket-machine refresh
signals.signal: Budapest's transport authority is running the largest Hungarian payments-modernisation programme visible on the procurement register, across at least two live procedures. · One procedure is open and biddable: "Pénzügyi tranzakciók feldolgozása cEMV e-jegyhez", covering acquiring and transaction processing for open-loop contactless-bank-card ticketing. In that model a passenger taps a payment card straight on the validator, with no separate ticket. This is procedure EKR001340842026, first published 16/07/2026. It was re-published as KÉ 14300/2026 / TED 568993-2026 on 17/08/2026, which moved the bid deadline to 08/09/2026 10:00. It is a 48-month utilities contract, deliberately not split into lots, with a HUF 10,000,000 bid bond. Its scope explicitly includes real-time and near-time fraud prevention, master-data management for the validators and ticket-sales points, and full compliance with the Visa and Mastercard transit rulebooks. No estimated value is published. Running alongside it is the separate cEMV e-ticket system build, EKR000407142026, published April–May 2026 (A2). · A second contract is already awarded, and it is the reason the hardware layer is now visible. BKK's "Bankkártyaelfogadás POS terminálok" contract was signed 16/06/2026 at HUF 1,318,733,639 excl. VAT for 36 months (TED 424870-2026). BKK itself planned to swap these for Ingenico Self/7000 and Self/8000 by Q3 2026. There are also 15 POS and 350 mPOS for on-street penalty collection to be commissioned within 30 days, and softPOS on about 350 devices within 60. · There is an important scope limit. The 317 ticket machines are BKK's own property, and they are serviced and terminal-managed by a separate subcontractor. A2 identifies Senso-Media Zrt. as the framework holder for ticket-machine network operation and deep refurbishment. signals.bank_theme: Hungary — state-sector card acceptance consolidating on SimplePay (OTP Mobil)

SimplePay Zrt., part of the OTP Mobil group, won both lots at a combined HUF 13,200,000,000 excl. VAT over 36 months, with the Treasury committing to draw 70% of each lot. Lot 1 requires the supply, installation, operation and maintenance of 180 dual-currency or 360 single-currency physical POS terminals, plus helpdesk, fraud management and training. · Budapest's transport authority then awarded its own card-acceptance contract to SimplePay on 16/06/2026 at HUF 1,318,733,639. The notice records only two bidders: SimplePay and the incumbent OTP Bank Nyrt., which bid again and lost its own flagship transit contract in a head-to-head race (A2, A6). A6 adds that the transit notice names SimplePay and OTP Bank Nyrt. jointly as awardees. signals.bank_theme: Országos Rendőr-főkapitányság — EU Entry/Exit System border kiosk and biometric capture tender
signals.signal: The Hungarian National Police's two-lot EU-threshold supply tender "ABC kapu, kioszk és biometrikus felvételező pont" closed on 28/07/2026 at 12:00. signals.date: 28/07/2026 — bids closed, award or a sixth re-publication expected September–November 2026 · 30/06/2027 latest date for option deliveries
signals.implies: This is a concrete order of 16 to 20 self-service kiosks plus eight automated gates, in a government rather than a banking setting. It uses the same kiosk hardware, outdoor enclosure and field-service capability sold to banks for branch transformation, with a biometric-enrolment layer attached. · Five re-publications indicate a procurement in difficulty over specification or bidder availability. signals.bank_theme: Hungary — competitor and channel map: Mellon arrives, Euronet is already embedded, cash-machine field service is thin
signals.signal: Several separate findings point to the same conclusion. Hungary is no longer an uncontested market, and its service layer is thinner than assumed. · On Mellon: its audited FY2025 group accounts, signed 07/07/2026, disclose group revenue of EUR 258.8m (+17%), EBITDA of EUR 14.1m and 9,606 staff. They record that during 2025 it founded Mellon Hungary LLC in Budapest, wholly owned, with share capital of EUR 10,000, alongside a Slovenian sibling. A verifier re-check of Mellon's own public company list on 31/08/2026 found Hungary and Budapest appear zero times. The entity is therefore a capitalised pre-launch shell rather than a staffed operating unit, which leaves a short window before it hires. Mellon's standard bundle is Hyosung ATMs and recyclers with KAL multivendor ATM software and its own field service (A6). · On Euronet: it is already inside the market twice over. An MBH job advert of 17/08/2026 confirms MBH's card and ATM switching runs on Euronet-owned Arksys (A5). Euronet also markets a "Közösségi ATM" community programme to Hungarian municipalities. Under it the council supplies a free site, and Euronet installs and runs the machine. A6 could find no dated 2026 source for its scale, so that must not be quoted (A6). · On field service: Mile Banktechnika Kft. won the maintenance of Budapest Spas' entire cash-processing estate at HUF 50,000,000 over 24 months, extendable to 48, on one bid, with the contract signed 10/08/2026. The estate covers banknote handlers, banknote recyclers, cash and coin processing units and their software as one connected system. Its own service pages describe its workshop as brand-independent (A2, A6). A single-bid outcome at roughly EUR 127k shows how thin the Hungarian field is. · On cash logistics: the state railway's cash-in-transit award of July 2026 names CRITERION Készpénzlogisztikai Kft. and Prompt Security Zrt. as the only two bidders. Prompt Security alone holds the lot for emptying a fleet of 65 to 110 cash-in deposit machines. That is an installed self-service estate entirely outside the banks (A2, A6). · On closed-loop payments: FestiPay Zrt. holds Budapest Spas' cashless payment system for a third cycle in a row, at HUF 180,000,000 over 24 months. Finally, ASEE/Payten's H1-2026 subsidiary schedule shows no registered entity in Hungary at all (A6).
signals.date: 07/07/2026 — Mellon's audited accounts disclose the newly incorporated Budapest entity · 10/08/2026 Mile Banktechnika signs the Budapest Spas recycler-maintenance contract on a single bid · 17/08/2026 the Arksys role advertisement confirms Euronet inside MBH's switching
signals.implies: Hungary should move from "safe" to "contested" in the account plan. A regional rival with ten times the revenue has set up a capitalised legal entity and has not yet hired, so the head start is short rather than permanent. · Euronet is already in the transaction path at the country's second-largest bank. It is also pitching municipalities the exact answer for the rural sites banks least want to own. · The most important point for margin is the service layer. A brand-independent Hungarian workshop that will maintain banknote recyclers it did not supply removes the service income that makes recycler and teller-recycler deals profitable. That argues for quoting hardware only with a locked multi-year service and telemetry wrap. · On the other hand, the cash-logistics firms are a channel rather than competition, because neither sells machines. The railway's 65 to 110 deposit machines are a hardware refresh nobody is tracking.
signals.likelihood: High that Mellon makes its first Hungarian commercial approaches within 6-12 months and that Mile reappears on Hungarian cash-automation service tenders
signals.follow_up: Secure multi-year managed-service and software renewals with existing Hungarian accounts before Mellon hires local sales staff. Watch the Hungarian company register and Mellon's own recruitment pages for the first Budapest hires. · Establish which recycler brands Mile Banktechnika is certified on, and whether it holds commercial-bank contracts as well as public ones. Approach Criterion and Prompt Security as channel partners. Find who supplied and maintains the railway's 65 to 110 cash-in machines. Find a dated 2026 Hungarian source for Euronet's community-ATM wins before quoting any figure.
signals.product_review_why: The main point is protecting the service and telemetry wrap around recycler deals before rivals and independent workshops take it.

signals.bank_theme: Hungary — 2026-27 payments-infrastructure deadline stack: the VIBER address gap and the instant-euro build
signals.signal: Two dated obligations reach the same nine Hungarian banks within fifteen months, and one of them has a verified gap specific to Hungary. The first is the change to postal address data. The European Payments Council's guidance EPC153-22 v2.1 sets 15/11/2026 as a cut-off date. From then, an unstructured postal address is no longer allowed in the SEPA scheme rulebooks and "will hence lead to rejects". This applies to the inter-bank leg and to corporate file upload. The same weekend carries the SWIFT standards release. Germany's Bundesbank separately confirms the removal of unstructured postal address data from the European RTGS system's messages. Production deployment is on 14/11/2026, and the real hard stop is the end of release testing on 28/10/2026. Against that, A3 downloaded and text-extracted the MNB's currently effective business terms and their annexes. It found no occurrences of "ISO 20022", "strukturált cím" or "hibrid" anywhere in the effective annex set, including annexes updated as recently as 03/08/2026. Hungary's domestic real-time gross settlement system VIBER runs ISO 20022 messages, but it has no structured or hybrid postal-address rule and no date, eleven weeks before the international cutover. The second obligation is the instant-euro calendar for non-euro EU states, re-read from the Regulation itself and corrected this cycle. On 09/01/2027 Hungarian banks must be able to receive instant euro credit transfers. They must also price instant transfers no higher than equivalent non-instant ones, with payee-verification services free of charge. On 09/04/2027 the same receiving duty reaches electronic-money and payment institutions. On 09/07/2027 all non-euro payment service providers must send instant euro and provide Verification of Payee, the payee-name-to-account match. Two reliefs exist. There is a carve-out until 09/06/2028 for national-currency accounts, and a right to ask the MNB for permission to cap sending outside business hours (A3).

sources.text: MNB Üzleti feltételek, 2. melléklet benyújtási rend

signals.date: 15/11/2026 — unstructured postal addresses stop being accepted across the SEPA schemes, with the international testing hard stop on 28/10/2026 and no matching Hungarian domestic rule in force · 09/01/2027 Hungarian banks must receive instant euro transfers and meet charge parity · 09/07/2027 sending plus Verification of Payee
signals.implies: Hungarian banks will run two address regimes at the same time across the same customer base. Structured or hybrid formats apply to SEPA and correspondent traffic from mid-November, while free text is still allowed at home. That dual-regime problem is the commercial opening. It calls for dual-format handling, and for monitoring of rejects and rejection messages at cutover. It also calls for sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening re-tuned to the structured town and country fields. Customer-data cleansing then has to satisfy the international leg without breaking the domestic one. The instant-payments step is a re-scope rather than a new product. Payee verification has to reach the self-service and kiosk channel as well as the core. The January step is close enough that any bank still scoping it is already late. The conclusion is to sell remediation and managed services on the address leg, because the budget-commit window for it has closed. In parallel, scope the July-2027 sending and payee-verification step now.
signals.likelihood: High — both are fixed, directly applicable dates, and the Hungarian domestic gap was verified at annex level rather than inferred
signals.follow_up: Watch the MNB's consultation page for proposed amendments to its business-terms annexes before 15/11/2026. A Hungarian hybrid-address rule would appear there first. Ask each Hungarian bank whether its payee-verification scope covers domestic forint and non-account-number identifiers, since that gap is the follow-on opportunity. Check whether the MNB has published any policy on the outside-business-hours sending permission or the national-currency-account carve-out.
signals.product_review_why: The ISO 20022 address cutover and instant-euro dates drive payment-hub remediation, screening re-tuning and managed support.

signals.bank_theme: Magyar Nemzeti Bank — banknote-processing estate held single-source by Giesecke+Devrient

MNB's closed-loop banknote-processing system is maintained by Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH. The contract was awarded 15/07/2025 and signed 03/09/2025. It was published as result notice KÉ 15068/2025 on 25/09/2025 (TED 626259-2025). The material new detail is the subcontracting disclosure. Giesecke+Devrient declared that 65% of the contract value, EUR 2,160,207 excl. VAT, will be performed by subcontractors doing "service and maintenance tasks". The notice does not name them. The vendor has held MNB banknote-machine work continuously since at least 2019. signals.date: STANDING: 25/09/2025 — result notice published; the contract runs 60 months to roughly September 2030 and is renewed single-source at each cycle, so there is no competitive window
signals.implies: The Hungarian central bank's cash centre is a closed single-vendor estate on the hardware side, and there is no opening there. The actionable item is the disclosure that 65% of the value, EUR 2.16m over five years, is subcontracted field service and maintenance to an unnamed party. That is a live, recurring services subcontract of exactly the kind a regional field-engineering organisation performs. Set a watch for the next voluntary ex-ante transparency notice rather than for a competitive notice, since that is the only advance signal of a renewal.

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — POS whitespace + deposit-ATM upgrade (BPB Printec-incumbent)
signals.signal: The market numbers changed sharply this cycle. The central bank's August-2026 card report, with data to 31/12/2025, shows card-accepting POS terminals reaching about 30,300, up from 20,913 a year earlier. That is a 45% jump of roughly 9,400 terminals deployed in a single twelve-month period, and the largest single movement in Kosovo's payment infrastructure (A1, A4). The ATM picture went the other way. The fleet grew only 8% to 686 machines, of which just 394 can accept a cash deposit and only 57 can start a credit transfer. Because banks added dispensers faster than deposit-capable machines, the deposit-capable share fell from 59.4% to 57.4%. The cash-in gap therefore widened to 292 machines that cannot take a deposit and 629 that cannot make a transfer (A1). The commercial case is now quantified. ATM deposits carry 32.1% of all card-transaction value on those 394 machines, while POS payments carry only 17.8%. The highest-value work in the country is done by the smallest and least-equipped part of the estate. Monthly data to June 2026 show both flows still speeding up. ATM deposit counts are up 14.0% year-on-year and ATM withdrawals up 10.5%, while POS payments are up 47.0% (A4). Terminals offering cash-back at the till rose from 18 to 245 in one year, an early sign of merchant-based cash-out replacing ATMs.

sources.text: CBK — Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë, August 2026 edition

signals.date: 14/08/2026 — the central bank published its August-2026 card-usage report with 2025 device counts; monthly Bulletin No. 298 of 07/08/2026 extends the series to June 2026
signals.implies: There are two separate, independently sized openings. First, a 45% one-year expansion of the acceptance estate creates demand for terminal supply, estate management, encryption-key injection and terminal-management software at real scale, and it is happening now. A fleet installed in one burst starts its refresh clock together. Second, 292 dispenser-only ATMs in a euro-using, cash-heavy economy form a countable and widening upgrade pipeline for cash recyclers. A recycler re-dispenses the notes customers deposited, so cash-in-transit runs and vault cash both fall. Add to that ATM application software to bring transfer and bill-payment functions to the 92% of machines that lack them.
signals.likelihood: High — both series published and still accelerating in H1-2026
signals.follow_up: Ask the central bank's Payment Systems Department (payment.systems@bqk-kos.org) for the per-bank breakdown of the 686 / 394 / 57 split, which the public report withholds. That one table turns a market-level gap into a named target list. Separately, ask each acquirer who supplied the ~9,400 net-new 2025 terminals. Also ask when that fleet's first refresh and terminal-management renewal falls.
signals.product_review_why: A fast-growing terminal fleet needs supply, management and key injection, and 292 dispenser-only ATMs need recyclers.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — KIPS upgrade and instant-payment bank-side integration across all banks
signals.signal: The programme moved from planning into live operation this cycle. Banca d'Italia confirmed that the shared TIPS Clone instant-payment platform officially went live on 20/07/2026. The platform is a standalone copy of the European Central Bank's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement system, built for the Western Balkans. The central banks of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro were the first to join. A second onboarding window is scheduled for November 2026, when the central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected to join (A3, A4). The platform settles in participating countries' own currencies in central bank money, and in euro in commercial bank money. That dual-money model has separate screening and reconciliation consequences. Kosovo's central bank has now bought both pieces it needed. The connectivity layer was awarded to Nexi (see the separate Nexi row). A ten-month advisory contract for design and programme management was awarded to Paylume SRL of Brussels at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026, from exactly one expression of interest (A2). The central bank's Annual Report 2025 names the four overlay schemes being scoped on top of the national system: QR Code, Request to Pay, Proxy ID and Verification of Payee. It records that during 2025 it signed an agreement with the European Payments Council for use of the SCT, SDD and SCT Inst schemes (A4). At sector level, the Banking Association's payments committee chair has stated commercial banks' full commitment to join. The central bank's own invited expert described the work as "elimination of existing technical gaps" (A3, A5). No commercial-bank connection date has been published anywhere.

sources.text: Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone platform for instant payments in the Western Balkans goes live

signals.date: 20/07/2026 — the shared instant-payment platform went live regionally; November 2026 is the scheduled onboarding window for Kosovo's central bank; the Paylume advisory contract awarded 22/07/2026 runs to about May 2027
signals.implies: The central rail is bought and dated, so the remaining money is on the bank side. Every Kosovo commercial bank must connect to the national system, map ISO 20022 payment messages, offer instant payments through mobile and internet banking, and reconcile a rail that never closes. The banks are Raiffeisen, NLB, TEB, ProCredit, BKT, Banka Ekonomike and Banka për Biznes. Round-the-clock irrevocable settlement removes the overnight batch window in which fraud used to be caught. That pulls through real-time transaction monitoring, instant sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening, hardware security modules and 24/7 managed operations. The four named overlays, QR, Request to Pay, Proxy ID and Verification of Payee, are the merchant-acceptance and channel work that follows.
signals.likelihood: High for the platform and the window; Medium for Kosovo specifically, since Banca d'Italia says "expected to join" rather than committed, and Kosovo's Payment Services law is still unpromulgated
signals.follow_up: Get in front of the central bank's Payment Systems Department (director Lumni Rrustolli) and the Banking Association payments committee (chair Akile Cernobregu Hashani) before the November window. Establish which banks are in wave one. Approach Paylume SRL in Brussels directly while the overlay scope is still being written. Ask the central bank and Nexi which local integrators are being subcontracted.
signals.product_review_why: Every bank must connect to the instant rail, which pulls through real-time monitoring and sanctions and AML screening.

signals.bank_theme: Nexi Payments SpA — Kosovo central-bank instant-payment connectivity core
signals.signal: The central bank awarded contract BQK-26-014-211, "TIPS Clone Connectivity Services", to Nexi Payments SpA of Italy. The final price was EUR 685,000, for 120 days of delivery plus five years of maintenance. The work is funded under the World Bank-financed Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project. The award was notified on 03/06/2026 and the notice published on 12/08/2026. Only two bids were received. S.W.I.F.T. SC bid EUR 301,138, which was 56% lower, but it was declared non-responsive because the Section IV bidding forms were not completed, so evaluation was impossible. Nexi therefore won a two-horse race by default at more than twice the rival price (A2, A6). This is not a competitive loss for Printec. The funder restricts the connectivity layer to a network service provider already authorised for TIPS, meaning SWIFT or Nexi or a party they formally authorise. Printec could not have bid for it. The material point is positional. Nexi now holds a five-year contract and a standing relationship at the Kosovo central bank. That gives it a natural path to sell overlay services outward to every commercial bank in the country (A6).

signals.bank_theme: Banka Qendrore e Kosovës (BQK) — cash-centre maintenance cycle
signals.signal: This has moved materially and is now more open than the master row recorded. The open procedure for technical maintenance of the central bank's cash-processing machine, procurement number BQK 26 057 221, was cancelled on 10/08/2026. Exactly one tenderer submitted, and its offer was not assessed as responsive, so the procedure fell under Article 47 of the bank's own procurement rule. The central bank's banknote-processing machine is therefore left with no contracted maintenance provider. A re-tender is the expected next step, into a field that attracted only one bidder last time (A2). Separately, and in the same window, the central bank awarded the supply of consumable material for cash processing, procurement number BQK 26 054 121. It went to "Panamic ICT" LLC of Prishtina at EUR 25,017.50 on 04/08/2026, from two tenderers, on lowest responsive price (A2, A6). Both notices were published as PDFs on the central bank's own website, not on the national e-procurement portal.
signals.date: 10/08/2026 — the cash-processing machine maintenance procedure was cancelled for lack of a responsive bid; the consumables lot was awarded 04/08/2026
signals.implies: There is a live, uncontested cash-automation service opening at a central bank: one bidder, disqualified, and the machine now without maintenance. Printec's banknote-processing service capability is a direct fit, and the competitive field is clearly thin. The consumables award matters as intelligence rather than revenue. Consumables are machine-specific, so whoever supplies them knows which banknote-processing platform the central bank actually runs. That is exactly what Printec needs before bidding the re-tender. Panamic ICT is now the local incumbent to beat.

signals.follow_up: Ask prokurimi@bqk-kos.org for the cancelled tender dossier, the make and model of the installed cash-processing machine, and why the single bid failed responsiveness. Watch bqk-kos.org/shpalljet/tenderet/ for the re-tender. Profile Panamic ICT LLC in the Kosovo Business Registration Agency for ownership, and for which cash-machine brands it represents.
