signals.bank_theme: Banka Qendrore e Kosovës (BQK) — centralised IT access-management project, twice unfilled
signals.signal: The central bank ran an open tender to buy and install a centralised access-management project for its IT systems. In practice this is a privileged access management platform: software that controls and records who can use administrator-level accounts. The procurement number is BQK 26 061 111, and it was cancelled on 24/08/2026. Two bids came in and neither was judged responsive, meaning neither met the tender's requirements. The procedure was therefore closed under Article 47 of the bank's procurement rule. This is the second central-bank tender cancelled for non-responsive bids inside three weeks. The other was the cash-processing maintenance tender on 10/08/2026. A re-tender with a revised specification is the likely next step (A2).
signals.date: 24/08/2026 — procedure cancelled after both bids failed responsiveness; re-tender expected
signals.implies: Two bidders failed to satisfy the central bank on an identity and access-governance project. That is an opening for Printec's security-integration and access-control line: privileged access management, strong authentication and access certification. Note that the scope is internal IT access control, not customer-facing electronic signature. It therefore sits next to, not inside, the digital-identity practice. Two failed rounds mean the buyer will welcome a bidder that reads the specification properly. It also fits naturally with the newly binding cyber-risk regulation.
signals.likelihood: High — a re-tender is expected
signals.follow_up: Ask prokurimi@bqk-kos.org for the technical specification of the cancelled dossier before the re-tender. Ask what made both bids non-responsive. Confirm whether the scope is privileged access management only, or full identity and access management.
signals.product_review_why: Privileged access management is internal IT security tied to cyber-risk rules, closest to the resilience and compliance line.

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — CBK Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (Kosovo's DORA)
signals.signal: Kosovo's version of the EU's digital operational resilience rules is now binding, and the compliance date has already passed. The central bank's board approved the regulation on 29/08/2025, and it came into force on 15/09/2025. Article 67 required financial institutions to comply from 01/06/2026. It is a rulebook of roughly 50 pages. It covers governance, ICT asset and information management, and management of third-party service providers. It also covers budget forecasting, project management and IT acquisition, secure development, testing, patch deployment, access rights and cloud services (A3, A4). It goes further than the EU minimum on incident timing. Article 31(10) requires the central bank to be told no later than four hours after an incident is discovered. An interim report follows within 72 hours, and a final report within 30 days. The reporting template asks for the hardware manufacturer, the software developer, and the make and model of the affected applications and the systems they run on. The template explicitly names ATMs ("bankomatet") alongside SWIFT, RTGS and ACH as critical systems whose compromise must be declared (A4). Commercially, the most important clause is Article 10. Institutions must set aside enough budget for cyber preparedness. Article 10 also states that "the cybersecurity budget should be independent of the FI's overall ICT budget". The stated purpose is "to ensure that business-related systems developments do not compete for resources allocated to protecting ICT systems" (A3).

sources.text: CBK — Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (English, PDF)

signals.date: 01/06/2026 — the compliance obligation took effect for every Kosovo financial institution; supervisory examination, not preparation, is now the live conversation
signals.implies: Every Kosovo bank is non-compliant today if it cannot show an ICT asset register, a third-party provider register, a documented patch process and a four-hour incident pipeline. The reporting template names ATMs as regulated critical infrastructure and asks for make, model and firmware evidence. That turns directly into demand for ATM and device telemetry and monitoring, multi-vendor estate visibility software, and managed field services for documented patching. It also creates demand for auditable encryption key management, remote key injection and real-time transaction monitoring. The ring-fenced cybersecurity budget in Article 10 is the most commercially useful clause in the market. It forces a spending line the board can see, and ordinary business projects are not allowed to draw on it. Kosovo has no firm SEPA date, so this regulation, rather than payments, is the near-term spend trigger.
signals.likelihood: High — binding since 01/06/2026 and supervisory enforcement is the next step
signals.follow_up: Offer every Kosovo bank a gap assessment against this regulation. Build it on device telemetry and an ICT asset register that produces the four-hour incident evidence. Lead the commercial conversation with the Article 10 ring-fenced budget. Ask the central bank's supervision department whether on-site inspections have begun, and how it plans to check ATM-estate compliance.
signals.product_review_why: A binding resilience rulebook with a ring-fenced budget drives demand for compliance tooling, device telemetry and auditable key management.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

cited.label: CBK — Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (English, PDF)

signals.bank_theme: TEB Sh.A. (BNP Paribas / TEB group), Kosovo — recurring cash-handling, digital-onboarding and ATM-services tender cycle
signals.signal: TEB runs a large public tender board with roughly 100 invitation-for-bid notices and downloadable documents. Several fall squarely in Printec's scope. TEB is the only Kosovo commercial bank that publishes its buying at this scale (A1, A2). The documents themselves confirm the following. Tender 259/26 "Supply of Cash Handling Machines", covering counting and sorting for coins and banknotes, was issued 22/05/2026 and closed 02/06/2026. It repeats Tender 292/25 of June 2025, so this is an annual cycle with a predictable next window around May-June 2027. Tender 270/26 "Remote (Digital) Onboarding & Digital Signature Integration" was issued 28/05/2026 and extended twice, to a final close of 29/06/2026. That plainly shows it struggled to attract qualified bidders. Tender 311/26 "E Archive Project" was issued 22/06/2026 and closed 03/07/2026. It is itself a second attempt, after an identical project ran in April 2025. Tender 031/26 covers thermal paper rolls for POS terminals. Tender 636/24 covers physical security, cash-in-transit, ATM replenishment and monitoring-room supervision, which confirms TEB outsources its ATM estate. Ref 375-25 covers ATM kiosk production and servicing. TEB publishes invitations, re-tenders and deadline extensions, but never award notices. No budget figure appears in any notice. All dossiers are released only on request to procurement@teb-kos.com. Nothing has been published since June 2026. Behind this sits a counted estate of 83 to 87 ATMs against 35 branches on the bank's own locator as at 27/08/2026. Cardless QR-code cash withdrawal is newly marketed as "the newest ATM service for our customers". There is no mention of deposit or 24/7 capability anywhere on the estate pages (A1). On the intent side, four roles were advertised at the same time for the Deçan location with a 25/08/2026 deadline, and the bank's Qafa branch in Prishtina is relocating (A5).
signals.date: 25/08/2026 — a four-role staffing cluster for the Deçan location closed and the Qafa Prishtina branch relocation is live; the 2026 cash-handling lot closed 02/06/2026 and the annual cycle reopens around May-June 2027
signals.implies: This is the most concrete, repeatable way into a Kosovo commercial bank. TEB buys banknote and coin counting and sorting machines every year. It buys ATM and POS thermal paper as a recurring consumable, and it tenders ATM kiosk production and servicing. It outsources cash-in-transit together with ATM replenishment and monitoring. It is also actively trying to buy a remote-onboarding and qualified electronic-signature stack, which it has failed twice to land. The cardless QR withdrawal launch means TEB has recently changed its ATM application software, and that is the moment a bank is most open to a wider self-service conversation. At the same time, the complete absence of deposit language across an 85-machine estate makes it a prime candidate for a dispenser-heavy fleet that needs a recycler upgrade. A branch relocation and a four-role staffing cluster both put fit-out budget in play. All of these are Unscoped, because TEB publishes no budgets and no winners.
signals.likelihood: High that the cash-handling and paper-roll cycles recur — each has now run in two consecutive years
signals.follow_up: Email procurement@teb-kos.com to get onto the standing bidder list. Ask who won 259/26, 270/26 and 311/26. Ask whether 270/26 was awarded at all, given the two extensions, and whether it requires a Kosovo-accredited qualified trust service provider. Diarise May 2027 for the next cash-handling lot. Ask how many of the ~85 machines can take deposits, and who supplied the cardless QR application. TEB is a BNP Paribas and Türk Ekonomi Bankası joint venture, so also ask whether ATM decisions are taken in Istanbul rather than Prishtina.
signals.product_review_why: TEB tenders cash-handling machines every year, is trying to buy remote onboarding with e-signature, and outsources its ATM estate.

signals.bank_theme: ProCredit Bank Kosova — 29-site branch-light estate and an open numbered tender programme
signals.signal: ProCredit Kosovo runs a clearly branch-light network. Its own locator, re-counted 27/08/2026, shows 29 physical sites: 15 branches with an ATM on site, 13 stand-alone ATMs and one formal "ATM Zone" at Prishtina Mall. The stand-alone machines are deliberately off-premise, at petrol stations, malls and a military base. That is exactly the kind of estate that needs remote monitoring, cash forecasting and managed first-line service. The bank markets the fleet as round-the-clock and deposit-capable, but does not publish how many machines actually accept deposits. It sells a named service for cash deposits above EUR 10,000 (A1). Alongside this it runs an open, numbered, roughly monthly tender programme routed to a single group procurement mailbox. Reference numbering had reached T-0010 by August 2026. Posted lots include supply of coins and banknote bags (closed 09/06/2026) and supply of UPS units and UPS batteries (offers due 25/08/2026). Further lots cover fuel and charging for the electric vehicle fleet, motorcycles and bancassurance. All notices carry a "Restricted to ProCredit Group" classification, so group-level framework agreements may sit above the Kosovo entity. Financially the unit has headroom: total assets EUR 1,503m and profit after tax EUR 13.1m at 30/06/2026, the group's second-largest single-bank profit. Its capital adequacy ratio is 15.9%. A new EUR 16.0m "other capital instruments" line appeared in the quarter, having been nil the quarter before. Group practice on identity is informative. The banking app is built in-house by the group's own IT subsidiary Quipu, but electronic identity and signature are bought from local qualified providers in each market. That makes the Kosovo identity slot a genuine vendor-selected procurement (A1). ProCredit also sent an acceptance lead to the national Tap-to-Phone merchant roadshow (A4, A5).
signals.date: 25/08/2026 — the UPS and UPS-battery lot closed; the tender reference numbering reached T-0010 in August 2026, showing roughly monthly procurement activity
signals.implies: A 29-site estate is small enough to replace in one or two awards rather than piece by piece. That makes it a realistic single-award target for self-service hardware plus managed services. What the bank actually buys is informative: uninterruptible power supplies and batteries for a machine estate, plus coin and banknote bags. These are precisely the extras a managed-services provider folds into a single availability contract covering power, consumables and first-line maintenance. The "ATM Zone" exists as a distinct category in the bank's own taxonomy, with only one site built. The round-the-clock zone format is therefore already decided strategy, and the pipeline is zone number two onward. The EUR 16m of fresh capital instruments is the budget question worth asking.
signals.likelihood: Medium — no refresh announced, but the tender cadence is monthly and the estate is a natural candidate
signals.follow_up: Register with kos.Procurement@procredit-group.com now. Given the tender rhythm, it costs almost nothing and could return a lot. Ask to be invited to the next cash-handling and self-service lots, and whether the UPS lot was awarded or will re-run. Ask how many of the 29 points can take deposits or recycle, who the incumbent manufacturer is, and whether more ATM Zones are planned. Find out what the EUR 16m capital instrument is, and whether any of it is earmarked for technology.
signals.product_review_why: A small off-premise ATM estate suits a single hardware-plus-managed-services award, with a separate open slot for local e-identity.

signals.bank_theme: Banka Ekonomike — İşbank Kosova absorption plus an open cash-equipment tender board
signals.signal: The open question in the master row is now settled, and the answer changes the recommendation. The bank's news archive carries the same customer notice twice with different dates: an original of 28/08/2025 and an identical re-publication of 23/04/2026. This fixes the Türkiye İş Bankası Kosovo branch cutover at 01 September 2025, three days after the original notice. The April-2026 item is a re-post, not a fresh announcement. The transfer rested on central-bank approval reference 2025/312 of 29/07/2025 (A1). The integration is therefore roughly a year old, not imminent. The fleet-standardisation and channel-harmonisation decisions have most likely already been taken, and the Prishtina and Prizren branches are already running on Banka Ekonomike systems. Do not brief this as a live integration opportunity. What remains is the tender board, re-pulled 27/08/2026. It shows a clear annual rhythm and no new equipment notice in five weeks. The complete July-2026 run is as follows. On 02/07/2026 the bank posted its annual requirements for supply and servicing of banking equipment, in three lots. The lots are banknote counting, verification and identification equipment; counting, verification, identification and processing equipment; and ultraviolet banknote detection machines. It required serial-number and denomination reading software and a minimum three-year consumables warranty, and it invited leasing terms. On 22/07/2026 it posted supply of paper rolls for POS and ATM terminals, with bids due 30/07/2026. The 41st annual general meeting of 30/04/2026 had a Strategic Plan 2026-2028 on its agenda, though adoption is not published (A1).
signals.date: 22/07/2026 — the POS and ATM paper-roll lot was published (closed 30/07/2026); the annual banking-equipment lot ran 02-09/07/2026, so the next window is about the first week of July 2027; the İşbank cutover is now fixed at 01/09/2025
signals.implies: This is calendar intelligence rather than live demand. It is valuable precisely because nothing else in Kosovo is visible from outside. Banka Ekonomike's cash-handling and consumables buying clusters in early July every year. The equipment specification covers counting, verification, processing and ultraviolet detection, with serial-number reading required and leasing invited. That is a direct read on what a Kosovo mid-tier bank buys for back-office cash, and it maps straight onto the fitness-checking duties in the cash-operations regulation. The value here is the supplier relationship and visibility, not the ticket size, because no lot values are published. Opportunity size is revised down from the master row's M to S on this cycle's evidence, which shows consumables and back-office counting equipment rather than a fleet programme.
signals.likelihood: High that the July cluster recurs — the banking-equipment notice is explicitly for the bank's annual requirements
signals.follow_up: Register as a supplier before June 2027 and diarise the first week of July 2027. Ask whether the annual banking-equipment framework was awarded and to whom, and whether the leasing option the notice invites was taken up. Move the conversation away from the İşbank cutover and onto the Strategic Plan 2026-2028. First establish whether it was in fact adopted at the 30/04/2026 meeting, which is not published.
signals.product_review_why: The bank's annual July lot is back-office banknote counting, sorting and verification equipment, not a fleet programme.

signals.bank_theme: NLB Banka Kosovo — group-mandated ATM and cash-deposit-system upgrade
signals.signal: Re-verified. The evidence gap is now narrower, but the Kosovo leg still shows no visible movement. The Kosovo bank's own page, re-pulled 27/08/2026, still carries exactly the same figures from its Annual Report 2025. These are 35 branches, "over 100 ATMs", total assets EUR 1,634m, 17.1% market share as the third-largest bank in Kosovo, 252,713 active customers and net profit EUR 40.3m. NLB Group's 1H-2026 results presentation of 06/08/2026 confirms 35 Kosovo branches within a group total of 371. It also gives a Kosovo cost-to-income ratio of 31.0%, the second best in the group. The group's H1-2026 interim report was obtained and read this cycle. It contains no Kosovo ATM or cash-deposit-system count, because every such reference in it belongs to the Slovenian bank. That avenue is now closed, and the Kosovo fleet number remains un-cross-checked. The group-level commitment stands. The Investor Day of 07/05/2026 in Sarajevo names "ATM & CDS network upgrade at Group level driving cash out of branches" and a "Cash-at-POS rollout" as delivered or in progress. Branch cash transactions fell from 32% in 2023 to 13.5-15.1% in 2026, against a target below 10%. New this cycle, the group also put numbers on merchant acquiring. It has about 20,000 acquiring merchants today, and acquiring partnerships are up from 5 to 11 against a 2030 target above 20. The addressable regional transaction pool is above EUR 120bn, with 64-80% still paid in cash at the till. Payments revenue was EUR 236.5m in FY2025, targeted above EUR 320m by 2030. Digital merchant onboarding is live in Slovenia and Serbia, and is to be extended to the remaining markets, including Prishtina, by 2030. End-to-end terminal-to-cash-register integration, softPOS and digital tips are named as the next build (A1). NLB sent its Head of Cards and E-Banking to the national Tap-to-Phone merchant roadshow (A4, A5).

sources.text: NLB Group Investor Day 2026 — NLB Group Payments deck

signals.date: 06/08/2026 — NLB Group 1H-2026 results confirm the Kosovo network and cost/income; the group ATM and cash-deposit-system upgrade commitment dates from Investor Day, 07/05/2026
signals.implies: A named fleet of over 100 machines, in a euroised and cash-heavy market, sits under a publicly committed group mandate. The mandate has a numbered branch-cash target, which gives a recycler business case something to anchor on. Because the commitment is at group level, a single frame agreement would span Slovenia, Serbia, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia and Montenegro. The approach should therefore go to group procurement in Ljubljana as well as to Prishtina. The newly quantified acquiring plan adds a second and larger front. A funded merchant-acquiring expansion, with digital onboarding, terminal-to-cash-register integration and softPOS explicitly on the roadmap, is core acceptance and onboarding territory.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the group programme is committed and dated, but no Kosovo timing, budget or tender has been disclosed and the H1-2026 narrative shows the work landing in Slovenia
signals.follow_up: Stop looking in the group interim report, which has been read and holds no Kosovo figure. Ask NLB Group investor relations, or the Kosovo bank directly, for the Kosovo ATM and cash-deposit-system split and the incumbent manufacturer. Open in Ljubljana using the Investor Day language word for word. Separately, confirm the per-market timetable for digital merchant onboarding in the five markets not yet live, Prishtina among them.
signals.product_review_why: A group mandate to upgrade ATMs and cash-deposit systems sits beside a funded acquiring expansion with merchant onboarding and softPOS.

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — softPOS / Tap-to-Phone shift in merchant acceptance
signals.signal: A national Tap-to-Phone programme, "Paguaj me një TAP", is moving Kosovo merchant acceptance onto ordinary Android phones instead of dedicated card terminals. It is run by the Kosovo Banking Association with Visa, Helvetas, Sweden/Sverige and the IMAA. The association's chief executive opened it, and the central bank's Payments Department director presented the regulator's next steps. Two merchant events are firmly evidenced: Prishtina on 16/04/2026 and Prizren on 25/05/2026. Three banks showed live products: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, NLB Banka and ProCredit Bank Kosovo (A4, A5). The underlying acceptance demand is real and measured. There were about 9,400 net-new POS terminals in 2025, and POS payment counts were up 47% year-on-year in June 2026 (A1, A4). At group level, NLB names softPOS, end-to-end terminal-to-cash-register integration and digital tips as its next acceptance build across the region (A1). One caveat applies. The two agents disagree on whether the roadshow continued past May. A4 records "Paguaj me një TAP" entries for Gjakovë dated June 2026 on the association's events calendar, while also stating that two other claimed dates do not exist. A5 records that the association has published nothing since 25/05/2026. The programme's current status is therefore unresolved.

sources.text: Kosovo Banking Association — Pay with One TAP, Businesses in Focus

signals.date: 07/08/2026 — the central bank's June-2026 bulletin shows POS payment counts up 47% year-on-year, the demand behind the shift; the association's merchant roadshow ran April to June 2026 with three banks live
signals.implies: This works both ways and should be briefed honestly. Phone-based acceptance shrinks demand for classic POS hardware in the micro-merchant segment, where most of Kosovo's growth is happening. That is a genuine threat to a terminal-led position. It does not remove the back end. softPOS still needs merchant onboarding and electronic identity checks, device and terminal management, and encryption key injection. It also needs hardware-security-module-backed protection behind a phone-based PIN, and certified attestation for the acquirer. The conclusion is to sell the platform rather than the box. The four banks without a live Tap-to-Phone product, namely TEB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike and Banka për Biznes, are the addressable white space. The three that are live are warm entry points on the back end.
signals.likelihood: Medium — three banks live and a multi-city roadshow ran in the first half of 2026, but nothing has been published since June 2026
signals.follow_up: Ask the Banking Association's payments committee directly whether the programme is still running after a publication gap of roughly three months. Ask which banks acquire for the scheme, whose softPOS platform sits behind it, and what the merchant enrolment numbers are, since none are published. Then approach the four banks without a live product with a bundle of white-label softPOS, terminal management and merchant onboarding.
signals.product_review_why: Tap-to-phone shrinks terminal hardware demand but still needs a softPOS platform, terminal management, key injection and merchant onboarding.

cited.label: Kosovo Banking Association — Pay with One TAP, Businesses in Focus

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — remote onboarding and electronic identity: national eID, the ARC remote data-update regulation, and unmet bank demand
signals.signal: Three strands came together this cycle. The first is the state layer. The European Commission's Kosovo Report 2025 confirms that Kosovo adopted a Law on electronic identification and trust services, and that a national electronic identity system became operational in 2024. It also confirms that the national eID and eWallet are in a launched piloting phase, and that 230 online services now run on the e-Kosova portal. However, the law follows the first-generation EU eIDAS framework, not the new Digital Identity Framework. A further alignment amendment is therefore expected, and no production date for the eWallet is published (A3). The second strand is a concrete legal unlock. The Civil Registration Agency, supported by the Banking Association, finalised a draft Ministry of Internal Affairs regulation. It lets bank customers' personal data be updated remotely, without a visit to a branch, for customers assessed as low risk. All relevant parties agreed the draft on 12/05/2026, but its adoption and publication remain unconfirmed three months later (A5). The third strand is proven unmet demand. TEB tendered "Remote (Digital) Onboarding & Digital Signature Integration" (270/26) and had to extend the deadline twice, to 29/06/2026. That shows the requirement is funded and still unmet (A2). Group practice elsewhere confirms the shape of the buy. ProCredit builds its banking app in-house through Quipu, but buys electronic identity and signature from local qualified providers market by market. The Kosovo slot is therefore a genuine vendor selection (A1).
signals.date: 29/06/2026 — TEB's remote-onboarding and digital-signature tender closed after two extensions, with no award published; the Civil Registration Agency remote data-update regulation was agreed 12/05/2026 and awaits adoption
signals.implies: Kosovo is the most advanced non-EU market in the footprint on state electronic identity, after Ukraine. It has a law in force, a national eID operational and an eWallet in pilot. That makes it the best non-EU candidate for a remote-onboarding play tied to the national eID. The Civil Registration Agency regulation is narrower than full remote onboarding. It covers periodic know-your-customer refresh, meaning the re-checking of existing customers' details, for low-risk customers. That still needs an integration to the state civil register, plus risk-tiering and screening behind it. Size it as a data-refresh integration rather than a brand-new onboarding platform. TEB's twice-extended tender is the proof that at least one bank is trying to buy this now and cannot find a qualified bidder.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the pilot is running and the draft regulation is agreed, but neither has a published production or compliance date; the near-term pull is bank demand rather than a deadline
signals.follow_up: Confirm whether the Civil Registration Agency regulation has been adopted and published in the Official Gazette since May 2026, and get its compliance date. That date is the sales trigger. Check the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Gazette directly, rather than waiting on the association. Ask the central bank whether the national eID is accepted on its own as a customer-due-diligence identification method for remote account opening. Approach TEB about 270/26, and the other six banks with the same offer.
signals.product_review_why: National eID plus a remote data-update regulation and a twice-extended bank tender point to remote onboarding with KYC refresh behind it.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — Law 08/L-304 on Banks compliance deadline, with the Payment Services law still blocking SEPA
signals.signal: Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks, adopted 05/12/2024, was promulgated by presidential decree of 20/01/2026. It was published in Official Gazette No. 2 of 27/01/2026 and entered into force about 11/02/2026. Article 147(1) gives banks and branches of foreign banks that held a licence at entry into force twelve months to comply. That is a statutory date of about 11/02/2027, with three years for foreign bank branches on certain provisions. Article 1(2) states the law is harmonised with the EU capital requirements regulation and directive, and with the bank recovery and resolution directive. That leaves only the Payment Services law 08/L-328 and the AML/CFT law 08/L-333 stuck in constitutional review. The central bank spells out the consequence in its own annual report, word for word. The restrictions from non-promulgation "prevented the final application to SEPA and, consequently, resulted in the loss of the opportunity to keep pace with neighbouring countries". A replacement route is already moving. The Government approved a new Draft Law on Payment Services at its 8th meeting, by Decision No. 08/08 of 03/04/2026, and it is heading to the Assembly. The same blockage holds back a second opportunity. The central bank's Regulation on access of non-bank payment service providers to payment systems, adopted 25/11/2025, lets non-bank providers open settlement accounts directly in the national system. Its Article 18 states that it enters into force ten days after Law 08/L-328 does (A4).

sources.text: Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo No. 2 / 27 January 2026, Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks

signals.date: 11/02/2027 — the statutory deadline for every licensed Kosovo bank to be in compliance with Law 08/L-304 on Banks; the Payment Services law 08/L-328 remains unpromulgated and a replacement draft was approved by Government on 03/04/2026
signals.implies: A statutory compliance date roughly five months away, on an EU-aligned prudential and resolution law, puts every Kosovo bank on a fixed timetable. Each bank has to fix regulatory reporting, data quality and risk systems. That means core and channel integration, regulatory reporting and data quality work, anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer screening, and managed services. It also removes one of the three blockers to Kosovo's SEPA application, which shortens the runway once the remaining two clear. Kosovo is the one Western Balkan market where the SEPA compliance wave is held back rather than already spent. Two independent release valves now exist: a court ruling, or Assembly passage of the replacement draft. Either would trigger a compressed multi-bank remediation programme. Behind that sits a new buyer class of e-money institutions, payment institutions and fintechs. They will join the national system directly and own none of the required infrastructure.
signals.likelihood: High for the 11/02/2027 bank-law deadline, which is statutory and already running; Low for the payment-services unlock within 6-12 months, since commencement depends on a law in constitutional limbo
signals.follow_up: Time bank outreach against the roughly 11/02/2027 adaptation deadline. Track the Assembly agenda for the 03/04/2026 Draft Law on Payment Services, the faster of the two paths. Also track the Constitutional Court docket for a judgment on 08/L-328 and 08/L-333. Check whether the replacement draft renumbers the legal basis that the non-bank access regulation relies on, which would force it to be re-issued.
signals.product_review_why: A fixed compliance date on a prudential law drives reporting and AML work, and clears one blocker on the SEPA and instant-payments path.

cited.label: Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo No. 2 / 27 January 2026, Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks

signals.bank_theme: Kosovo — cash-operations compliance spine: the ECB tested-machine gate and the new Counterfeit Monitoring System
signals.signal: Kosovo's Regulation on Cash Operations was board-approved 27/12/2023 and has been in force since 01/02/2024. It was obtained and read in full this cycle, and it is stronger than previously understood. Article 5(4) covers the processing machines that financial institutions use to check the authenticity and fitness of euro banknotes and coins. Such a machine may only be put into use if the Eurosystem has successfully tested it. Article 5(5) requires banknote machines in use or planned to appear on the European Central Bank's published list of tested machines. Coin machines must appear on the European Commission's equivalent list. Articles 17(3) and 18(3) explicitly extend the same requirement to machines operated by the customer. Article 22 copies the ECB machine taxonomy in full, covering cash-in, cash-recycling and combined cash-in and cash-out machines, with recyclers required to check both authenticity and fitness. The regulation also bars anyone from providing cash deposit or withdrawal services through customer-operated machines without a central-bank licence, or from importing or holding such machines. A linked implementation plan of 12/02/2024 commits the central bank to "the deployment of several ATMs and other devices enabling the electronic payments (POS), or financial self-services". This applies in Serb-majority municipalities, including the four northern ones (A1). New this cycle, on 15/07/2026 the central bank announced it had begun EU-supported work to set up a Kosovo Counterfeit Monitoring System. Only the headline and date are verified, because the site sits behind a Cloudflare gate and no archive copy exists (A1). The volume behind all this is large. About 20.65 million euro banknotes, 33.23% of everything banks deposited in 2025, were classified unfit and withdrawn. Total banknote operations were EUR 6.73bn and 132.5 million pieces (A4).

sources.text: CBK — Rregullore për operacionet me para të gatshme (full 39-page regulation, PDF)

signals.date: 15/07/2026 — the central bank began EU-supported work to establish a national Counterfeit Monitoring System, layered on a machine-testing regime binding since 01/02/2024
signals.implies: This regulation is the compliance base under every recycler and cash-in machine sold into Kosovo. It is a qualification gate rather than a sales opportunity in itself. Any machine proposed must already be on the ECB tested-machine list. Printec's manufacturer partners either pass that test or do not, and failing it disqualifies them. Check this before any Kosovo proposal. Because the machine taxonomy is written into Kosovo law, proposals can be scoped in the regulator's own words. Two commercial consequences follow. A third of all notes banks hand in are unfit, so fitness sorting is needed at the deposit point rather than at the central bank. The licensing clause also makes non-bank ATM deployers a legitimate but licensed, and therefore addressable, operator segment. The central bank's published commitment to see ATMs and self-service deployed in the four northern municipalities is a concrete door-opener. It pairs directly with BPB cutting counter hours in North Mitrovica.
signals.likelihood: In force and current since 01/02/2024; the Counterfeit Monitoring System has no published timetable or funding instrument
signals.follow_up: Check every machine model Printec would propose against the current ECB tested-banknote-machine list and the European Commission tested-coin-machine list before any Kosovo proposal. Article 5(5) makes listing a precondition, not a preference. Get the 15/07/2026 press release directly from the central bank rather than by scraping. Identify the EU instrument funding the Counterfeit Monitoring System and its timetable. Ask whether it adds testing or certification duties beyond Article 5. Use the northern-municipalities deployment commitment as the door-opener there.
signals.product_review_why: The rule makes ECB-tested recyclers and cash-in machines a legal precondition and licenses customer-operated self-service deployment.

signals.bank_theme: Banka për Biznes (BPB) — North Mitrovica counter-hour cut and an outsourced ATM-management bundle
signals.signal: Two findings together change how Printec should approach this bank. The first is a dated trigger. BPB published a customer notice on 26/08/2026 stating that from 14 September 2026 its North Mitrovica branch moves to shortened opening hours of 09:00 to 14:00. The notice explicitly directs customers with banking needs outside those hours to the bank's digital services, and it is published in both Albanian and Serbian. It does not say what the previous hours were, so the size of the cut is not established. The second finding is a structural disclosure. BPB's public invitations-to-tender board carries exactly two lots. One of them combines security services, meaning cash-in-transit, physical guarding and a monitoring centre, with ATM management, tendered as a single bundled lot. Both entries were published 09/07/2025, and both download links point to a one-page placeholder file rather than a real tender document. This is therefore a standing statement of how BPB buys, not a live open tender. The board itself notes that these invitations are also published in the daily newspapers, so a live notice may never appear on the website at all (A1).

sources.text: BPB — Njoftim nga Banka e Vendit (bank's own customer notice)

signals.date: 14/09/2026 — the North Mitrovica branch moves to shortened 09:00-14:00 counter hours (notice published 26/08/2026); the security-plus-ATM-management sourcing bundle has stood since 09/07/2025
signals.implies: Cutting staffed teller hours, in a market where cash use is high and digital substitution is weakest, leaves a cash-in gap at that site. That is the standard trigger for a cash recycler or cash-in ATM, plus a round-the-clock self-service lobby. It also supports managed services to run a location the bank may not want to staff. It pairs directly with the central bank's own published commitment to see ATMs and self-service deployed in the four northern municipalities. The tender board finding is the more important of the two. BPB does not run its ATM estate in-house. It buys cash-in-transit, guarding, a monitoring centre and ATM management as one outsourced bundle, which is close to a word-for-word scope statement for managed services. That changes the view of the assumed BPB incumbency, because whatever it is, it sits in a re-tenderable services contract rather than a hardware sale. The renewal, not a box refresh, is therefore the entry point.
signals.likelihood: Certain that the hours change happens, since it is dated and published by the bank; Medium that it converts into a self-service capital decision within 6-12 months
signals.follow_up: As a priority, ask BPB procurement (informata@bpbbank.com) who currently holds the security-plus-ATM-management bundle and when it expires, and ask to be added to the invitation list. signals.bank_theme: Montenegro — fastest-growing SEE ATM fleet
signals.signal: The national fleet has now been confirmed from the bottom up for the first time. The central bank's Q1-2026 device census counts 664 cash machines, of which only 126 can accept a cash deposit. That leaves 538 machines that can only dispense cash. Deposit-capable machines have risen in every quarter since end-2024 (86 → 106 → 111 → 117 → 125 → 126). Unlike the total fleet, they do not fall back in winter, so deposit capability is a permanent part of the estate (A4). · Agent 1 rebuilt the same fleet independently from nine banks' own published branch-and-ATM locators. The counts were NLB 153, CKB ~117, Prva banka 109, Lovćen 101, Erste 81 and Hipotekarna 49. They also include Addiko ~18 ATM-bearing sites, Universal Capital 7 and Adriatic 6. That gives about 641 published locations, which is within 3.5% of the regulator's 664. · The same work showed where the gap sits: NLB 124 withdrawal-only, Prva 92, CKB 87, Erste 69 and Hipotekarna 49. Roughly four-fifths of the national gap is therefore at five named banks (A1). · Deposit demand is growing about nine times faster than withdrawal demand. ATM cash-in transactions were 127,719, worth EUR 42.7m, in Q1-2026. A year earlier they were 86,798, worth EUR 28.9m, so the count rose 47%. Withdrawals grew 5% over the same period. All of this deposit traffic runs on those 126 machines (A1). · The fleet is also strongly seasonal. It swings by roughly 90-110 machines between the Q1 low point and the summer peak, from 751 at end-2025 to 664 at 31/03/2026. That pattern suits a recurring deploy, service and remove contract rather than a one-off sale (A1, A4).

signals.bank_theme: Montenegro — instant payments live at all 11 banks: Verification of Payee mandate, irrevocable rail, 5-cent fee cap
signals.signal: On 20/07/2026 the Central Bank of Montenegro put the TIPS Clone instant-payment platform into production. It is a national settlement system cloned from the European Central Bank's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service. It was built with Banca d'Italia and financed by an EUR 8m World Bank credit. Banca d'Italia confirms that Montenegro and Bosnia were the first two central banks to join. Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected in a second window in November 2026 (A3). · Uniquely in the region, the whole sector went live at once. The regulator publishes customer video guides from all eleven banks: Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, NLB, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad banka and Ziraat. It states plainly that all 11 banks are IPS participants (A1, A4). · Three things follow for the banks. First, the enabling amendments to the Law on Payment Transactions make Verification of Payee compulsory, in line with EU Regulation 2024/886. Before confirming an order, the bank must check that the payee name matches the IBAN, warn the customer on a mismatch, and do this free of charge. Fines for non-compliance are EUR 10,000-40,000. Funds must reach the payee within ten seconds or be returned without delay (A6). · Second, the rail is irrevocable. The regulator's own FAQ says instant payments as a rule cannot be recalled. Two days after go-live, the central bank had to warn the public about a phishing wave impersonating itself and Western Union with a fake EUR 50 giveaway link. This is the typical pattern for authorised-push-payment fraud, where the victim is tricked into sending the money themselves (A4). · Third, a Council Decision of 17/07/2026 caps the fee on a domestic instant transfer of up to EUR 200 made by mobile or internet banking. The cap is five euro-cents on both the sending and the receiving side, against a previous average of 32 cents. The regulator estimates EUR 1m of annual savings, rising to EUR 2.8m (A1, A4). · First official volumes were 56,678 instant transfers worth EUR 21.53m in the 12 days of July, at an average ticket of EUR 380 and full availability. The regulator's directorate head reports that volume rose five-fold from launch day to end-July. He also reports that only "a little over 60%" of credit transfers are currently initiated electronically (A4, A5).
signals.date: 20/07/2026 — TIPS Clone go-live across all 11 banks · 17/07/2026 Council Decision capping the fee at 5 cents · 22/07/2026 central-bank phishing warning · 13/08/2026 first official IPS volumes published · monthly statistics continue, August figures due mid-September 2026
signals.implies: Every Montenegrin bank now carries the same three obligations at the same moment. It must run real-time payee-name matching. It must screen for fraud and sanctions inline, because a ten-second irrevocable payment makes after-the-fact review useless. It must also keep a 24/7/365 rail available with no overnight maintenance window. · In a market this small, that is one packaged offer sold eleven times. It covers real-time transaction monitoring, fraud scoring, a Verification-of-Payee matching engine, and 24/7 managed operations for the banks with thin in-house teams (Adriatic, Zapad, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Lovćen). · The 5-cent price ceiling is the most important commercial factor. It removes fee income on small payments, so a bank can only protect its margin by cutting its cost to serve. That is exactly the argument for self-service and automation.
signals.likelihood: High — the rail is live, the legal obligations are in force and the bank-side build has to happen over the next 6-12 months
signals.follow_up: Ask each of the 11 banks which engine screens IPS traffic in real time, and who supplied their Verification-of-Payee name matching. The first vendor in becomes the regional incumbent for Albania and Kosovo in November. Offer an authorised-push-payment fraud assessment based on the central bank's own warning of 22/07/2026. Get the text of the payments-law amendments to confirm the Verification of Payee wording, which currently rests on press reporting.
signals.product_review_why: Instant payments at all eleven banks require payee verification, inline fraud screening and 24/7 operations, sold as one package.

signals.bank_theme: Montenegro — instant-payments phase 2 (QR acceptance, phone-number alias, Request-to-Pay) and the digital-channel gap
signals.signal: The regulator has put a date on the next wave of instant-payment services. Its own Terms of Reference for the TIPS Clone programme commit to Phase III adoption over Q4-2026 to Q1-2027. Phase IV overlay services are set for March 2027 to March 2028. The Terms of Reference explicitly name QR-code payments for merchant acceptance and Request-to-Pay. · The regulator's public roadmap adds payment by mobile phone number, through an alias directory. Customers would pay a phone number instead of an IBAN. The roadmap also covers preparation for cross-border SEPA Instant (A2, A4). · Two facts make this urgent rather than theoretical. A licensed non-bank is already shipping the whole phase-2 experience. PrestoPay DOO Podgorica, register number 07 in the central bank's Register of Payment Institutions, has been authorised since 14/10/2024 for payment initiation and account information services. That is a PSD2-style third party that can start payments from, and read balances on, other banks' accounts. It markets alias-based person-to-person payments, split-the-bill requests and camera-and-QR bill scanning. On 31/08/2026 its app sat at number 45 in Montenegro's overall free-app chart, ahead of every bank app in the country (A4). · Meanwhile the banks' own channels are weak. App-store metadata pulled on 31/08/2026 shows that almost the entire sector shipped releases in the six weeks around go-live. But four domestic incumbents rate below 2.5 out of 5: Hipotekarna 2.33, Prva banka 2.26, Lovćen 2.26, Erste Montenegro 2.37, NLB 2.77. The only strong local performer is Addiko at 4.69 on 514 ratings, roughly ten times any other bank's review base (A4). · Underlying demand exists. There were 304,691 mobile-payment users at Q1-2026, about 48% of the population, growing every quarter with no seasonal dip, against 498,969 card users. Internet-payment users number 321,203, though the legal-entity part is falling (70,313 → 57,471) as businesses consolidate onto mobile and office banking (A4).

signals.date: 03/2027 to 03/2028 — regulator-committed overlay-services window for QR merchant acceptance and Request-to-Pay, with Phase III adoption Q4-2026 to Q1-2027 · 31/08/2026 PrestoPay charting ahead of every bank app

Terminals offering cash-back at the till fell from 206 at Q1-2025 to 85 at Q1-2026, a drop of 59%. signals.bank_theme: Montenegro — branch and counter cash automation (teller recyclers, business cash deposit)
signals.signal: Counter cash volumes are falling steadily but remain very large, and the flow is mostly business cash. Over-the-counter cash orders fell from 6.81m in 2022 to 5.48m in 2025, a drop of 19.5%. In Q1-2026 they were 1,197,753, down 6.0% year on year. The value is still EUR 5.77bn a year. · Within 2025, cash deposits by companies and entrepreneurs were EUR 2.95bn of the EUR 3.62bn total deposit value, or 81%. Individuals accounted for 88% of withdrawal value (A4). By comparison, ATM cash deposits in Q1-2026 were only EUR 42.7m, about 6% of the counter deposit value (A1). · Banks are already acting on this. CKB reopened its Podgorica Business Point on 24/07/2026 as a small-business centre where cash transactions are no longer available at the counter at all. Non-cash transfers run only through a six-month transition that closes around 24/01/2027. Customers are directed to ATMs for withdrawal and to cash-in devices for free deposit of daily takings. CKB had already run a two-month campaign paying EUR 20 each to the first 500 customers who deposited at an ATM twice and never used a teller (A1). · Two banks still run manual overnight cash drops that a smart safe or deposit recycler replaces outright. NLB publishes 11 day-and-night safes as a separate location type, and Erste 12 across 10 addresses (A1). · A reference example already exists in this market. Addiko Montenegro runs 12 deposit-and-withdrawal machines, seven of them branded self-service "Zona 24/7" lobbies. Uniquely in the region, they accept coins as well as notes through a dedicated perforated coin tray. They have a 150-banknote limit and a business daily-takings flow tagged by date and organisational unit (A1). · Macro backdrop: retail deposits grew 13.45% year on year to June 2026, more than double total deposit growth, on a tourism season up about 6% (A1).

signals.bank_theme: Montenegro — CRD VI / CRR III and resolution alignment, with EU accession negotiations targeted to close by end-2026
signals.signal: On 03/07/2026 the central bank's Council approved a draft Law amending the Law on Credit Institutions. It aligns Montenegro mainly with the final European CRD VI and CRR III prudential packages, which are the EU's bank capital rules. It also aligns with the regulations behind the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the European Central Bank close-cooperation regime. The draft is explicitly framed around the central bank's future integration into the European System of Central Banks. · The Council also approved a draft Law amending the Law on Resolution of Credit Institutions. That aligns with the Single Resolution Mechanism and Single Resolution Fund, with the post-accession provisions applying later. The Council held the countercyclical capital buffer at 1%. · Montenegro's stated strategic goal is to finish EU accession negotiations by end-2026. The central bank coordinates Chapter 9 on financial services and Chapter 17 on economic and monetary policy. On 24/08/2026 it welcomed constitutional amendments strengthening its independence (A4). · The raw evidence contradicts itself on digital operational resilience. An earlier press report of a September 2025 Council draft claimed the amendments would carry the EU DORA operational-resilience requirements. That press source could not be re-read this cycle, and the central bank's own pages returned errors. The agent reading the 03/07/2026 approval says the draft contains no DORA transposition article (A3, A4).

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — instant payments arrive on two rails (TIPS Clone + KIBS Instant), MIPS rebuilt on ISO 20022
signals.signal: North Macedonia is about to get real-time payments on two separate systems at once, and every bank has to connect to both. Banca d'Italia's TIPS Clone is a copy of the euro-area instant settlement service, built for the Western Balkans. It went live on 20/07/2026 with Bosnia and Montenegro. A second joining window in November 2026 is expected to bring in North Macedonia alongside Albania and Kosovo (A3, A5). ECB President Lagarde referred to the accession on 24/07/2026 and the National Bank (NBRSM) repeated it, but both say "expected", with no day named (A4). · In parallel, NBRSM confirmed on 04/08/2026 that during July it completed the first testing cycle of the rebuilt MIPS national payment system with the banks. Most project messages were processed in ISO 20022, the international payment-message standard (A4). · Separately, KIBS, the private clearing house, already holds an instant-payment operator licence for denar payments settled in under 10 seconds, 24/7. It runs the "Strela" app with QR, contactless, an alias register and request-to-pay. Trade press reports that two banks are preparing to initiate payments over it by 15/09/2026, with the names not published (A1, A5). · NBRSM's own statistics still report zero instant payments in every month from Jan-2024 to Mar-2026. So this is a standing start with a clean baseline for comparison (A4). NBRSM and the World Bank ran a two-day readiness workshop for banks and payment service providers (PSPs) on 16/06/2026, focused clearly on participants' technical and operational readiness (A3).
signals.date: 04/08/2026 — first MIPS test cycle completed on ISO 20022; 15/09/2026 — first banks expected to initiate on KIBS Instant; November 2026 — expected TIPS Clone joining window
signals.implies: Every one of the seven main NBRSM-licensed banks faces two integrations, not one, on two different calendars. Each needs ISO 20022 message mapping, and 24/7/365 channel and liquidity operations. Each also needs real-time sanctions and fraud screening that clears in seconds, because an overnight batch cannot score a payment that settles instantly. Further requirements are key management and hardware security modules (HSMs) for the new scheme, plus QR acceptance across the terminal estate. This is the largest single discrete opportunity in the market, and the same work repeats across the whole TIPS Clone group of countries.
signals.likelihood: High that the MIPS ISO 20022 go-live proceeds — first test cycle passed and the project is EU-funded; Medium-High specifically on the November-2026 instant window, which NBRSM and the ECB both call "expected" rather than fixed
signals.follow_up: Ask NBRSM's Payment Systems Department (director Biljana Donovska-Gecheva) for the exact go-live date and the wave-one bank list. Also request the TIPS Clone message specification. The assumption that it carries ISO 20022 pacs messages is currently unsourced and must not be repeated to a client as fact. Identify the two banks joining KIBS Instant by 15/09/2026. Re-pull NBRSM Table 7 after November to catch the first non-zero instant month.
signals.product_review_why: Two instant rails create ISO 20022 integration work, and real-time screening and scheme key management follow directly from settling in seconds.

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — NBRSM TIPS-clone connectivity tender (2nd attempt) closing 18/09/2026, and the incumbent suppliers around it
signals.signal: The National Bank's tender to connect the country to the TIPS Clone platform is open, closes soon, and is a second attempt. Notice 14505/2026, "Поврзување на клонот на ТИПС", is an open procedure for services, published 19/08/2026, with bids opened 18/09/2026 at 10:00. It is awarded on lowest price, with no e-auction. The registry shows why the first run failed. The identical notice 09887/2026, published 04/06/2026 with opening 06/07/2026, was cancelled on 28/07/2026 because no bid, or no acceptable bid, was submitted (A2, A6). · Only a TIPS-authorised network service provider, in practice SWIFT or Nexi, or a party formally authorised by one, can bid for the connectivity layer. So this is timing and competitor intelligence rather than a bid Printec can enter itself. The Kosovo equivalent went to Nexi at EUR 685,000 (A2). · The same registry also names the suppliers already inside NBRSM. ASEE (Asseco South Eastern Europe) DOOEL Skopje holds the support contract for the MIPS and SWIFT equipment (MKD 2,947,640, contract 22/07/2026). Lirex Skopje holds the privileged-access management system (MKD 5,985,000, 06/07/2026). Sektron, Vorsal, Smart Solutions and A-Zero hold smaller IT and physical-security contracts (A2). · Two further NBRSM procedures are open. Money-transport insurance opens on 11/09/2026, and 2,000-denar banknotes on 25/09/2026, the second of these also a repeat attempt. Its 2026 register does contain cash-handling buys such as a banknote-banding machine and a vault renovation, which corrects last cycle's reading of no cash machines (A2).
signals.date: 18/09/2026 — bids opened on the second TIPS-clone connectivity tender; 28/07/2026 — first attempt formally cancelled for want of an acceptable bid
signals.implies: Whoever wins after 18/09/2026 will sit beside NBRSM and the Macedonian banks for the next five years. That supplier will sell further services from that position, exactly as Nexi now does in Kosovo. ASEE already supports the national payment system's MIPS and SWIFT equipment, so it is a direct competitor inside the layer where the TIPS work lands. · In practice, Printec should be in front of Komercijalna, Stopanska and NLB with the bank-side instant-payments proposition before the award lands. It should also treat a third failed call as a real possibility that would buy extra months. No estimated value is published for 14505/2026.
signals.likelihood: Award expected within weeks of the 18/09/2026 opening if this attempt draws a compliant bid; a third attempt is a live possibility given the first drew none
signals.follow_up: Re-query the ESJN CompletedProcedures and Cancelations data services after 18/09/2026 for the outcome. Profile ASEE DOOEL Skopje first, as the MIPS and SWIFT support incumbent and likeliest connectivity bidder, then Lirex Skopje. Open notice 14505/2026 itself for the estimated value and the exact network-service-provider requirement.
signals.product_review_why: This is timing and competitor intelligence around the national instant-payments connectivity award, and the cash and security buys are incidental.

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — central bank's merchant-acceptance programme: national QR, aliases, request-to-pay and low-cost softPOS
signals.signal: The central bank has publicly made card acceptance at small merchants its priority, and has named cheap acceptance devices as the answer. At the NBRSM-World Bank stakeholder forum on 18/06/2026, Vice-Governor Igor Velichkovski said 84% of citizens hold a payment account and three in four have paid digitally. Even so, more than 90% of payments at small merchants are still cash. Only about 16,700 merchants hold roughly 36,000 accepting devices, a base he called concentrated and unequal. · His named remedies are instant payments "by the end of the year", a national interoperable QR code usable across all providers, and payments by simple alias. He also named instant confirmation of every transaction, request-to-pay, and more mobile apps including from non-bank providers. He described the high cost of acceptance devices as a core barrier (A4). · The banks are already moving. NLB launched "NLB Smart POS", the first certified tap-on-phone Android application in the country, where a merchant's own phone becomes the terminal with no hardware. Installations are up 46% year on year and transaction volume has doubled. It is giving away 50 free softPOS units under the "Value of Cashless Payment — Bitola" project, which closed enrolment on 31/08/2026. Halkbank is running a parallel "Cashless Bitola" offer on its Halk Mobi POS (A5). · NLB Group has separately quantified a regional acquiring push, with end-to-end POS-to-cash-register integration and softPOS on the 2026-2030 roadmap (A1). KIBS's own cost-benefit work for the World Bank counted converting part of the grey economy into formal payment channels as a benefit of instant payments (A1). NBRSM's Q1-2026 data shows payments at physical points of sale still grew 11.7% year on year, even as mobile took 72.8% of electronically initiated payments. So the terminal estate is being extended, not cannibalised (A4).

sources.text: NBRSM — Вицегувернерот Величковски на форумот за прифаќање електронски плаќања

signals.date: 27/08/2026 — NLB Smart POS growth figures published; 18/06/2026 — NBRSM/World Bank forum sets the national QR, alias and request-to-pay agenda; 18/08/2026 — Halkbank "Cashless Bitola" softPOS offer opens
signals.implies: This is a regulator-sponsored, World-Bank-backed push to widen acceptance well beyond 16,700 merchants, with the cost of the device named as the obstacle. That is an explicit opening for tap-to-phone softPOS and entry-level terminals. · More durable is the acquiring back end that softPOS does not remove. It covers merchant onboarding and eKYC (electronic identity checks), terminal management systems, key injection and security backed by hardware security modules. It also covers integration work for the national QR scheme, the alias register and request-to-pay. Phone-based acceptance weakens the case for selling terminal boxes, so the revenue sits in the platform and in the field and operational layer.
signals.likelihood: High — a central-bank-sponsored programme with World Bank support and a stated end-2026 milestone, with two banks already running city-scale merchant giveaways
signals.follow_up: Watch for NBRSM actually issuing the national QR standard; nothing is published yet. Approach the acquirers (Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB, Halkbank) with a softPOS plus terminal-management bundle aimed at the small-merchant tail. Ask them directly whether softPOS is displacing hardware or adding micro-merchants who would never have taken a terminal. Treat Bitola as a multi-bank pilot city and check whether Stopanska and Komercijalna are also in it.
signals.product_review_why: The regulator wants cheap merchant acceptance, so softPOS and terminal management lead, with national QR integration and key injection behind them.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — NBG Stopanska + SEPA + deposit-ATM growth
signals.signal: The market-level deposit-ATM position is confirmed on primary regulator data, and the Stopanska picture has changed considerably. NBRSM Table 3 (reference March 2026) shows 1,136 ATMs, up 7.0% year on year, of which 473 take cash deposits. Deposit-capable machines are up 16.5% year on year and up 24 in the quarter. But the total fleet has been essentially flat since December 2025 (1,132 / 1,132 / 1,132 / 1,136). So 2026 growth is happening inside the fleet rather than in unit count, and 663 machines are still dispense-only (A4). · Table 5 gives the recycler economics. March 2026 ATM cash deposits were 230,698 transactions worth MKD 3.65bn, up 31% by count and 53% by value. Withdrawals were 2,498,982 transactions worth MKD 19.27bn, up 3.4% and 11.8%. Deposit value is now 19.0% of withdrawal value, up from 13.8% a year earlier (A4). Branch numbers keep falling: 371 at end-2025, from 409 in 2020, a fall of 9.3% (A4). · At Stopanska specifically, H1-2026 pre-tax profit fell 30% year on year and net fee income fell 7%. In its own filing the bank blames reduced payment and card tariffs and, at the same time, higher commission expenses charged by the suppliers of those services. It also completed a move into a new LEED Gold head office in Q2-2026 (A1). Its own ATM locator shows a large dispense-only tail (see the count conflict in the notes). Its mobile app rates 2.2 out of 5 on Google Play against NLB's 3.7, making it the clear laggard among large-bank apps (A4). · Leadership is now settled. CEO and Board Chair Hrisula Koutoudi received a fresh four-year mandate on 18/08/2026 with NBRSM consent. CFO Mirjana Trajanovska was re-appointed to 2029 on 10/07/2026, and Zorica Božinovska-Lazarevska joined the Supervisory Board (A1, A5).

signals.date: 18/08/2026 — Stopanska CEO re-appointed for four years with NBRSM consent; 25/06/2026 — NBRSM Q1-2026 payment statistics confirm deposit-capable ATMs at 473, up 16.5% y/y
signals.implies: Stopanska has told the market in writing that its suppliers' fees are rising while its own tariffs fall. That is the strongest managed-services and vendor-renegotiation argument in the country, and the executives who signed it are now in post to 2030. · The market data says the live pipeline is a deposit and recycler upgrade and swap-out programme, on a fleet that has stopped growing in units. It also covers multivendor ATM software, device telemetry and managed field services. Cash-in value at 19% of cash-out means a recycler here can already re-dispense roughly a fifth of what it pays out, which cuts cash-in-transit runs and vault float. The weak app rating adds a near-term argument for assisted-service kiosks and deposit ATMs to absorb traffic pushed back off the phone. · Two corrections to last cycle. signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — Komercijalna banka repeatable branch-transformation template plus a 191-machine ATM estate
signals.signal: The largest bank in the market by assets, with a 20.8% share, is running a repeating branch-modernisation template. It has said that modernising the business network is a 2026 priority. Its Makpetrol branch was fully modernised, as reported on 27/04/2026. It now has a digital kiosk for commission-free utility and telecom bill payment with no teller involved, an ATM that takes deposits as well as withdrawals, and fully accessible access. The branch is staffed only 08:00-16:00 on weekdays, with the self-service devices covering the rest. · The bank's own newsroom documents the same treatment at at least four more sites: Novo Lisiče, Negotino, the Nabizi retail park in Struga and Avtokomanda. This is therefore a template, not a one-off (A4). Under a promotion running to 31/12/2026, businesses can pay daily takings into that ATM free of charge on a Visa or Mastercard business debit card. That is a deliberate push of SME cash off the counter (A4). · The bank's own machine-readable ATM feed was re-pulled on 27/08/2026. It carries 191 records across 39 cities, 188 of them active. The feed has an unpublished three-way "TypeATM" split of 98 / 82 / 11. Its ATM page confirms cash withdrawal, cash deposit at labelled machines, and euro-to-denar exchange at the machine. All of this is contactless, including phone wallets, with a cash-in ceiling of 40 notes per transaction (A1). · H1-2026 pre-tax profit was MKD 2,798.2m, down 5.5% year on year but 110.9% of plan. Net fee income was up 6.6%, achieved despite cuts to domestic payment fees, so volume is outrunning tariff cuts. Stated forward priorities are further process digitalisation, "modernisation of the business network" and adapting to the payment-services regulation (A1).
signals.date: 30/07/2026 — H1-2026 filing restates "modernisation of the business network" as a priority; 31/12/2026 — free business cash-deposit promotion expires; 27/04/2026 — fifth documented branch on the modernisation template
signals.implies: The national decline in branch numbers is turning into per-site spending at the biggest bank in the country. The bundle is a kiosk, a deposit-capable ATM and an accessible fit-out. With five or more branches already done, the addressable pipeline is the rest of the network, plus teller cash recyclers behind the counter and managed field services. The 40-note cash-in ceiling is a concrete efficiency argument for higher-capacity recyclers. The free business-deposit promotion ends on 31/12/2026, which is the natural moment to pitch cash forecasting and optimisation against the deposit volumes it will have generated.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High over 6-12 months — the template has been executed at five or more identified branches and the internal mandate is stated in the bank's own filing
signals.follow_up: Ask Komercijalna how many branches are scheduled for the same treatment in 2026-2027, and who supplied the kiosk and the deposit ATM. Get the "TypeATM" legend confirmed. Once 98 / 82 / 11 is decoded, the deposit-capable share of the 191-machine estate can be counted. Pitch cost-per-transaction migration off the counter against the stated modernisation priority.
signals.product_review_why: A repeating branch fit-out with a kiosk and a deposit ATM is branch transformation first, with recyclers and field services as the follow-on.

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — NLB Banka Skopje digital-concept branches, contact-centre modernisation and fresh parent capital
signals.signal: NLB Skopje is spending on physical channels and has just been given the capital to continue. On 13/07/2026 it converted its "Sobranie" branch in Skopje into a 140 m2 digital-concept branch. The branch has a 24/7 self-service zone holding two deposit-and-withdrawal ATMs plus a separate CDS cash-deposit machine for businesses. That is a live cash-automation reference and a template the bank is likely to repeat (A5). · Its H1-2026 filing records a new branch at Univerzalna Sala and a full rebuild of the Dame Gruev branch in six months. It names modernisation of the business network, modernisation of the contact centre, upgraded lending and payment platforms, and advanced analytics as forward priorities. It launched Visa Direct real-time transfers in the half and calls itself the market's digitalisation leader (A1). · Funding is in place. There is a EUR 10m subordinated loan from the parent that counts as Additional Tier 1 capital, disclosed 30/07/2026. There is also a EUR 30m long-term parent loan, of which EUR 15m was drawn by 30/06/2026. Other sources are a fully drawn EBRD EUR 30m green line, and MKD 2.6bn of 2025 profit retained (A1). · At group level, NLB's Investor Day deck states verbatim an "ATM and CDS network upgrade at Group level driving cash out of branches". Branch cash transactions are down from 32% at end-2023 to 13.5% in March 2026, against a target below 10% for 2030. The 2026 priority list puts digital authentication and self-service legal-entity onboarding explicitly "across group" (A1). · Skopje itself runs 46 branches for 469,626 active clients, or 10,209 clients per branch. Its cost-income ratio of 42.8% is already better than the group's 46.5%, so further gains must come from channel mix (A1).

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — ProCredit Bank's near-branchless model runs on 24/7 self-service zones with an ageing sub-fleet
signals.signal: ProCredit Skopje runs the most branch-light model in the market. As at 27/08/2026 it has three full branches, in Skopje-Manapo, Strumica and Bitola, plus 13 service units. Customers are served through "24/7 Zones" with an unusually deep confirmed set of features. These include card-controlled entry after hours, and denar and euro cash deposit and withdrawal. Every zone has a euro deposit and withdrawal ATM. The zones also have coin deposit machines and daily-takings deposit, either at the ATM or into a night safe. The night safe uses barcoded single-use security bags with magnetic-card door access. Each zone also has information terminals for statements and a free direct handset to the 24/7 contact centre. Deposit capacity is 40 or 150 notes per transaction, "depending on the ATM model". That is direct evidence of a mixed-generation fleet with an older sub-fleet due for replacement. The bank also runs an online branch, e-signing, OneID electronic identification, Apple and Google Pay and a PSD2 open-banking portal (A1). At group level, ProCredit Holding's Q2-2026 deck confirms that North Macedonia received the new mobile retail banking app in H1-2026. A new business-client mobile app also went live there, with digital onboarding advertised at under 15 minutes. The banking app itself is built in-house by the group's IT subsidiary Quipu. Identity, e-signature and liveness checks are bought from local qualified providers in each market, which is OneID in North Macedonia. The eKYC layer is therefore a genuine vendor-selected slot (A1). Governance has been refreshed. Maja Mihajlova was re-appointed to the Management Board for four years, with NBRSM consent issued 15/07/2026. A new Supervisory Board member was appointed around 21-24/08/2026, and is unnamed in the published summary (A5).

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — OneID national digital identity is now the live remote-onboarding rail, with three banks still outside it
signals.signal: OneID is the national mobile electronic identity. It was built by KIBS with Nextsense under the KibsTrust qualified-trust brand. It was registered as the first Macedonian eID scheme in December 2021. It is now in production across almost the whole top tier of the market. The adoption timeline comes from OneID's own news page. Komercijalna and Halkbank joined in October 2022, and Sparkasse in November 2022. ProCredit and Triglav followed in April 2024, and Silk Road Bank in September 2024. NLB Banka joined in March 2025. The state Central Register followed in June 2025 and Stopanska Banka in January 2026. The partner wall as at 27/08/2026 lists seven banks. The banks not on it are UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola (A1). The scheme's own rules create a recurring workload. The electronic identity is valid for two years and must then be renewed, and it can be active on only one device. It requires biometric authentication on a device running at least Android 6.0 or iOS 11.4. Data updates through it are capped at once per month. Stopanska runs "Client update with OneID" as a standing free service and accepts no other eID app (A1). The commercial ceiling has now moved. On 25/08/2026 Komercijalna was reported to be issuing online consumer loans of up to MKD 2,600,000 (roughly EUR 42,000). These are granted end to end through OneID, fully remote, with an immediate decision and no branch visit (A5).

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — eIDAS 2 transposed; bank wallet-verifier obligation from 01/06/2027
signals.signal: This cycle upgrades the evidence from a reading of the consolidated text to the primary bill text plus independent corroboration, and it holds. A3 re-verified the 43-page Government bill (Skopje, June 2025, proposed by Minister for Digital Transformation Stefan Andonovski). It confirms verbatim that Article 27 sets application from 1 June 2027. It also confirms that new Article 20-м(2) mirrors eIDAS Article 5f(2). Under that article, private relying parties other than micro and small enterprises must accept registered European digital identity wallets when the user asks. This applies where they require strong user authentication for online identification, in areas expressly including "банкарство, финансиски услуги" (banking, financial services). Bylaws are due within six months of entry into force. Articles 71-а to 71-в set graduated fines of EUR 500-1,000 for micro traders up to EUR 5,000-10,000 for large traders. That schedule falls on the wallet issuer, not on bank relying parties. The fiscal lines start at MKD 9m for 2025. They then run at MKD 200m for 2026 and MKD 200m for 2027, funded first from Digital Europe and then from the EU Growth Plan for the Western Balkans (A3). The European Commission's North Macedonia Report 2025 (04/11/2025) independently states that the law "was amended to transpose the eIDAS 2.0 Regulation and to introduce the Digital Identity Wallet". The same report notes that existing e-identification tools are still not user-friendly or free (A3). A4 separately confirms that Parliament passed the amendment among four digital-transformation reform laws at its 58th session in June 2025. Passing the package unlocks over EUR 19m under the Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans, of which EUR 5.7m is direct budget support (A4). One point is still outstanding: only the draft was verified. The adopted gazette text was not obtained, so it is not proven that Article 20-м and the 01/06/2027 date survived unchanged (A3).

sources.text: MKD.mk — Собранието ги донесе реформските закони за дигитална трансформација

signals.date: 01/06/2027 — statutory application date for bank relying parties; bylaws due within six months of entry into force; 04/11/2025 — European Commission confirms the transposing amendment was adopted
signals.implies: If the adopted text matches the bill, North Macedonia becomes the first non-EU footprint market with a legal duty on banks to accept an EU-style identity wallet. That duty would start six months before the EU's own derived acceptance date. Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB Skopje, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse and UNIBanka must all build a wallet-verifier into digital onboarding and login. Budget therefore has to be committed from H2-2026 into H1-2027. The addressable work is the relying-party acceptance and verification layer, plus remote identity proofing. It also covers HSM and key handling for relying-party keys, plus screening behind the wallet. Wallet identity data does not cover full customer due diligence. Document management for retained evidence is a further element. Do not pitch on the penalty schedule, because those fines fall on wallet issuers, not on banks. The six-month bylaw window is the moment to shape technical requirements with the Ministry.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high that banks scope the work within 6-12 months — the application date is fixed in statute, but the technical specification only arrives with the ministry bylaws
signals.follow_up: Priority: get the adopted Службен весник text and number, and prove that Article 20-м and the 01/06/2027 date survived unchanged. The ministry portal and ener.gov.mk could not be reached from the collection environment. Then track the six-month bylaws and any NBRSM guidance to banks. Check the MKD 200m 2026 line against the official state budget rather than the draft-law PDF. Map the OneID integration boundary before pitching.
signals.product_review_why: A legal duty to accept EU identity wallets is an onboarding and identity build, with relying-party keys and evidence retention as supporting pieces.

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — Single Register of Accounts (ЕРС) + electronic forced-collection system
signals.signal: There is no fresh development this cycle, and the evidence base got weaker rather than stronger. The obligation stands as recorded. The transitional provisions of the amended Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (Службен весник на РСМ 144/25) require the Central Register to set up a national electronic register. It must cover denar and foreign-currency payment and deposit accounts, linked payment instruments and safe-deposit boxes. It must also cover account holders, beneficial owners and legal representatives. The Financial Intelligence Office gets direct unrestricted access. Separately, the law requires an electronic forced-collection system to be set up and exchanging information. Forced-collection orders must be submitted through it from 01/11/2027. Scope covers every NBRSM-licensed bank plus payment and e-money institutions, and no contract value is published anywhere. This cycle A3 filed no new primary work on it. A3 explicitly flagged that the deadline dates were imported from other rows without a source. It cited 30/09/2026 in two places against the master row's 01/12/2026, so the register go-live date is still genuinely unresolved (A3).
