signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — mandatory app-based strong authentication in force, with tokenised cards up 137%
signals.signal: Two card-side facts now rest on regulator primary sources. First, NBRSM's own announcement confirms that the legal duty on banks to apply strong customer authentication to online card payments came into force on 1 March 2026. Instead of the old SMS code, the customer gets a notification in the bank's official mobile app. The customer must then approve with the app PIN, a fingerprint or face recognition. Without that approval the payment cannot go through, even if someone holds the card details. NBRSM says the duty comes from the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems and has been introduced in stages. It already covers online account access, card payments at physical points of sale and e-/m-banking orders. NBRSM adds that extending it to internet payments "completes the process of alignment" with EU rules (A4). Second, NBRSM Table 2 for March 2026 shows 2,020,552 cards in total, up 2.7% year on year. Cards with a mobile-payment (tokenised) solution were 353,863, against 148,970 a year earlier. That is up 137.5%, and up 21.9% in a single quarter, the fourth quarter in a row of double-digit growth. Contactless cards were 1,977,099 (97.8%). Credit cards were down 2.5% year on year to 264,232, so growth is coming from wallet provisioning rather than new plastic. NBRSM's Q1-2026 release adds that mobile apps carry 72.8% of electronically initiated payments, which are themselves up 25.9%. Each digitised card averaged only four domestic mobile transactions in the quarter (A4).

sources.text: NBRSM — Од 1 март 2026 година, побезбедни онлајн плаќања

signals.date: 25/06/2026 — Q1-2026 card statistics published showing tokenised cards up 137.5% y/y; obligation itself in force since 01/03/2026
signals.implies: Every Macedonian card issuer now has to run app-based authentication, biometrics and cryptographic key handling across a two-million-card base. More than 350,000 of those cards are already tokenised. That drives demand for hardware security modules, PCI-PIN compliance and remote key injection across the provisioning and PIN estate. It also drives card-issuing and token-management work. Behavioural transaction monitoring and fraud rules are a third area. Pushing authentication into the app moves fraud from card-present toward social engineering and account takeover. The compulsory and technically hard token migration also gives the app-quality problem at Stopanska a plausible cause. Four transactions per digitised card per quarter is low usage, and that headroom is what the national QR scheme and the instant rail are designed to unlock.
signals.likelihood: Certain that the obligation is in force, stated by the regulator; High that tokenisation keeps compounding, having grown more than 15% quarter on quarter for four straight quarters
signals.follow_up: Get the underlying NBRSM decision text from the regulations pages. Check whether a transaction-risk-analysis or low-value exemption regime is defined, because that is where risk engines get sold and the press release does not mention exemptions. Pull Table 4.2 on fraudulent payment transactions for the card-not-present fraud trend that would justify the monitoring pitch. It was not checked this cycle.
signals.product_review_why: Mandatory app authentication over a tokenised card base drives HSM and key work, token management on the issuing side, and new fraud patterns to monitor.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: North Macedonia — Payten holds Halkbank Skopje's softPOS acceptance product
signals.signal: Payten's SoftPOS is software that turns an ordinary Android phone into a contactless card-acceptance terminal. It is live at Halkbank AD Skopje under the brand "Halk Mobi POS", confirmed by Payten's own dated article of 17/03/2026. The article says merchants without a traditional terminal can accept contactless cards and wallets directly on Android phones. It states that "the first results are encouraging", but it gives no merchant or transaction counts (A6). Halkbank is now actively pushing that estate. From 18/08/2026 it is running a "Cashless Bitola" offer for businesses in Bitola. The offer gives them Halk Mobi POS at no cost, plus a Visa Business Debit card with the annual fee waived for twelve months. Applications are at the Bitola branch, and the offer runs until the pre-set slots are filled (A5). Payten's corporate newsroom has published nothing since 16/06/2026. There is therefore no new named Macedonian win from Payten this cycle, and its only quantified acceptance figures sit in the group investor deck (A6).
signals.date: 18/08/2026 — Halkbank expands the Payten-supplied Halk Mobi POS estate through the Cashless Bitola campaign; deployment itself confirmed 17/03/2026
signals.implies: A named competitor holds the acceptance software at one of the market's five large banks, and that bank is now scaling it city by city. The softPOS platform slot at Halkbank is therefore closed. The remaining opening is the operational layer that phone-based acceptance does not remove. That layer covers terminal and device management, certification, key injection, HSM-backed security, merchant onboarding and eKYC, and field service. Treat Bitola as a competitive proving ground, because NLB is running its own free-softPOS campaign in the same city with its own platform.

The alternative is that it simply adds micro-merchants who would never have taken a terminal. That answer decides whether to compete on platform or on the operational layer. Get merchant and terminal counts behind Halk Mobi POS. Check the Payten newsroom monthly, because it has no usable feed and needs a rendering fetch.
signals.product_review_why: A competitor holds the softPOS slot, so the opening is terminal management, key injection and field service around phone-based acceptance.

signals.bank_theme: Romania — draft law B409/2026 would force a screen-flow change on every ATM in the market inside 90 days
signals.signal: The bill has now passed every advisory opinion, and none opposed it. We read the initiators' own text at the primary source. A new Art. 221¹ in Law 209/2019 would require every provider running cash-withdrawal ATMs in Romania to let a cardholder type in any withdrawal amount they choose. This applies to cards from any issuer authorised in Romania. The text says clearly that preset fast-cash buttons are not enough. A breach becomes a contravention (a minor offence) fined RON 50,000–100,000. Operators get 90 days from entry into force to comply. What moved this cycle is the National Bank of Romania's opinion no. G/161 of 17/08/2026, signed by Governor Isărescu. It says the measure could improve access to cash, especially in rural areas, and concludes that BNR "does not oppose" it. BNR also formally asked that the banking system be consulted on the technical features of the terminals. The Competition Council opinion of 18/08/2026 found no competition or State-aid problem. As at 27/08/2026 the bill is still in the first chamber, with no committee report and no vote scheduled (A1).
signals.date: 18/08/2026 — Competition Council opinion, the last of four, all favourable; BNR opinion 17/08/2026 does not oppose; 90-day compliance clock starts on entry into force
signals.implies: Every ATM deployer in Romania would have to make one screen-flow change across mixed hardware and re-certify it within 90 days. That is roughly 11,000 machines across BCR, BT, BRD, ING, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CEC and independents including Euronet. No bank can buy, build, test and certify that from scratch inside the window. That is exactly what multivendor ATM software and managed services offer. The central bank has also invited a technical consultation with the industry. There is therefore an open, named door to shape the specification before the text is fixed. Free-amount entry also changes the mix of banknotes a machine pays out. That brings in cash forecasting and denomination optimisation, meaning the choice of which notes to stock. No value is published, so the item is carried without a size.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high that it is adopted — cross-party, urgency requested, four favourable opinions and no opposition
signals.follow_up: Build the multivendor free-amount screen-flow package now, not after the law is promulgated. Ask the Romanian Banking Association to be included in the technical consultation BNR asked for. That request is on the file and is the cheapest way in. Track the Senate committee report, then the Chamber of Deputies, which is the deciding chamber.
signals.product_review_why: A forced ATM screen-flow change across 11,000 machines is multivendor ATM software and managed-service work, not a physical security matter.

The product page still lists exactly the same five pilot sites on 27/08/2026. There is no sixth address, so the decision to move from pilot to rollout is still open (A1). signals.date: 04/08/2026 — Cash2Card opens CEC's deposit machines to every Romanian debit cardholder; ~350 branches named for operating-model redesign; next hard checkpoint is the H1-2026 interim due 30/09/2026
signals.implies: CEC has the widest branch network in Romania, at 1,011 units, 460 of them rural. It has publicly committed to converting units rather than closing them. The gap between 46 zones today and about 350 branches marked for redesign is therefore a measured, bank-published pipeline. It covers recyclers, which are ATMs that re-use deposited notes, plus FX kiosks and video-banking pods. Cash2Card is the argument that justifies the spend. Every extra deposit machine now serves the whole Romanian card base, not just CEC's own customers. That pushes the economics toward true recycling rather than deposit-only machines. The capital position fixes the commercial shape. Equipment capex is cut 59% and an unquantified competition-fine contingency is outstanding. This must therefore be pitched as a lease, as-a-service or managed service, not a hardware purchase. A 2025 pace of five zones a year is itself the sales argument, because a financed, standard roll-out-in-a-box is what unblocks it.
signals.likelihood: High that the concept continues — proven at 46 sites and named as a strategic pillar; the pace is the risk, and no rollout date is published
signals.follow_up: Ask CEC for the standard equipment list per 24/7 zone and the 2026 conversion target. Then price the roughly 350-branch programme against that pace. Approach the Cards Directorate on the Cash2Card volume ramp. Find out whether the 270-plus MFMs actually recycle or only accept cash. Do not walk in claiming Temenos. Register as a qualified supplier with Serviciul Independent Achiziţii before a device lot appears. The last published bid window was 16 days, too short to qualify from cold.
signals.product_review_why: A 350-branch self-service redesign with deposit and recycling machines, which capex cuts push toward an as-a-service deal.

signals.bank_theme: Romania — public-sector POS acquiring pool; Banca Transilvania is the channel
signals.signal: This cycle's contract-by-contract check changes the earlier conclusion. CEC Bank, not Banca Transilvania, is the most-awarded public-sector card acquirer. It has nine SICAP award notices totalling roughly RON 30.7m of contracted acquiring in four months. These cover regional tax directorates in Bucureşti, Iaşi, Braşov and Ploieşti, the National Trade Register Office, Bucharest Sector 6 and Municipiul Bacău. They also cover Poşta Română online card processing at RON 10.76m and the National Lottery at RON 3.76m. There are also 22 further TED award notices naming CEC Bank between 01/05 and 24/08/2026 (A2). Banca Transilvania remains strong at the municipal end. It holds RON 4.99m at Baia Mare on its Globalpay platform, Cluj-Napoca awards made by negotiated procedure without prior publication, and Braşov Lot 2. It also holds every one of the 12 small SNEP direct awards published in August (A2). BCR and Garanti also win at scale. BCR takes DGRFP Craiova treasury banking. Garanti holds the ANCPI/OCPI online card-processing framework with 473 contracts worth RON 6.4m (A2). At a structural level, the Romanian state is also closing its own treasury cash desks and buying the counter service from banks. DGRFP Ploieşti awarded a 48-month cashier-services framework to CEC Bank at RON 4,457,700 (A2). Non-bank operators keep winning unattended collection on a rental model, with Salt Bank as framework holder and SelfPay as terminal operator (A2, A6).

signals.date: 24/08/2026 — CEC Bank named winner of the National Lottery electronic-transaction contract, the ninth verified public acquiring win in four months; treasury cash-desk outsourcing framework awarded 25/05/2026

signals.bank_theme: Banca Naţională a României — security + HSM procurement stream

The detail that matters is that the lots are three regional agencies, Bacău, Prahova and Suceava, not head office. Bids closed 06/08/2026 and no award appears among BNR's 21 TED notices to 27/08/2026. The service side is locked up. Regia Autonomă RASIROM R.A. (RO 7061781) is the state technical-security operator under the Romanian Intelligence Service. It holds the BNR security-maintenance contract 49/P/2026 at RON 2,676,424.64. HSM support went to a Romanian SME, Digital Professional Services SRL (RO43040394), at RON 335,000 on 18/05/2026 on lowest price. HSMs are hardware security modules that protect encryption keys. The next notice is therefore due around Q2-2027. BNR's payments core is closed to competition. ION/Wall Street Systems holds STP at EUR 2.47m and EUR 2.80m, both by negotiated procedure without prior publication, and Montran holds ReGIS and SaFIR development (A2, A6). Cash-centre consumables at RON 1,292,285.06 name two further embedded suppliers (A2).
signals.date: 20/07/2026 — three-lot regional-agency security tender published, closed 06/08/2026, award still pending as at 27/08/2026
signals.implies: Lot sizes of roughly RON 1.0–1.3m are exactly the scale a mid-size vendor can bid for selectively. The three-lot regional structure means Printec does not have to take the whole thing. But RASIROM holds the service side, backed by its intelligence-service status. That is a practical barrier to a foreign security vendor bidding for BNR alone. The realistic route is RASIROM as consortium or delivery partner rather than a head-on fight. The work would cover anti-skimming, ATM safes and banknote-neutralisation systems, which spoil the notes if a machine is attacked. The HSM line is the more strategic one. An SME on EUR 67k a year holds the central bank's HSM support, while the commercial banks' HSM and key-management estates are far larger and are bought privately.
signals.likelihood: High — the procurement stream recurs annually and one item is in evaluation now

Profile Digital Professional Services SRL and size the BNR HSM estate ahead of the successor notice due around Q2-2027. Sell the same managed HSM and key-injection service into BCR, BRD, CEC and BT, where the estates are much bigger. One item still needs reconciling: the CN1088908 RON ~12m control-room security programme carried in the master row was not re-verified this cycle, and its status is unknown.

signals.bank_theme: BCR (Erste) — fleet rationalisation + ~780-unit off-site ATM perimeter
signals.signal: The machine count was independently re-pulled from BCR's own locator API on 27/08/2026 and is now precise. There are 1,100 cash-dispense-only ATMs, 568 multifunctional machines and 282 branch records, giving 1,668 devices in total. Every one of the 568 multifunctional machines accepts cash in, and none of the 1,100 ATMs does. Their whole service set is withdrawal, mini-statement, balance and PIN change. Exactly two thirds of the self-service estate cannot take a deposit, and that is the pool for conversion to recyclers (A1). There are two new branch-side numbers. 211 of the 282 branches are tagged cashless with no staffed cash desk, and only 71 still run a teller counter. Only 66 branches accept business cash at a machine, in RON only (A1). One moving target was missed in the master row. Voice-guided ATMs rose from 376 to 422, and contactless from 1,023 to 1,061, in the 27 days to 27/08/2026. BCR is therefore retrofitting accessibility in-house at roughly 46 units a month. Accessibility should not be sold as a forced-replacement trigger. Law 232/2022 Art. 29(2) gives legacy self-service terminals 20 years from entry into use, so there is no 2030 cliff (A1). Pressure is disclosed and structural. H1-2026 net profit was RON 1,205m against RON 1,473m, and segment cost/income worsened from 40.0% to 42.3%. The banking levy nearly doubled to EUR 39m, 142 FTE have gone since December, and a ROBOR fine of RON 577,361,887 is outstanding. Retail units are down from 290 to 284 on BCR's own measure. BCR posted no technology, payments or self-service vacancies for a third month in a row, because technology is centralised at Erste group (A5). Merchant acquiring is run by Global Payments, not BCR (A1, A6). One caveat on incumbency: 736 of the 1,100 ATM records carry an "NCR"-prefixed asset id. This is suggestive, but it is BCR's internal register convention and not a vendor field. The NCR Atleos page naming Printec as channel partner is dated 23/03/2018, and its "2,600 ATMs / 500 branches" figures must be removed from all collateral (A1).
signals.date: 27/08/2026 — locator re-pull confirms 1,100 dispense-only ATMs of 1,668 devices and 211 of 282 branches already teller-less; H1-2026 results 30/07/2026
signals.implies: Three quarters of BCR's branches already run without a cash desk. All 211 of them depend on in-lobby machines staying up. That makes uptime-based managed services contractually critical rather than optional. It also turns SLA, cash forecasting and incident management into the lead product. Two named, finite conversion pipelines sit alongside it: 1,100 dispense-only machines to convert to recyclers, and 71 remaining teller branches. Business cash-in is the third gap, because only 66 of 282 branches take SME cash at a machine, and only in lei. With profit down 18%, the levy doubled and a half-billion-lei fine outstanding, this is a cost-per-transaction and operating-cost conversation, not a box sale. It has to be timed to the 2027 budget cycle. Printec's foothold here is real but nine years old, so it must be re-qualified internally before it is presented as incumbency. Because BCR hires no technology staff in Romania, the buying conversation runs through Erste group procurement and Erste Digital as much as through Bucharest.
signals.likelihood: High — the pressure is disclosed and structural, and the estate gaps are measured, not inferred
signals.follow_up: Re-qualify the Printec–BCR service relationship internally before any approach. Build the named lists from the API: the 71 teller branches and the 216 branches with no business cash-in. Price two per-unit programmes against them. Put a RON figure on the 1,100-unit recycler conversion, and set it against the EUR 39m levy increase and the FTE run-rate. Re-pull the API monthly and track the multifunctional count as the deployment signal. Never quote 1,750 and 1,668 as the same measure.
signals.product_review_why: Mostly cashless branches make uptime-based services the lead, with 1,100 dispense-only machines as the recycler conversion pool.

signals.bank_theme: BRD-SocGen — 24/7 cash-zone saturation and acquiring in reverse
signals.signal: A fresh locator pull on 27/08/2026 replaces the dead boilerplate with a live count. There are 1,174 records tagged ATM against 303 tagged MBA, which are multifunctional machines taking RON, EUR and USD deposits. That resolves to roughly 1,233 distinct self-service sites, of which about 946 are cash-out-only. Deposit capability is 23.3% by site (A1). The branch side shows an even wider gap. BRD's own endpoint classes 322 of 335 agency records as "cash agencies" with a staffed counter, and only eleven as cashless. BRD has therefore built and labelled its own cashless-branch template and simply never scaled it (A1). Meanwhile staff are being cut 1.7 times faster than branches. Active bank employees fell to 4,641 from 4,965 in six months, and staff costs are down 8.3%. 24/7 zones now cover 268 of 334 branches, at a proven build rate of 49 new points a year (A1). The purchasing constraint is now evidenced. H1-2026 capex is overwhelmingly software, at RON 82.9m of intangible additions against only RON 9.1m of IT and office equipment brought into service. That equipment figure is roughly a sixth of the 2025 run-rate, and forward commitments are 2.8 times larger for intangibles than for tangibles (A1). Acquiring is also falling, and the deck did not show it. There were 178.2m acquiring transactions in H1-2026 against 184.8m in H1-2025, about −3.6%, after a +32% year. The year-on-year comparison was quietly dropped from the deck (A1). On 06/08/2026 BRD launched RoPay Instant to merchants inside the YOU BRD app. It covers QR at the till, static in-store QR, online checkout and invoice QR, with no card and no fee (A1, A5). Even so, BRD is eighth of ten live banks on RoPay feature breadth. It is the only broad-feature bank with no phone-number Alias payment (A1). BRD hiring can no longer be seen from Romania, because recruitment routes to the Société Générale group portal (A5). Note that BRD co-owns 33.33% of its cash-in-transit provider CIT One SA (A1).

sources.text: BRD — lansare plăţi RoPay Instant către comercianţi

signals.date: 06/08/2026 — RoPay Instant merchant payments go live in YOU BRD; locator re-pull 27/08/2026 gives ~946 cash-out-only self-service sites and only 11 cashless agencies
signals.implies: There are two openings and one hard constraint. The self-service opening is upgrade rather than greenfield. It covers about 946 cash-out-only sites. A further 223 sites already have both an ATM and a deposit machine, so they are close to an upgrade. The branch opening is BRD's own cashless template, stuck at 11 sites while headcount falls. The pitch is scaling a model BRD already built, not introducing a new one. The constraint is that BRD is funding software, not machines. This therefore has to be a managed-service, pay-per-transaction or hardware-as-a-service structure. It needs software content such as cash forecasting, monitoring and device management that fits the intangible and IT-services budget lines. On acceptance, a pure card-terminal volume pitch now pushes against a falling line while BRD switches on an account-to-account rail. Lead with multi-rail acceptance, terminal software and estate management. Do not lead with cutting the cash-in-transit bill, because BRD owns a third of its own CIT provider and a third of the saving comes off its own books. CIT One is a channel partner rather than a target.
signals.likelihood: High — the zone programme is funded and running, but the capex envelope is modest and software-weighted
signals.follow_up: Ask BRD directly for machines per site, deposit capability, age and OEM inside the 268 zones before sizing anything. Ask what equipment the 11 existing cashless agencies run, because that is the reference design. Track the MBA and cashless counts monthly, since either one moving is the trigger. Ask why the acquiring year-on-year comparison was removed, because the answer decides whether that is a threat or an opening. Cross-reference the 25 branches on shifted hours with a compulsory lunchtime closure against the deposit-machine list to build the most precise target list.
signals.product_review_why: About 946 cash-out-only sites need a deposit upgrade funded as a service, while acceptance needs multi-rail terminal software rather than more terminals.

signals.bank_theme: UniCredit Bank Romania — network cut to ~200 branches plus a dated 40-unit Prime refit
signals.signal: The half-year report filed to the Bucharest exchange on 25/08/2026 puts the branch count at 246 for the Bank and 249 for the Group at 30/06/2026. The comparable figures at 31/12/2025 were 265 and 268. That is 19 bank branches gone in six months, and down from about 300 when the merger completed in August 2025. UniCredit's own group divisional database gives the retail-only cut. Romania fell from 253 to 218 retail branches in the same six months, a drop of 35 units and the steepest fall in the CEE division. Group headcount in Romania is down to 4,261 from 4,475 (A1). A full tiled re-crawl of the bank's own locator on 27/08/2026 returns 1,207 ATM records at 1,143 distinct addresses. Decoded against UniCredit's own published filter taxonomy, only 114 of them (9.4%) can take a cash deposit. That leaves 1,093 machines that pay out but cannot take cash in, and 789 records are coded off-branch (A1). Twenty-seven branch records are flagged "SUCURSALĂ CU ATM — FĂRĂ NUMERAR LA CASIERIE", so cashless branches are already live here (A1). The commercial shape is clear. Operating expenses rose 39.9%, mainly because of the 4% turnover tax. Fixed assets are flat at RON 1.26bn, and a RON 431m ROBOR fine sits with no provision. A bank taxed on revenue before costs wants to rent equipment, not buy it (A1). The Prime affluent format is confirmed as a nine-market group programme launched 13/05/2026 with "exclusive Prime zones in selected branches". The Romanian prototype on Calea Dorobanţi opened in July with two Prime offices. The 2-to-40-units-in-a-year figure carried in the master row was not re-verified this cycle (A1). Digital onboarding is live and in-house. UniCredit Consumer Financing shipped a new video-identification and digital-onboarding solution with 82% automation on personal loans and 97% on point-of-sale loans (A1).

sources.text: UniCredit Bank S.A. — Half-Year Report as of 30 June 2026 (BVB filing)

signals.date: 25/08/2026 — H1-2026 report filed: 246 bank branches against 265 at 31/12/2025, 35 retail branches shed in six months
signals.implies: Cutting branches and staff at this pace, while the roughly 1,200-machine footprint stays flat, forces transactions onto self-service. 1,093 machines that cannot take cash in is the single largest measured deposit-automation gap at any Romanian bank, per machine. The 27 already-cashless branches are the immediate recycler candidates and the reference design for the rest. Two lanes are closed and should not be pitched. The central AML, KYC and analytics layer sits inside a group ten-year Google Cloud agreement, and consumer-finance onboarding is already built. The turnover tax settles the commercial structure: operating cost, lease and device-as-a-service. A third of the estate is run by Euronet and is covered separately below.
signals.likelihood: High — reduction is continuing quarter on quarter and the bank has a stated end-2026 network target
signals.follow_up: Re-pull the locator every cycle using a tiled crawl, because the endpoint silently cuts off at about 99 records per call. Treat a rising count of bank-note-acceptor codes as the early sign that a recycler programme has started. Find out who supplies the 114 existing deposit-capable units. Ask what happens to the ATMs at closing branches, and get the Prime fit-out specification before the format is frozen. Re-confirm the 2-to-40 Prime figure directly with the bank before using it.
signals.product_review_why: The largest per-machine deposit gap in Romania, to be leased or rented rather than bought, with cashless branches and Prime zones as the fit-out angle.

signals.bank_theme: Raiffeisen Romania / Garanti BBVA Romania — closing early October 2026 and a budgeted 2027 migration and rebranding programme
signals.signal: RBI's H1-2026 conference deck and its German-language release give a dated, budgeted integration plan. The purchase price is EUR 591m at 1.28x price-to-book. Regulatory filings and approvals run through Q3–Q4/2026. Closing is expected in Q4/2026, stated in German as "Anfang Oktober", meaning early October 2026. "Data migration and rebranding" run through 2027. The legal merger is expected in Q4/2027, and synergies start from 2028. The one-off integration cost is put at about EUR 70m, mainly in 2027. Against that, profit accretion is roughly EUR 90m in 2028, rising to EUR 130m by 2030, with about 200,000 new active customers. Garanti adds roughly EUR 4.3bn of assets to Raiffeisen's EUR 17.5bn, making RBI the third-largest bank in Romania (A1). RBI states that integration planning is already under way. The money is pre-funded. On 20/08/2026 Raiffeisen Bank Romania raised EUR 600m in a 6.4-year eurobond at 4.626%, with an order book above EUR 1.3bn. RBI has flagged a further EUR 400–600m of Romanian issuance in 2027 (A1). Garanti already runs its own eID onboarding, using a selfie, an NFC read of the Romanian electronic identity card chip and a liveness test. It launched on 14/04/2026 with no technology vendor named (A1). It also holds the ANCPI/OCPI online card-processing framework across every county land-registry office, with 473 contracts worth RON 6.4m (A2). Raiffeisen Romania's own vacancy posted on 31/08/2026 is a "Product Manager Cards Issuing and Merchant Acceptance", closing 23/09/2026. Issuing and acquiring are therefore being put under one owner just as the merger lands (A5).

signals.date: 31/07/2026 — RBI confirms closing expected early October 2026, data migration and rebranding across 2027, legal merger Q4/2027, EUR 70m one-off integration budget; EUR 600m pre-funding raised 20/08/2026

This is still missing after several passes and should be escalated. Time outreach to the integration PMO in the window between closing and Q1-2027, before the migration scope freezes and before the 23/10/2026 quiet period. Identify the vendor behind Garanti's NFC and liveness flow. Approach the new cards-issuing-and-merchant-acceptance product manager once in post.
signals.product_review_why: A funded 2027 migration re-fascias and re-keys every ATM, merges two acquiring books and TMS stacks, and re-issues two card portfolios.

signals.bank_theme: Raiffeisen Bank Romania — 1,211-device own estate and the sole large-bank RoPay acceptance gap
signals.signal: A cleaner pull of the bank's own locator feed on 27/08/2026 corrects both headline numbers in the master row. The feed returns 2,069 network points: 263 branches and 1,806 ATM entries. Excluding 595 Euronet-branded machines, the bank's own estate is 1,151 machines, not 1,211. That comprises 603 "Bancomat multifuncţional EUR", 548 plain "Bancomat" and 60 Smart Cashbox corporate deposit units. 1,151 matches exactly the 1,150 ATMs and multifunctional machines disclosed in the H1-2026 release. More importantly, by actual service listing only 534 of the 1,151 own machines offer cash deposit. So 617 machines, or 54%, are cash-out-only, not the 807 carried before. A further 69 machines named "multifunctional" list no deposit service at all, and are either mislabelled or degraded units (A1). Across the whole customer-facing set including Euronet devices, 1,031 of 1,806 cannot take a deposit (A1). The acceptance gap is unchanged and confirmed. On the RoPay scheme's own participant register, re-harvested 31/08/2026, Raiffeisen is still live with one feature, Alias phone-number payment. Six banks are live with eleven features, and VISTA Bank with twelve including NFC. That is the narrowest of any active participant. Meanwhile its acceptance estate grew from "over 42,000" POS terminals at 31/03/2026 to "nearly 45,000" at 30/06/2026, about 3,000 more in a quarter (A1, A5). Accessibility is downgraded as an opportunity. The bank states that voice guidance for cash withdrawal was extended nationally across ATMs and multifunctional machines in Q1-2026, so this is no longer a fleet-wide legal retrofit opportunity (A1).
signals.date: 31/08/2026 — RoPay participant register still shows Raiffeisen live on Alias only; locator re-pull 27/08/2026 corrects the own fleet to 1,151 machines with 617 cash-out-only
signals.implies: There are two open gaps at one bank, both software and enablement rather than hardware. A 45,000-terminal acquiring book has no merchant-side RoPay QR acceptance, while every large peer has it and the bank adds 3,000 terminals a quarter. Separately, 617 own machines cannot take a deposit, in a market where deposit capability is becoming the differentiator. The 69 machines carrying the multifunctional name with no listed deposit service are worth probing, as either a data-quality problem or degraded units. Correct any deck quoting 962 or 1,211 as Raiffeisen's machine count, because 1,151 is the reconciled figure. Everything here should be scoped so it can be folded into the Garanti integration programme rather than sold as a standalone fix.

signals.follow_up: Take a RoPay QR merchant-acceptance and terminal-software package to Raiffeisen merchant and acquiring. Frame it against the named peers, and time it to the new cards-and-acceptance product manager taking post. Ask the bank why 69 "multifunctional" units list no deposit service. Find out which of the 617 cash-out-only machines sit at branches, as those are the in-branch recycler candidates. Re-pull the feed after the October closing, because a changed count is itself the signal.
signals.product_review_why: A 45,000-terminal book lacks RoPay QR acceptance, and 617 own machines cannot take deposits.

signals.bank_theme: Banca Transilvania — IT/digital + cards platform
signals.signal: The H1-2026 interim report, filed on 21/08/2026, gives the fleet for the first time this cycle. It lists over 2,000 ATMs, of which 691 are multifunctional, plus 616 BT Express terminals. It also lists over 200,000 installed POS, 51,000 STAR partner locations, 8,800 e-commerce merchants and 8.5 million cards. That leaves roughly 1,300 machines that can only dispense cash. On BT's own disclosure, that is the largest single cash-automation gap in Romania (A1). The fleet is flat to slightly smaller while acceptance grows quickly. Multifunctional machines slipped from 696 to 691 and BT Express from 632 to 616 across the two quarters. Over the same period POS went from over 188,000 to over 200,000. This fits a self-service estate that is being kept running rather than refreshed. Changes this small over one quarter could also be routine churn (A1). The budget is verified and partly corrected. The AGM of 28/04/2026 approved RON 1,017.40m for 2026. The board-approved sub-lines that can be quoted are IT and cards RON 663.17m, digital RON 177.22m and buildings RON 105.94m. They also include machines RON 21.39m, security RON 9.79m and cash processing centre RON 7.88m. Together that is RON 39.06m, about EUR 7.8m, of confirmed hardware-related capex. The RON 51.92m retail-cards-hardware sub-line carried previously does not appear in the filing and must not be quoted (A1). Insourcing has gone further. Code Crafters' employees, contracts and development activity were transferred into the bank itself during H1-2026. Chat BT's AI resolution rate rose from 43% to 82% in a year. A front-end digital pitch is close to unsellable here (A1). Twelve agencies closed in six months, from 475 to 466 to 463 (A1). BT names third-party and outsourcing dependency as a board-level cyber risk, which raises the evidence bar on any managed-services proposal (A1). The data-protection authority fined BT on 02/07/2026 and ordered it to fix internal access controls (A1). In recruitment, both cards-domain enterprise-architecture roles came off the board in August. A Security Operations Centre engineer role and two data engineer roles went up (A5). BT continues to win municipal acquiring on Globalpay and every SNEP direct award (A2).

sources.text: Banca Transilvania — Financial results 30 June 2026 (BVB filing)

signals.date: 21/08/2026 — H1-2026 interim discloses 691 multifunctional of over 2,000 ATMs and 616 BT Express; the AGM-approved RON 1,017.4m programme is in execution through 2026
signals.implies: This is Romania's largest self-service and acceptance account. It is strongly profitable, with 21.96% capital adequacy and a 44.6% cost/income ratio. Transaction volume is up more than 17% while the machine fleet is flat to shrinking. That is the capacity squeeze that cash recyclers are designed to solve. Lead only with the board-approved lines: machines, cash processing centre and security. The realistic openings are the physical self-service layer, which an internal software team does not build. The other opening is the regulated back-office layer: identity verification, AML screening, transaction monitoring and privileged-access monitoring. A regulator has now ordered BT to strengthen privileged-access monitoring. Two qualifiers must be respected. BT's filings say "multifunctional", never "recycling", so do not claim that BT already runs recyclers. Also, the removal of the cards-architecture roles is not proof that they were filled.
signals.likelihood: High — the budget is approved and in execution, and the fleet disclosure is at the reporting date
signals.follow_up: Find out how many of the 691 multifunctional machines actually recycle notes, rather than only accept deposits, before pitching. Get the AGM supporting materials with the IT-and-cards sub-breakdown. The bank's site returns 403 to automated fetches, so go through investor relations. Check on LinkedIn whether the cards-domain architect role was filled or withdrawn, before assuming the bank is moving to execution. Get BT's DORA third-party register requirements. Document exit plans and the sub-outsourcing chain before making any managed-service proposal.
signals.product_review_why: A flat fleet under rising cash volume points to recyclers, and a regulator order opens the access-monitoring and AML back office.

signals.bank_theme: Romanian banking sector — RON 3.73bn competition fines reset the 2026-27 capex climate
signals.signal: The fines are now confirmed bank by bank from each institution's own filings, rather than from the announcement. Erste's H1-2026 interim report, Note 31, records that BCR received the Competition Council's investigation report on 06/04/2026. The fine announced in early June is 6.1875% of BCR's 2025 turnover, or RON 577,361,887. The reasoned decision had still not been served at the 30/07/2026 reporting date. RBI's semi-annual report shows that the preliminary report proposed the legal maximum of 10% of Raiffeisen Bank S.A.'s 2025 unconsolidated turnover. After hearings this was cut to 6.6%, on a retained finding of "excessive exchange of information". RBI also reports about RON 158m of additional Romanian taxes and RON 105m of penalties. UniCredit's own half-year report puts its exposure at RON 431m, with no IAS 37 provision booked. It says it will challenge the decision before the Court of Appeal within 30 days of communication, and seek suspension of enforcement. CEC Bank filed a formal current report on 08/06/2026 rejecting the decision outright. It has committed to appeal to the Bucharest Court of Appeal and, if necessary, to European courts. That filing states no amount and books no provision. The RON 332.98m figure carried in the master row could not be re-sourced this cycle (A1). Banca Transilvania carries RON 875.74m, plus RON 85.03m inherited for OTP Bank Romania (A1).

sources.text: Erste Group Interim Report H1 2026, Note 31 "Contingent liabilities — legal proceedings"

signals.date: 25/08/2026 — UniCredit's H1 filing confirms RON 431m carried unprovisioned; reasoned decision still pending, 30-day appeal clocks start on its communication
signals.implies: Every large Romanian bank is carrying a contested contingency at the same time. Each is worth between a quarter's profit and a full year's capex, plus years of legal cost. This lands exactly while branch refits and fleet decisions are being taken. Most banks have booked no provision, so the cash outflow is still ahead of them. The practical read is about commercial structure, not lost demand. Romanian procurement through 2026-27 will lean toward opex, lease and as-a-service models. It will also lean toward payback-period arguments rather than outright hardware purchases. Board-level appetite for proven compliance tools should rise as well, covering transaction monitoring, market-conduct surveillance and tamper-proof audit trails. All ten panel banks are named, so this is a sector-wide trigger for compliance spending.
signals.likelihood: High — provisioning and appeals run through 2026-27
signals.follow_up: Re-price every open Romanian proposition as a managed service with a stated payback period. Watch for publication of the Competition Council's reasoned decision. It starts the appeal clocks, and may carry compliance-programme obligations that are themselves the procurement trigger. Check CEC Bank's 30/09/2026 interim statements to see whether a provision is booked. Do not quote a CEC fine figure, because it is not in any CEC filing.
signals.product_review_why: Sector-wide fines push buying toward opex and as-a-service structures and raise appetite for compliance and monitoring tools.

signals.bank_theme: Romania — dual ATM + POS estate expansion
signals.signal: The acceptance mandate is the main driver, and it is still not verified at the primary source. Law 239/2025 is reported as published in Monitorul Oficial no. 1160 of 15/12/2025, and is reported to have amended OUG 193/2002. Under it, from 01/01/2026 essentially every entity registered with the Trade Register, including sole traders, must accept card or other modern electronic payment. The previous RON 50,000 turnover threshold is abolished. Accepting institutions must install a terminal within 30 days of a request. Reported fines are RON 20,000–50,000 for failing to provide electronic acceptance, and RON 5,000–7,500 for refusing a card payment. None of the article numbers, fine bands, the threshold repeal or the 30-day deadline could be confirmed against the Monitorul Oficial text this cycle. All three agents that tried failed to confirm them (A1, A5, A6). The circumstantial support is strong. Terminals reported by BNR rose by 161,396 in the second half of 2025, to 729,408, with 685,731 acceptance points and 28.63m active cards. ATMs are reported at 11,136, up 1,108. An ATM increase of roughly 11% in six months is too large to be organic in a mature market. It may reflect a scope change, such as newly counted independent deployers, and the BNR primary page could not be reached (A1, A5). The market is answering mainly with software rather than hardware. Banks have shipped their own softPOS apps, and BCR through Global Payments' GP tom is the only one sourced. SIBS Romania completed testing of POS Sharing on softPOS on 16/07/2026. TRANSFOND argues on its own site that a RoPay QR code can meet the acceptance obligation. That is a vendor's reading of a law, not a verified legal position (A1, A6).

sources.text: BNR payment indicators at 31/12/2025, as reported by AGERPRES

signals.date: 16/01/2026 — acceptance obligation reported in force from 01/01/2026; BNR H2-2025 indicators reported 17/05/2026 show +161,396 POS terminals in six months
signals.implies: Romania remains one of the few markets where both estates grow. The shape of the POS opportunity has changed, though, and it is not a windfall in terminal sales. Most newly-obliged merchants will be served by bank softPOS apps, shared terminals and agent networks. The revenue Printec can reach is therefore terminal management, certification, key injection, PCI services and HSM capacity. That capacity serves acquirers running mixed estates of software and hardware terminals. It also includes the attended and unattended hardware a phone cannot serve: branch kiosks, unattended payment, parking and fuel. The pitch to Romanian acquirers is estate complexity: several acceptance form factors managed on one platform. The terminal cost sits with the acquirer under the reported rules, so the buyer is the acquirer, not the merchant and not the bank.
signals.likelihood: High that a broadened acceptance obligation is in force; the specific thresholds, fine bands and the ATM growth direction are NOT established
signals.follow_up: Do the following before any client use. Retrieve Law 239/2025 from Monitorul Oficial or legislatie.just.ro. Confirm the amending act, the article, the fine bands, the threshold repeal and the 30-day installation deadline. Re-source the BNR figures from the primary statistical dataset. Check the ATM series methodology note for a scope change between June and December 2025. Then size the remaining unequipped merchant base against Trade Register counts.
signals.product_review_why: A universal acceptance mandate is met mostly by softPOS, so the reachable revenue is terminal management, certification, key injection and HSM capacity.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: Romania — instant euro payments: banks must receive by 09/01/2027 and send with Verification of Payee by 09/07/2027
signals.signal: The timetable is now settled at the Official Journal text, after two cycles of conflicting corrections. Under Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Art. 5a(8), as inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/886, payment service providers (PSPs) in non-euro Member States face two dates. They must offer receiving of instant euro credit transfers by 09/01/2027. They must offer sending by 09/07/2027. The 09/04/2027 date applies only to electronic-money and payment institutions, not to banks. The 09/01/2027 date also brings charges parity, so an instant transfer may cost no more than the equivalent non-instant one. 09/07/2027 brings mandatory Verification of Payee, the check that the payee name matches the IBAN (A3). Romania has already legislated. On 12/02/2026 the Government adopted an emergency ordinance amending Law 231/2015. It requires providers to settle within a maximum of 10 seconds, regardless of day or hour. It requires the service through all payment-initiation channels used by clients, and mandatory Verification of Payee. It also adds a duty the baseline missed: periodic reporting of fee levels and the percentage of rejected transactions to the European authorities. The ordinance also gives payment and e-money institutions access to designated payment systems. The ordinance number could not be confirmed, and "OUG 5/2026" must not be cited (A3). Salt Bank ran the first local implementation of instant euro over TRANSFOND's RO-TIPS on 14/01/2026. It was built in about three months with TRANSFOND and Montran. Montran's own boilerplate in that release claims anti-fraud and QR products alongside instant payments, so it competes for the fraud layer too (A3, A6). Montran also holds BNR's ReGIS and SaFIR maintenance. It supplied the central RoPay and instant-payments solution behind UniCredit's 02/02/2026 go-live. Ten banks are live on RoPay, with BRCI still in implementation (A6).
signals.date: 09/01/2027 — Romanian banks must receive instant euro credit transfers and meet charges parity; 09/07/2027 — sending plus mandatory Verification of Payee
signals.implies: The first hard date is roughly four months away. The budget for it is therefore either already committed, or the bank is late. The commit window for the 09/07/2027 sending and Verification-of-Payee step is now, from Q3-2026 to Q1-2027. The expensive words in the Romanian ordinance are "all payment-initiation channels". Internet banking, mobile, branch and file-based corporate channels each need instant payment plus name-matching. The new rejected-transaction and fee reporting duty is a straightforward transaction-monitoring and regulatory-reporting requirement. The sellable layer is what Montran does not claim. That includes instant sanctions and AML screening, deep transaction monitoring and HSM key capacity. It also includes Verification-of-Payee name-matching tuning, channel work and managed cut-over. The ATM and kiosk side matters too, where the free-amount bill and instant rails meet. Expect to displace existing suppliers rather than simply add to them. The size of the remediation market is not established. The circulating figure that "only four or five of about thirty Romanian PSPs are live" has no source and must not be used.
signals.likelihood: High — these are fixed, directly applicable EU dates with national implementing law already adopted
signals.follow_up: Get the ordinance from Monitorul Oficial. Establish its number, the sanction levels, the competent authority and whether BNR holds any deferral power. The deferral point materially changes the pipeline. Get TRANSFOND's RO-TIPS participant list and onboarding calendar, so the unsourced readiness figure can be replaced with a real count. Find out which banks bought Montran and which built their own solution. Approach BRCI ahead of its RoPay go-live.
signals.product_review_why: Hard 2027 dates for instant euro and Verification of Payee, with screening, monitoring and reporting duties that Montran does not cover.

signals.bank_theme: Euronet Romania — entrenched independent off-site deployer
signals.signal: Two banks' own live locator feeds now size Euronet's Romanian position precisely. Both were re-pulled on 27/08/2026. At UniCredit, 401 of 1,207 ATM records are titled "ATM UniCredit Euronet", which is 33% of the estate. Of those 401, 398 are coded off-branch, and none has a bank-note acceptor, so the whole Euronet tranche is cash-out-only. UniCredit's own April-2025 reciprocal-ATM announcement with Alpha Bank carried a footnote excluding Euronet machines from the fee-parity arrangement (A1). At Raiffeisen, 595 of the 1,806 customer-facing ATM entries are Euronet-branded: 414 withdrawal-only and 181 multifunctional. Every one of the 181 non-EUR multifunctional deposit-capable devices in the whole feed is Euronet's (A1). One correction is important. The claim that Raiffeisen's own fleet is managed by Euronet is unproven. The only evidence is a Euronet Q4-2003 SEC presentation listing Raiffeisen Romania under ATM outsourcing network participation. Euronet is not mentioned once in RBI's Q2/2026 deck or semi-annual report. Presence in the locator shows customer access, not outsourced management. The "600 ATMs and 2,700 EFTPOS" figures could not be verified anywhere (A1). At group level Euronet's estate is essentially flat, at 57,071 active ATMs on 30/06/2026 against 56,760 a year earlier, about +1%. Its growth now comes from card issuing and acquiring rather than from taking over bank fleets. It named no new European ATM-outsourcing win on its Q2 call (A6). It carries about USD 935m of ATM cash risk at the seasonal peak. It is also running a sustained ATM-as-a-Service total-cost-of-ownership campaign aimed at bank CFOs, most recently on 03/08/2026 (A6).
signals.date: 04/08/2026 — Euronet Q2 filings show a flat 57,071-ATM estate and no named European outsourcing win; UniCredit and Raiffeisen locators re-pulled 27/08/2026 confirm 401 and 595 Euronet devices inside their networks
signals.implies: The Romanian off-site lane is largely already taken. Two top-six banks extend their fleets through Euronet rather than through an operator partnership. Any pure off-site proposal will therefore be compared with a network the cardholder often uses for free. Two findings do improve Printec's competitive position. First, every Euronet device inside both banks' networks is cash-out-only. An off-site outsourced fleet cannot deliver deposit capability by its nature, so deposit and recycling is uncontested ground. Second, the argument that Euronet's ATM economics are collapsing does not hold, and must not be put in front of a bank CFO. The margin dip is a non-cash accounting effect of the CoreCard purchase, and cash ATM profitability rose. The honest counter to the outsourcing pitch is total cost of ownership on an owned estate. That means multivendor software, telemetry, cash forecasting and field services. Sell it on control of brand, fee and customer relationship. Attach a named cash-in-transit partner, so the gap on transferring cash risk is visibly closed.
signals.likelihood: Medium — no near-term regulatory event was re-verified this cycle; the PSD3 Art. 38 registration regime for independent deployers carried in the master row was NOT re-confirmed in this cycle's PSD3 evidence
signals.follow_up: Model off-site unit economics against the Euronet zero-fee benchmark before pitching any Romanian off-site structure. Do not repeat the 2003 outsourcing framing. Do not claim that Raiffeisen's own fleet is Euronet-managed until it is established. Find the term and start date of the UniCredit–Euronet contract, so the renewal can be contested. Rebut the Datos Insights study that Euronet cites across its whole campaign, because rebutting the study rebuts the campaign.
signals.product_review_why: Euronet's ATM-as-a-service campaign is countered with owned-estate services, and its cash-out-only fleet leaves deposit and recycling open.

signals.bank_theme: Romania — non-bank self-service and agent networks are substituting for rural ATMs and for card terminals
signals.signal: Three national networks are scaling at once, and all three now handle cash. PayPoint Romania launched cash withdrawal at assisted POS terminals with Mastercard, capped at RON 500 per transaction. It is live at over 14,000 partner locations and publicly targeted to reach 26,000 points during 2026. It is aimed at rural communities where the nearest ATM is tens of kilometres away. PayPoint runs more than 35,000 assisted terminals, over 75% of them card-enabled, on more than 10.5 million transactions a month. It is targeting 50,000 by 2028. SelfPay confirmed on 21/05/2026 that it runs more than 13,000 active self-service payment stations across more than 3,000 localities. It opened 277 new locations in the first half of May alone. It is bond-funded toward roughly 19,000 stations by end-2026. Its "Rapid Transition Program" now also gives local retailers an optional bank card POS terminal. Mobile Distribution, operator of the Un-Doi platform, obtained a BNR payment-institution authorisation announced 27/05/2026. It covers about RON 4bn of annual transactions across 2,500 terminals and 11,000 partner locations, and states nationwide expansion as its strategy (A6). The same operators are winning public buyers. Salt Bank is the framework holder, with SelfPay as terminal operator. Together they have won unattended-terminal collection at Bucharest Sector 6 (RON 6.11m), Timişoara (RON 1.14m) and Braşov Lot 3 (A2). Acquiring is also cutting out the middleman. Netopia was licensed as a payment institution active from 10/07/2026. EuPlateşc connected directly to TRANSFOND's RoPay infrastructure on 24/08/2026 as a "Processor", with a payment-facilitator rollout stated for autumn 2026 (A5, A6).

sources.text: PayPoint Romania and Mastercard — cash withdrawal at assisted POS terminals

signals.date: 24/08/2026 — EuPlateşc connects directly to TRANSFOND's RoPay rail; PayPoint's cash-at-POS rollout to 26,000 points runs through 2026
signals.implies: Cash at the counter of 26,000 rural shops is the cheapest substitute yet for a rural ATM. It weakens the business case for cash-dispensing machines in exactly the places banks were least willing to fund them. The Romanian ATM pitch therefore has to move away from rural coverage. It should move toward high-value deposit automation and recycling in urban branches, where cash at POS cannot compete. On acceptance, a merchant paid by QR code or phone number needs no card terminal at all. Terminal management must therefore be sold as multi-rail rather than card-only. These three operators are also among the largest managed-services targets in the country. They run a 35,000-terminal estate, a 13,000-station estate heading for 19,000, and a 2,500-terminal estate in mid-expansion. None has a publicly named device-management or field-service supplier. Approaching them as customers for telemetry, remote monitoring and field service is a better use of effort than competing with them for consumer transactions.
signals.likelihood: High — the 26,000-location cash-withdrawal rollout, the 19,000-station target and the payment-facilitator launch are all publicly committed for 2026
signals.follow_up: Find out who makes, services and manages the PayPoint, SelfPay and Un-Doi estates today. That answer is both the displacement target and the managed-services pitch. Find out whether any of these stations take cash deposits, which would put them in direct competition with bank recyclers. Check whether Verifone and Castles firmware in Romania already shows a RoPay QR code. If it does not, that is a live product gap. Track whether PayPoint actually reaches 26,000 points in 2026, because that number decides the effect on rural ATMs.
signals.product_review_why: Three large non-bank estates need telemetry and field service, terminals must go multi-rail, and the ATM case shifts to urban deposit automation.

signals.bank_theme: Romania — domestic cash-automation and kiosk incumbents, plus an unconsolidated State Treasury counting-machine estate
signals.signal: Two findings together define where Printec can and cannot win on the ground. The first is that the channel is partly blocked. ROPECO Bucureşti is part of the Romanian Business Consult group. It published on 28/04/2026 that its general director was honoured at the Glory EMEA Distributor event, for a partnership of over three decades. That places Glory's Romanian EMEA distributor relationship with ROPECO, a firm that sells branch automation, cash processing, recyclers and self-service nationally. A Glory-led branch cash-automation pitch to a Romanian bank will collide with the vendor's own partner. Alongside it, Eutron Invest Romania distributes RIBAO, GUNNEBO and OBERTHUR CASH PROTECTION. It runs 27 service centres with national coverage and over 3,000 clients, and supplies banknote deposit and recycling systems. It has already delivered a self-check-in kiosk inside Alpha Bank Romania's head office, which is a Printec footprint account. EasyPay Romania makes its own self-service terminals at roughly EUR 10m revenue. It runs over 1,100 payment terminals, and is scaling a digital-reception product toward about 100 clinic installations in 2026 (A6). The second finding is that the public cash-equipment estate is entirely unconsolidated. The regional tax directorate in Craiova buys counting-machine maintenance on five separate county frameworks, totalling RON 649,228, from one micro-vendor, CA.DA GRUPP. The Cluj-Napoca directorate published fourteen below-threshold direct awards between 04/08 and 25/08/2026, every one to Eutron Invest, totalling RON 25,463.94. They cover repair of low-cost RIBAO BCS 160 banknote counters at named treasury offices. Each call is priced separately, between RON 274 and RON 5,852 (A2 — flagged unverified by A6, which could not re-retrieve the notice IDs).
signals.date: 25/08/2026 — latest of fourteen Cluj treasury counting-machine direct awards in three weeks; ROPECO's Glory distributor position published 28/04/2026
signals.implies: Printec cannot lead with Glory in Romania, and cannot win on national service coverage alone. Eutron already has 27 service centres, and is inside at least one Printec footprint account on kiosks. The differentiators that remain are bank-grade security, cash handling, PCI compliance and multivendor software. Unit price against a local manufacturer that makes and sells its own machines is not a differentiator. The genuine opening is the fragmentation itself. The Romanian State Treasury runs an estate of cheap counters with no service contract and no national framework holder, repaired call-by-call by micro-vendors. A single national managed-service framework with the tax administration would cover service levels, a spares pool and uptime reporting. With a phased fleet upgrade behind it, none of the incumbents could match that offer, and it would consolidate dozens of micro-awards. The money involved is small. Even so, it is the only directly matching cash-automation demand visible in Romanian public procurement.
signals.likelihood: High that these firms appear against Printec in Romanian bank kiosk, deposit or cash-processing bids in the next 6-12 months; the fragmented treasury pattern most likely persists absent a consolidating bidder
signals.follow_up: Find out through NCR and Sesami whether Printec has a competing recycler line it can lead with in Romania instead of Glory, and map ROPECO's installed bank base. Ask Printec Romania whether it has met Eutron in a bank teller-recycler or kiosk bid, and defend Alpha Bank Romania on kiosks. Re-source the fourteen Cluj direct awards by hand before any figure is used externally. Then draft an unsolicited national counting-machine managed-service proposition for the tax administration. Confirm that Romanian procurement law allows below-threshold buys to be centralised.
signals.product_review_why: Local recycler and kiosk incumbents block Glory-led pitches, while a fragmented treasury counting-machine estate invites a national service framework.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: Romania — chip electronic ID becomes the onboarding standard; national wallet due Dec-2026
signals.signal: Adoption has moved from announcement to live use at three banks. BRD enabled the new Romanian Electronic Identity Card with chip for remote customer identification and mobile-app activation in Q2-2026. It flags "eID accepted for onboarding" as a new customer journey, clearly on the mobile channel. It makes no claim of branch or self-service chip reading. Garanti BBVA Romania went further and earlier. On 14/04/2026 it launched in-app onboarding using a selfie, an NFC read of the eID chip and a liveness test. This supports fully remote account opening and in-app lending. It states that data is taken directly from the document without image processing, and cites over 1.3 million electronic ID cards issued. No technology vendor is named, so there is no publicly entrenched incumbent. UniCredit Consumer Financing introduced its own new video-identification and digital-onboarding solution in H1-2026. BCR reports over 40% of mortgages taken on a fully digital flow, against 17% a year earlier, on more than a million retail products sold digitally (A1). The technical baseline is now testable. The Commission published EUDI Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework v3.0.0 on 23/07/2026. It adds a Relying Party Services concept and wallet-to-wallet interactions. It also requires trust-anchor retrieval from both Trusted Lists and Lists of Trusted Entities. It adds a Functional Conformance Assessment Framework with a live public test catalogue (A3). certSIGN, Romania's incumbent qualified trust service provider, has published on the banking angle roughly every two to three weeks since April 2026. That includes EUDI Wallet as a strong-customer-authentication mechanism for the financial sector on 21/08/2026. It also confirmed interoperability at ETSI Plugtests in July 2026 (A6). It holds the Ministry of Defence multi-technology smart-card framework at a RON 9.08m ceiling, and leads the public-sector e-signature award stream (A2, A6).

sources.text: EUDI Wallet ARF v3.0.0 release, European Commission

signals.date: 23/07/2026 — EUDI ARF v3.0.0 published with a live conformance test catalogue; Garanti's eID/NFC onboarding live since 14/04/2026 and BRD's since Q2-2026
signals.implies: A greenfield digital-onboarding pitch is effectively closed at Romania's tier-1 banks. They have built it themselves, in-house and on the national chip identity. The lane that opens instead is anchored on the chip and on the wallet. It covers NFC document reading and chip authentication, chip-reading branch and kiosk hardware, and relying-party certificate and key management. These can now be tested objectively against a published conformance framework, before any acceptance duty applies. One competitive point matters. certSIGN is the local provider that actually holds the certificates. A Romanian bank can therefore source identity, signature and preservation from it directly, and never run a separate eKYC tender. The correct position is orchestration and customer journey that consume a Romanian qualified provider's certificates. Bundle this with AML and monitoring, so the conversation covers compliance as a whole rather than signatures only. The Garanti stack is the nearest concrete decision, because the keep-or-replace choice falls inside the 2027 Raiffeisen integration.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high — the technical framework and the bank-side adoption are both live; the Romanian national wallet date carried in the master row was NOT re-confirmed this cycle
signals.follow_up: Re-base the eKYC stack on ARF 3.0.0 credential formats, relying-party registration certificates and the presentation protocol. Score an EUDI acceptance-readiness assessment against the published conformance test cases. Confirm whether certSIGN is a partner or a competitor before approaching any Romanian bank on onboarding. Attach chip-reading capability to the CEC digital-agency and UniCredit Prime specifications. Find the normative act that names Romania's national wallet operator and relying-party registrar. Note that the December-2026 deadline was not re-verified this cycle.

signals.bank_theme: Romania — DORA and AML supervisory evidence is becoming the gate on Printec's own managed-services sales
signals.signal: Two supervisory cycles now bear on whether Printec can be bought, rather than on what it sells. The first is the DORA Register of Information. 31/12/2026 is the reference date, not the deadline. Financial entities file to their national supervisor on that supervisor's own earlier cut-off, typically in February or March 2027. The supervisor then forwards the filing to the European supervisory authorities by 31/03/2027. The authorities do not publish the national cut-offs, so BNR must be watched separately. Only subcontractors that effectively underpin ICT services supporting critical or important functions are reportable (A3). The second is threat-led penetration testing, a controlled attack by hired testers, under DORA Articles 26-27. It is specified by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190. That regulation covers scope, method, internal testers, remediation phases and supervisory cooperation for mutual recognition. Scope is set at entity level and covers critical functions end to end. For a retail bank, that pulls in the ATM channel, the acquiring and terminal estate and the monitoring layer (A3). The Romanian hook is explicit. Banca Transilvania's H1-2026 risk narrative names growing dependency on third-party providers and outsourced services as a board-level risk, amid a persistent cyber threat landscape. At the same time, the bank has pulled software development in-house (A1). Alongside these, AMLA's provisional list of entities for direct supervision is expected at the end of September 2026. National supervisors submitted their input by 15/08/2026. Harmonised AML sanction standards are heading to the Commission for adoption ahead of the 10/07/2027 application date (A3).

sources.text: EBA — FAQ on reporting of registers of information under DORA

signals.date: 31/12/2026 — reference date for the Register of Information; Romanian banks file to BNR on its own earlier cut-off, expected Feb–Mar 2027, and BNR forwards by 31/03/2027
signals.implies: This is a sales-readiness cost rather than a bank capex line, and it cuts both ways. Every Romanian bank client will ask Printec for register-grade data on itself during Q4-2026 and Q1-2027. That means the legal entity identifier, service-type classification, where data is stored, the subcontracting chain and an exit plan. Supplying a clean pre-formatted pack is a cheap way to defend renewals. Failing to supply it is a common trigger for re-tendering an ICT service. BT has already said in public that third-party dependency is a board-level risk. Expect DORA-grade evidence to be a gating requirement there on any managed-service proposal, not an optional extra. On threat-led testing, Printec must be contractually ready to support a designated client's red-team window. That includes the disclosure and cooperation terms the standard sets out. Mutual recognition means a group-level test at Erste or RBI can pull Printec-operated estates in several countries into one scope at once.
signals.likelihood: Certain as an annual statutory cycle; high for designated entities on threat-led testing
signals.follow_up: Build a standard DORA Register of Information data pack for Printec's own entity. Send it to every Romanian bank client during Q4-2026, ahead of their February-to-March 2027 filing. Monitor BNR specifically for its 2027 entity-level notice, expected in January or February 2027. Ask BNR which entities it has designated for threat-led testing, and in which window. Check whether existing Printec contracts with Romanian banks carry the cooperation and disclosure clauses that testing requires. Get BT's third-party register requirements and critical-provider criteria before pitching anything outsourced there.
signals.product_review_why: DORA register and threat-led testing evidence now gates whether banks can keep or buy Printec managed services.

signals.bank_theme: NLB Komercijalna banka — group ATM and cash-deposit upgrade against 102 non-deposit ATMs

Only 105 dispense euro, so 200 machines cannot dispense EUR in a market that uses euro heavily (A1). The branch-level flags are just as precise. There are 129 branches, of which only 52 have a 24/7 self-service zone, so 77 do not. In addition, 88 branches have a merchant cash-deposit device, and only 51 are marked accessible to people with disabilities (A1). There is a dated trigger inside the window. On 26/08/2026 the bank re-published its four ATM-capability location lists, generated the day before. Every count in them already lags the live API: 183 versus 203 deposit-capable, 234 versus 303 QR-payment and 117 versus 131 merchant-deposit. In other words, capability is being switched on machine by machine right now (A1). The fastest-growing device class is not the ATM. Merchant cash-deposit units rose from 72 at 31/12/2025 to 95 on 27/08/2026, an increase of 31.9% in eight months. Over the same period the ATM count moved only from 299 to 305 (A1). Branches keep shrinking, from 162 at end-2024 to 139 at end-2025. There were 129 at 30/06/2026. The 305 machines cover 132 towns, against 84 towns for the branches, so 49 towns have a machine and no branch behind it (A1). The 2025 accounts show capital spending in progress up 15.7%. NLB Group's H1-2026 results, published 06/08/2026, put the Serbian bank at EUR 66.0m profit. Its cost/income ratio is 44.2%, against a group 2030 goal of 'low 40s'. The 77 branches with no 24/7 self-service zone are a repeatable per-site package. signals.signal: The 21-page official decision was read in full this cycle, so the detail is now confirmed. NBS Executive Board decision no. 14 of **07/05/2026** was published in Službeni glasnik RS 43/2026. It enters into force on the eighth day after publication, and it fully repeals the 2019/2020/2021 regime (A1, A3). · Point 33 sets two transition periods for institutions already running video identification. They must align their business and internal acts **within six months** of entry into force. They must adapt their **technical solutions within one year** (A1). · Point 30 adds a requirement the master row missed. Any institution planning to offer video identification must notify NBS **at least 30 days before starting**. It must submit internal acts, proof of staff training, and the list of document-issuing states its staff are trained on. It must also submit evidence of premises, and a full description and prior assessment of the technical solution. Before that period ends, it must give NBS staff a **live real-time demonstration of the entire process for every customer category** (A1). · The decision creates two modes. In the direct mode, an employee takes part in a live call. In the indirect mode, supervision and verification can happen before the relationship begins. In exceptional cases they can happen within 72 hours afterwards, under enhanced monitoring and transaction limits (A1). · The demand pattern has changed, and this is the most material change this cycle. NBS Q2-2026 data show 168,733 distance contracts concluded electronically, up 25.9% year on year. Of these, **129,728 were fully electronic (+40.6%), but only 39,005 used video identification — down 6.5% year on year, the first fall on record**. In the 2025 base year, video identification was the faster-growing leg at +75.4% (A4). Loan contracts drove the growth at +82.3%, while account openings fell 24.5% (A4).

sources.text: NBS — Odluka o video-identifikaciji, Sl. glasnik RS 43/2026 (official PDF)

signals.date: ~27/11/2026 — derived six-month deadline to align business and internal acts; ~27/05/2027 derived technical-solution deadline · decision adopted 07/05/2026, gazette publication date NOT confirmed (see NOTES) · 24/08/2026 NBS Q2-2026 data show video-ID contracts falling for the first time
signals.implies: Every Serbian institution running video identification now has a fixed date by which its technical stack must meet a prescriptive standard. The standard covers document authenticity, liveness detection (a check that a real person is present), qualified electronic timestamping and end-to-end encryption. It also requires a continuous connection to a reliable time source, image and sound quality thresholds, and full session recording. On top of that comes the live demonstration to the regulator. Most banks buy a specification of this kind rather than build it. · The commercial case is stronger this cycle. Staffed video identification is now in decline, while fully automated onboarding grows 40% a year. The pitch should therefore be a migration business case, not only a compliance one. The new unattended route is what removes the limit set by staffed hours. · AikBank is the clearest single case, because its online account opening depends on a staffed call limited to weekday and Saturday daytime hours. Target selection still matters. A rival holds the digital-onboarding stack at AikBank, and the electronic-signature layer at Banca Intesa is the state service. The open ground is therefore OTP Srbija, NLB Komercijalna and Raiffeisen.
signals.likelihood: High — a dated statutory obligation on a live channel across the whole sector
signals.follow_up: **Confirm the Službeni glasnik RS 43/2026 publication date before quoting any deadline to a customer.** Both dates come from the NBS filename (20260519), not from the decision text. Build one Serbian compliance-by-design package, mapped clause by clause to the decision. It should include the point-30 notification pack and the live NBS demonstration. Take it to OTP Srbija, NLB Komercijalna and Raiffeisen first, then to AikBank. Lead the commercial case on the video-identification decline against fully-electronic growth, not on compliance alone.
signals.product_review_why: A dated rulebook forces every Serbian video-identification stack to be rebuilt to a prescribed standard, with a compliance pack for the regulator.

signals.bank_theme: Serbia — CReM electronic bills of exchange: statutory retail deadline 30/11/2026
signals.signal: NBS's Annual Financial Stability Report 2025, published 05/08/2026, sets out a dated compliance timeline for the Central Register of Electronic Bills of Exchange (CReM). A bill of exchange is a written order to pay a set sum. · The register went live on **01/12/2025**. From that date banks must enable electronic bills of exchange for legal persons and entrepreneurs. From **01/06/2026 banks must accept electronic bills of exchange as collateral**. From **30/11/2026 the system must be available to natural persons**. · Electronic bills are signed with a **remote qualified electronic signature via the state ConsentID app with multi-factor authentication**. A bill can neither exist nor be transferred outside the register. · NBS says clearly that the phasing needs gradual adjustment of information systems, internal procedures and control mechanisms in banks. It also needs revised procedures for accepting and activating collateral, and stronger IT security. Unlike the bank-by-bank platform models used elsewhere in the region, CReM is a single central register run by NBS, so every bank connects to the same interface (A4). · There is supporting context on the same qualified-signature stack. OTP banka Srbija's August-2026 app release already uses ConsentID to sign loans above RSD 1.2m, so at least one bank has the retail capability in production (A1).

sources.text: NBS — Annual Financial Stability Report 2025, Text box 4

signals.date: 30/11/2026 — statutory date by which the electronic bill-of-exchange register must be available to natural persons · 05/08/2026 NBS Financial Stability Report published setting out the phasing · 01/06/2026 banks already required to accept e-bills as collateral
signals.implies: A legal deadline three months away forces every Serbian bank to open remote qualified electronic signature and identity flows to **retail** customers, not only to companies. This is the same capability the video-identification rulebook demands, on a tighter timetable. NBS itself names the work: information-system adjustment, revised collateral procedures and IT-security hardening. · Banks that already run a qualified electronic-signature stack for retail will meet the deadline. Those that do not have a buying decision to make in the next quarter. The two deadlines should be sold as one Serbian identity-and-signature programme, rather than as two separate compliance projects.
signals.likelihood: High — a fixed statutory date less than three months away, with bank-by-bank readiness the only variable
signals.follow_up: Map which Serbian banks already have a qualified electronic-signature stack for retail customers and which do not. Do this before the end of September 2026, because the banks without one are the buyers. Lead with qualified electronic signature plus ConsentID interoperability. Bundle it with the Gazette 43/2026 technical-adaptation work as a single programme.
signals.product_review_why: A legal deadline makes Serbian banks open qualified electronic-signature and identity flows to retail customers.

signals.bank_theme: ProCredit Bank Serbia — live fraud-monitoring procurement, and a cash-at-POS model that displaces ATMs

Beograd published an invitation to tender for a **fraud-monitoring application, procurement reference 878/26**, on its own supplier-tender page. The **submission deadline was 24/08/2026**, three days before the page was re-checked on 27/08/2026. Documentation is issued only on request from srb.nabavka@procredit-group.com, so anyone not on the invitation list is invisible (A1). · The tender also shows that this bank buys fraud tooling from the market, rather than taking it from the group's own IT arm. · Second, ProCredit Serbia is actively **replacing ATM withdrawal with merchant cashback**. Its live 'Brzi keš' service lets customers take up to RSD 5,000 in cash from any merchant running a ProCredit terminal marked with the scheme sticker. The purchase amount is expressly irrelevant. Even so, Serbia contributed EUR 6.8m of the group's EUR 38.5m H1-2026 result (A1).
