signals.bank_theme: Serbia — SEPA / instant-payments wave
signals.signal: The regulator has now confirmed the shape of this precisely, and it is narrower than the master row assumed. NBS's own FAQ, re-read 27/08/2026, states that Serbia became the 41st SEPA member on **22/05/2025**. It also states that **18 of 19 banks** went live on SEPA Credit Transfer on 4 and 5 May 2026. · Serbian banks are only in the initial phase. All of them take part as **indirect** participants, routing through correspondent parents abroad, and **there is still no Serbian date for SEPA Instant Credit Transfer** (A3). Raiffeisen's own explainer confirms the mechanics from the bank side. It is credit transfer only, with no 24/7 operation. It runs on working-day cycles with settlement no later than next day, and a 13:00 cut-off set by its Austrian parent (A1, A5). · OTP's customer article is blunter still. Euro payments from Serbia to SEPA banks remain international payment traffic, executed under clearer rules rather than as domestic SEPA payments (A1). · There is a new competitive fact. **ASEE announced on 16/06/2026 that it completed SEPA implementation for 14 Serbian banks, all going live on the same day**. It combined its own gateway platform with changes inside the banks' core systems (A6). · The forward-looking evidence is now in the central bank's own procurement plan v9 of 26/08/2026. That plan carries **accession to SEPA and TIPS**, and a payment-systems software upgrade to link NBS infrastructure to the EU's (A4). NBS separately plans an **ISO 20022 migration in 2026** of the Serbia–Bosnia–Montenegro FX clearing platform. That platform is a nameable set of 20 banks plus three central banks, which currently exchange SWIFT MT messages (A4). · Meanwhile the domestic instant rail keeps growing on its own. There were 34,459,117 instant transactions in Q2-2026, up 30.7% year on year and worth RSD 442bn. July 2026 alone carried 11.3m payments at a one-second average execution time, with three banks carrying about 64% of value (A4). Serbia is aligning to PSD2, not PSD3, and three draft laws went to consultation in late May and early June 2026 (A3).

sources.text: NBS — SEPA u Republici Srbiji: najčešća pitanja i odgovori

signals.date: 26/08/2026 — NBS 2026 procurement plan v9 adopted carrying SEPA/TIPS accession and the payment-systems software upgrade · 16/06/2026 ASEE delivered SEPA for 14 Serbian banks in one same-day go-live · SEPA credit transfer live since 05/05/2026, no instant-payment date exists
signals.implies: The work that can be bought in Serbia over the next 12 to 18 months is the move from indirect to direct scheme participation. That means clearing and settlement connectivity, ISO 20022 messaging, and screening at scheme service levels. · Add the three-country FX clearing platform's move off the SWIFT MT format. It forces every one of those 20 banks to remap message flows, retest reconciliation, and retune sanctions and money-laundering screening on richer data fields. That is integration, testing and tuning work, not licence sales. · Two disciplines follow. Do not sell against a Serbian instant-euro deadline, because the regulator confirms that none exists. Do not sell PSD3 or payment-regulation compliance into Serbia either. The country is a full regulatory cycle behind, aligning to PSD2 and to the 2024 EU instant-payments amendment. · One competitive fact has to be absorbed. A rival has just taken a same-day core-payments change live at 14 Serbian banks. It will be first in the room for every adjacent payments project for the next two years.

Put the same question to the Bosnian and Montenegrin central banks, so one regional offer covers all three. Pitch cash forecasting, transaction monitoring and screening into the payments-modernisation budgets those banks have just opened, rather than head-to-head core-payments displacement. Track the Official Gazette for adoption of the amended Law on Payment Services.

signals.bank_theme: Serbia — cash-in, not cash-out, is where the ATM channel is growing
signals.signal: The Q2-2026 regulator series, published 19/08/2026, moves every number in the master row and strengthens the argument. · The national estate reached **3,412 ATMs and 195,121 POS terminals at 30/06/2026**. That is up from 3,336 ATMs and 187,957 POS terminals at Q1-2026, and from 3,196 and 177,185 a year earlier. The year-on-year change is **+216 ATMs (+6.8%) and +17,936 POS (+10.1%)**. Add 6,278 virtual points of sale (+21.4%) and 13.7m cards issued to 7.1m users (A1, A4, A5). That +6.8% is **the highest year-on-year ATM growth in the whole published NBS series back to Q1-2016** (A4). · Deposits are moving faster than withdrawals. **ATM cash-deposit transactions reached 3,406,129 worth RSD 173.9bn in Q2-2026, up 31.9% by count and 53.6% by value year on year. Withdrawals grew just 4.5% by count and 15.7% by value.** Deposit value is now 31.5% of withdrawal value, up from 23.7% a year earlier. Deposits are 11% of ATM transactions by count, but 24% by value (A1, A4, A5). Cash withdrawal at the branch teller **fell 3.9%** (A5). · On the wider cash series, deposit value has run at 1.4 to 1.5 times withdrawal value since 2024. In H1-2026 withdrawal value was flat year on year at +0.4%, while withdrawal count fell 5.8%. So cash out is no longer growing even in nominal terms, while cash in still is (A4). Card purchases at Serbian merchants hit 237.9m in Q2-2026, up 19.3% year on year and more than double the Q2-2022 figure (A1, A4). · The branch base is going the other way. NBS told the press in May 2026 that bank organisational units fell from 1,558 in March 2021 to **1,288 in March 2026**. That is a cut of 17.3%, with sector headcount down to 21,732 (A4). Bank-level disclosures confirm the same shift independently. Some 86% of Banca Intesa's dinar deposits and 97% of Raiffeisen's Premium-segment cash transactions already happen on machines (A1).

sources.text: NBS — Payment transactions in the acceptance network (trans_prihvatna_mreza.xlsx)

signals.date: 19/08/2026 — both NBS workbooks updated with Q2-2026, superseding the Q1-2026 figures of 3,336 ATMs and 187,957 POS · 26/08/2026 NBS press release on card growth · next quarterly refresh expected ~November 2026
signals.implies: This is the single set of numbers that supports every Serbian self-service proposal, and it should be the first slide in all of them. The claim is now stronger. Serbia is one of the very few European markets adding ATMs, at the fastest rate in a decade. At the same time a branch network 17% smaller than five years ago pushes cash onto the machines. · Money going into ATMs is growing roughly three and a half times faster in value than money coming out. A near one-to-one deposit-to-withdrawal ratio is exactly the condition where recycling beats separate deposit and dispense machines. Recycling machines re-use deposited notes, which starts to cut cash-in-transit journeys and vault holdings. A dispense-only machine is therefore a depreciating asset, whatever the fleet size. · Two disciplines apply. The ATM upturn is only three or four quarters old, so present it as a trend rather than a guarantee. NBS publishes no split of the 3,412 machines by deposit or recycling capability, so any deposit-capable share must be built bottom-up from bank locator feeds.
signals.likelihood: High — structural and consistent across six consecutive quarters and corroborated by bank-level disclosure
signals.follow_up: Standardise a one-page Serbian market slide on the deposit-versus-withdrawal gap plus the branch-network contraction, and attach it to every bank-level proposal. Build a Serbia-specific recycling return-on-investment model from the NBS deposit and withdrawal volumes, and take it to the top five banks. Ask the NBS Payment System Department whether deposit and recycling-capable ATMs can be broken out on request. Write to Bank Supervision for the post-2019 organisational-unit and employee series, which they clearly still hold. Refresh both workbooks each quarter.

signals.bank_theme: Serbia — the incumbent competitor set is now named: Payten/ASEE, Mellon and MoneyGet
signals.signal: Three separate types of evidence point to a clear competitive map. · **Payten (Asseco SEE) is entrenched and locally incorporated through four Serbian legal entities**: Payten d.o.o. Beograd, Chip Card a.d. Belgrade, Afusion and Monri Payments. Its catalogue overlaps almost line for line. It covers ATM infrastructure and outsourcing, multivendor ATM maintenance, ATM software, cardless cash and softPOS. It also covers POS infrastructure and software, acquiring and issuing processing, tokenisation and transaction monitoring (A1). · Its **MoneyGet independent ATM network was re-counted at 198 unique locations in Serbia on 27/08/2026**, about 5.8% of the national estate. It runs on a no-capex partner model that recruits site owners with free installation and maintenance. That targets exactly the off-premise sites a challenger would want (A1). · In the public register Payten holds **38 Serbian public contracts**. These include the Office for IT and eGovernment's POS system usage service, at RSD 10.0m for 12 months from **20/01/2026**. A renewal therefore falls due around January 2027. The contracts also include a payment-gateway upgrade, the card-payment device estates of Belgrade's public parking and garage operators, and a small POS order at the central bank (A2). · The group has publicly reported a retreat in hardware. ASEE's H1-2026 management report of 31/07/2026 shows the Payment Solutions segment down 5% to EUR 102.8m. The ATM line is down EUR 3.4m, put down explicitly to *lower equipment deliveries in South-Eastern Europe, particularly in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro*. The POS line is down EUR 1.9m. Meanwhile the independent-terminal-network and fiscal-cash-register lines grew EUR 2.7m, and independent-network transactions rose 41% year on year (A6). · Serbia remains ASEE's largest country at EUR 53.8m revenue (+13%) and EUR 8.5m EBIT (+33%). This is a shift from equipment sales to a recurring service book, not a withdrawal (A6). · Separately, **Mellon Serbia has built three Serbian bank relationships inside twelve months**. They are Ingenico terminals at Raiffeisen (20/08/2025), a queue-management rollout across 60-plus OTP branches (18/02/2026), and POS acquiring at ProCredit (12/02/2026). That makes it the most active non-Payten challenger, and it puts the firm inside two priority accounts (A6). · Euronet, by contrast, named **no new European ATM-outsourcing win at all** on its Q2-2026 call of 30/07/2026. It is running a sustained total-cost-of-ownership campaign aimed at bank finance directors (A6).
signals.date: 31/07/2026 — ASEE's H1-2026 report discloses falling ATM and POS deliveries naming Serbia first among the affected markets · 27/08/2026 MoneyGet's Serbian network re-counted at 198 locations · eGovernment POS contract renewal falls due ~January 2027
signals.implies: The dominant regional rival has put in writing that its Serbian ATM hardware deliveries shrank in the first half of 2026, while its recurring service book grew. That opens a real displacement window on hardware refresh and estate modernisation. It does not open the whole relationship, and it should be framed that way. · Its order backlog shows contracted revenue flat to down while contracted margin rises. That is the sign of a company taking fewer, better-priced deals. Autumn 2026 is therefore the moment to test firm rather than defensive pricing. · The genuine structural threat is not ATMs at all. It is the independent terminal network growing 41% a year. In that model a single device replaces several acquirer terminals, and the terminal relationship moves away from the bank entirely. · Mellon is also moving into two accounts from the POS and queue-management side, one step from bidding self-service work at renewal. Euronet's cost-of-ownership campaign is the argument that will appear in every Serbian self-service bid over the next year, written for finance rather than technology.
signals.likelihood: Standing competitive condition; the concrete near-term events are the January-2027 eGovernment renewal and the ASEE Q3 disclosure on 26/10/2026
signals.follow_up: Build a written counter-model to the ATM-as-a-service total-cost-of-ownership argument. It should concede each cost category — connectivity, compliance and software upgrades, lifecycle management, cash availability — and show that each can be handled without giving up the estate. Name a local cash-transport partner on every bid, so the risk-transfer gap is visibly closed. · Ask Printec Serbia which Payten-supplied ATM contracts fall due in 2026-27. Find out whether Mellon's Raiffeisen and ProCredit scope includes terminal management and field service, or is hardware supply only. Re-read the ASEE Q3 report on 26/10/2026 to see whether the ATM retreat is structural. Track the independent-terminal-network transaction count quarterly, as the measure of how fast bank-owned terminal estates are being displaced.
signals.product_review_why: The rival map covers ATM hardware and outsourcing, POS estates and independent terminal networks.

(PIB 100093505)** is bank-grade. As the joint bidder group 'Master Team Olimp-ex' it holds the National Bank of Serbia's **automatic banknote sorting and packing systems**. There are two contracts, both dated 05/02/2024, at RSD 206,546,000 and RSD 7,072,000 excluding VAT — a combined **RSD 213.6m, roughly EUR 1.8m**. Both are recorded as fully paid and completed. · Master Team also supplies NBS control note-counting machines, most recently at RSD 768,000 on 07/10/2025. Its other customers include Pošta Srbije, the Customs Administration and a steady stream of municipal utilities through 2026, the latest on 11/08/2026 (A2). · **Vivex Group d.o.o. (PIB 100828591)** is the second tier-one player, and it holds the state Treasury's whole stack. It supplied multifunction vault counting and sorting machines at RSD 8.3m (23/09/2025) and money-banding machines at RSD 3.99m (02/03/2026). It also signed safe and vault repair at RSD 4.0m on 10/07/2026. Most of these procurements had only one or two bidders (A2). · On the kiosk side, **Inova Tech d.o.o. and Elektro Energy d.o.o.** won the Velika Plana municipal self-service kiosk contract for paying administrative fees, at RSD 17,973,000 (~EUR 153k). signals.date: 11/08/2026 — Master Team's most recent municipal cash-machine award · 15/07/2026 Vivex awarded Treasury safe and vault repair · 15/06/2026 municipal kiosk contract awarded to the Inova Tech and Elektro Energy consortium
signals.implies: The Serbian public cash-automation market has two technically qualified defenders, not a soft dealer layer. One of them has already delivered a multi-million-euro automatic sorting installation to the central bank. That changes the entry strategy completely. · There are two realistic routes. The first is to partner with or acquire one of the two firms for local service reach. The second is to bid the next central-bank automatic-sorting cycle directly, on qualification and service depth. Neither route should assume an incumbent can be beaten on specification and price. · The kiosk award carries a second lesson. The winning structure for Serbian municipal work is an integrator paired with a local civils-and-power firm. Elektro Energy is therefore better treated as a candidate installation partner than as a competitor. · The bank segment should be defended on what a municipal kiosk supplier typically cannot offer. signals.bank_theme: Slovakia — eKasa cashless mandate + deposit-ATM expansion
signals.signal: The legal duty to let customers pay cashlessly on any sale above EUR 1 is live, and the legal detail is now pinned down in the primary text. Act 384/2025 Z. z. took effect 01/01/2026. Its section 15(1) acceptance duty applied from 01/05/2026, after Act 30/2026 Z. z. postponed it from 01/03/2026 (A1, A2). · Four points are new this cycle. First, section 15(3) expressly allows a third party to supply the technical means that confirm a QR-code payment back to the cash register. That is an explicit legal opening for a private vendor to run the payment-confirmation layer. Publishing the technical specification is a legal duty, and the Financial Directorate had still not done so at 27/08/2026. · Second, the penalty ladder is far harder than previously reported. A first detection brings a formal instruction only. A second carries EUR 500-15,000, and each further detection EUR 3,000-40,000. Sections 17(5)-(6) class it a "particularly serious breach" that can cost the merchant its trade licence. · Third, on the Financial Directorate register of valid certifications at 19/08/2026, Printec Slovakia holds decision 322095/2025 for "Printec eKasa Service verzia 1.2", effective to at most 20/06/2030. The register carries 65 decisions across 38 companies, so certification is a qualifier to compete rather than a differentiator. Diebold Nixdorf holds two of its own decisions, and also supplies the protected data store into a third party's certified stack. · Fourth, the regulator confirms two recurring merchant-side replacement cycles. eKasa credentials expire every 2 years. The protected data store fills up and must be swapped every 2-6 years. The 5-year certification clock binds only the manufacturer, and must not be sold to merchants as a forced replacement. · The QR-code alternative means the smallest merchants can comply with no hardware. That caps terminal upside and favours SoftPOS. The reported jump from 70,943 to 77,711 POS terminals could not be verified this cycle, and must not be quoted.

sources.text: Slov-lex — zákon č. 384/2025 Z. z. §§15-17, consolidated 28/02/2026
FR SR register of valid eKasa certifications at 19/08/2026

signals.date: 27/08/2026 — FR SR eKasa portal and certification register re-read; mandate live since 01/05/2026; Printec certification valid to at most 20/06/2030
signals.implies: This is the largest single POS and acquiring trigger in Slovakia. It happens entirely through private merchants and acquirers, so it is invisible on the public-procurement portal. · There are three things to sell. The first is SoftPOS plus terminal management for the micro-merchants that still have no terminal. The second is a certified third-party QR payment-confirmation service, once the Financial Directorate publishes the specification. The third is a managed service around credential renewal and protected-data-store swaps for the installed base. That third item is genuine recurring revenue rather than a one-off equipment sale.
signals.likelihood: High — the duty is in force and the live variable is the enforcement ramp through 2026-27
signals.follow_up: Size the tail of merchants with no terminal, and pitch SoftPOS plus terminal management to Slovak acquirers. Position it against the QR carve-out rather than against the mandate. Watch financnasprava.sk for the section 15(3) technical specification. Publishing it is a legal duty, so it is a trigger with a date. Get the terminal count from NBS payment statistics before quoting any figure to a client.
signals.product_review_why: The cashless-acceptance mandate drives SoftPOS and terminal management, plus a recurring service around eKasa renewals.

signals.bank_theme: Finančné riaditeľstvo SR — SAFE, the replacement national revenue-recording platform
signals.signal: A notice on the Financial Directorate's eKasa portal, read 27/08/2026, states that the section 11(4) duty to report cash-register faults "sa v súčasnosti neuplatňuje" (is not currently applied). The reason is that the technical solution will only arrive with a new national revenue-recording system called SAFE. The start of its operation "sa nepredpokladá v roku 2026" (is not expected in 2026). The regulator promises to tell sellers in advance through its portal and social channels, but gives no target go-live year (A1).

sources.text: Finančná správa SR — eKasa portal notice on reporting register faults under §11(4) of Act 384/2025

signals.date: 27/08/2026 — FR SR states SAFE will not enter operation in 2026 and gives no replacement date
signals.implies: A full replacement of the national fiscalisation platform is coming. Fiscalisation is the system that records sales for tax. Every certified cash-register program and protected data store in Slovakia would need re-integration, and probably re-certification against a new specification. · That is a multi-year point-of-sale replacement and integration wave, which an already-certified vendor is well placed to win. The right move is to get onto the consultation list now, before the specification freezes, rather than to wait for a tender.

signals.bank_theme: Slovenská pošta — self-service kiosks + EUR 1.75m security managed services
signals.signal: The EUR 1,745,311.25 / 36-month contract for higher-level support of the information-security systems across Slovak Post's IT estate is still open. The deadline has moved twice, from 14/08/2026 to 08/09/2026 10:00, with opening at 10:30. The change was made by correction notice 11298-IOX of 06/08/2026, republished on TED as 542285-2026. · Two clarifications change the bid team. The scope is information-security operations — administration, maintenance, monitoring, testing and further development — and not physical guarding. Bids go through Slovak Post's own ERANET portal at posta.eranet.sk, not JOSEPHINE or EVO. The only award criterion is lowest price excluding VAT, so the decision comes down to cost base. · There are two more developments at the same buyer. A EUR 13,692,340 / 48-month logistics information system covering the branch and BalíkoBOX estate closed 24/08/2026. It is in evaluation with no award published. Its winner becomes the systems integrator that any later counter or self-service work must go through. · The BalíkoBOX parcel-locker field-maintenance framework was awarded to KOVAL SYSTEMS a.s. at EUR 1,957,059.50 for 24 months, on a single bid, within EUR 62 of the estimate. That is direct evidence that Slovak Post has no competitive field-service market for self-service terminals (A2, A6). The five-branch self-service cash-kiosk pilot still has not turned into a procurement, and no incumbent is locked in.
signals.date: 08/09/2026 10:00 — extended bid deadline for the EUR 1.75m security-support tender; logistics IS closed 24/08/2026 awaiting award; BalíkoBOX framework runs to ~May 2028
signals.implies: The easiest openings in Slovakia sit at one buyer. A EUR 1.75m three-year support contract is open for bids for another week, and it is awarded purely on price, which favours a regional cost base. · The BalíkoBOX single-bid award is the closest match in the market to Printec's own business. Printec already maintains Pošta Slovenije's parcel lockers next door. The award points to a re-tender around May 2028 with no competition to beat. · The unconverted kiosk pilot is still the one self-service opening at Slovak Post with no incumbent.

signals.follow_up: Make the bid or no-bid call before 08/09/2026, and register on posta.eranet.sk rather than JOSEPHINE. Approach Slovak Post now with the Pošta Slovenije locker reference, and ask for the ~2028 BalíkoBOX market consultation. Separately, push to convert the five-branch kiosk pilot.

signals.bank_theme: Národná banka Slovenska — core-banking pre-RFP + ageing cash estate
signals.signal: The core-banking replacement (CORBS) is still pre-procurement. Two market consultations have run, the latest in April 2025. A sweep of every NBS notice from 06/07/2026 to 27/08/2026 found no CORBS tender. · What is new is that the central bank's cash-equipment cycle now has dates, not just descriptions. A full sweep of all 465,236 notices in the ÚVO archive shows the ATM category has never carried a single Slovak notice. Banknote equipment has had only four notices, and coin equipment only two. · The winners are now named. NBS's banknote-processing contract went to Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH, signed 06/05/2019, at EUR 6,519,820 excluding VAT on a single bid. It covers ten machines with built-in shredders, plus warranty and eight years of post-warranty service, so it expires around mid-2027. The coin processing and packaging lines went to QEX a.s. of Trenčín, at EUR 1,589,050.07, with ten years of service. · At the same time NBS awarded HICO s.r.o. a four-year, EUR 298,198.80 construction-supervision framework on 15/07/2026 for its permanent backup site at Kremnica. That dates the main works to roughly 2027-28, along with the vault, cash-handling, physical-security and IT fit-out procurements (A2). · Two more signs point the same way. NBS has just committed up to EUR 56.25m of collector-coin minting frameworks to the Kremnica Mint through about 2030. And the ECB opened its public vote on ten shortlisted new euro banknote designs on 23/07/2026, with a Governing Council decision due around end-2026. That will eventually force recognition-sensor and note-template upgrades on every note-handling machine in the country (A6).

signals.date: 30/07/2026 — Kremnica supervision framework awarded, dating the fit-out to 2027-28; G+D banknote-processing service term expires ~mid-2027; CORBS still unlet

CORBS is still unclaimed, but the best approach is most likely through a local partner rather than as a prime bid.

Prepare a case to replace Giesecke+Devrient at the ~2027 banknote-processing renewal. Profile QEX a.s. as a Slovak coin-line partner or competitor. Ask whether a third CORBS consultation is planned.

signals.bank_theme: Národná banka Slovenska — integration platform, tender notice expected 14/09/2026

It says NBS plans an above-threshold open procedure, with the tender notice expected on 14/09/2026. The notice had not been published as at 27/08/2026. · The scope has four parts. It covers taking over an existing part of the integration platform (SAP Integration Suite) delivered under another project, and delivering the integrations. It also covers supplying software components, including IBM MQ and a SharePoint connector, and then operational support and further services. · Consultations were held in person on 13, 15, 20 and 22 July 2026. signals.bank_theme: Národná banka Slovenska — central identity platform and the named-integrator map
signals.signal: NBS's "Stabilizácia a servisná podpora prevádzky IS CSI" is a EUR 804,700, six-year contract for its central identity management system. That system issues and controls staff and system identities and access rights. The notice text commits the supplier to removing defects and non-standard workarounds. signals.bank_theme: Slovakia — commercial-bank deposit-ATM and recycler build-out
signals.signal: This is the best-evidenced hardware cycle in the cluster. This cycle it gained a much firmer base number and a new driver. · Slovenská sporiteľňa's H1-2026 disclosures state 733 ATMs, including 296 deposit machines, which is the largest network in Slovakia. That means roughly 437 machines are cash-out only, and deposit penetration is already 40.4%, not the third assumed before. The fleet shrank from 752 to 733 in six months, while branches fell from 140 to 128. So branches are shrinking about 3.4 times faster than machines (A1, 30/07/2026). · VÚB publishes 150 deposit ATMs, banknotes only, with a 50-note versus 200-note per-deposit split. That split is a clear sign of two hardware generations. VÚB is holding its network exactly flat at 163 outlets while headcount falls, which means automation inside the branch rather than closure (A1, 28/07/2026). · ČSOB Slovakia's own list carries 124 deposit machines at 99 addresses. Of these, 66 accept coins, but only 23 addresses are away from a branch (A1, 27/08/2026). Tatra banka runs 355 deposit machines handling about 450,000 deposits a month. Seven Slovak banks now operate deposit ATMs across a national estate of roughly 1,000 (A5). · There is a new driver. As at 17/08/2026 branch cash desks are being removed across all five large banks. SLSP has 93 of 128 branches with no cash desk, Tatra 48 of 69, ČSOB 47 of 120, VÚB 25 of 121 and UniCredit 16 of 47. The banks themselves name security regimes, staff training and vault equipment as the cost they are escaping (A5). · Erste's group disclosures show Slovakia taking the deepest branch cut in the group, from 150 to 128 in twelve months. Coin deposit is missing from SLSP's and VÚB's published offers, so a coin offer has no incumbent product to displace.

sources.text: Slovenská sporiteľňa — SLSP v číslach, 1. polrok 2026

signals.date: 17/08/2026 — cash-desk removal quantified across all five large banks; SLSP H1-2026 fleet and deposit counts published 30/07/2026
signals.implies: Every closed cash desk has to be replaced by a recycler or deposit machine in the branch lobby. The banks have stated the problem themselves, in exactly the terms a managed cash service answers. · VÚB at 25 of 121 and UniCredit at 16 of 47 are the least converted, so they are the largest remaining retrofit pipelines. ČSOB Slovakia at 47 of 120 is third. · At SLSP the pitch has to change. At 40% deposit penetration the case is refresh, managed services and the roughly 437 cash-out-only machines, rather than new deposit capability. Coin handling is open white space at both of the market's largest banks. · None of this is bought through public procurement. Slovak retail banks are private and outside procurement law, so this is a direct commercial sale.
signals.likelihood: High — the conversion is on the record and running at five banks simultaneously
signals.follow_up: Build a branch-by-branch conversion model for VÚB and ČSOB Slovakia, and lead with total cost of cash rather than hardware price. Take SLSP a refresh and managed-services case built on displaced transactions per closed branch. Pull its published deposit-ATM list to map the ~437-machine upgrade backlog by location. Test coin-deposit appetite with SLSP's business cash-handling team.
signals.product_review_why: Closed cash desks have to be replaced by recyclers and deposit machines, sold with a managed cash service.
signals.not_biddable_why: no named buyer and no deadline — a market condition, not a deal anyone can bid for

signals.bank_theme: ČSOB Slovakia / 365.bank / Poštová banka — ~600-machine shared ATM network heading into a legal merger
signals.signal: ČSOB Slovakia's own press release of 03/06/2026 sets out a shared network. From 01/07/2026 clients of ČSOB, 365.bank and Poštová banka can use a combined network of nearly 600 ATMs on their own bank's terms. The previous EUR 200 cross-bank withdrawal cap is abolished. ČSOB contributes 428 machines and 365.bank 176. · The arrangement covers withdrawals only. ČSOB's deposit machines stay closed to the other two banks' customers. A legal merger of the two banks was planned for autumn 2026 (A5). · KBC's own 2Q2026 quarterly report separately confirms the corporate side, and settles what A5 could not source. The 98.45% acquisition of 365.bank from J&T Finance Group completed on 15/01/2026 for EUR 708m. It created EUR 176m of goodwill, was consolidated from January 2026, and added EUR 3,647m to the Slovak loan book. KBC justified it in part by "significant cost synergies related to the branch network and head office in Slovakia". 365.bank's distribution rests on a long-standing partnership with Slovak Post, and integration costs were booked as exceptional in 2Q2026 (A1, 06/08/2026).
signals.date: 06/08/2026 — KBC restates the completed acquisition and the branch-network cost-synergy case; shared 600-machine network live since 01/07/2026; legal merger planned autumn 2026
signals.implies: This is the largest single ATM rationalisation and refresh decision in the Slovak market. Two overlapping estates and two self-service fleets have to be merged. Duplicate sites have to be removed, surviving sites moved onto one platform, and a postal-counter channel brought onto that platform. A clearly stated branch cost-synergy target drives the work. · The unsolved problem is deposit interoperability, which means letting either bank's customers deposit at any machine. It needs recyclers and cross-bank deposit switching. The integration clock started in January 2026, so the target operating model is being set now.
signals.likelihood: High that a network and channel rationalisation programme runs through 2026-27; vendor choices likely tied to ČSOB and KBC group frameworks
signals.follow_up: Get in front of the ČSOB Slovakia integration programme office before the merger fixes the target operating model. Confirm whether the legal merger completed in autumn 2026. Obtain the combined estate plan and the deposit-interoperability roadmap. Identify the incumbent ATM vendor on each of the two fleets, and whether 365.bank's Slovak Post counters carry their own machines.
signals.product_review_why: Two ATM fleets must be merged onto one platform with recyclers and cross-bank deposit capability.

signals.bank_theme: Slovakia — cross-bank deposit-ATM interoperability, still at the analysis stage with no vendor locked in
signals.signal: Deposits at Slovak deposit ATMs are still closed to other banks' customers across the whole market. signals.bank_theme: Slovakia — the EU supervisory deadline stack landing on Slovak banks in the next twelve months
signals.signal: Four dated obligations land on Slovak institutions together. (1) ECB letter SSM-2026-0301 of 07/07/2026, signed by Claudia Buch, requires every significant institution to submit an action plan on AI-enabled cybersecurity threats. The plan goes to the institution's joint supervisory team by 31 October 2026. Its focus areas name accurate ICT asset inventories and patch management at scale, which explicitly pulls supplier service-level agreements into scope. They also name "modernising infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies". That maps directly onto ageing ATM estates and unsupported ATM operating systems. The annual IT risk questionnaire has moved from September 2026 to February 2027. (2) The same letter pre-announces a second ECB letter on post-quantum cryptography, with no date. That is an announced supervisory action, not a deadline, and must not be presented as one. (3) Under DORA the Register of Information has a reference date of 31/12/2026. National supervisors set their own earlier filing cut-offs for entities, before forwarding to the European authorities by 31/03/2027. Printec will therefore be asked for register-grade data on its own contracts during Q4-2026 and Q1-2027. (4) Threat-led penetration testing is set out in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190, and covers critical functions end to end. For a retail bank, that pulls in the ATM channel and the terminal-management layer. Separately, relying-party registration under the EU digital identity rules applies from 24/12/2026, with acceptance following at 24/12/2027. National wallet programmes, including Slovakia's eDoklady, are widely expected to be late (A3).

signals.bank_theme: Slovenia — draft Cash Access Act sets a statutory ATM density floor
signals.signal: **The bill is alive and now in direct negotiation with the banks. Its headline density numbers are now formally disputed.** The Ministry of Finance closed the public consultation on the draft **Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi plačilnih sredstev (ZDUPS) on 17/08/2026 with 23 written responses**. The ministry's own release records what respondents proposed. They asked for different or new criteria for the cash-point network, wider exemptions from mandatory cash acceptance, moving the electronic-payment-acceptance duty into a separate procedure, and a longer adaptation period. On **24/08/2026 the ministry met the Banka Slovenije working group and the Bank Association of Slovenia (ZBS)** and said it will continue "constructive dialogue with the banks". There were no decisions, no revised criteria and no timetable. **An ECB opinion under Art. 127(4) TFEU is still outstanding.** The bill had not reached a government session or the Državni zbor as at 31/08/2026 (A3, A5). There is a **verification conflict this cycle**. A5 reports the density obligations as confirmed in a summary published by the municipalities' association ZMOS. These are at least 60 ATMs per 100,000 inhabitants, and 95% of the population within 5 km. They also include an ATM within 5 km of settlements above 1,000 people, and a branch or post office within 5 km for settlements above 3,000. At most 3% would be replaceable by cashback or cash-in-shop, plus a merchant duty to accept at least one electronic payment instrument. But A3 re-read the ministry's own releases and found **none of those figures appear there, and could not verify them against the bill text**. The bill pairs the access-to-cash mandate with a **free basic payment-services package** for everyone receiving salaries, pensions or other regular income. The ZBS calls this problematic in principle, and press reporting says it may face a constitutional-court challenge. Field context (press-tier): NLB now has 69 branches and 508 ATMs, against 113 and 558 ten years ago. OTP banka Slovenije has 71 branches and 400 ATMs, against a combined NKBM plus SKB total of 126 and 493. In parallel the EU **Legal Tender of Cash Regulation moved into trilogue** (final talks between the EU institutions). ECON voted to open negotiations 23/06/2026, and plenary confirmed this on 08/07/2026. This would put an EU floor under the same obligation, with no published conclusion date.
signals.date: 24/08/2026 — Ministry of Finance opens negotiation with Banka Slovenije and the Bank Association · consultation closed 17/08/2026 with 23 responses · ECB opinion pending · press-reported adoption target end-2026, not confirmed by the ministry
signals.implies: This is still the largest potential ATM and self-service capex trigger in Slovenia, and it is **still unpriced and still open to change**. That makes now the right time to sell into it. The banks are formally at the table, and the state intends them to carry the cost of both the ATMs and the free accounts, so cost-to-serve is the whole argument. Printec's move now is pre-legislative readiness work, not hardware. It should build a per-site cost model for a low-volume rural cash point. NLB, OTP banka Slovenije, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka, Addiko and Pošta Slovenije can then price any geographic floor before it is fixed. If a floor survives, the purchase has four parts. First, dispense and recycling ATMs with through-the-wall installs. Second, multivendor ATM software, so new rural sites are not locked to one vendor stack. Third, telemetry and monitoring to prove uptime where no branch staff are there to clear a jam. Fourth, managed field services with rural cover. The free-services part helps Printec: banks forced to give away basic accounts fight harder on cash-network cost, which favours recyclers over plain dispensers. **No density figure may be quoted to a customer.**
signals.likelihood: High that a cash-access law passes in some form — it implements a constitutionally recognised right to cash. Whether any specific density or geography criterion survives is genuinely open, and no legislative date exists
signals.follow_up: Get the actual ZDUPS draft text from e-uprava or gov.si to settle whether the 60-per-100,000 and 5 km criteria are in it. Neither agent could do this in this cycle. Then watch for the ECB opinion, the revised draft sent to Government, and any Državni zbor first reading. Ask NLB and OTP banka Slovenije what their ZBS submission asked for. Brief both, plus Intesa SI and Delavska hranilnica, on compliance-cost scenarios now, in the 2027 planning round of September to November 2026. Confirm whether independent ATM deployers count toward any floor.
signals.product_review_why: A density floor would drive rural ATM and recycler purchases backed by telemetry and field services.

signals.bank_theme: NLB d.d. — ATM accessibility retrofit to 2030 under the Slovenian accessibility act
signals.signal: **The accessibility act was amended, and the amendment makes accessibility a procurement requirement. The master row did not capture this.** The Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Zakona o dostopnosti do proizvodov in storitev za invalide (**ZDPSI-A**) was passed on 11/02/2026. It was published in Uradni list RS 14/2026 on 24/02/2026. It has been **in force since 25/02/2026**. The commercially decisive change is a new Art. 3(5). It provides verbatim that the accessibility conditions "constitute mandatory accessibility requirements which are taken into account in public procurement procedures when drawing up the technical specifications of the contract". Also new: the market-surveillance inspectorate **TIRS must take immediate restrictive measures, including withdrawing a product from the market**. An operator claiming disproportionate burden must notify the surveillance bodies. The minister may set functional-performance criteria as an alternative to technical conditions. Self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life, but **no longer than 20 years** from entry into use. Art. 18(5) lets a contracting authority amend **live** tender documents to apply the new rule where the deadline has not passed (A3). Carried forward and still valid: NLB Group's Annual Report 2025 states that 58 ATMs in Slovenia support voice-guided transactions for blind and partially sighted customers. A further 26 were due by Q1-2026, against a group commitment to equip **all** ATMs by **2030**. Press-tier field data this cycle puts NLB's Slovenian fleet at **508 ATMs**, so several hundred machines remain to upgrade (A5). The master row's verifier correction stands. Banka Slovenije has **not** asked payment service providers for accessibility plans, and its National Payments Council minutes of 21/03/2025 closed the topic.

sources.text: Uradni list RS 14/2026 — ZDPSI-A full text

signals.date: STANDING: 25/02/2026 — ZDPSI-A in force, making accessibility a mandatory technical specification in every Slovenian public tender · NLB commitment deadline 2030 · legacy terminals capped at 20 years from entry into use. No trigger inside the next 18 months: the procurement-gate mechanism is continuous and the estate deadline is 2030, so this is standing context that shapes every Slovenian bid rather than a dated event.
signals.implies: Two things changed. First, accessibility is now a hard **qualification requirement**. Any ATM, kiosk, teller recycler or payment terminal bid to a Slovenian public-sector or state-owned buyer must carry EN 301 549 accessibility evidence in the technical specification. That includes Pošta Slovenije, which the cash-access bill would make a cash-point operator. Without that evidence a bid is non-compliant on its face, and the rule can be brought into tenders already running. A supplier with the documentation clears it; one without cannot. TIRS can remove a non-compliant terminal model from the Slovenian market entirely. Second, the two Slovenian bills interlock. If any density floor survives the cash-access act, NLB, OTP banka Slovenije and Pošta must **add** cash points. Every added machine must be accessible from day one, with no exemption for older kit. At NLB itself the work stays a deadline-bound fleet programme. It covers audio and accessibility hardware kits, voice-guidance ATM software and nationwide field-service delivery across several hundred machines. There is no supervisory prompt, so timing follows the ordinary fleet cycle and the target is the 2027 hardware plan.
signals.likelihood: High that the retrofit work continues to 2030; the procurement gate bites today in every live Slovenian public tender
signals.follow_up: Get a current NLB Slovenia ATM count from the bank. The only figures available are a three-year-old press release and this cycle's press-tier 508. Find out whether NLB delivers by retrofit or by speeding up hardware replacement. Confirm whether the minister has issued the functional-performance-criteria implementing act. Watch for the first TIRS restrictive measure against a self-service terminal. Make sure Printec's accessibility documentation is bid-ready for Slovenian public buyers now, since it can be brought into tenders mid-flight.
signals.product_review_why: It is an ATM fleet accessibility programme, and the amended act makes accessibility compliance a hard bid requirement for all self-service kit.

signals.bank_theme: Bankart — the bank-owned processor gating every Slovenian ATM and POS win
signals.signal: **Bankart has a new chief technology officer and a new central-bank mandate this cycle.** Bankart appointed **Siniša Jančić to the Management Board in the CTO role on 17/04/2026**. This is the only item the company published on its own channels all year, with no product launch, tender or partnership visible (A6). Separately, Banka Slovenije contracted Bankart to **process and settle its SEPA cross-border credit transfers**, at EUR 100,000 excl. VAT on a single bid. The contract was signed 30/04/2026 and runs 34 months to about February 2029. The tender caps a pacs.008 customer-credit-transfer message at **EUR 0.017 excl. VAT** (A2). Its structural position is re-confirmed at source. Bankart calls itself the leading Slovenian processor of modern payment instruments. It **controls and manages both the ATM network and the POS terminal network for its member banks**. That covers card issuing and lifecycle, ATM and POS acquiring processing, terminal management, SEPA and instant clearing, wallet enablement, routing, monitoring and fraud prevention. It is **100% bank-owned — NLB 46.03%, OTP banka 43.06%, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo 7.25%, UniCredit Banka Slovenija 2.24%, Deželna banka 1.42%**. It organises development as seventeen product teams across five business areas and four technical platforms. It markets instant-payment infrastructure to central banks outside Slovenia (A1). NLB's report records OTP's 43.06% as above the 25% cap in Bankart's founding agreement.
signals.date: 17/04/2026 — new CTO appointed, the only Bankart publication of 2026 · SEPA cross-border processing contract for the central bank signed 30/04/2026, running to about February 2029
signals.implies: Bankart is the single control point for ATM and POS driving, terminal management and authorisation across most of Slovenia. Any Printec device win therefore depends on Bankart certification. It is a gatekeeper to qualify with rather than an account to sell to, and qualification should start before a bank deal is in play. **A new chief technology officer is the point at which technology roadmaps reopen.** Multivendor ATM software, device telemetry and terminal management are all decisions that sit with that role. Because Bankart buys almost entirely outside public procurement, there will be no tender to wait for. Against that, seventeen in-house product teams show build capacity, so Bankart is unlikely to buy software it can write itself. The realistic path is hardware, recyclers and anti-skimming supply, plus co-bidding on its central-bank instant-payment plans outside Slovenia. OTP's stake above the founding-agreement cap remains a live governance issue.
signals.likelihood: Structural and stable; the near-term opening is relationship access off the CTO appointment, not a procurement event
signals.follow_up: Request an introduction to the new CTO on the strength of the appointment itself, and brief him on multivendor ATM software and device telemetry. Pull Bankart's annual accounts from AJPES for current ATM and POS counts, which it publishes nowhere. The accounts should also settle whether its authorisation-system replacement completes end-2026. Confirm which Slovenian banks drive their own machines and which use Bankart. Test Bankart as a reseller channel for recyclers and anti-skimming. Re-check its RSS feed monthly, as the only working primary channel.
signals.product_review_why: Bankart certifies every ATM and POS device in Slovenia and also sells instant-payment infrastructure that Printec could co-bid.

signals.bank_theme: NLB d.d. — cash-light branch format and cash-deposit-system rollout in Slovenia
signals.signal: NLB has a **named, funded, group-level self-service programme that is already running in Slovenia.** Its Investor Day "Cash Transition" slide states verbatim an "ATM and CDS network upgrade at Group level driving cash out of branches". Upgraded ATMs and expanded cash-deposit systems allow deposits with instant visibility. Alongside this, a cash-at-POS rollout moves withdrawals from branches to merchant tills. Retail cash transactions in branches fell from 32% at YE2023 to 15.1% at YE2025. They were 13.5% in March 2026, against a 2030 target below 10%. In H1-2026 in Slovenia specifically, the bank **opened three new branches on the cash-light concept, one of them fitted with a cash deposit system letting companies deposit daily takings**. The corporate chapter states the CDS self-service deposit network "was further expanded". Slovenian branches went from 69 to 70, while the SEE subsidiaries shed 16. Slovenia is therefore a stable estate being retrofitted, not closed. Group card and ATM fee income rose 6% to EUR 71.965m in H1-2026, while the matching expense rose 11% to EUR 48.851m. Net card and ATM fee income actually fell about 1.5% year on year, a margin squeeze visible across two periods. The technology budget behind Strategy 2030 is **EUR 160–200 million**, with a clear shift to "vendors integrated into cross-functional delivery model" (A1). Demand is confirmed from the buy side too. NLB won Lekarna Ljubljana's three-year contract to **receive the pharmacy chain's daily cash takings** at EUR 102,028.50, 48% below estimate. It holds similar cash-handling and day-night-safe lots at other public pharmacies (A2).
signals.date: 06/08/2026 — H1 interim report records three cash-light branches opened and the cash-deposit network further expanded in Slovenia · Investor Day cash-transition programme 07/05/2026 · 2030 target of under 10% branch cash transactions
signals.implies: The cash-light branch format **is** a self-service equipment specification. Each new branch is an ATM, recycler and cash-deposit-system order, and the format is being repeated. This is the largest Slovenian estate, at a press-tier 508 ATMs, held by a bank that has publicly committed to moving cash out of branches. The bank is being squeezed on card and ATM margin, with 11% cost growth against 6% revenue growth. It has a stated EUR 160–200m technology budget and a preference for vendors inside its own delivery model. A margin squeeze of this kind is the usual trigger for an ATM managed-services or outsourcing tender. The pharmacy cash-deposit contract gives a costed proof point. NLB is contractually taking on third-party cash deposit and day-night-safe duties at prices it must now defend. That is the business case for teller cash recyclers and deposit automation behind the counter.
signals.likelihood: High — already in delivery, the branch format is being repeated, and further cash-deposit rollout is signalled
signals.follow_up: Find out which cash-deposit-system and recycler manufacturer NLB standardised on. Its 2025 annual report indicates the group ATM and CDS tender was already finalised in 2025. Find out whether the cash-light branch specification is being passed down to the six SEE banks. Break the EUR 48.9m fee-expense line into scheme fees versus ATM operating cost. Ask whether any NLB bank has an ATM-as-a-service tender in preparation. Use the Lekarna Ljubljana price as the cost baseline in a retail cash-automation pitch.
signals.product_review_why: Each cash-light branch is a recycler and cash-deposit order, and the margin squeeze points to an ATM outsourcing tender.

signals.bank_theme: NLB d.d. — merchant acquiring, POS estate modernisation and the digital-euro pilot
signals.signal: NLB is spending money to grow its merchant acquiring business, which is the service that lets shops take card payments. **Linking POS terminals to cash registers is openly on its plan**. It is also Slovenia's bank in the digital-euro pilot. Its Investor Day gives the figures. There are about 20,000 acquiring merchants today. Acquiring partnerships rose from 5 at YE2023 to 11 at YE2025, with a 2030 target above 20. The regional market is worth over EUR 120bn, of which an estimated 64–80% is still paid in cash at the till. Payments revenue was EUR 236.5m in FY2025, with a target above EUR 320m by 2030. The **next things it plans to build are full POS-to-electronic-cash-register integration, soft POS (card acceptance on a phone) and digital tips**. In Slovenia in H1-2026 the bank let merchants order any type of POS terminal fully online, with no paper, using Rekono digital identification. It launched a business-analytics module in its Merchant Portal. It **finished a major POS project for a large merchant, so that several business activities run through one terminal with automatic settlement**. It also grew micro-merchant acquiring through partnerships with fiscal cash-register providers (A1). NLB holds the Slovenian state's portable-POS contracts too. These are the Ministry of the Interior's contract for up to 100 terminals at EUR 213,114.75, and a parallel 14-terminal contract, both for 48 months to about 2030. The pricing shows where the value sits: **terminal rental is worth about EUR 141 per terminal per year, while all the money is in the acquiring commission** (A2). NLB is Slovenia's bank in the **ECB digital-euro pilot**, which starts in H2-2027 and runs for 12 months (A5).

signals.date: 06/08/2026 — H1 report records the single-terminal multi-activity merchant project and online paperless terminal ordering · MNZ POS contracts signed 21/05/2026 running to 2030 · digital-euro pilot participation confirmed 14/07/2026, pilot starts H2-2027

The single-terminal project for several activities, plus the fiscal-cash-register partnerships, are exactly the POS-to-cash-register integration Printec already delivers elsewhere. The Rekono paperless ordering and electronic-ID signing show NLB is also buying digital-onboarding and e-signature tools. Two limits shape the pitch. First, **Bankart runs NLB's POS estate**, so the way in is hardware, cash-register integration or value-added services, not the acquiring core. Second, the Slovenian state never buys terminals, only card acceptance, so NLB is the buyer for anything terminal-shaped. The pilot gives a dated reason to open a terminal-readiness talk before the H2-2027 budgets.

signals.follow_up: Find out which POS hardware and terminal-management platform is used on the large-merchant project and under the two Ministry of the Interior contracts. The platform, not the box, is the part that can be won. Name the fiscal cash-register partners as possible channel partners. Ask NLB whether it plans to pilot digital-euro cash-in and cash-out at ATMs. Put the state POS re-tender in the diary for about H2-2029.

signals.bank_theme: OTP banka Slovenija — post-merger estate consolidation and an active ATM skimming wave
signals.signal: Slovenia's second-largest bank holds about 26.8% of assets. It is **closing branches faster than any other bank in the OTP group, while its ATM fleet stays almost flat. At the same time it is dealing with live card fraud at those machines.** OTP's group half-year report covers the changes between 31/12/2025 and 30/06/2026. OTP Slovenia went from **74 to 69 branches (-5)**, the largest drop in absolute terms in the group. Its ATMs fell from **390 to 384 (-6)** and its POS terminals from **13,001 to 12,830**, with headcount down from 2,117 to 2,100. Its own H1-2026 release reports net profit of EUR 128m and total assets of EUR 15.7bn. It also reports the integration of OTP Skladi asset management and the roll-out of "a new operational model of Value Streams". On **06/08/2026 the bank published a public security notice**. It said it had recently found payment-card abuse at its ATMs through skimming. Criminals fit a device that copies magnetic-stripe data, and capture the PIN with a hidden camera or a fake keypad overlay. The bank told customers to check the card slot and keypad before use. It says it monitors card security "together with partners", and names no locations, models or case numbers (A1). The leadership map was fixed this cycle. **Vojko Božiček has sat on the management board in charge of digital and operational business** since 14/01/2025, with Andras Hamori as board president. The same page still lists John Denhof as president from 23/08/2024, so an undated handover appears to have taken place (A5).

sources.text: OTP Bank Nyrt. half-year report, network table p.42

signals.date: 06/08/2026 — public skimming warning issued on a roughly 384-machine fleet · 05/08/2026 half-year network table confirms 74 to 69 branches and 390 to 384 ATMs in six months
signals.implies: There are two reasons to spend at once, on the estate most exposed to the draft cash-access law. The **skimming wave is reactive budget available now**. It points to anti-skimming detection modules, card-slot and keypad hardening, jitter and camera shielding, and card-fraud transaction monitoring. Skimming only pays where magnetic-stripe fallback is still switched on, so there is also a credible consulting angle on disabling the stripe and hardening EMV (chip) security. The **merged Nova KBM plus SKB estate** is a fleet with two legacy vendor stacks. Branches are closing at nearly 7% in six months while the machine count barely moves. That is the usual starting point for a recycler and cash-deposit upgrade programme, plus work to decommission and move machines. A named board owner for digital **and** operations is the right way in for all of it.
signals.likelihood: High — closures are continuing on trend and the security notice is dated this month
signals.follow_up: Find out whether OTP SI is actually buying anti-skimming or fraud-monitoring upgrades, or only warning customers, and whether Bankart runs its card-fraud detection centrally. Pull OTP Slovenia's own ATM locator to see how many of the 384 machines take deposits, and check this against the press figure of 400. Map which of the Nova KBM and SKB legacy ATMs come from which manufacturer, and who the current maintenance provider is. Put a date on the handover from Denhof to Hamori as president.
signals.product_review_why: A live skimming wave calls for anti-skimming hardware and card-fraud monitoring, and the merged fleet is due a recycler upgrade.

signals.bank_theme: Slovenia — digital identity, key management and secure-document procurement, all through local channels
signals.signal: Slovenia buys cryptographic and identity infrastructure through **small local integrators, usually on single bids**. Printec's realistic route is through those partners rather than head-on. The Ministry of Digital Transformation bought **hardware security modules (HSMs) from OSI sistemske rešitve d.o.o. at EUR 303,685.36 on a single bid**. These are tamper-resistant boxes that create, store and use the cryptographic keys behind payment and identity credentials. The same ministry rented mobile biometric-enrolment units for the administrative units from CENT SI d.o.o. at EUR 386,280 on two bids. It also has **two live 2026 digital-identity procurements**. The first is SI-CAS, the central authentication system, whose award notice was published **26/08/2026**. The second is SI-CeS, the central server-side e-signing system, published 27/04/2026. Both are worth checking for wallet and signing-module scope. A portal sweep also found four other Slovenian public HSM buyers, across public administration, defence, interior and the academic research network. Outside government, **Elektro Primorska** tendered a cryptographic key-management system for smart-meter infrastructure. Bids closed 28/07/2026 and no award has been published. A separate and much larger contract sits with CETIS. **CETIS d.d. holds a 10-year, EUR 41,901,521.90 framework for the design, production, storage, personalisation, dispatch and destruction of Slovenian biometric travel documents**. It won this unopposed on a single bid in November 2025. A corrigendum of 08/05/2026 extended it to all **58 administrative units and the foreign ministry**, which is the whole national issuance counter network (A2).

sources.text: TED 568377-2025 — Ministry of Digital Transformation HSM award

signals.date: 26/08/2026 — SI-CAS central authentication award notice published · SI-CeS e-signing procurement published 27/04/2026 · CETIS travel-document framework runs 10 years from 24/11/2025
signals.implies: The lesson here is about channels, not a single deal. OSI sistemske rešitve and CENT SI are possible reseller partners for payment HSMs and wallet enrolment hardware before the next refresh. The single-bid result on the ministry's HSM purchase is the easiest kind of incumbent to challenge at renewal. CETIS is the national incumbent for secure-document personalisation, locked in for ten years, with **no way to displace it at all**. The right move is to treat CETIS as a regional partner for card-issuing and identity work, not as a competitor. The Elektro Primorska key-management tender shows there is live Slovenian demand for key management outside banking. signals.bank_theme: Slovenia — the cash-in-transit and cash-service field, all channel partners rather than competitors
signals.signal: This cycle mapped the Slovenian cash-logistics field in full. No player in it supplies cash-automation hardware, so each one is a possible route to market rather than a competitor. The confirmed awards are as follows. GVS d.o.o. took the largest court contract. It covers guarding plus cash collection and transport for the Novo mesto, Črnomelj and Trebnje courts and the Ljubljana Labour and Social Court. It is worth EUR 746,292.81, was won on a single bid, was signed 05/05/2026 and runs 2026–2030. Sintal d.o.o. holds Pošta Slovenije's armed cash-transport framework for the Ljubljana logistics region. It has a EUR 70,000 ceiling and runs to about April 2028. The Maribor lot was left unawarded despite a bid. Aktiva Varovanje d.d. services Pošta's intelligent banknote-neutralisation cash cases, which are cases that spoil the notes if attacked. That award was made under a formal "no competition for technical reasons" finding, at EUR 110,000 to about October 2027. There is also a live gap in supply. Maribor District Court had to buy a six-month emergency bridge contract from Aktiva Varovanje and Protect Infra on urgency grounds from 01/08/2026. Its 24-month open procedure for guarding plus cash transport closed on 22/06/2026 and is still not awarded. The award must be made before the bridge runs out by 31/01/2027. Meanwhile FURS runs its own cash logistics through Pošta Slovenije rather than a security firm, under a contract to 31/01/2029. Its spend on cash-counting equipment is very small. It bought a EUR 7,560 desktop counter that only one local reseller bid for, after an identical procedure drew zero bids (A2).

signals.bank_theme: Slovenia — commercial banks sit outside public procurement, so the pipeline is invisible to tender monitoring
signals.signal: This is a structural negative finding, confirmed again this cycle over a wider period. Portal sweeps re-run on 27/08/2026 show the following results. The automatic-banknote-dispensing-machine classification and all its sub-codes have zero notices since 01/01/2024. Coin-handling machines also have zero notices since 01/01/2024. Sorting and banknote-handling equipment has six notices since 2024, but all of them are Pošta Slovenije parcel and letter sorters, and none is a banknote sorter. Counterfeit detection has six notices, all of them the tax authority's desktop counters, with no bank at all. A title search for "bankomat" returns two notices in the portal's entire history. Both come from a 2019 municipality paying towards the running costs of rural ATMs. So the only ATM procurement Slovenia has ever published is a town paying to keep village machines running, and never a bank buying a machine. The reason is legal. NLB, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, OTP banka, SKB, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka and Addiko are private companies, so they are not contracting authorities under the Slovenian public procurement act. Bankart does not publish either. The only banking-sector contracting authorities are Banka Slovenije, SID banka and, as a utilities buyer, Pošta Slovenije (A2).

sources.text: Portal javnih naročil — classification and title sweeps re-run 27/08/2026

signals.date: STANDING: 27/08/2026 — portal sweeps re-run and confirmed unchanged; structural since at least 01/01/2024
signals.implies: Procurement intelligence cannot reach the Slovenian ATM, recycler and self-service market at all, and no amount of portal watching will find it. This row exists so that the pipeline is never written off because the portal is silent. The lack of notices reflects who counts as a contracting authority. It is not evidence that there is no demand. The same cycle found clear direct evidence of demand at NLB, OTP banka and Pošta. Everything must therefore be sold direct to NLB, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo Slovenia, OTP banka Slovenija and Bankart.
signals.likelihood: Structural — it will not change unless the public procurement act's scope changes
signals.follow_up: Route the Slovenian ATM and recycler pipeline through direct bank contact and through Bankart. Stop spending tender-sweep effort on Slovenian ATM classifications. Keep the sweep only for Banka Slovenije, SID banka and Pošta Slovenije.

signals.bank_theme: Slovenia — MONEYVAL enhanced follow-up meets NLB's "AI at scale: AML"
signals.signal: The core of the master row still stands. MONEYVAL published Slovenia's 6th-round mutual evaluation on 07/07/2026 and placed the country in enhanced follow-up. It found moderate improvement in risk assessment, but significant remaining gaps on terrorism financing, held back by structural data gaps. What changed this cycle is the EU layer and the hiring evidence. AMLA's 2027 selection timeline is now dated from primary sources. National supervisors, including Banka Slovenije, had to send data to AMLA by 15/08/2026. The provisional list of eligible obliged entities is expected to be final at end-September 2026. The first selection process must start by 1 July 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2024/1620, and must finish within six months. Direct supervision then follows from 2028. To be eligible, a group must operate in at least six Member States including its home state, which catches the cross-border groups active in Slovenia. On transposition, the Commission's monitoring page as at 07/08/2026 records Slovenia as having communicated full measures for the 10/07/2025 tranche. The fixed general deadline is 10/07/2027. The beneficial-ownership and bank-account-register articles were due 10/07/2026 (A3). Separately, the Slovenian market is clearly hiring for exactly the skill the evaluators say is missing. Addiko Slovenia was running three data roles at once: data engineer, data governance analyst and data analyst. It was also running two group market and liquidity risk roles. Delavska hranilnica posted a data-governance specialist on 25/08/2026 (A5). Carried forward and still valid, NLB's own technology deck names "AI at scale: AML, retail credit risk, chatbots" as a board-level programme.

sources.text: AMLA — next step toward 2027 selection for direct supervision

signals.date: 15/08/2026 — national supervisors' AMLA data submission fell due · provisional list of directly supervised entities expected end-September 2026 · first AMLA selection must commence by 01/07/2027 · MONEYVAL enhanced follow-up opened 07/07/2026
signals.implies: The named weakness in Slovenia is data: the quality of risk assessment, complete customer and beneficial-owner records, and the ability to prove a risk-based approach. That maps onto transaction monitoring and screening, and onto electronic know-your-customer checks that close onboarding gaps. It also maps onto management reporting that produces the evidence the evaluators say is missing. The terrorism-financing finding also points at how sanctions screening is tuned. Two data tests now fall within twelve months for cross-border groups. The hiring at Addiko and Delavska hranilnica shows that Slovenian banks are staffing up for this rather than buying yet. Three data roles at once indicates a platform build rather than backfill, and it is happening inside a bank whose new owner will scope a data-estate migration in 2027. The commercial conclusion is to sell one combined regulation-plus-evaluation-remediation programme into the FY2027 budget round of September to December 2026, rather than two separate programmes.
signals.likelihood: High — enhanced follow-up sets a fixed reporting cycle and supervisors pass it down through inspections; the AMLA dates are in the legal text
signals.follow_up: Pull out the MONEYVAL immediate-outcome ratings on supervision, preventive measures and beneficial ownership, word for word. Do the same for the recommended actions for the financial sector. Each one is a named control gap. Find out NLB Group's current transaction-monitoring vendor, and whether its AI work is in-house or bought in. At end-September 2026, check whether AMLA publishes the provisional eligible list and whether Banka Slovenije submitted by 15/08/2026. Check whether Addiko's data cluster also appears in Croatia, and whether the new owner freezes it.
signals.product_review_why: MONEYVAL and AMLA pressure drives AML data, transaction monitoring and eKYC remediation spend.

signals.bank_theme: PrivatBank — 1,000-unit recycler renewal (live tender PB-2026-03-17-3068329)
signals.signal: The main development this cycle is that stage-1 qualification on the recycler programme closed on 25/08/2026. The portal now shows the qualification window as 08/04/2026 15:00 to 25/08/2026 08:48 Kyiv time. The tender is therefore no longer parked. The stage-2 commercial round is the next event, and the status is `active.stage2.waiting` (A2, A6). PrivatBank does not publish a shortlist for this procurement, so it is not known whether Printec passed stage 1 at all. On the parallel banknote-sorter tender at the same bank, where the shortlist is published, Printec is absent. The specification is confirmed word for word, and it is written on a Diebold Nixdorf software baseline. It requires extended module statuses for the DN "Vynamic View" monitoring handler. It also requires full compatibility with DN ProFlex 4.x / VCP Pro 7 across every module: recycler, card reader, NFC reader and encrypting PIN pad. Further requirements are licensed Windows 11 64-bit LTSC with CEN/XFS 3.50, and at least 4 recycling denominations at once. The machine must handle UAH, USD and EUR at the same time, plus two more currencies. Worldline processing support is also required. The warranty is 2 years including parts, and all adaptation must be at the vendor's own cost. No budget is published, and the portal value is 0. Printec's position as incumbent is re-verified on primary sources. Prozorro UA-2025-01-17-010779-a was signed 16/01/2025 and covers 1,140 NCR recyclers for UAH 838,639,173.73 incl. VAT. The split is 800 SelfServ 2062 lobby machines and 340 SelfServ 2064 through-the-wall machines, at unit prices of EUR 13,870 and EUR 14,641. Delivery was by 30/11/2025, with a 24-month warranty. The end of warranty and the managed-service renewal therefore fall around Nov-2027, not 2026 (A1, A2). The bank is visibly preparing to turn over its fleet. It ordered 700 technical-condition reports plus 300 defect schedules on ATMs and self-service terminals (UA-2026-08-03-004344-a, UAH 178,000, awarded 03/08/2026 to RENOME-SMART, running to 26/07/2027). It also bought 43,000 rolls of ATM thermal paper (A1, A2, A5, A6). One piece of counter-evidence should be kept in mind. An independent sweep of all 125 PrivatBank notices under CPV 30123200-9, run on 27/08/2026, finds zero whole-machine ATM or recycler purchases dated 2026. All 14 of the 2026 records are spares and modules (A1).
signals.date: 25/08/2026 — stage-1 qualification CLOSED; the stage-2 commercial round is now the decision point and is expected within weeks. Context: spec amended 30/03/2026; Printec's 1,140-unit incumbency contract signed 16/01/2025 with warranty to ~Nov-2027
signals.implies: This is still the largest single ATM-hardware opportunity in the footprint, but the timetable has now moved and the risk is higher. The bank has written the requirement around Diebold Nixdorf's own monitoring and device-control software. An NCR-and-x-core answer therefore does not meet the specification. To bid, Printec would have to certify against ProFlex 4.x / VCP Pro 7 and integrate with Vynamic View, or get the clause challenged before stage 2 is fixed. The first question is not price. It is whether Printec is on the qualified list at all.
signals.likelihood: High — qualification has closed and stage 2 is due; the award itself may still slip into 2027
signals.follow_up: Find out within days, through the named PrivatBank buyer, whether Printec passed stage-1 qualification. If it did not, that is the main problem and it must be fixed before stage 2 opens. At the same time, get a technical view from NCR Atleos and x-core on certifying against ProFlex 4.x / VCP Pro 7 and Vynamic View. Prepare a clarification challenge to the vendor-funded-adaptation and Vynamic View clauses. Check `get-ptr.json?ad-id=3068329` weekly.
signals.product_review_why: It is a large recycler hardware tender with a managed-service renewal on the existing NCR fleet due in 2027.

signals.bank_theme: PrivatBank — Android POS estate plus an unassigned terminal-management and field-service requirement
signals.signal: PrivatBank has bought roughly USD 9.0m of Android POS hardware in 2026 alone. It also has two live but unassigned service needs that fit Printec's business. On hardware, PB-2026-06-26-3070719 covers mobile Android POS with a HAL API at USD 7,125,000 excluding VAT. Its auction was on 13/07/2026 and the award phase closed on 11/08/2026. The status is `active.awarded`, and the winner is not published. A2 gives no unit count, while A6 reads the lot as 65,000 units. The second lot is PB-2026-01-30-3067542, for 20,000 portable units. It is valued at USD 1,900,000 on the bank portal, but at USD 2,180,000 on the matching Prozorro contract report UA-2026-06-11-013572-a. It was awarded on 11/06/2026 to Newland Payment Technology (H.K.) as a direct purchase with no competition (A1, A2, A6). Printec Ukraine holds the stationary half of the estate: 39,000 Castles Saturn 1000 S1F3CT Android terminals with HAL API, at UAH 151,734,960 incl. VAT, awarded 25/10/2025 (UA-2025-10-25-000676-a). The bank asks for a HAL API on every lot. A HAL API is a hardware-abstraction layer that lets one payment app run unchanged on different makes of terminal. This is deliberate, because it keeps vendors interchangeable and turns the box into a commodity. Two needs remain open. PB-2026-01-15-3067375, an Android POS remote-management system, also called a TMS, was cancelled on 06/02/2026. The published reason was that the bank had taken the results of a market-survey RFI into account and would then decide whether to go ahead. PB-2025-12-09-3066621, for servicing of ATMs, self-service terminals and POS, was cancelled on 26/12/2025 with the same wording. Both are live unmet needs rather than abandoned ones. Two independent security assessments of the PAX A930CL fleet also failed to attract a compliant bidder (PB-2026-04-13-3068908 and PB-2026-06-16-3070386) (A2).

That layer is multivendor terminal management across a mixed Castles, Newland and PAX estate, remote key injection, PCI-PIN attestation and in-country field service. Both of those needs are at the RFI stage right now. That is the only moment when a supplier can shape the specification rather than answer it.

signals.bank_theme: PrivatBank — Thales payShield HSM refresh running entirely outside Printec
signals.signal: PrivatBank refreshes its payment-key estate continuously, and every purchase goes to a non-Printec reseller through an uncompeted direct award. There have been seven payShield awards in twelve months. The first was EUR 219,250 on 24/09/2025. The second was EUR 199,630 on 13/11/2025. The third was UAH 11,125,380 on 14/11/2025. On 23/05/2026 the bank awarded EUR 282,450 for 3 payShield 10000 Standard Build units with the PS10-RPM-X Premium 2,500 cps package, to Apius Technologies SA of Poland (UA-2026-05-23-000548-a). BUDKONTAKT AS (EDRPOU 38858287) took Lviv, Ternopil, Khmelnytskyi, Poltava and Cherkasy at UAH 5,600,000, on a contract running 03/01/2026 to 02/01/2027.
