Every one was a reported direct contract. Separately, PrivatBank has just opened PB-2026-08-27-3072187, published 27/08/2026. It is a nationwide 18-lot framework for maintenance and repair of bank safes, doors, vaults and other banking equipment. Questions close 03/09/2026 12:00 UTC. Bids and the auction follow on 11/09/2026. There are 16 regional lots, several of them flagged as Ukrainian-controlled front-line territory, plus 2 nationwide lots. The structure lets a bidder take a single oblast (A2).
signals.date: 02/01/2027 — the Budkontakt regional logistics contract expires and the Polovetskyi contract runs only to end-2026, so the next annual round is tendered Nov–Dec 2026. Nearer deadline: 03/09/2026 12:00 UTC, questions close on the 18-lot safe-maintenance framework (auction 11/09/2026)
signals.implies: Paying sixteen suppliers, two of them sole traders, roughly UAH 49m a year to move machines around is a coordination cost that one national field-services vendor could remove. This capacity is also the physical precondition for installing any new recycler fleet. It therefore becomes a gating factor as soon as the hardware programme restarts. The 18-lot safe framework is a low-risk way in, because Printec can bid for one oblast rather than commit to national coverage.
signals.likelihood: High — the regional lots re-tender annually and the current round expires at end-2026
signals.follow_up: Build the full list of counterparties per oblast, and model a combined national install, relocate and field-service offer. Put that to PrivatBank before the Nov–Dec 2026 round, instead of bidding oblast by oblast. Separately, register on tender.privatbank.ua and submit questions on PB-2026-08-27-3072187 before 03/09/2026 12:00 UTC. Ask whether the UAH 22,786.78 per-lot figure is a rate or a ceiling.
signals.product_review_why: The opportunity is a national ATM install and relocation field service, plus a safe and vault maintenance framework.

signals.bank_theme: Sense Bank — live HSM support + ATM cassette repair tenders
signals.signal: This account has grown far beyond the master row's two small lots, and a competitor has just taken the biggest piece with no opposition. The live and material item is UA-2026-08-19-010667-a, for servicing of self-service banking terminals plus support of their communications equipment. It is worth UAH 29,777,476.47 excluding VAT, about EUR 573k, on a 12-month term from 01/09/2026 to 31/08/2027. Bids closed 28/08/2026, and RENOME-SMART LLC (EDRPOU 32625525) was the sole bidder, with the award raised 28/08/2026 pending qualification (A2, A5, A6). Alongside it sits UA-2026-08-21-002726-a, for post-warranty service of the POS terminal estate, at UAH 18,395,006.43 excluding VAT in three lots. It closes 01/09/2026, with zero bids recorded as at 31/08/2026. Lot 1 (UAH 9,631,912.05) covers Verifone and Castles Saturn 1000F2 terminals, which is exactly the hardware Printec Ukraine supplied to PrivatBank at 39,000-unit scale. Lot 2 is Ingenico (UAH 6,249,162.06) and lot 3 is PAX (UAH 2,513,932.32) (A5, A6). The master row's cassette lot ended in a cancellation and re-run. UA-2026-07-30-004472-a was cancelled and relaunched as UA-2026-08-17-003847-a at the same UAH 432,200, and it drew three bidders. Lot 1, for Wincor cassettes, is pending to RENOME-SMART at UAH 353,424. Lot 2, for NCR cassettes, is pending to TOV Svit Innovatsii ta Tekhnolohii (EDRPOU 43440342) at UAH 76,000 (A2, A5, A6). A twice-failed physical-security maintenance lot is still unfilled. It is CPV 50610000-4, UAH 722,530 incl. VAT, covering time-delay cash safes from Koval Systems, Euro Multi and Smart Multi, and deposit lockers with Rosengrens and Diebold locks. UA-2026-05-26-000817-a drew two bidders, SalesServiceSolutions at UAH 136,620 and Paritet-K at UAH 524,780, but was declared unsuccessful. The re-run of 12/06/2026 drew none (A6). There is also a governance risk that directly affects contract approval. Management board chair Stupak was suspended and supervisory board member Hladyshenko removed by Cabinet decision on 22/08/2026, after NABU published material in the "Midas" case. The NBU began unscheduled inspections into alleged interference with the bank's automated systems on 21/08/2026. On 27/08/2026 it publicly called on the government to restore the bank's governing bodies. Peter Novak, a career banking operations and IT executive from Tatra Banka, RBI Vienna, VUB and Prima Banka, joined the supervisory board on 24/08/2026 (A1, A5).
signals.date: 01/09/2026 — the UAH 18.4m POS post-warranty service lot closes with no bids yet. Immediately before: 28/08/2026, the UAH 29.8m self-service service contract went to RENOME-SMART on a single bid, contract starting 01/09/2026
signals.implies: Sense Bank outsourced both device channels in the same two weeks, and the larger contract went to a single domestic bidder with no contest. The POS lot closing 01/09/2026 is the last near-term chance, and lot 1 covers Printec's own Verifone and Castles ground. The twice-failed physical-security lot is the cheap way in. The market turned it down twice, so a direct-negotiation quote is realistic, priced against a known UAH 137k–525k range rather than against an empty field. However, a bank with a suspended chief executive and an incomplete supervisory board cannot cleanly approve a multi-year managed-service contract. Novak should therefore be treated as a patient relationship route rather than a short-cycle trigger.
signals.likelihood: High — three procurements are in qualification or closing now, the service contract starts 01/09/2026, and the security lot must be re-run
signals.follow_up: Confirm whether Printec Ukraine is registered on the it.ua marketplace that Sense Bank uses, and whether the 01/09/2026 POS deadline can still be met. If it cannot, pull the award and target the 2027 renewal. Approach Sense Bank facilities and security procurement now on the twice-failed CPV 50610000-4 lot, with a direct-negotiation quote for Diebold and Rosengrens lock servicing. Check whether Printec Slovakia can source Koval Systems spares, since Koval is a Slovak manufacturer. Get Annex 1.2 of UA-2026-08-19-010667-a, which lists the terminal fleet by model.
signals.product_review_why: The live lots are self-service terminal servicing, POS post-warranty service and a failed safe-lock maintenance lot.

signals.bank_theme: Ukrgasbank — 81-ATM competitive loss + Printec software incumbency
signals.signal: The account has settled into a rolling ATM lifecycle programme across several makers, held end to end by one small local firm, and none of it was competitively tendered. There are three fresh awards, all to TOV SalesServiceSolutions (EDRPOU 39906179, Brovary), and all filed as contract-conclusion reports with no e-auction. The first is ATM modernisation at UAH 1,927,692 incl. VAT, awarded 26/08/2026 (UA-2026-08-26-012958-a). It covers a PC-core refresh of 112 NCR SelfServ machines, with delivery by 31/12/2026. The breakdown is 43x SelfServ 6623/6627 with Riverside cores, 43x SelfServ 6622/6626 with Pocono cores and 26x SelfServ 6622/6626 with Talladega cores. The second is an NFC contactless-reader retrofit on 20 ATMs at UAH 429,600, awarded 16/07/2026. The third is service maintenance of Wincor-built ATMs at UAH 172,599.46, on a contract running 01/07/2026 to 30/06/2027 (A2, A5, A6). The same firm also holds Ukrgasbank's Hyosung ATM servicing contract. It was extended by amendment on 27/04/2026 to 31/05/2027, with the ceiling raised to UAH 2,490,000 incl. VAT (A6). The compliance opening is now explicit. The Wincor service contract was amended on 10/08/2026 to add restated ATM restore-time SLA norms and a new Annex 14. That annex is a PCI DSS responsibility matrix, which splits card-data security duties between bank and vendor. The Hyosung contract carries the same Annex 14 (A2, A6). Master-row evidence is carried forward. The 81-ATM purchase, made up of 36 through-the-wall machines, 37 lobby machines and 8 full-cycle recyclers, was awarded on 16/04/2026 to TOV ATM sistems at UAH 49,720,800. Printec was the initially selected supplier in the failed first run, and lost on qualification paperwork rather than on price.
signals.date: 26/08/2026 — ATM modernisation award covering 112 NCR SelfServ PC-core refreshes. Forward deadlines: Hyosung service contract expires 31/05/2027 and Wincor service 30/06/2027, so the re-tender window opens Q1-2027
signals.implies: A local firm is doing lifecycle work on NCR SelfServ hardware, including PC-core upgrades and contactless retrofits, at a bank where Printec has only a small software foothold. It is getting that work with no competition run. Price is not the point to attack, because SalesServiceSolutions will always win on price. The point to attack is the PCI DSS responsibility matrix and the restore-time SLAs that the bank itself has started writing into these contracts. A formal split of card-security duties is far easier to sign for a vendor with an audited compliance practice than for a small servicer. The size should be stated honestly: the whole Hyosung second-year ceiling is about EUR 33k. This is a reference and a foothold at a state bank, not revenue.
signals.likelihood: High — a verified stream of awards across three consecutive months, with two datable renewals in H1-2027
signals.follow_up: Engage Ukrgasbank now, well before the Q1-2027 renewals, because this buyer awards outside the e-system and watching the portal will be too late. Lead with NCR-authorised PC-core and contactless upgrade kits, multivendor ATM software, SLAs backed by telemetry, and a signed PCI DSS responsibility matrix. Find out whether SalesServiceSolutions gets genuine NCR kits through an authorised channel, and whether it holds any Hyosung authorisation at all. That one fact changes the pitch. Also run the bid-compliance post-mortem on the 81-ATM disqualification.
signals.product_review_why: A local firm holds ATM upgrade and service work, and the bank's new PCI DSS responsibility matrix is the angle to win it.

signals.bank_theme: Oschadbank — competitive cash-automation entry point
signals.signal: The master row's two live lots have been decided, and the wider picture is now clearer: a large, slowly shrinking branch estate with no self-service spend at all. On safes, UA-2026-07-30-007518-a, estimated at UAH 1,951,000, was awarded on 25/08/2026 to sole bidder TOV AV-PROM (EDRPOU 42915052) at UAH 1,001,484. That is 48.7% below the buyer's own estimate. A second, larger lot, UA-2026-08-04-009239-a, estimated at UAH 2,433,125, is pending to TOV Nikol (EDRPOU 20148124) at UAH 2,199,999 against Paritet-K (A2, A5, A6). An independent Prozorro re-sweep found no Oschadbank ATM or self-service lot in the period, which is a confirmed negative (A5). Even so, the demand case is the strongest in the country. The NBU branch register at 01/07/2026 shows Oschadbank running 1,115 operating structural subdivisions, by far the largest estate in Ukraine, down only 16 (-1.4%) in H1-2026. It is therefore not cutting its way out of teller cost. It also has 640 temporarily suspended subdivisions, a dormant pool larger than any private bank's whole network (A1, A4). Together with PrivatBank, Raiffeisen and PUMB, it carries a legal duty to exchange the withdrawn 1, 2, 5 and 10 hryvnia notes free and without limit until 28/02/2029. Ordinary banks lose that duty on 26/02/2027. This is regulator-ordered manual teller work in a network the bank is keeping (A1). Its ability to pay has got worse. H1-2026 net profit fell 2.9x to UAH 3.38bn, dropping the bank from second to fourth in the sector, against total assets of UAH 518.87bn. A 50% temporary bank corporate tax rate is in force, and UAH 4.8bn of dividends were paid to the state budget (A1). There are two further ways in. Oschadbank went live as an open-banking ASPSP on 03/08/2026, meaning a bank that opens its accounts to licensed third-party apps. It is also one of the 26 banks in the NBU's 2026 resilience assessment (A1, A5).
signals.date: 25/08/2026 — first safes lot awarded at 48.7% below estimate; second lot pending. Context: H1-2026 profit down 2.9x reported 14/08/2026; branch register at 01/07/2026
signals.implies: Oschadbank is buying safes, which are the manual alternative to a teller cash recycler, and it buys them one deal at a time on price from single local bidders. A hardware-only pitch will therefore lose, and a long education cycle should be expected. The right framing is the opposite of the one used at PrivatBank. Raiffeisen is shrinking hard and needs self-service to replace counters. Oschadbank is keeping a 1,115-branch footprint and needs efficiency inside it, with a legal small-note exchange duty running to 2029 that guarantees manual counter volume. A bank whose profit fell threefold will sign operating expenditure rather than capital expenditure. So lead with cash automation inside a managed-service wrapper, and use the 04/09/2026 banknote work as the entry point the bank cannot avoid.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the buyer is active and accessible but is currently in a low-tech, price-led buying pattern with no self-service line visible
signals.follow_up: Use the named branch-equipment procurement desk that ran both safes lots as the way in for a teller-cash-recycler and branch-transformation pitch. Register Printec Ukraine on Oschadbank's Prozorro procurements, and watch its ATM and security categories. Open on the 04/09/2026 banknote reconfiguration and the open-banking security layer, rather than on safes. Note that the bank's own site sits behind an Imperva challenge. Its H1-2026 interim report, capex line and ATM count therefore still need a browser session or a direct ask.
signals.product_review_why: A large branch estate with manual teller volume suits teller cash recyclers sold inside a managed-service wrapper.

signals.bank_theme: Ukrposhta — POS estate + CIT outsourcing; Printec already qualified
signals.signal: The master row's open cash-in-transit item has been decided, and the largest self-service opportunity has gone to a named rival. On cash-in-transit, UA-2026-07-17-010455-a covers collection and delivery of valuables in Kyiv, at 66,736 service units, estimated at UAH 18,352,400 excl. VAT. There was a single bidder, so there was no auction. It was won by PAT KB Akordbank (EDRPOU 35960913), a commercial bank rather than a cash-in-transit firm, at UAH 18,018,720, a 1.82% saving. The award was made 31/07/2026. The contract was signed 17/08/2026 and runs to 31/12/2027 (A2). On parcel lockers, UA-2026-05-05-011053-a covers 1,000 main modules plus 1,000 type-1 and 200 type-2 additional modules. It also covers 100 high-autonomy batteries, 50 chargers and 500 solar panels, with installation, and delivery by 31/07/2027. It was won by the Ukrainian-Polish joint venture Modern-Expo (EDRPOU 21751578) at UAH 195,999,000 incl. VAT, about EUR 3.77m, against a UAH 211,932,000 estimate. The award was made 25/05/2026 and the contract was signed 09/06/2026. The only other bidder was TOV Trio-Treid (A2, A6). Master-row evidence is carried forward and still valid. Verifone POS estate maintenance went to a sole bidder at UAH 42,020,013.60, and card processing went to UKRCARD at UAH 69,774,360, also as sole bidder. Printec Ukraine is already a cleared supplier to Ukrposhta and has delivered 150 POS batteries (UA-2026-05-06-007814-a, 20/05/2026).
signals.date: 17/08/2026 — Kyiv CIT contract signed with Akordbank, locked to 31/12/2027. Context: parcel-locker contract signed 09/06/2026 with Modern-Expo, delivering to 31/07/2027
signals.implies: Two doors have shut and one stays open. The lockers have gone to an established CEE manufacturer, and the cash-in-transit route runs through a banking licence rather than a vendor contract, so neither can be won. What remains, and still matters, is that every layer here is bought as a service, with no competition, at or near budget. Printec is already a cleared supplier, which is the hard part. The winnable next step is counter automation, branch transformation and combined terminal-estate management, rather than lockers or cash logistics. Modern-Expo should also be logged as a credible rival to Printec in postal self-service across the whole footprint, not only in Ukraine.
signals.likelihood: Medium — the CIT and locker contracts are locked into 2027; regional CIT lots and the POS estate-management renewal recur sooner
signals.follow_up: Use the cleared-supplier status to bid for the POS estate-management renewal, and propose a combined terminal-estate-management offer against the single-bidder incumbents. Do not chase Modern-Expo on lockers. Instead, map its references in Poland, Romania and the Baltics. That will show whether it is likely to appear against Printec in the Posta Slovenije, Posta Romana and Slovenska posta renewals. Treat Akordbank as a possible cash-logistics partner rather than a competitor.
signals.product_review_why: The winnable next step is the POS estate-management renewal plus counter automation and branch transformation, all bought as a service.

signals.bank_theme: NBU — UAH 2,000 banknote fleet reconfiguration (~38,700 devices, Aug–Dec 2026)
signals.signal: The device count is now confirmed from the NBU's own data file rather than from the press, and a second dated regulatory workstream has opened. The UAH 2,000 note (Vasyl Stus, 75x166 mm) enters circulation on 04/09/2026. It is a completely new highest denomination. The NBU's banknotes-in-circulation page still lists only 1000/500/200/100/50/20, which confirms that it is not yet issued (A1, A4). The exact estate at 01/07/2026, taken from NBU PC_table_1.xlsx, is 38,721 self-service devices. That is 15,768 ATMs and 22,953 PTKS self-service payment kiosks, against 38,685 devices at 01/06/2026 (A4). The NBU is giving banks, cash-in-transit firms and device service companies free technical configuration capability during August 2026. It says this is the first time it has run such a procedure before a banknote's circulation date. The reason is that the materials cannot be released until the note is declassified at its presentation (A4). Separately and new this cycle, on 26/08/2026 the NBU opened consultation on changes to the Instruction on organising bank cash operations. The changes are driven expressly by preparation for the new denomination. They add the note to the list of notes banks must hand back to the NBU, and refine the standard packaging-material specifications for 2,000-hryvnia notes. Written comments close 04/09/2026 inclusive (A1). The scope should be clear. That resolution covers hand-back lists and packaging, so the validator and recycler work is a commercial consequence of the new note, and not something the resolution requires. PTKS kiosks are 59% of the fleet, rather than bank ATMs. So the work lands heavily on independent kiosk operators such as EasyPay, iBox and City24. These operators have thinner engineering teams than banks (A4).
signals.date: 04/09/2026 — the note enters circulation, and the same day comments close on the NBU's cash-operations amendments. Free configuration materials opened August 2026; the reconfiguration itself runs on past the circulation date
signals.implies: A fixed-date, market-wide field-services and firmware event across roughly 38,700 devices: note-template and firmware updates on every acceptor, dispenser, recycler and back-office sorter, cassette re-planning, changes to the denomination mix in cash forecasting, and device-by-device checks. Because a new **highest** denomination changes the cassette mix and the economics of refilling, it also triggers a re-tune of cash forecasting. Commercially this is not a 04/09 cliff but a race that starts on 04/09 and is won on speed and verified coverage of every device. The devices still not done after the date are the retrofit pipeline.
signals.likelihood: Certain — the note enters circulation 04/09/2026 and the device counts are from the NBU's own file
signals.follow_up: Get the NBU draft resolution, impact analysis and comparison table posted 26/08/2026 for the exact packaging specifications. File or track comments before 04/09/2026. Find out which note-set and firmware versions NCR Atleos, Glory, Sesami and the bill-validator vendors have released for the UAH 2,000 note. From 05/09/2026, chase which banks and which PTKS operators still cannot accept or dispense it, because that list is the pipeline. Also test whether the 6 mm extra length forces any cassette hardware change, as no source currently says it does.
signals.product_review_why: A new banknote forces firmware and cassette work on every ATM, recycler and payment kiosk, delivered as a field-services race.

signals.bank_theme: NBU Resolution No. 67 — mandatory one-time-password identity capture at self-service cash-in terminals
signals.signal: This resolution was re-checked line by line against the official 9-page NBU PDF this cycle, and is now sized against the exact device count. Resolution No. 67 of 16/06/2026 was officially published on 18/06/2026. It came into force on 26/06/2026. New clause 124-2 applies to every cash-in at a self-service payment kiosk, whatever the amount. It requires the payer to key their full mobile number on the kiosk screen. The provider or its commercial agent must then check that the payer owns that number, using a one-time password sent by SMS or read out by phone call. The payer keys that password on the kiosk screen. Clause 124-3 obliges the provider, including where commercial agents are used, to take continuous steps to make it impossible or less risky to pass the password to someone else. That includes shortening how long the password is valid. Clause 124-4 has a much longer list of exemptions than first reported. It covers budget payments, meaning taxes, fines and administrative-service fees. It covers utilities under the Housing-Services Law, plus fixed telephony, TV, internet and security. It covers rail tickets including suburban, urban and suburban transport fares including e-tickets, route passenger transport, and transport-card top-ups. It also covers mobile-service payments within the provider up to UAH 500 per month per number, and cash-in to top up an account with an issued payment instrument. The resolution also sets cash-handling rules for the new financial-inclusion bank licence type and its commercial agents (A4). On scope, there were 22,953 PTKS kiosks at 01/07/2026. Each one needs a screen-flow change plus SMS or voice one-time-password integration (A4).
signals.date: 26/06/2026 — in force; a non-compliant terminal may not execute the cash-in at all. Re-verified against the official PDF and sized at 22,953 kiosks as at 01/07/2026
signals.implies: Every cash-in kiosk in Ukraine needs a new screen flow, an SMS or voice one-time-password integration, and a remote roll-out across a fleet that cannot be visited machine by machine. That is a terminal-management job rather than a site visit. Clause 124-3 makes the risk of password-sharing, which is money-mule activity, a standing legal duty. It is therefore a rules-and-monitoring requirement rather than a one-off interface patch. The broad exemption list cuts both ways. Operators will want conditional branching rather than one blanket prompt, which means more integration work, not less.
signals.likelihood: In force since 26/06/2026 — the remediation demand is immediate, and the ban on executing the payment makes non-compliance an outage rather than a project
signals.follow_up: Ask EasyPay, iBox and City24 directly how they built the one-time-password step and the exemption branching, and whether the NBU has started enforcing it. The independent operators are the ones most likely to be short of capacity. Approach banks on the receipt-retention and monitoring feed, not only on the terminal interface. Combine the pitch with the UAH 2,000 note reconfiguration, since both land on the same 22,953 kiosks in the same quarter.
signals.product_review_why: Every cash-in kiosk needs a new screen flow rolled out remotely, and the password-sharing duty adds a standing monitoring requirement.

signals.bank_theme: NBU Resolution No. 81 — customer verification methods widened for financial inclusion
signals.signal: The master row's headline needs correcting. Two agents separately re-checked Resolution No. 81 of 15/07/2026 against the NBU's own notice of 16/07/2026 and the official legal portal. Neither found the geolocation, geotagging, photo-metadata-timestamp or no-editing requirements that the master row leads with (A3, A4). What is confirmed is different and narrower. The resolution amends the Regulation on banks' financial monitoring, which is Regulation No. 65 of 19/05/2020, and it came into force on 17/07/2026. First, it allows the original identity document to be presented during verification by a third party, meaning an accompanying or authorised person. That document may also be handled by the verifying bank employee where the client cannot present it alone. Second, it allows the client's consent to a photo to be shown by audio or video recording, where a handwritten or electronic signature is impossible. Separately, under the financial-inclusion law, the new financial-inclusion bank licence type may use a commercial agent. That agent may establish the beneficiary of a transaction, and carry out identification and verification under the same regulation. The NBU adopted the surrounding rules for this type of institution in June 2026 (A3, A4). The master row's other elements were not re-confirmed this cycle and should be treated as unverified. Those elements are acceptance of the Diia e-passport and the electronic taxpayer card including QR versions, and replacing "authorised employee" with "authorised bank employee or qualified electronic seal".
signals.date: 17/07/2026 — in force; compliance required now. The financial-inclusion bank package was adopted in June 2026 and the first licences are the forward trigger
signals.implies: Ukraine has made agent-assisted and third-party-assisted verification legal, with consent captured on audio or video. That is a real fit for a digital-onboarding and e-signature stack: video identification, audio and video consent capture, and qualified timestamping. It can be delivered through tablets and kiosks at agent points rather than in branches. Most importantly, it creates a new kind of buyer that has never bought branch technology. That buyer is the agent networks, post offices and retailers acting for a financial-inclusion bank, which need an onboarding device and eKYC software instead of a branch. The master row's remediation-buy framing rested on the geotag claim, and it does not survive this cycle's re-reading.
signals.likelihood: In force since 17/07/2026; agent-based and financial-inclusion-bank onboarding scales through 2026–2027 as licences are issued
signals.follow_up: Get the consolidated text of Regulation No. 65 as amended, and map the capture and consent requirements to the Namirial video-KYC flow. Do not brief the geotag or unedited-photo requirement until it is found in the amended annex text. Two agents looked for it this cycle and neither found it. Track the first financial-inclusion bank licences, and who supplies their agent-onboarding stack. Clear any biometric or photo-capture design with Printec's DPO before pitching.
signals.product_review_why: Agent-assisted verification with recorded consent is a video-KYC and e-signature sale, delivered on tablets and kiosks at agent points.

signals.bank_theme: NBU — AML enforcement biting at named banks, plus a published 2026 inspection calendar and an outsourcing-friendly monitoring rule
signals.signal: Three strands come together into the clearest dated compliance trigger in this market. **(1) Fines, published 07/08/2026** for July enforcement against 2 banks and 19 non-bank institutions: **JSC Raiffeisen Bank fined UAH 16,100,000** for poor customer due diligence (checks on who customers are), not using a risk-based approach and risk-reduction measures, not managing risks from new and existing information products, business practices or technologies (including those that allow transactions without direct customer contact), late reporting of threshold transactions, and not giving the NBU complete information. It also received a written warning covering missing enhanced measures on politically exposed persons, **failure to configure and automate generation of the standard response forms in Annex 1 to Regulation No. 90**, not updating customer questionnaires within 10 working days, and not passing on all received payer information on transfers. **JSC Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital fined UAH 42,545,000** in total, including the same automation failure and being unable to give data to inspectors on time (A3, A4). **(2) A named, dated inspection calendar**: the NBU's plan, revised 31/07/2026 and updated 25/08/2026, lists Q1 Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital, Q2 Cominbank and UkrSibbank, Q3 Sky Bank and EPB, **Q4-2026 Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD**. The chain is already proven: the Q1 bank was fined in July (A3). **(3) A draft resolution on payment-service-provider control over payment operations** (consultation opened 17/07/2026, closed 14/08/2026, comments published 21/08/2026) sets single standard approaches to monitoring and reconciling payment operations, and **explicitly allows third parties to perform parts of the monitoring function**. That is regulatory permission to sell monitoring as a managed service. It also adds anti-miscoding measures and a set list of signs of unusual user behaviour (A4). Related pressure at the top of the market: the NBU opened unscheduled inspections of Sense Bank on 21/08/2026 over alleged **interference with, and switching off of, the bank's automated systems** during transactions. It stated that finding and stopping suspicious transactions is the banks' own duty (A1).
signals.date: 07/08/2026 — fines published against Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine and Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital. Forward: Q4-2026 on-site AML inspections at Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD, which must be briefed before end-September 2026
signals.implies: The regulator is fining banks by name for exactly the things this software does. Those things are risk scoring, customer due diligence and profile data quality, screening of politically exposed persons, threshold-transaction detection, and complete payer data on transfers. They also include failure to automate the regulator's own response forms. Fixes follow NBU orders within one supervisory cycle, so budget is committed at once rather than at the next planning round. The published inspection calendar turns this from a general argument into three named accounts with a known deadline. The draft monitoring resolution matters more still, because it allows the monitoring function to be outsourced. That is explicit permission to sell it as a managed service to providers that cannot staff a 24/7 desk.
signals.likelihood: Very high — the NBU publishes enforcement monthly, the inspection plan is binding on the regulator, and remediation is mandatory
signals.follow_up: Approach Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine on risk scoring, screening of politically exposed persons and client-data clean-up, citing the 07/08/2026 findings. Brief Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD before end-September, ahead of their Q4 inspections. Pull the August and September NBU enforcement notices. Read the comments file published 21/08/2026 on the monitoring draft, because it names which providers pushed back and on what. That is a qualified prospect list. Track the adopted resolution and its transition period.
signals.product_review_why: Named AML fines and an inspection calendar drive compliance-suite and transaction-monitoring spend, and the draft rule lets monitoring be outsourced.

signals.bank_theme: NBU Resolution No. 85 — TrekSEP payment-tracking duties, one-hour SLA already live
signals.signal: This is a dated payments-tracking rule that is already binding, rather than a future deadline. NBU Board Resolution No. 85 of 05/08/2026 was officially published 06/08/2026. It amends the Instruction on interbank payment operations in the national currency, which is Resolution No. 16 of 03/03/2023. It defines the TrekSEP message and service, a support service that lets users track the stages of a SEP payment. It also defines the concept of a SEP instant-transfer participant. New point 46-4 applies to every SEP participant. It must send the payment-execution status to the SEP central processor as soon as possible, and no later than one hour after that status is set. This covers the status set in the participant's own automation system, and in the system of any non-bank provider settling through an account with that participant. New point 46-5 obliges the participant to let the user check payment status remotely by sending a TrekSEP message. It must also return the execution-stage information to the user through the remote channel. A critical correction is confirmed from the legal text. Point 4 of the resolution delays only paragraphs five to seven of sub-point 3 of point 1, that is point 46-5 and its two sub-points only, to 01/01/2027. Everything else, including the one-hour status-push duty in point 46-4, took effect the day after publication, on 07/08/2026 (A3, A5). For context, SEP carries over 99% of Ukrainian interbank payments. It is a designated systemically important RTGS, or real-time settlement system, running 24/7 on ISO 20022 since 01/04/2023. It averages 1.5m payments a day worth about UAH 778bn. It has offered instant credit transfer within 10 seconds since 01/12/2024, and SEP-4.2 with multi-currency support is being developed. The NBU also says it is preparing the ground for eventual SEPA accession (A3).
signals.date: 07/08/2026 — the one-hour status-push duty to the SEP central processor is already in force; the customer-facing TrekSEP query and status display follow on 01/01/2027
signals.implies: Any Ukrainian bank or non-bank provider without end-to-end payment-status tracking is out of compliance now. Banks are also expressly made responsible for the status data of the non-bank providers settling through their accounts, and most will not have connected them. By 01/01/2027 the same institutions must also offer a status query and show the tracking stages in mobile and internet banking. The order of work is transaction tracking first and channel work second. Because the duty is already binding, it should move budget faster than a January date would. The customer-facing half is the part second-tier banks are least likely to have built.
signals.likelihood: Very high — this is a published normative act and the entry-into-force dates were read directly from the text
signals.follow_up: Request the TrekSEP message specification from the NBU Department of Payment Systems and Innovative Development. Start talking to second-tier banks now about how they plan to show TrekSEP status in their channels before 01/01/2027. Confirm the paragraph-count reading of point 4 with Ukrainian counsel before telling any client it is already in breach.
signals.product_review_why: The duty is end-to-end payment-status tracking on the ISO 20022 rail first, then showing that status in digital channels.

signals.bank_theme: NBU Resolutions No. 70, 72 and 73 — third-party risk management now binding on banks and payment providers
signals.signal: Three NBU Board Resolutions introduce third-party risk management, which means managing the risks that come from outside suppliers. All three are dated 30/06/2026 and all took effect on 01/07/2026. Resolution No. 70 covers banks and banking groups, and amends the Regulation on the organisation of the risk-management system. Resolution No. 72 covers financial payment service providers, and Resolution No. 73 covers insurers. The NBU's own notice confirms the requirements. Institutions must identify, assess, control, monitor and reduce third-party risks. They must **assess counterparties in advance, covering financial condition, business reputation and operational capability**. Contracts must meet minimum requirements, and provider compliance must be monitored on an ongoing basis. Institutions must also set out the actions to take when a provider, or a critical provider, falls short. Business-continuity management must take third-party risk into account, and termination and exit plans are required. Institutions must set criteria for when a third-party relationship creates critical risk to continuity or to clients. The NBU says institutions have "sufficient time" to review existing supplier contracts, but it publishes no transition date. The stated legal basis is Basel Committee recommendations, the payment services directive and Solvency II. It is not the IMF memorandum, PSD2 Article 20 or an EBA consultation paper, which were the basis assumed before. One further point was verified separately. NBU Resolution No. 143 of 09/12/2025, on organising information-security and cyber-protection measures by financial service providers, exists and came into force on 13/12/2025. The widely quoted "13/12/2026 transition end" could not be confirmed and is not stated on the NBU legislation page (A3). This regime applies directly to Printec's own supplier contracts, and it also creates new demand.

sources.text: NBU — third-party risk management requirements established

signals.date: 01/07/2026 — in force for banks, payment service providers and insurers; contract re-papering is live now with no published transition deadline
signals.implies: Every Ukrainian bank must now list, pre-assess and continuously monitor each critical technology supplier. That includes ATM and recycler vendors and outsourced field-service providers. Banks must also hold written exit plans. This has two effects for Printec. It raises the due-diligence standard an existing supplier has to meet, so Printec's Ukrainian contracts need checking against the critical-contract criteria. It also creates budgeted demand in three areas. The first is auditable device telemetry, which means remote data from the devices themselves. The second is monitoring, managed and field services backed by service level agreements. The third is documented continuity and exit evidence. Ukrgasbank has already started writing this same compliance-grade wrapper into its ATM service contracts.
signals.likelihood: High — already in force since 01/07/2026, and re-papering of existing supplier contracts is under way
signals.follow_up: Get the text of Resolution No. 70 from zakon.rada.gov.ua, because the SSL handshake to that host failed this run. Use it to find any transition deadline for re-papering existing supplier contracts. Use it also to confirm or reject the 13/12/2026 date attributed to Resolution No. 143. That date should not be quoted to a client until it is sourced. Confirm whether Printec's Ukrainian contracts meet the NBU's critical-contract criteria, before a bank's own review reaches them.
signals.product_review_why: Third-party risk rules create demand for resilience evidence and for telemetry and SLA-backed managed services, and Printec's own contracts fall in scope.

signals.bank_theme: Ukraine open banking — ASPSP platform layer already delivered by a named incumbent
signals.signal: This corrects the reading in the master row. The bank-side build for open banking, known as the ASPSP side, is not an opportunity still to be bought. It has already been delivered. On 03/08/2026 the Open API HUB, via the EMA association, announced that OTP Bank, Sense Bank and Oschadbank had officially joined Ukraine's open-banking ecosystem. All three run Open API HUB's "API KIT" solution, deployed on-premise inside each bank's own perimeter. Credit Agricole Bank and MTB Bank are at the final implementation stage (A1, A5). API KIT ships the full stack. It includes an API specification based on Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 / openFinance, plus consent management. It includes third-party-provider verification against the NBU payment-infrastructure register, with certificate validation. It adds an admin and monitoring platform with call logs and limits, a developer portal and dynamic sandbox, and a standard core-banking connector. The regime itself is confirmed. It rests on NBU Board Resolutions No. 80, 81 and 82 of 25/07/2025. Those sit on top of Resolution No. 58 of 03/05/2023 on strong customer authentication, and Resolution No. 43 of 19/05/2021 on information protection. Banks must expose compliant account-information and payment-initiation APIs by 01/08/2026. They must also publish API technical documentation, and verify each provider's authorisation in real time before granting access (A1, A5). The NBU's machine-readable register, pulled 31/08/2026, shows only three authorised institutions. All three are banks, and all were authorised in 2026. PUMB was authorised from 02/03/2026 and PrivatBank from 06/03/2026. UkrSibbank followed from 01/05/2026. That gives exactly six active service entries, one payment-initiation and one account-information per bank. No non-bank third-party provider is yet authorised (A6).

sources.text: EMA / Open API HUB — three banks live on API KIT

signals.date: 03/08/2026 — Oschadbank, OTP Bank and Sense Bank went live on a competitor's platform; the 01/08/2026 statutory deadline has passed and the register was re-pulled 31/08/2026
signals.implies: The API, consent, strong-authentication and certificate-verification work at the large Ukrainian banks is sunk cost held by a named incumbent. It is not a platform sale, and it should be dropped from the account plans. Three honest smaller angles remain, and all of them are adjacent. The first is hardware security module and key management work behind the on-premise deployments. A hardware security module is a secure device used to store payment encryption keys. The second is API traffic security and fraud analytics on top of the new payment-initiation rail. The third is the mid-tier banks that have not gone live. The thin register is also useful negative evidence. With no non-bank provider authorised, the risk of apps cutting banks out of the customer relationship has not yet formed in Ukraine. Near-term competitive pressure therefore remains in hardware, ATM service and cash automation.
signals.likelihood: High that the API layer stays with the incumbent through 2027; medium that adjacent security and monitoring scope opens as account-information coverage widens
signals.follow_up: Drop the bank-side API build from the Oschadbank, OTP and Sense Bank plans. Ask Open API HUB and the banks who supplies the hardware security module and key management around API KIT. Ask the same question about the API-gateway security layer, and whether payment-initiation transaction monitoring is in anyone's scope yet. Find which mid-tier banks have not gone live. That shortlist, not the majors, is the addressable set. Re-pull the NBU register each cycle, because the first non-bank authorisation marks a new class of competitor.
signals.product_review_why: The platform is already sold, so what remains is HSM and key management behind it, API fraud analytics, and the mid-tier banks not yet live.

signals.bank_theme: Ukraine — flat ATM fleet against 96% cashless and continuing branch contraction
signals.signal: The structural case is now backed by exact counts from the NBU's own data file, and the single most useful number has finally been published. PC_table_1.xlsx at 01/07/2026 records 15,768 ATMs. Only 2,785 of them, or **17.7%**, can take deposits. That share has been flat since 2024: 2,624 at 01/01/2024, then 2,754, 2,727 and 2,785. Self-service payment kiosks, known as PTKS, grew 68% in a single year on a smooth monthly path. They rose from 13,310 at 01/01/2025 to 22,376 at 01/01/2026. By 01/07/2026 they reached 22,953. Trade POS terminals reached 582,547, up 4.3% in six months, and card-accepting points reached 699,258, up 13.9%. SoftPOS tap-to-phone devices grew 65% to 69,783, and POS with cash-out reached 319,345 (A4). Cashless payments are 96% of card transactions by count, but only 67% by value. So roughly UAH 1.27tn still came out of the cash channel in H1-2026, across about 196m withdrawals. There are 153.2m cards issued, but only 61.1m are active, or 40%. That is down from 65.4m in January, as state support programmes ended. 21.1m cards (34.5%) are tokenised. About 99% of in-store cashless transactions are contactless, by both count and value (A1, A4). Cash itself is not shrinking. Currency in circulation rose from UAH 759,753m at 01/01/2025 to 866,943m at 01/01/2026. It then reached 921,808m at 01/08/2026, a rise of 14.1% in 2025 and a further 6.3% in seven months (A4). Branches continue to close. There were 4,754 operating structural units at 01/07/2026, down 38 in the quarter and down 5.1% since 01/01/2025. A further 787 are temporarily suspended: Oschadbank 640, Raiffeisen 52 and PrivatBank 2 (A1, A4). Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine shows the steepest reduction. It had 256 business outlets at 30/06/2026 against 295 a year earlier, a fall of 13.2% and the largest cut in RBI outside Russia. Over the same period its customers rose 8.2% to 3.124m (A1). The NBU's 2026 resilience assessment covers 26 named banks holding over 90% of system assets, with results due by 31/12/2026 (A5).
signals.date: 18/08/2026 — NBU H1-2026 card-market release and payment-infrastructure data file published; branch register and device counts as at 01/07/2026
signals.implies: Rising note volumes are handled by a flat ATM estate that is only 17.7% deposit-capable. That means a rising cost per note handled and more reliance on cash-in-transit. This is the strongest structural argument in this market, and it is now a published fact rather than an inference. It points to a replacement and upgrade market, not a market for new footprint. The products that fit are recyclers, which are ATMs that re-use deposited notes, and teller cash recyclers to close the deposit gap. Cash forecasting to cut replenishment runs also fits, as does back-office automation in the 4,754 remaining branches. The 68% kiosk growth makes kiosk hardware, software and managed services the fastest-growing physical channel in the country. Every one of those 22,953 devices is both a Resolution-67 software job and a UAH 2,000 note reconfiguration job. This sizes the demand. It is not itself a procurement.
signals.likelihood: Structural — the series is published monthly and every component moved in the same direction again this cycle
signals.follow_up: Refresh PC_table_1.xlsx and the branch register each quarter. Note that the NBU has flagged the branch dataset for discontinuation, in favour of the bank directory and the open-data API. Capture the API endpoint before the spreadsheet disappears. Chase the one remaining split the NBU does not publish: how many of the 2,785 deposit-capable ATMs are true recyclers rather than deposit-only machines. Use the published 26-bank resilience list as the Ukraine account map, and diarise the 31/12/2026 results. A capital-constrained outcome would push the whole market from capital spending to operating spending.
signals.product_review_why: Rising cash on a low-deposit ATM estate points to recyclers and cash forecasting, while fast kiosk growth pulls in kiosk hardware and services.

signals.bank_theme: Ukraine — domestic full-stack self-service rivals now hold software, hardware and service
signals.signal: Ukraine has domestic vendors that match Printec's whole stack, rather than local parts-and-labour shops. This is the most significant competitive finding of the cycle. RENOME-SMART LLC (EDRPOU 32625525) is a software vendor whose products match Printec's ATM portfolio one for one. RS.Core is central management of all self-service devices linked into banking systems. CashLAB manages the cash cycle across ATMs, terminal networks, cash desks and vaults. X.5 covers device monitoring, fault diagnosis, alerting and remote recovery. Smart Service is a mobile field-service app. Its bid pack holds software-registration certificates for five of its own products. It also makes its own deposit machines, ATMs, banknote sorters, parcel lockers and kiosks in Ukraine. It self-reports 54 service centres, more than 200 specialists including over 60 in research and development, and customers in 15 countries. Its recent wins are as follows. UkrSibbank (BNP Paribas) began moving its entire ATM network onto RS.Core on 25/02/2026. maib, Moldova's largest bank, rolled RS.Core out across its network, announced on 03/04/2026. RENOME-SMART opened Libya on 23/04/2026, with a partner met at a Diebold Nixdorf summit. On 28/08/2026 it took Sense Bank's UAH 29.8m self-service service contract as sole bidder. It had first won the small cassette-repair lot and the PrivatBank condition-assessment lot (A6, A2, A5). Servus Systems Integration (EDRPOU 31089403) is the closest structural match. It has the same Verifone POS franchise, self-service and kiosk lines and field-service model, plus Hyosung TNS ATMs as an NCR alternative. It has 27 service centres and more than 50,000 terminals under service. Its published customer logos cover PrivatBank, Oschadbank, OTP, UkrSibbank, PUMB, Raiffeisen and Ukrposhta (A6). I.B.S. / Inovatsiini Bankivski Systemy (EDRPOU 36184511) holds both the Glory and the Diebold Nixdorf franchises, each for roughly 20 years. It won Glory's "Top Sales Achievements FI 2025/2026" award in April 2026, and Diebold Nixdorf's "Best Performance 2024/25". It already holds PrivatBank's UAH 116.7m contract for 57 Glory UW-F12 sorters. It describes its own work as cash-recycling technology, Diebold Nixdorf software integration and self-service terminal attack protection (A6). Two further names belong on the list. SalesServiceSolutions does NCR SelfServ core refreshes and Hyosung/Wincor service at Ukrgasbank. Bankivski Tekhnolohii supplies sorters at both PrivatBank and Ukrgasbank (A6).
signals.date: 28/08/2026 — RENOME-SMART took Sense Bank's UAH 29.8m self-service service contract unopposed, starting 01/09/2026. Context: UkrSibbank ATM-platform migration to RS.Core began 25/02/2026 and maib Moldova scaled it from 03/04/2026
signals.implies: This changes the competitive picture for the whole market. In Ukraine, Printec cannot rely on multivendor ATM software, telemetry or managed services on their own as differentiators. A domestic vendor sells all three, builds its own hardware and undercuts on price. It has also crossed the border into Moldova, which makes it a regional rival rather than a purely Ukrainian one. A single Kyiv firm holds both the Glory and the Diebold Nixdorf franchises. A Glory-based route into Ukrainian banks therefore cannot be assumed either. The remaining defensible ground is narrower, and Printec should lead with it openly. It is NCR-authorised parts and software, Thales hardware security modules and PCI-PIN, and the AML and eKYC stack. AML means anti-money-laundering, and eKYC means electronic know-your-customer checks. None of these rivals advertise any of those. Treat Sense Bank and UkrSibbank as contested accounts.
signals.likelihood: High — these firms are already inside PrivatBank, Oschadbank, UkrSibbank, Sense Bank, Ukrgasbank, OTP, PUMB, Raiffeisen and Ukrposhta, and will bid every Ukrainian service renewal
signals.follow_up: Add RENOME-SMART, Servus Systems Integration, I.B.S., Bankivski Tekhnolohii, DIIP 2000, SalesServiceSolutions and Svit Innovatsii ta Tekhnolohii to the competitor register with their EDRPOU numbers. Profile RS.Core, CashLAB and X.5 feature by feature against Printec's own software and telemetry line, and build a defensive position from that. Check whether RENOME-SMART is bidding for maib or other Moldovan and CEE accounts against Printec. That is now a question about the whole footprint, not only Ukraine. Establish whether SalesServiceSolutions actually holds NCR and Hyosung authorisation.
signals.product_review_why: Domestic rivals now match Printec's ATM software, telemetry, field service and self-service hardware in one stack.

signals.bank_theme: NCR Atleos / Brink's merger — partner-channel risk (+ Partner of the Year)
signals.signal: The merger now has a set regulatory timetable. The UK Competition and Markets Authority formally opened its Phase 1 merger inquiry into Brink's purchase of NCR Atleos on 26/08/2026, by notice to the parties. It set a statutory Phase 1 decision deadline of **22/10/2026**. That is the material change since last cycle, when only the informal invitation to comment had closed. In parallel, Atleos chief executive Tim Oliver moved the expected completion forward to "early in the first quarter of 2027". Brink's confirmed clearances already secured in the United States, Brazil, India, Turkey and Colombia. It also confirmed foreign-investment clearances in France, Germany, Spain, Italy and the UK. One point needs care. The UK item Brink's management referred to on its call was a foreign-direct-investment clearance, not competition clearance. The CMA competition review only began three weeks later. Atleos held no Q2 earnings call and published no financial outlook, because of the pending deal. As a result, the usual EMEA commentary Printec uses to read its partner has stopped for at least two quarters (A6).

signals.bank_theme: Brink's — ATM-as-a-Service and the bank-consortium outsourcing model
signals.country_raw: Footprint-wide, Greece / Romania / Czechia / Cyprus first
signals.signal: Brink's Q2 2026 results, published 05/08/2026, show that the shift to outsourcing is real, funded and most advanced in Europe. Group revenue was USD 1,392m, up 7%. The ATM Managed Services and Digital Retail Solutions lines grew 14% organically, the fourteenth quarter in a row of mid-teens or better growth. The stated 2026 target is for those lines to reach 30-32% of group revenue. The Europe segment is the proof. Revenue rose from USD 358m to USD 377m, while adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 59m to USD 71m. The margin rose from 16.6% to 18.7%, on only 2% organic growth. That margin gain comes from a shift out of low-margin cash-in-transit into high-margin ATM outsourcing, not from extra volume. Europe now has a 46% outsourcing mix, the highest of Brink's four regions. Brink's also disclosed a new European ATM outsourcing win. Chief executive Mark Eubanks described it on the call. "we were recently awarded a full ATM outsourcing agreement for a network consortium of banks in Europe that will come online over the second half of the year". No country, member banks or estate size were named. Separately, Mellon hosted an ATM Innovation and Strategy Forum in Athens on 01/04/2026, jointly with KAL and Brink's Global AMS. That put the Brink's outsourcing pitch in front of National Bank of Greece and Eurobank decision-makers (A6).

sources.text: Brink's Q2 2026 investor deck, SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.2 (CIK 78890)

signals.date: 05/08/2026 — Q2 results disclose a new European bank-consortium ATM outsourcing win going live in H2-2026; Athens forum 01/04/2026
signals.implies: An ATM consortium is the model that most directly removes Printec's addressable market. When several banks pool their machines into one shared network and outsource the whole thing, they stop buying ATMs, multivendor software, telemetry and field service separately. One contract replaces five. Brink's already runs cash-in-transit in Greece, Romania, Czechia and Cyprus, and each of those relationships is a route into full outsourcing. The defensive move is co-sourcing. Printec should offer x-core, ATM telemetry and monitoring, APTRA OptiCash cash forecasting and field services as the technology layer a consortium buys. That is better than waiting to lose an entire estate to a single end-to-end Brink's bid.
signals.likelihood: High that the pressure is real and growing; moderate that a footprint country hosts the next consortium win within 12 months
signals.follow_up: Listen to the Brink's Q3 2026 call, expected in early November 2026, for the consortium's identity and any first named CEE or SEE outsourcing customer. Test each footprint banking association for live ATM-pooling discussions before a tender exists, starting with Greece. Package Printec's own per-ATM managed offer and lead with it at Alpha Bank, BCR, Erste Croatia and Bank of Cyprus before Q1-2027.
signals.product_review_why: Full ATM outsourcing to a consortium replaces separate ATM, software and service purchases, so the defence is a co-sourced managed offer.

signals.signal: Printec's closest regional rival has publicly reported that its hardware business is shrinking in six of Printec's own countries. ASEE's H1 2026 management report, dated 31/07/2026, puts the Payment Solutions segment at EUR 102.8m. That is down EUR 5.2m, or 5% year on year, with Q2 down 7%. The ATM line fell EUR 3.4m, "primarily from lower equipment deliveries in South-Eastern Europe, particularly in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro". Central Europe was also negative, on lower Romanian deliveries. The POS line fell EUR 1.9m, mainly on lower Slovenian and Croatian deliveries within South-Eastern Europe. The important detail is that Payten is not retreating. It is re-shaping. Its POS operating result rose by EUR 0.3m on growing Serbian recurring revenue, and group Q2 operating profit was up 27%. The order backlog shows contracted revenue flat to down, while contracted margin rises 7-8%. That is the profile of a company taking fewer, better-priced deals. Structurally it is also tightening its grip. It is buying out minorities in Bosnia (BS Telecom, EUR 8.5m), Slovenia (Monri) and Serbia (AFusion). Further put options are outstanding on Dwelt in Bosnia and Helius in Albania. It has no operating entity at all in Greece, Cyprus, Austria or Hungary (A6).

signals.date: 31/07/2026 — H1-2026 report: Payment Solutions EUR 102.8m, -5%; ATM line -EUR 3.4m across RS, HR, BA, ME, RO; next reading 26/10/2026

signals.bank_theme: Euronet — Greece + Croatia + platform pivot (threat)
signals.country_raw: GR, HR, AT, and footprint-wide as a bid narrative
signals.signal: This entry carries two corrections and one confirmation. First, the CrediaBank deal has still not closed. Euronet's Q2 10-Q of 04/08/2026 does not mention CrediaBank anywhere, and no 8-K has been filed since 30/07/2026. The Hellenic Competition Commission's concentration register carried no Euronet notification when checked on 31/08/2026. The stated target remains Q3-2026, which gives a hard decision point of 30/09/2026. That covers the merchant-acquiring business, plus management of CrediaBank's 141 ATMs. Second, the claim that Euronet's ATM economics are collapsing is wrong, and it must not be used with a bank chief financial officer. The segment's operating-income squeeze is a non-cash accounting effect of the CoreCard purchase. Gross margin actually improved to 49.4%, and cash ATM profitability rose. What is true is that the estate is flat: 57,071 active ATMs against 56,760 a year earlier. That is roughly 300 net machines added on a base of 57,000. So Euronet's growth now comes from acquiring, card issuing and software, not from buying bank fleets. It renamed the segment "Payments Infrastructure" in May 2026 to say exactly that. Third, on the Q2 call of 30/07/2026, management named no new ATM-outsourcing win anywhere in Europe. Every named win was in Peru, the United States, Asia-Pacific and Costa Rica. Meanwhile Euronet is running a sustained content campaign aimed at chief financial officers, pre-selling the ATM-as-a-Service cost-of-ownership case. The third instalment was published on 03/08/2026 (A6).

signals.bank_theme: Diebold Nixdorf — European banking hardware decline, but a hard push on recyclers and branch automation
signals.country_raw: EMEA incl. footprint, with a named Romanian retail win
signals.signal: Diebold Nixdorf's Q2 2026 filings, dated 29/07/2026, show that its European banking hardware cycle has softened, while its services and branch-automation push has not. Banking net sales fell 6.1% to USD 638.1m. Banking product sales fell 13.0% to USD 236.6m, and the 10-Q states the decline was "primarily due lower volume in Middle East, Africa and Europe". Banking services were near flat. Against that, the earnings release claims a record number of teller cash recyclers shipped in the quarter. It also claims "major Branch Automation Solutions, cash management and service contracts" won, with Banking backlog growing quarter on quarter and total product backlog at USD 814m. On the call, chief executive Octavio Marquez described Europe as mature, with "very, very modest growth, but we're really winning in that market". He cited an approximately 1,100-unit DN Series win at a new UK customer, bundled with a long-term service agreement. The only named win inside Printec's footprint was retail: 1,600 point-of-sale units with a Romanian retailer, alongside European POS unit sales growing nearly 170%. Capital is going to share buybacks, roughly USD 60m in the quarter, rather than to acquisitions. Diebold Nixdorf filed only three 8-Ks all year, and none discloses M&A. Separately, it holds a small software incumbency inside Geldservice Austria (A6).

Glory's own view of the bank side is weaker than the headline figures. It says European teller-recycler sales to financial institutions "remained weak". signals.bank_theme: Worldline — Financial Services keeps shrinking, and outsourced bank estates come back to market
signals.country_raw: Regional (all 17), with the digital-euro angle in AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK
signals.signal: Worldline's bank-facing Financial Services division shrank again in H1 2026, and its profitability fell harder than its revenue. The division covers card issuing and acquiring processing, ATM management, account payments and instant payments. H1 revenue was EUR 363m, down 7.1% organically, with the adjusted EBITDA margin down about 300 basis points to 18.5%. The chief financial officer put a figure on the cause on the call. "We'll have a EUR 60 million impact coming from contract terminations, and we've seen exactly half of that". The chief executive said "the back to growth of FS will not be before the second half of 2027". No client names or geographies were given, and every Q2 win listed was Western European. Two things temper this reading. The disposal programme is declared complete, and it contained no CEE or SEE asset. All seven sold businesses sit outside Printec's 17 countries, so the idea that Worldline exits the Balkans no longer holds. Printec will instead compete against a recapitalised, Europe-only Worldline with net debt halved. Worldline is also positioning itself as infrastructure for the digital euro. The ECB selected 36 payment service providers for its pilot on 14/07/2026, and Worldline confirmed its selection the next day. It takes part through PAYONE in Germany and Austria, as both acquirer and technical service provider. Against that, Worldline is cutting 4-5% of Western European headcount every year to 2030, under its own guidance (A6).
signals.date: 30/07/2026 — H1 results: FS -7.1% organic, EUR 60m of full-year contract terminations half-booked, no return to growth before H2-2027; Q3 release 27/10/2026
signals.implies: Banks are ending legacy Worldline processing and ATM-management contracts at a run rate of EUR 60m a year. Worldline itself says the division will not grow again for six more quarters. That means outsourced bank estates are coming back to market across Europe. This is the best opening Worldline has created for Printec. The offer is multivendor ATM software, device telemetry and monitoring, cash forecasting and managed field services. It should be pitched to any footprint bank whose Worldline contract is up for renewal. Transaction monitoring is the migration-risk answer that a bank leaving an outsourcer needs to hear. A vendor cutting 4-5% of its regional staff a year is also weakest exactly where Printec is strongest, in named local engineers and evidenced uptime. But do not tell a bank that Worldline has exited digital banking or is leaving the region. Neither is true, and the contact will know it.
signals.likelihood: Likely that at least one footprint bank re-tenders Worldline-run services within 12 months — the terminations are already contracted and run through 2027
signals.follow_up: Identify by name which footprint banks use Worldline Financial Services processing or ATM management. That means Austria, via the former SIX Payment Services book, plus Slovakia, Croatia and Greece. Diarise their renewal windows. Re-read the Q3 release of 27/10/2026 for the remaining EUR 30m of the 2026 termination drag, and for any new disposal perimeter. Track local headcount and works-council notices at Worldline Greece and PAYONE Austria.
signals.product_review_why: Terminated Worldline ATM-management contracts bring estates back to market for managed services, ATM software and cash forecasting, with monitoring as the migration answer.

signals.bank_theme: Windows 11 and end-of-life ATM software — KAL's hypervisor pitch against the ECB's end-of-life mandate
signals.country_raw: GR, CZ, SK, RO and footprint-wide (SSM banks in AT, BG, CY, GR, HR, SI, SK)
signals.signal: Two separate developments meet on the same question: what happens to ageing ATM estates running unsupported software. On the regulator side, ECB Banking Supervision letter SSM-2026-0301 of 07/07/2026 was signed by Claudia Buch. It requires every significant institution to submit an action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by **31 October 2026**. One of six named focus areas is modernising infrastructure by "replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies". Another is accurate identification of information and communication technology assets. That wording reaches ATM operating systems, middleware and asset inventories directly. It also explicitly pulls supplier service level agreements and contract terms into scope (A3). On the competitor side, KAL is marketing its Kalignite Hypervisor. This is a Linux virtualisation layer that runs a newer Windows on old ATM hardware, "even if unsupported by the ATM hardware vendor". Česká spořitelna is quoted by name as its reference. KAL also runs a zero-licence "Software-on-Standby" offer. It pre-installs its software on a handful of a rival's ATMs, so that it can be switched on across the fleet at will. KAL reaches CEE through Asseco Central Europe, which names Slovenská sporiteľňa. KAL returns to Banktech in Athens on 8-9 October 2026 as a guest of Mellon, selling multivendor ATM software to Greek and SEE banks (A6).

sources.text: ECB Banking Supervision — letter SSM-2026-0301 on AI-enabled cybersecurity threats

signals.date: 31/10/2026 — supervisory action plans naming end-of-life ICT are due; Banktech Athens 08-09/10/2026; KAL newsroom re-swept 19/08/2026
signals.implies: Every supervised bank in the footprint has to write down which of its technologies are end-of-life, on a fixed date that a supervisor will then monitor. ATM fleets on unsupported operating systems sit squarely in that inventory. That is a funded remediation trigger, and KAL is competing for it with the opposite answer: keep the old machines and buy software instead of hardware. Printec must counter on total cost of ownership. A fleet kept alive on a hypervisor still fails mechanically. It cannot take deposits or recycle notes, and it cannot carry the deposit-automation revenue that a recycling refresh unlocks. Software-on-Standby is also a direct wedge under any Printec multivendor-software account. Renewals should therefore be tied to roadmap commitments and Windows 11 certification dates.
signals.likelihood: High — the 31/10/2026 submission is mandatory and dated, and Windows 11 ATM migration decisions run through 2026-27
signals.follow_up: Get Printec sales to Banktech Athens on 8-9 October 2026, and report which banks attend the KAL and Mellon sessions. That is a cheap, dated intelligence opportunity six weeks out. Ask the NCR channel for x-core's Windows 11 certification status, and publish a total-cost-of-ownership counter to hypervisor-based fleet life extension. Ask SSM-supervised Printec accounts what their 31/10/2026 plan commits on ATM operating-system end-of-life. Treat Asseco Central Europe as KAL's Czech and Slovak delivery arm in every bid there.
signals.product_review_why: The end-of-life mandate funds ATM refresh, and KAL's hypervisor competes for that money against a recycling hardware upgrade.

signals.bank_theme: ECB SSM-2026-0301 — end-of-life ICT action plans due to supervisory teams by 31/10/2026
signals.country_raw: SSM footprint (AT, BG, CY, GR, HR, SI, SK)
signals.signal: This was re-verified word for word at the primary PDF. ECB Banking Supervision letter SSM-2026-0301 was signed by Claudia Buch on 07/07/2026. It tells the chief executives of every significant institution what to do with their AI-cyber action plan. The plan "should be submitted to the respective Joint Supervisory Team (JST) by 31 October 2026". After that, the Joint Supervisory Team engages on the plan and monitors progress, and the ECB runs a horizontal analysis across all plans (A3). Three things moved this cycle. First, the same 31/10/2026 deadline is now recorded in Official Journal text. It appears in recital 13 of the ESRB's formal Warning ESRB/2026/3 of 25/06/2026 on systemic cyber risks from frontier AI models, published on 16/07/2026. So it is no longer only a letter (A3). Second, the three European Supervisory Authorities issued a joint statement on 31/07/2026. It extends the same governance expectation down to less-significant institutions supervised nationally by BNB, BoG, CBC, HNB, NBS-SK, Banka Slovenije and FMA. That is the mid-market tier where most of Printec's estate sits (A3). Third, the ECB's annual IT Risk Questionnaire collection has been pushed from September 2026 to February 2027. That extends the evidence window rather than closing it (A3). Annex 1 sets out the focus areas. Focus area 5 requires "modernising infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies". Focus area 1 requires accurate information and communication technology asset inventories. signals.signal: The dormant file on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins has moved into trilogue. Trilogue is the three-way talks between Parliament, Council and Commission. This was checked on the Parliament's own procedure file. The economic affairs committee voted at first reading and decided to open negotiations on 23/06/2026. The report was tabled 26/06/2026. Plenary confirmed the mandate on 08/07/2026, not 09/07/2026 as previously reported (A3). The plenary press release confirms the file was not contested. Euro-area countries would have to keep cash accessible, businesses could not ban cash, and monitoring would pay special attention to the elderly, low-income and unbanked (A3). Agent 3 attaches a clear health warning to the substance. It rests on a Parliament summary page last updated 20/06/2026, which is before the committee vote. It therefore describes the draft report, not the adopted mandate. On that basis, Member States would designate national authorities over cash acceptance and access. They would file an annual assessment against common indicators set by a Commission implementing act. The named indicators include "density of cash access points in relation to the population". A negative assessment triggers remedial measures, including geographical access requirements. If a Member State fails to act, the Commission may impose country-specific measures. The Council's December-2025 position adds a near-prohibition on refusing cash. It also mandates resilience measures to keep cash payments working during major electronic outages (A3).

signals.bank_theme: PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation — package slipped, all compliance clocks re-based
signals.country_raw: EU footprint (AT, BG, CY, CZ, GR, HR, HU, RO, SI, SK)
signals.signal: Re-checked live on 27/08/2026 and confirmed: there is no adoption and no Official Journal publication. Both Parliament procedure files still read "Awaiting Council's 1st reading position". The last event on each is the 05/05/2026 text agreed in interinstitutional negotiations. The only forward entry is an indicative plenary date of 14/12/2026. The Council must adopt its position before that plenary can happen (A3). The compliance clocks run from entry into force. A December plenary therefore puts publication around Q1-2027 and general application around Q4-2028. It puts the Verification-of-Payee and liability tier around Q2-2029. That is arithmetic, not law. The substantive articles were confirmed word for word in the final compromise texts, and they are what banks will eventually buy for. Article 7 requires ATM charges to be displayed before the transaction is started. On request, the charges must also be provided on a durable medium at completion, with currency-conversion rates no more than ten minutes old. Article 88 forbids making authentication depend on owning a smartphone, unless that individual customer agreed. It requires banks to develop more than one authentication means. A bank can keep an app-only customer, but not an app-only estate. Article 59 imposes a standalone duty to prevent impersonation of the bank's own channels. It also requires a full refund within 15 business days of notification and police report, with the burden of proof on the bank. Articles 50 and 57 extend Verification of Payee to credit transfers outside the instant-payments perimeter, though corporate bulk files can opt out. Separately, PSD3 Article 38 makes independent ATM deployers register before starting activity. They must also prove DORA-grade resilience, including for outsourced operations. Agent 3 checked the transitional articles and found no run-off for deployers already operating (A3). The European Banking Authority expects 40 to 50 technical mandates, half delivered by end-2027 and half by end-2028 (A3).

sources.text: European Parliament Legislative Observatory — procedure file 2023/0210(COD)

signals.date: 14/12/2026 — indicative Parliament first-reading plenary, the only forward date on either file; publication then falls around Q1-2027, general application around Q4-2028 and the Verification-of-Payee and liability tier around Q2-2029 — all derived, none legally fixed

That is a real advantage over integrators working to a fixed scope, and bids should say so explicitly. The accessibility article is a further, less obvious opportunity. It points authentication back onto the bank's own attended and self-service estate.

RBI had cut its own minimum threshold from 75% to 55%. NLB's rival offer was raised from EUR 29.00 to EUR 33.50 and finally EUR 37.00 a share. It took only 31.22% against a condition of 50% plus one share, and will not settle or be extended (A1, A5). RBI retains Croatia, Slovenia and Austria. It has budgeted a **one-off integration cost of about EUR 75 million across 2027-2028**, with about EUR 60m profit accretion in 2028.
