signals.product_review_why: A funded merger will consolidate two ATM fleets onto one software and service contract and migrate card acquiring.

signals.bank_theme: Addiko carve-out to Alta Group — a six-bank Western Balkans group under a first-time owner
signals.signal: Serbia, both Bosnian banks and Montenegro do not go to Raiffeisen. RBI keeps Croatia, Slovenia and Austria. It will carve out the four Western Balkans banks and sell them to Alta Group d.o.o., Belgrade (Serbian register no. 2103524). The four are Addiko Bank AD Beograd, Addiko Bank d.d. Sarajevo, Addiko Bank a.d. Banja Luka and Addiko Bank AD Podgorica. Alta is named in RBI's own offer document and signed its transaction agreement with RBI on 08/05/2026. Alta is an NBS-licensed e-money institution. It already owns Alta Banka AD Beograd and Alta Banka AD Bitola in North Macedonia, and directly holds 9.63% of Addiko (A1, A5). The dated clock that matters is not closing, but the exit from shared services. **A Transitional Services Agreement runs 12 months after carve-out closing, with a single 12-month extension.** After that, the carved-out banks must source services from the buyer or from third parties. Replacements must therefore be running roughly 2H2028 to 2H2029. Carve-out closing is expected H2-2027. Addiko's CEO said on 13/08/2026 that integration runs at least to end-2027 and probably into 2028. The equipment gaps are counted from the banks' own published lists. Addiko Sarajevo publishes 74 ATM locations, of which only 25 accept cash, leaving 49 cash-out-only. Addiko Banja Luka operates just five cash-accepting ATMs against roughly 45 cross-listed locations. It already markets a merchant cash-deposit flow and a 'Zona 24/7' deposit concept. Neither Bosnian bank has any own POS estate. Addiko Serbia is the opposite. Its product page states that every branch has an 'Addiko Express' dual-currency recycler, across 33 branches and 50 ATM locations. Montenegro is about 4% of group assets but has the group's best deposit build. It has 12 deposit-and-withdrawal machines across 18-19 ATM sites, the highest deposit share of any bank in the country, including coin acceptance and an SME daily-takings flow (A1). Alta is expanding fast beyond banking. It bought insurer ZOIL Makedonija. In April 2026 Alta Retail took five Fortenova Serbia companies for about EUR 140m, bringing roughly 300 Idea, Roda and Mercator stores. Sava Ivanov Dalbokov left the Addiko Group Supervisory Board on 31/07/2026. He joined Addiko Bank a.d. Beograd on 01/08/2026 as planned Chief Operating Officer, subject to NBS approval (A1, A5).

sources.text: RBI takeover offer document, s.2.2.3/2.2.4 and 6.4

signals.date: 13/08/2026 — Addiko's 1H26 report names Alta Group as the buyer and discloses the 12+12-month transitional-services clock · 03/11/2026 additional share-acceptance deadline · carve-out closing expected H2-2027, all conditions by 14/05/2027 · services must be re-sourced by roughly 2H2028-2H2029
signals.implies: Six banks across four jurisdictions are being merged under an owner that has never run a group this size. These are Alta Banka Serbia, Alta Banka Bitola and the four Addiko banks. That is a greenfield-scale platform programme: core and card consolidation, one ATM and cash-automation estate, and one AML and transaction-monitoring platform answering to four regulators. It also includes a forced exit from Addiko's shared services, with a date written into the deal documents rather than guessed. A first-time buyer at that scale depends on vendors. Every incumbent contract inherited from Addiko becomes re-tenderable under new ownership. The roughly 300-store retail chain Alta now owns needs card acceptance and merchant cash handling in its own right, separate from the bank deal. **The single most important correction this cycle is that the previous table assumed a combined Raiffeisen plus Addiko Serbia estate to harmonise. That is now wrong, and any pitch built on it must be withdrawn.** Buying is frozen until ownership resolves, so this is relationship building now for a 2027 procurement.
signals.likelihood: High — the buyer is named on primary deal documents and the services-exit clock is contractual; timing runs to H2-2027
signals.follow_up: Open a relationship with Alta Group in Belgrade now, before closing, while the target operating model for six banks is still being drawn. That is the whole opportunity, and it will not reopen. Establish which services the Transitional Services Agreement actually covers, because that list is the 2028-29 replacement scope. Quantify the Sarajevo 49 and Banja Luka roughly 40 cash-out-only machines as a recycler retrofit case, against a bank already selling merchant cash deposit that it cannot serve. Position Addiko Serbia's all-branch recycler estate and Montenegro's deposit build as the template for the group. Pitch card acceptance and merchant cash handling to Alta Retail's roughly 300 stores separately.
signals.product_review_why: A six-bank platform build needs one cash-automation estate, card acceptance for the banks and the retail chain, and one AML platform.

countries.name: Montenegro
countries.atms: 664 (Q1-2026); 751 at end-2025, +20.0% y/y — highest year-end in the 2018-2026 CBCG series (Q1 is below the preceding Q4 in every year of the series; the cause is not published). 126 of 664 cash-deposit-capable (+46.5% since end-2024, and no Q1 dip) — 538 machines without deposit capability
countries.branches: — (no branch / organisational-unit count published by CBCG or any Montenegrin authority; negative re-confirmed this run by my own full-text extraction of Bilten 7-2026, which has no payment-infrastructure chapter at all, plus the publications index showing the 2025 Work Report still unpublished)
countries.cash_trend: Falling: over-the-counter cash orders 5,478,745 in 2025 (-7.1% y/y, -19.5% since 2022) worth EUR 5.772bn (-4.7%); Q1-2026 -6.0% y/y on both count and value. countries.instant: IPS live 20/07/2026 (TIPS Clone, with Banca d'Italia under the ECB umbrella, financed by an EUR 8m World Bank credit); all 11 banks live simultaneously and Montenegro was the first country to put the TIPS Clone platform into operation. July-2026 first 12 days: 56,678 orders / EUR 21.53m, ~EUR 380 average ticket, full availability. Per-order cap EUR 3,000, covering almost 80% of all transactions; fee on sub-EUR-200 mobile/internet instant payments capped at 5 cents on both send and receive (previous average 32 cents), and above EUR 200 no more than the bank's ordinary transfer fee. Phase 2 = QR, mobile-phone-number alias, Request to Pay; SEPA Instant named as a next step, no date
countries.implication: 5-cent fee cap plus CBCG's published 'just over 60% electronic' share of credit transfers makes cost-to-serve the whole story: deposit/recycling ATMs and TCRs against 538 non-deposit ATMs and ~EUR 2.9bn of annual business cash deposits, kiosks and cash-cycle optimisation for the seasonal coastal swing; real-time monitoring and fraud scoring for an irrevocable rail amid a CBCG-reported phishing wave; POS/TMS against +4,475 terminals in five quarters, with softPOS a competitive rather than greenfield pitch now that Hipotekarna fields ProvisionPay-powered MojPOS; digital-channel, open-banking-API and e-signature work against four incumbent bank apps rated below 2.5/5 and a licensed PISP/AISP (PrestoPay) out-charting every bank app in the national free chart

countries.branches: 749 bank organisational units (end-Dec-2025, CBBiH, pub. 30/03/2026) — flat vs 749 in 2024; FBiH 450 / RS 283 / Brcko District 16
countries.cash_trend: Cash outside banks +8.56% y/y to 7.46bn KM at 31/12/2025 (tourism-driven, per CBBiH), and CBBiH notes bank VAULT cash stabilised and grew mildly in 2025 after falling through 2024 — yet the cash share of card turnover fell 68% to 65%; ATM withdrawals 13.59bn KM = 64% of the 21.10bn KM card total. More notes to handle, smaller share of spend.
countries.instant: IPS BiH (Banca d'Italia TIPS Clone, ECB-consented, EUR 2m EU-funded) went live 20/07/2026 with 3 banks, now 5 of 21 licensed banks (CBBiH separately counts 22 offering e-banking); 24/7/365, 5,000 KM cap, BAM-only, mobile/e-banking initiation MANDATORY; no volumes published yet. countries.implication: A conversion market, not an expansion one: recyclers/TCRs and intelligent-deposit ATMs against 1,281 remaining dispense-only units, sold bank-by-bank off FBA's and ABRS's published device tables. SEPA plus IPS force ISO 20022 payment-hub, digital-channel and HSM work at the 16 non-live banks inside ~18 months, with a CBBiH-stated six-month post-admission clock. FATF grey-listing and the binding FBA IKT decision (in force since 31/12/2025, external ICT-audit filing due every 31 March) open AML, transaction-monitoring and cryptographic key-management lanes. Two things to avoid overselling: ATM bill payment is a lost battle, not whitespace — banks retired 108 payment ATMs in 2025; and fully-remote eKYC stays legally blocked until an e-identity/trust-services law passes, which the EC recorded as no-progress on 04/11/2025.

countries.implication: Rare growth market, but the growth has changed shape: the ATM fleet added 91 units across 2025 and only 4 in Q1-2026, while deposit-capable machines rose 449 to 473 in that same quarter — so the opportunity is a deposit/recycler UPGRADE of the 663 remaining dispense-only ATMs plus branch transformation (kiosks, TCRs, accessible fit-out), not fleet expansion; Komercijalna banka has already run that template at five or more branches. Cash-in at 19% of cash-out value is the strongest recycler business case in the footprint. The expected November-2026 instant go-live drives ISO 20022 mapping, 24/7 channels, real-time fraud monitoring and HSM/key work (XL). Acceptance is concentrated at only ~16,700 merchants against ~36,000 devices, with the central bank publicly calling for cheap simple acceptance — a softPOS/TMS opening endorsed from the top. Tokenization +137.5% y/y against a shrinking credit-card count (-2.5%) makes card issuing, token provisioning and CNP fraud monitoring the digital-side lane.

competitors.name: Mellon Group
competitors.latest:
Audited 2025 group accounts were filed on 07/07/2026. They show revenue of EUR 258.8m (+17%), gross profit of EUR 36.0m and EBITDA of EUR 14.1m (+39%). Net profit was EUR 6.8m (+73%), with 9,606 staff. That is roughly Printec's EBITDA on about ten times the revenue, so Mellon can absorb a thin-margin bid that Printec cannot.

The same filing also records four ownership moves, which matter more than the financial figures. Mellon bought Camelot Sistemi in Croatia outright. It founded wholly owned companies in Ljubljana and Budapest. On 24/06/2026 it completed the buy-out of the remaining 45% of Mellon Cyprus.

Slovenia, Hungary, Croatia and Cyprus should therefore move from safe to contested. There is still no confirmed Romanian ATM win, and its Bulgarian incumbency is unproven.

competitors.name: Euronet
competitors.latest:
As at 31/08/2026, the takeover of CrediaBank's Greek merchant-acquiring business and management of its 141 ATMs had still not closed. It was absent from the Q2 filing, and there has been no relevant filing since 30/07. There is also no notification on the Hellenic Competition Commission register, against a stated Q3 target. That makes 30/09 a hard decision point.

Two earlier readings are corrected. The ATM operating-income squeeze is a non-cash accounting effect of the CoreCard acquisition, and gross margin actually improved to 49.4%. The estate is essentially flat at 57,071 active machines, so growth now comes from acquiring, card issuing and software rather than from taking over bank fleets.

No new European ATM-outsourcing mandate was named on the 30/07 call. Euronet is running a sustained cost-of-ownership campaign for ATM-as-a-Service aimed at bank finance directors, and the third instalment was published 03/08/2026.

competitors.name: NCR Atleos
competitors.latest:
The UK CMA (the UK competition regulator) opened a Phase 1 merger review of the Brink's takeover on 26/08/2026. Its legal deadline to decide is 22/10/2026. CEO Tim Oliver now expects the deal to close in early Q1 2027, which is earlier than before.

Because the deal is pending, Atleos held no Q2 earnings call and gave no outlook. A full-text scan of its release found no mention of Europe or EMEA. The only public European figure left is USD 352m EMEA revenue, up 2.9%.

competitors.latest:
H1 management report (31/07/2026): Payment Solutions, the line that overlaps Printec most directly, fell to EUR 102.8m. That is down EUR 5.2m, or 5%, with Q2 down 7%. The ATM line fell EUR 3.4m on lower equipment deliveries in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro, and Romania was also negative. The terminal line fell EUR 1.9m on lower Slovenian and Croatian deliveries.

This is reshaping rather than collapse. Group operating profit rose 27% in the quarter. The terminal line's operating result improved on growing Serbian recurring revenue. Contracted margin is rising while contracted revenue is flat to down.

This is a company taking fewer, better-priced deals, so it is unlikely to buy a tender cheaply. It bought out minority owners in Bosnia (EUR 8.5m), Slovenia and Serbia. It still has no operating entity in Greece, Cyprus, Austria or Hungary.

competitors.name: Diebold Nixdorf
competitors.latest:
Q2 filings (29/07/2026): banking net sales fell 6.1% to USD 638.1m, and banking product sales fell 13.0% to USD 236.6m. The filing blames the fall mainly on lower volumes in the Middle East, Africa and Europe. That is the clearest public evidence that its European hardware refresh has softened.

The company is not retreating. It shipped a record number of teller cash recyclers, and its banking backlog is growing. The CEO cited a fleet win of about 1,100 units at a new UK customer, bundled with a long-term service agreement. That is a hardware-plus-service displacement move it will run at NCR-installed banks.

The only named win inside the footprint was a 1,600-unit POS order with a Romanian retailer. With ~USD 60m of buybacks and no acquisitions all year, it will compete on price and service.

competitors.name: Worldline / Cardlink
competitors.latest:
H1 results (30/07/2026): the bank-facing Financial Services division fell 7.1% organically to EUR 363m, with margin down about three points to 18.5%. The CFO put EUR 60m of contract terminations on the full year, half of it already booked by end-June. The CEO said the division will not return to growth before H2 2027.

Two corrections are needed. The disposal programme is finished, and all seven sold businesses sit outside Printec's 17 countries, so the claim that Worldline is leaving the region is wrong. Worldline has also not exited bank digital banking or ATM management.

It is cutting 4-5% of Western European headcount each year to 2030, while positioning itself as digital-euro infrastructure. It was among the 36 PSPs the ECB selected for its pilot on 14/07/2026, taking part through PAYONE in Germany and Austria.

competitors.name: PayPoint Romania
competitors.latest:

The service is live at over 14,000 partner locations and is targeted to reach 26,000 during 2026. It is explicitly aimed at rural communities where the nearest ATM is tens of kilometres away.

competitors.latest:

On 19/05/2026 Hellenic Post awarded it a five-year operational lease of 300 banknote counting and quality-sorting machines. The price is EUR 19.25 per machine per month, or EUR 346,500 in total, with an unexercised option for 200 more. It won with Double Power machines rather than Glory, so this was a loss on price and lease model, not a channel change.

BOOS also holds the service contract on Hellenic Post's legacy counting fleet. That affects Printec's cash-automation and field-services lines at the same time. It also gives BOOS a live public-sector reference to bid against Printec at Greek banks.

Printec's device-management line is therefore now publicly described as a national utility function in Bulgaria. OpenWay is a structural competitor that was missing from the tracked vendor list entirely.

competitors.name: Datecs Payment Technology
competitors.latest:
On 27/08/2026 the Bulgarian National Bank's Governing Council extended Datecs Payment Technology's payment-institution licence. The licence now also covers cash withdrawal from a payment account, execution of card transactions and credit transfers, and the issuing of payment instruments.

Datecs was already a licensed acquirer with an EU passport and a Bucharest agent. What is genuinely new is the issuing permission and, more importantly, the cash-withdrawal permission. That permission underpins cashback at merchant terminals and independent cash-out deployment.

A Bulgarian terminal maker that owns the device, the acquiring rail and now the cash-out permission can bundle services in a way a terminal reseller cannot match on price.

competitors.name: Glory
competitors.latest:
Q1 results (07/08/2026): EMEA revenue was JPY 27.3bn, up 27.1%, and for the first time it was more than half of all overseas revenue. Overseas operating profit more than doubled, with margin rising from 5.0% to 8.7%. Management called that step-up structural on 17/08.

The cash-automation arm behind the recycler line Printec resells grew from JPY 10.0bn to JPY 13.3bn. Its kiosk business Acrelec grew about 29%, which makes Glory a self-service kiosk rival in Europe as well as a supplier.

Glory told investors that special demand from the euro banknote redesign is expected from around 2029. The ECB's survey on ten shortlisted designs closes 21/09/2026. As a counterweight, European teller-recycler sales to banks stayed weak, and Glory names no CEE or SEE customer anywhere.

competition_brief:
The most important development for Printec's competitive position this cycle was a regulatory review, not a lost deal. On **26 August 2026 the UK Competition and Markets Authority formally opened its Phase 1 inquiry** into **Brink's** acquisition of **NCR Atleos**. The legal deadline for a decision is **22 October 2026** ([CMA case page](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry)). Atleos has also moved its expected completion date forward to early in the first quarter of 2027.

For Printec the consequence is direct and uncomfortable. The company that supplies the hardware and software behind its whole ATM line is about to change hands. Its new owner is the company competing hardest against Printec's service business. Atleos has said little in the meantime. It held no second-quarter earnings call and published no outlook, and a full-text scan of its release found no mention of Europe or EMEA.

This change of ownership matters because the buyer's strategy is working well. **Brink's** reported second-quarter revenue of USD 1,392m, up 7%. Its ATM managed-services and cash-as-a-service lines, which run ATMs and handle cash for banks as an outsourced service, grew 14% organically ([SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/78890/000007889026000054/exhibit992_2q2026v-micro.htm)).

Europe is where this shift has gone furthest. Revenue there rose only a little, from USD 358m to USD 377m, but margin rose from 16.6% to 18.7%. Brink's is deliberately swapping low-margin cash-in-transit work for high-margin ATM outsourcing, rather than chasing volume.

Brink's announced a new full ATM outsourcing agreement for a European bank consortium, meaning a group of banks. The agreement starts in the second half of the year. It deliberately did not name the country, the banks or the number of machines. In April its ATM managed-services arm shared a stage in Athens with **Mellon** and **KAL**. There it sold full-lifecycle outsourcing directly to decision-makers at National Bank of Greece and Eurobank. That is exactly the revenue Printec earns in its largest market.

Consolidation is also happening closer to Printec's own markets. **Mellon Technologies** filed audited 2025 accounts showing revenue of **EUR 258.8m, up 17%**, with EBITDA up 39% ([group accounts](https://mellongroup.com/assets/uploads/2025_MT_Group_Notes_EN.pdf)). EBITDA means earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. That puts Mellon at roughly Printec's own EBITDA level on about ten times the revenue, so Mellon can absorb a thin-margin bid that Printec cannot.

Four ownership moves disclosed with the accounts matter more than the numbers. Mellon bought Camelot Sistemi in Croatia outright, set up wholly owned companies in Ljubljana and Budapest, and completed the buy-out of Mellon Cyprus. A bidder needs new, funded local subsidiaries before it can win local bank work. **Slovenia, Hungary, Croatia and Cyprus should therefore move from "safe" to "contested"** in account planning.

At the same time, pressure on account-to-account and card payment rails is causing some players to pull back as well as advance. **Payten / Asseco SEE** publicly admitted a retreat in hardware. Its Payment Solutions segment fell 5% to EUR 102.8m, and the ATM line dropped EUR 3.4m on lower deliveries in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro. This is a reshaping rather than a collapse: group operating profit rose 27%, and contracted margin is rising while contracted revenue falls. A company that takes fewer, better-priced deals is unlikely to buy a tender cheaply this autumn.

**Worldline**'s bank-facing Financial Services division shrank another 7.1% organically to EUR 363m. It booked EUR 60m of contract terminations for the year and expects no return to growth before the second half of 2027. Two convenient assumptions about Worldline should be dropped. In fact its disposal programme is finished, every business it sold sits outside Printec's seventeen countries, and it has not exited ATM management.

**Diebold Nixdorf**'s banking product sales fell 13.0%, and its filing blames lower volumes in the Middle East, Africa and Europe. Even so, it shipped a record number of teller cash recyclers, which are counter machines that re-use deposited notes. It also won a fleet of approximately 1,100 units at a new UK customer, bundled with long-term service. It will run this same replacement approach against NCR-installed banks in Printec's footprint.

Two quieter moves deserve board attention because they attack the business case, not the bid. **KAL** is marketing a Linux virtualisation layer, which is software that lets one operating system run inside another. It lets a newer Windows run on old ATM hardware, even where the hardware vendor no longer supports it. Česká spořitelna is quoted by name saying it can now significantly extend the life of older machines. This is designed to remove the hardware-refresh trigger that Printec's ATM sales depend on.

KAL returns to the Banktech conference in Athens on **8–9 October 2026**, hosted by Mellon. Brink's also holds 13.93% of KAL, which links this directly to the Atleos deal.

In Romania, **PayPoint** and **SelfPay** are doing the same thing from below. They offer cash withdrawal at more than 14,000 assisted point-of-sale locations, heading for 26,000. They also run over 13,000 self-service payment stations, heading for roughly 19,000. This is the cheapest substitute yet for a rural cash machine, and both work against the case for cash-dispensing ATMs.

A 35,000-terminal estate and a 13,000-station estate are also two of the largest managed-services targets in the country. The right first approach to each is as a customer, not a rival.

Among partners and adjacent players, **Glory** had the best quarter of anyone. EMEA revenue rose 27.1% and, for the first time, made up more than half its overseas revenue. Overseas operating margin rose from 5.0% to 8.7%.

Glory also put a date on the next cash-hardware cycle. It told investors that special demand from the **euro banknote redesign** is expected from around 2029. The ECB's public survey on ten shortlisted designs closes on **21 September 2026** ([ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260723~c2d43f9170.en.html)). The honest counterweight is that Glory names no CEE or SEE customer anywhere, and says European teller-recycler sales to banks remained weak.

**Euronet**'s Greek deal with CrediaBank had still not closed as at 31 August. It covers buying CrediaBank's merchant-acquiring business and managing its 141 ATMs. Merchant acquiring is card payment processing for shops. It appears nowhere in Euronet's second-quarter filing, and there is no notification on the Hellenic Competition Commission register, against a stated third-quarter target. That makes **30 September a hard decision point**.

Two earlier readings of Euronet were corrected. Its ATM economics are not collapsing, and its estate is essentially flat at 57,071 machines. Its growth now comes from acquiring, issuing and software, not from taking over bank fleets.

Finally, two names joined the tracked set that a 164-vendor list had missed entirely, and both are global tier. **Giesecke+Devrient**'s currency-technology arm holds the high-speed central-bank banknote-sorter tier that Printec's product line does not reach. It has now **won Banka Slovenije's six-year sorter-maintenance contract, awarded 21 August 2026 at EUR 1,890,000 on a single bid**. That locks the tier up until 2032. Its identity joint venture **Veridos** won Cyprus' end-to-end electronic travel-document contract at **EUR 22,900,450** on lowest price.

In Greece, **BOOS S.A.** was absent from the competitor list until this cycle. It won the year's largest Greek counter-cash-automation contract: a five-year operational lease of 300 banknote counting and sorting machines for Hellenic Post. The contract uses Double Power machines rather than Glory. This is a loss on price and lease model, not a change of channel. It also gives BOOS a live public-sector reference to bid against Printec at Greek banks.

deadlines.title: RESOLVED — RBI takes Addiko; Serbia, both Bosnian banks and Montenegro carve out to Alta Group
deadlines.forces: **Corrected this cycle: the 'five-market SEE integration' reading was wrong.** RBI's offer succeeded with acceptances for 10,831,435 shares — 56.16% of the shares subject to the offer, equal to 55.55% of total share capital (the two percentages are the same result measured two ways). NLB's rival offer FAILED at 31.22% against a 50%-plus-one condition and will not settle. RBI RETAINS Croatia, Slovenia and Austria and has budgeted about EUR 75m of one-off integration cost across 2027-2028. Serbia, Addiko Sarajevo, Addiko Banja Luka and Addiko Podgorica are CARVED OUT to Alta Group d.o.o. Belgrade, which already owns Alta Banka Beograd and Alta Banka Bitola — so the buying centre splits: Vienna and Zagreb for HR/SI, and a first-time owner in Belgrade for the four Western Balkans banks. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [RBI offer document](https://www.rbinternational.com/content/dam/rbi/ho/investors/news/publications-austrian-takeover-law/2026-05-14-RBI_Addiko_Angebotsunterlage_EN.pdf.coredownload.pdf))
deadlines.source: [RBI — status of acceptances after expiry of the acceptance period, 29/07/2026](https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/rbi-on-the-status-of-acceptances-of-the-voluntary-public-tender-offer-for-all-addiko-shares-after-expiration-of-the-acceptance-period-on-29-july-2026/2b17ddae-a690-4111-a8f0-282e5a322863_en); A1 findings 2026-07-30

deadlines.title: Greece: ELTA/Growthfund market consultation closes on a EUR 6m retail & delivery transformation
deadlines.forces: EESYP/Growthfund issued an amended preliminary market consultation for ELTA's 'Retail & Delivery Transformation Initiative — Integrated Retail Systems & Delivery Control Tower and Track & Trace', budget EUR 6,000,000 excluding VAT and ELTA-financed, with comments due 10/09/2026 through ESIDIS under reference 2026DIAB33462. A market consultation is the stage at which the specification is still movable, which makes this worth more than most open tenders — it is the only moment to shape the requirement before a likely Q4-2026 tender. ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md))

deadlines.title: North Macedonia: KIBS Instant / Strela — first two banks expected to initiate
deadlines.forces: North Macedonia is going instant on TWO rails at once, which forces every bank into two integrations on two calendars. KIBS Instant (Strela) expects its first two initiating banks by 15/09/2026, while the rebuilt MIPS system passed its first ISO 20022 test cycle with the banks in July (confirmed 04/08/2026) and TIPS Clone accession is expected in the November 2026 window. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md))

deadlines.title: North Macedonia: NBRSM TIPS-clone connectivity tender closes on its SECOND attempt
deadlines.forces: The central bank's own connectivity procurement, ESJN 14505/2026, closes 18/09/2026 — a re-run after the first attempt was cancelled for want of any acceptable bid. A procurement that failed once for lack of qualified bidders is an unusually open door. ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md))

deadlines.title: EPC Verification of Payee scheme rulebook v1.1 takes effect (03:30 CET) — DATE UNVERIFIED THIS CYCLE
deadlines.forces: **Not verified at primary source this cycle: the European Payments Council site was Cloudflare-blocked to every access route, so none of five EPC scheme dates could be confirmed.** The item is kept because it was verified in an earlier cycle, but it must not be quoted client-facing as a certification deadline until an operator re-reads the rulebook from a browser session. Substance as previously recorded: the EPC published rulebook v1.1 on 16/03/2026 with an effective moment of 20/09/2026 03:30 CET, binding every scheme participant at that instant on routing-and-verification connectivity, name-matching logic, revised response codes and certificate handling. ([A3 findings](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md))
deadlines.source: [EPC — Verification of Payee Scheme Rulebook v1.1](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/sites/default/files/kb/file/2026-03/EPC218-23%20v1.1%202026%20Verification%20Of%20Payee%20Scheme%20Rulebook_0.pdf); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: ECB euro banknote redesign: public survey on the ten shortlisted designs closes
deadlines.forces: The ECB published ten shortlisted designs on 23/07/2026 and its public survey closes 21/09/2026, with a design decision expected around the end of the year. Glory told investors that special demand related to the redesign is expected from around 2029, issued in stages over several years — so this is a note-recognition and sensor-upgrade cycle to plan for, not to sell this year. ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260723~c2d43f9170.en.html))

deadlines.title: UK CMA Phase 1 statutory decision deadline on Brink's / NCR Atleos
deadlines.forces: The Competition and Markets Authority opened its Phase 1 merger inquiry on 26/08/2026 with a statutory decision deadline of 22/10/2026, while both companies pulled expected completion forward to early Q1 2027. This is the date that decides whether Printec's principal ATM supply partner becomes a direct competitor's asset on the fast path or after a Phase 2 reference. ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [CMA case](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry))

deadlines.title: Romania: RBI quiet period begins — the Garanti BBVA integration scope must be shaped before it
deadlines.forces: RBI's acquisition of Garanti BBVA Romania is guided to close in early October 2026, with data migration and rebranding across 2027 and legal merger in Q4 2027, creating Romania's #3 bank. A one-off integration budget of about EUR 70m is already pre-funded by a EUR 600m eurobond raised on 20/08/2026. Two merged self-service, card and acquiring estates have to be scoped, and the practical window closes when RBI enters its quiet period on 23/10/2026 — the tightest dated commercial window anywhere in the footprint this cycle. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

deadlines.title: ECB SSM-2026-0301: end-of-life ICT action plans due to Joint Supervisory Teams
deadlines.forces: The ECB Banking Supervision letter of 07/07/2026 signed by Claudia Buch requires every significant institution to assess the AI-enabled cyber threat landscape without delay and to submit a comprehensive action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by 31 October 2026, after which the team engages on each plan, monitors progress and the ECB runs a horizontal analysis across all of them. The named structural measures include modernising infrastructure by updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies, alongside vulnerability and patch management at scale, monitoring and detection and third-party ICT risk management. ATM and self-service estates on unsupported operating systems sit squarely inside that written-down inventory, and the third-party focus favours one accountable managed-service partner over a fragmented vendor set. Plans are drafted August to October 2026 and the delivery money lands in the 2027 IT plan; as relief the annual IT Risk Questionnaire moves from September 2026 to February 2027. In footprint this binds NBG, Piraeus, Alpha, Eurobank, Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic, Erste, RBI, BAWAG, UniCredit Bank Austria, Zagrebacka, PBZ, Erste & Steiermarkische, NLB, NKBM, Slovenska sporitelna, VUB, Tatra, UniCredit Bulbank, DSK and UBB, plus the CEE subsidiaries that inherit group standards.
deadlines.source: [ECB — letter to CEOs on AI-enabled cybersecurity threats (SSM-2026-0301)](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: North Macedonia: electronic forced-collection system must be established and exchanging information
deadlines.forces: The transitional provisions of the amended Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (Sluzben vesnik 144/25) require the electronic forced-collection system to be established and exchanging information by 01/11/2026, with mandatory submission of forced-collection orders through it from 01/11/2027. Every NBRNM-licensed bank — Komercijalna, Stopanska (NBG), NLB, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse, UNIBanka — plus payment and e-money institutions must build the interface, and it is a second, separate integration landing in the same quarter as the Single Register of Accounts. That compression is what pushes banks toward outsourced delivery. No contract value is published anywhere in the evidence, and one deadline in this same law has already slipped once, so treat go-live as directionally firm rather than certain.
deadlines.source: [NBRNM — Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems, consolidated text 144/25](https://www.nbrm.mk/content/%D0%97%D0%B0%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BD_%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%B6%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D1%83%D1%81%D0%BB%D1%83%D0%B3%D0%B8_%D0%B8_%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D1%81%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B8_%20%D0%BD%D0%B5%D0%BE%D1%84.%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%87.%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%81%D1%82_144-25.pdf); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Addiko: additional share-acceptance period closes
deadlines.forces: The statutory grace period runs to 03/11/2026 17:00 CET, after which the official post-grace result is published; all remaining closing conditions must be met by 14/05/2027 and carve-out closing is expected in H2 2027. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

deadlines.title: SWIFT SR2026 structured-address cutover (14-15/11/2026 release weekend)
deadlines.forces: From the 2026 standards release, deployed over the 14-15 November 2026 weekend, unstructured postal addresses are removed from cross-border messages: town name and country code must sit in dedicated structured fields for all agents and parties. SWIFT's own readiness material still puts around 65% of payment messages on unstructured addresses. The euro RTGS release deploys the same weekend with testing open 25/09-28/10/2026, and a second wave upgrades the base messages in November 2027 — a separately funded budget cycle recorded identically for the euro RTGS, Romania, Albania and Ukraine. Two named exposures: Hungary's RTGS does not support hybrid postal addresses and has no confirmed timeline, and Bosnia's domestic clearing is contractually pinned to the EPC rulebook, pulling an EU date into a non-EU market. The RTGS core is not Printec's lane; the layer around it is — address and party-data cleansing, sanctions and AML screening retuned for structured fields, payment repair, exception monitoring and managed services. Banks not funded by Q3-2026 buy emergency remediation in September and October.
deadlines.source: [Swift — ISO 20022 milestone for November 2026](https://www.swift.com/news-events/news/iso-20022-milestone-november-2026-unstructured-addresses-be-removed); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: EPC retail cut-off for unstructured addresses, 03:30 CET (MOVED from 22/11/2026)
deadlines.forces: EPC guidance fixes the retail counterpart of the SWIFT cutover at 15/11/2026 at 03:30 CET for instant credit transfers, a date moved from the previously communicated 22/11/2026 — a one-week pull-forward that banks and their vendors may still be carrying wrongly in project plans, so it is worth checking every diary. After that moment unstructured data will, in the EPC's own words, lead to rejects. Bosnia is exposed even though it is outside the EU because its domestic clearing is contractually pinned to the EPC rulebook. The work is counterparty master-data remediation, message transformation, repair and exception monitoring, and it must be complete a day before the SWIFT weekend rather than after it. **Caveat added 2026-08-31: the EPC site was Cloudflare-blocked to every route this cycle, so this date is carried from an earlier verification and was not re-confirmed at primary. The SWIFT SR2026 release-weekend date of 14-15/11/2026 IS independently confirmed.** ([A3 findings](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md))
deadlines.source: [BIS/CPMI — Fostering ISO 20022 harmonisation, follow-up report (Feb-2026)](https://www.bis.org/cpmi/pietf/iso20022_2026.pdf); EPC guidance via A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Slovakia: AMLD6 Act 73/2026 — registration in the FIU's goAML reporting system
deadlines.forces: Act No. 73/2026 Z. z., amending Act No. 297/2008 and transposing Directive (EU) 2024/1640, took effect 01/06/2026. Every entity already obliged on that date must register in the financial intelligence unit's goAML reporting system by 30/11/2026 (new ones within 30 days); failure is an administrative offence, with Slovak professional commentary citing a EUR 1,000,000 ceiling. Obliged persons may no longer rely on the Register of Legal Entities alone for beneficial ownership and must verify from multiple reliable independent sources, applying to new clients and retrospectively to existing relationships during ongoing monitoring — that turns beneficial-owner verification into a bulk remediation of the existing book, not just an onboarding change. Suspicious-transaction and threshold-reporting interfaces must therefore be built or rebuilt against the FIU schema this half-year, not in FY2027, and the adapter should be configurable because the EU-level reporting-format standard re-cuts the same interface for 10/07/2027. Targets: SLSP, VUB, Tatra, CSOB SK, Postova banka and 365.bank.
deadlines.source: [Slov-Lex — zakon c. 73/2026 Z. z.](https://www.slov-lex.sk/ezbierky/pravne-predpisy/SK/ZZ/2026/73/); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Western Balkans: second TIPS Clone onboarding window (central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia)
deadlines.forces: Correcting the previous entry: Montenegro (all 11 banks) and Bosnia went live on the Banca d'Italia-run shared TIPS Clone on 20/07/2026, and the November 2026 second window onboards the CENTRAL BANKS of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia only — Banca d'Italia says nothing about commercial-bank deadlines, so 'completing regional participation' overstated it and national commercial-bank timetables remain unpublished. Kosovo is the most active: the central bank ran an all-bank standardisation workshop on 27/07/2026 covering technical standards, new file formats, transaction limits, ISO 20022 and e-banking adaptation, and awarded advisory RFP BQK-26-011-211 to Paylume SRL on 22/07/2026 at EUR 295,000 over 10 months, so the bank-side integration and merchant/QR acceptance packages are still ahead. This is the budget window in which payment hubs, 24/7 operations, instant-speed sanctions and fraud screening and HSM capacity get committed.
deadlines.source: [Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone platform goes live](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/); A3 findings 2026-07-24, A1 findings 2026-07-30, A4 findings 2026-07-24

deadlines.title: North Macedonia: Single Register of Accounts must be established
deadlines.forces: The same transitional provisions require the Central Register of RNM to establish the Single Register of Accounts by 01/12/2026 — a national electronic register of denar and FX payment and deposit accounts, linked payment instruments, safe-deposit boxes, account holders, beneficial owners and legal representatives, with the Financial Intelligence Office granted direct unrestricted access. Every licensed bank plus payment and e-money institutions must feed standardised data on a defined interface and keep it current: data extraction, mapping, quality and reconciliation work, dormant-account identification and an FIU enquiry-response workflow. The Central Register's technical specification is what sizes per-bank effort. A3 carries an unresolved internal conflict between 01/12/2026 and 30/09/2026 for this date, so confirm before quoting either.
deadlines.source: [NBRNM — Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems, consolidated text 144/25](https://www.nbrm.mk/content/%D0%97%D0%B0%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BD_%D0%B7%D0%B0_%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%B6%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D1%83%D1%81%D0%BB%D1%83%D0%B3%D0%B8_%D0%B8_%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%BD%D0%B8_%D1%81%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B8_%20%D0%BD%D0%B5%D0%BE%D1%84.%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%87.%D1%82%D0%B5%D0%BA%D1%81%D1%82_144-25.pdf); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: EU digital identity wallet: Member State issuance duty (CORRECTS the 06/12/2026 date previously carried)
deadlines.forces: Article 5a(1) of Regulation 910/2014 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1183 requires every Member State to provide at least one wallet within 24 months of the first implementing acts entering into force; those acts entered into force on 24/12/2024, so the hard national deadline is 24/12/2026, not the 06/12/2026 previously carried in this file. The implementing regulation on national relying-party registers applies from the same day and was amended on 15/07/2026 (in force 11/08/2026) to mandate automated issuance of registration certificates, add a Union-harmonised access policy and replace the certificate-policy standards. An April-2026 rollout tracker records seven of the ten EU footprint markets with no public sandbox — BG, HR, CZ, RO and SI, plus CY and HU on unconfirmed upgrade paths — against confirmed upgrades only in Austria, Greece and Slovakia. Those seven markets cannot self-serve, which is the commercial opening; Romania's national wallet is separately due December 2026 on the back of its chip electronic ID.
deadlines.source: [EUR-Lex — consolidated Reg (EU) No 910/2014, Arts. 5a(1) and 5f(2)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014R0910-20241018); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Albania: POS acceptance mandate extends to all remaining businesses
deadlines.forces: The 2026 fiscal package mandates a POS terminal for all taxpayers, with cash limits cut; the first phase for accommodation, transport and public institutions passed on 30/05/2026 and every other business follows by 31/12/2026. The POS estate is already at a record 32,224 terminals, up 28% year on year, and ATM cash-deposit transactions grew 109% by count and 110% by value in 2025 against a fleet of 1,091 ATMs of which 430 are deposit-capable. Mastercard's free-POS wave 2 runs 01/05/2026 to 31/12/2026 or 3,000 terminals through Raiffeisen, Union Bank and BKT, and Raiffeisen's variant is a free softPOS on a supplied smartphone — a live risk to the micro-merchant tail that has to be answered rather than ignored. Anchor the pitch on the market-wide NCR software and maintenance position and attach terminal management, monitoring and recyclers.
deadlines.source: [Monitor.al — Bank of Albania / fiscal-package POS mandate](https://monitor.al/ulet-kufiri-per-parane-cash-deri-ne-fund-te-vitit-2026-te-gjithe-bizneset-me-terminale-pos/); A4 findings 2026-07-15, A1 findings 2026-07-14

deadlines.title: Hungary: Act XVIII Phase 2 — an ATM in every settlement above 500 people
deadlines.forces: Roughly 631 net-new mandated rural ATMs into settlements of 500 to 1,000 people, on top of the approximately 1,039 delivered in Phase 1, all into low-traffic sites that favour low-cost deployment, recyclers, remote monitoring and outsourced operation. Two MNB rules stack on the same estate: since 01/07/2026 forint may be recirculated through an ATM only if verified by an MNB-listed banknote-validation machine, and decision H-KPL-I-B-5/2026 requires MBH to hold at least 98% annual-average cash-machine availability from 01/08/2026 — certified validators plus hard uptime SLAs. Procurement is private, so pursue the nine obligated banks directly against decree 19/2025's per-bank allocation (OTP 428, MBH 195/316, K&H 117, Erste 104 and so on); named Hungarian operators are NCR Magyarorszag, Diebold Nixdorf Kft and Civil Ertekiogisztika.
deadlines.source: [MNB decree 19/2025 — per-bank allocation list (Bank360)](https://bank360.hu/blog/megszuletett-a-lista-melyik-telepulesre-melyik-bank-telepit-atm-et); A1/A2 findings 2026-07-14, A4 findings 2026-07-15

deadlines.title: Bosnia & Herzegovina: compulsory participation in IPS BiH instant payments
deadlines.forces: The CBBiH Governing Board decision of 10/07/2026, Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant placanja, makes participation compulsory: Article 7 obliges any bank that executed 1 million or more cumulative RTGS and giro-clearing transactions between 01/01/2026 and 30/06/2026 to be a participant from 01/01/2027, with a rolling 500,000-transaction trigger catching further banks each following 1 July. Article 13 makes a mobile or electronic payment platform the mandatory initiation channel and caps a single order at BAM 5,000; Article 12 sets a 10-second gross, irrevocable, final settlement ceiling, so fraud and AML screening must complete inside it; Article 5 additionally requires an ESMIG connection, a payment-operations licence, a central-bank reserve account, an IPS settlement account and passed test scenarios. The rail went live on 20/07/2026 with only three banks connected — Intesa Sanpaolo, Raiffeisen and Sparkasse, about a quarter of sector assets — with Nova banka Banja Luka joining 28/07/2026, leaving some 18 to 20 banks to integrate. The EUR 2m EU envelope funds only the central platform and its first year, so bank-side spend is additive.
deadlines.source: [CBBiH — Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant placanja](https://www.cbbh.ba/data/dokumenti/pdf/1024-6_Odluka_o_pravilima_rada_instant_pla%C4%87anja.pdf); A1 findings 2026-07-30, A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Bulgaria: Verification of Payee and instant-payments obligation for all banks
deadlines.forces: **The legal basis is no longer contested — resolved this cycle.** The 01/01/2027 date is now traceable to the Official Journal text itself, Regulation 260/2012 Article 16(9) as inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/886, and recital 11 names ATMs and self-service terminals among the in-scope payment-initiation channels. That turns a legal argument into a DEVICE-ESTATE obligation with four months to run: every Bulgarian bank must be able to run a payee-name check on transfers initiated at its machines, not only in its app. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [EUR-Lex Reg. (EU) 2024/886](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/886/oj))
deadlines.source: [UBB — Verification of Payee service notice, 15/07/2026](https://www.ubb.bg/news/view/proverka-na-poluchatelya-verification-of-payee); A1 findings 2026-07-30, A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Croatia: shared national ATM network — interbank obligation bites (NN 105/2025)
deadlines.forces: The amendments to the payment-account comparability and basic-account law, enacted 23/07/2025 as Narodne novine 105/2025, give consumers two free monthly withdrawals at other banks' ATMs from 01/01/2027 unless the banks build a shared national network first. The banks rejected the government memorandum; HUB commissioned Ernst & Young, which produced three operating models (status 27/04/2026), and the operator is still undecided. The market at stake is 3,816 active ATMs, 106 million withdrawals worth EUR 19.24bn, roughly 1,000 machines already pooled in MBNet and around EUR 380m of bank revenue exposed. The route is bank-association-led rather than public: TED sweeps of Croatian ATM and cash CPV classes return zero commercial-bank notices, so nothing will appear on EOJN and pre-tender positioning with HUB and the Ministry of Finance is the only way in — position managed services and multivendor software before the model is fixed.
deadlines.source: [Narodne novine 105/2025](https://narodne-novine.nn.hr/clanci/sluzbeni/2025_07_105_1453.html); A2 findings 2026-08-01

deadlines.title: Instant Payments Regulation: RECEIVE obligation + equal charges (non-euro CZ, HU, RO)
deadlines.forces: Read from the Official Journal, non-euro payment service providers must be able to RECEIVE instant euro credit transfers and charge no more than for standard transfers from 09/01/2027 — but e-money and payment institutions in those states receive only by 09/04/2027, with a further derogation running to 09/06/2028. Article 5d separately requires sanctions screening of users at least once every calendar day, which is a monitoring build in its own right. This is the non-euro date and must not be applied to Bulgaria (see the contested Bulgarian entry). Payment-hub, ISO 20022 and fraud-screening budgets commit in H2-2026.
deadlines.source: [ECB — Instant Payments Regulation](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/integration/retail/instant_payments/html/instant_payments_regulation.en.html); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Brink's / NCR Atleos $6.6bn merger expected close (~Q1 2027)
deadlines.forces: Both shareholder votes passed on 30/06/2026 (99.85% of NCR Atleos votes cast), HSR antitrust clearance is in hand and Indian competition clearance was collected on 22/07/2026, leaving the UK Competition and Markets Authority as the notable outstanding gate before the targeted Q1-2027 close. Printec's key ATM partner then sits inside a cash-in-transit conglomerate that also part-owns KAL — whose Kalignite multivendor software already runs under Asseco Central Europe, Mellon's Greek estate and Ceska sporitelna — and that can bundle hardware, logistics and managed services end-to-end. Vote risk is gone; the live question is post-close channel terms. Counterweight to lead with now: Printec was named Atleos Global Partner of the Year outright on 11/05/2026, not merely the European title previously recorded here.
deadlines.source: [UK CMA — Brink's / NCR Atleos merger inquiry](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry); A6 findings 2026-07-24, A8 findings 2026-07-15

deadlines.title: Montenegro: instant-payments phase 2 — QR acceptance, aliases and Request-to-Pay
deadlines.forces: Montenegro put its TIPS Clone rail live at ALL 11 banks simultaneously on 20/07/2026, with a compulsory free Verification of Payee check, ten-second irrevocable settlement and a regulator-imposed 5-cent fee cap on transfers below EUR 200. Phase 2 — QR acceptance, phone-number aliases and Request-to-Pay — is dated to March 2027, which is the merchant-acceptance and channel build behind the rail. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md))

deadlines.title: Instant Payments Regulation: SEND obligation + Verification of Payee (non-euro CZ, HU, RO)
deadlines.forces: Non-euro payment service providers must be able to SEND instant euro credit transfers from euro accounts and to provide Verification of Payee, completing the instant-rails and name-matching build-out begun for the January 2027 receive date. Mandatory VoP has been live for euro-area PSPs since 09/10/2025, so the vendor patterns are proven and the sale is delivery capacity rather than design.
deadlines.source: [ECB — Instant Payments Regulation](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/integration/retail/instant_payments/html/instant_payments_regulation.en.html); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: EU AML Regulation applies — the real anchor (CORRECTS the 10/07/2026 'AMLA submits its RTS rulebook' entry)
deadlines.forces: The previous entry said AMLA submitted the bulk of its RTS rulebook to the Commission on 10/07/2026. It did not: the Article 28(1) customer-due-diligence RTS is still at 'consultation closed', past AMLA's own statutory submission date, on a tracker updated 21/07/2026; the only thing published was the final ITS on supervisory cooperation, on 21/07/2026. The dependable anchor is 10/07/2027, when the AML Regulation applies directly — a single harmonised rulebook for customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence and beneficial ownership across every EU footprint market, a EUR 10,000 cash cap, crypto-asset service providers in scope and wallet/eID remote KYC formally accepted, with the bulk of AMLD6's staggered calendar landing the same day. Onboarding and monitoring stacks must be compliant by then, cash thresholds touch recycler reporting workflows, and national programmes (Slovakia's goAML adapter, Slovenia's MONEYVAL enhanced follow-up, Cyprus's directive re-test) all have to be re-cut against it — sell one combined programme into the FY2027 budget round, not two.
deadlines.source: [AMLR (Reg. (EU) 2024/1624)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1624/oj/eng); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: EU digital identity wallet: bank acceptance duty for private relying parties
deadlines.forces: Article 5f(2) obliges private relying parties — expressly including banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions, and excepting only micro and small enterprises — to accept the wallet by 24/12/2027 wherever strong user authentication is already required by law or contract, which the EU authentication regime supplies, and only upon the voluntary request of the user. That makes it a dated, footprint-wide relying-party build inside onboarding and login, plus access and registration certificates and the hardware-security-module key custody behind them; because acceptance is request-driven, the verifier is sized for optional rather than universal traffic, which caps the sizing but not the obligation. North Macedonia has separately transposed eIDAS 2 with its own bank wallet-verifier obligation from 01/06/2027, so the non-EU footprint is not exempt from the pattern.
deadlines.source: [EUR-Lex — consolidated Reg (EU) No 910/2014, Art. 5f(2)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02014R0910-20241018); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: AMLA direct supervision begins + SSM TLPT first three-year cycle deadline (17/01/2028)
deadlines.forces: Around 40 cross-border groups — Erste, RBI and OTP are candidates — come under direct AMLA supervision, with the selection process running through 2027. In parallel, threat-led penetration testing under the SSM framework closes its first three-year cycle, driving remediation spend on telemetry, monitoring and HSM/PCI work; Austria, Czechia, Romania and Slovakia are the four footprint states that have adopted TIBER-EU.
deadlines.source: [AMLA — selection of entities for direct supervision](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en); A3 findings 2026-08-02

deadlines.title: Addiko carve-out banks: transitional services from Addiko expire (12+12 months from closing)
deadlines.forces: The Transitional Services Agreement runs 12 months after carve-out closing with a single 12-month extension option, after which Addiko Serbia, Addiko Sarajevo, Addiko Banja Luka and Addiko Podgorica must source services from Alta Group or from third parties. With closing expected in H2 2027 that puts the replacement window at roughly 2H2028-2H2029 — a date written into the deal documents rather than guessed, and the reason vendor selection starts well before closing. ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

deadlines.title: Digital euro: potential first issuance (target, contingent on the 2026 legislation)
deadlines.forces: A 12-month PSP pilot runs H2-2027 into 2028 with potential issuance in 2029, distributed through banks and PSPs — which implies ATM and POS acceptance-device work, DESP back-end certification, wallet and onboarding integration and HSM key management. Low confidence and a long fuse, but the acceptance-device specifications are being written now and Cyprus is already inside a pilot, so specification influence is cheap today and expensive later.
deadlines.source: [ECB — digital euro progress report](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/progress/html/ecb.deprp202510.en.html); A3 findings 2026-07-24

deadlines.title: European Accessibility Act: transition ENDS for pre-2025 self-service terminals
deadlines.forces: The operative date is 28/06/2030, not 2045: service providers may keep using self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 only until then, subject to a 20-year economic-life cap, with 28/06/2045 merely the outer backstop for the newest of those machines. Anything placed on the market after 28/06/2025 must comply immediately. There is no presumption of conformity today — EN 301 549 V3.2.1 is not cited in the Official Journal under the EAA, and the first EAA-track version, draft V4.1.0 realigned to WCAG 2.2, was still in ETSI public enquiry at 03/08/2026 — so conformity must be self-declared against the Annex I essential requirements with the supplier's own technical documentation, which makes test-evidenced accessibility a genuine tender differentiator. Enforcement has begun: Austria's market-surveillance authority had 84 proceedings open at 24/06/2026, 22 of the pending ones on banking services, plus 53 self-notifications and a maximum fine of EUR 80,000 (not the EUR 50,000 previously carried); Czechia issued its first breach findings on 15/07/2026; in Hungary the MNB itself supervises ATM accessibility with a ceiling of 5% of net revenue or HUF 500m. Bulgaria and Hungary carry a 28/06/2027 milestone, and Greek political pressure is live after the 14/05/2026 parliamentary referral. The replace-versus-retrofit cycle runs 2027-2030.
