outlook.scope: Kosovo: central bank instant-payment contracts awarded, bank integration still open
outlook.summary:
Kosovo's central bank has now bought both pieces it needed for instant payments. A connectivity core was awarded to Nexi Payments SpA at EUR 685,000, published 12/08/2026. A ten-month design and programme-management advisory was awarded to Paylume on 22/07/2026. Onboarding is scheduled for the November 2026 window ([BQK contract award notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Contract_Award_Notice_TIPS-Clone-Connectivity-Services.pdf)).

The core itself is closed to outside bidders. So the remaining money is at the seven commercial banks, none of which has published a connection date. Each must map ISO 20022 messages (the international payment-message standard), offer instant payments through mobile and internet banking, screen a rail that never closes, and build the four named overlays.

Expect growth in channel integration, real-time monitoring, key management and round-the-clock operations. Speed is the deciding factor, because a named competitor now sits inside the central bank for five years.
outlook.projected:
Growth, with the shape of the opportunity now settled.

Banca d'Italia confirmed that the shared instant-payment platform went live on 20/07/2026, with Bosnia and Montenegro as first joiners. A second onboarding window in November 2026 covers Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

Kosovo's central bank has completed its own buying. The connectivity layer went to Nexi Payments SpA at a final price of EUR 685,000, for 120 days of delivery plus five years of maintenance. It was notified on 03/06/2026 and published on 12/08/2026. The only rival bid, from SWIFT at EUR 301,138, was declared non-responsive because the bidding forms were not completed ([BQK award notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Contract_Award_Notice_TIPS-Clone-Connectivity-Services.pdf)).

A ten-month advisory for design and programme management went to Paylume SRL of Brussels at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026, from a single expression of interest. The funder restricts that core to a network service provider already authorised for the platform, so it was never open to contest. The real consequence is positional. A named competitor now holds a five-year contract and a standing relationship at the central bank, with an obvious path to sell overlay services outward.

The bank-side work carries the spending, and it has no date. Raiffeisen, NLB, TEB, ProCredit, BKT, Banka Ekonomike and Banka per Biznes must each connect to the national system and map ISO 20022 payment messages. They must also offer instant payments through mobile and internet banking, and reconcile a rail that never closes. The chair of the Banking Association's payments committee states the commercial banks' full commitment to join, but no bank connection date is published anywhere.

Round-the-clock irrevocable settlement removes the overnight batch window in which fraud used to be caught. That is what pulls through real-time transaction monitoring, instant sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening, hardware security modules and 24/7 managed operations. The central bank's Annual Report names four overlays being scoped on top of the national system. They are QR code, request to pay, proxy identifier and Verification of Payee. That last one is the check that the name on a transfer matches the account. This is the merchant-acceptance and channel work that follows.

Two funding and compliance currents run alongside. The World Bank operation behind the whole programme, Component 3 of the Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project, is costed at USD 5.0m within a USD 52m operation. It commits eleven institutions to invest private money in fast-payment-ready infrastructure by June 2030. The goods and IT procurement tables are still empty, and open international competition is required at or above USD 1.5m. Four programme-unit consultant contracts are planned for signature on 07/09/2026, which is the signal to start watching ([World Bank implementation status report and procurement plan](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051526174517828/pdf/P507881-c295d365-73e9-4972-93a5-a4072086c160.pdf)).

The second current is a binding cyber-risk rulebook whose compliance date passed on 01/06/2026. It requires a four-hour incident notification and names cash machines as regulated critical infrastructure. It also obliges institutions to hold a cybersecurity budget separate from the general technology budget ([CBK — Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en)).

Where to point it: the seven commercial banks, on channel-side integration, machine and kiosk software change, transaction monitoring and fraud screening. Start with the three that showed live tap-to-phone propositions at the national merchant roadshow, namely Raiffeisen, NLB and ProCredit, as warm back-end entry points. Then TEB, which has failed twice to land a remote-onboarding and qualified electronic-signature stack, most recently on a tender extended twice to 29/06/2026. The World Bank procurement channel is the third route, and it can be monitored from outside without a local portal account.

Conclusion: work the bank-side integration and screening layer across all seven banks now. Watch the empty World Bank goods and IT tables from the 07/09/2026 consultant signatures onward.
drivers: The regional platform has been live since 20/07/2026. Kosovo's central bank is scheduled for the November 2026 onboarding window ([Banca d'Italia](https://www.bancaditalia.it/media/notizia/tips-clone-platform-for-instant-payments-in-the-western-balkans-goes-live/)).

The central bank has bought both required pieces: connectivity to Nexi at EUR 685,000, published 12/08/2026, and advisory to Paylume at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026. So the remaining spend is bank-side ([BQK award notice](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Contract_Award_Notice_TIPS-Clone-Connectivity-Services.pdf)).
All seven commercial banks must connect, map ISO 20022 messages and reconcile a rail that never closes. No bank connection date has been published anywhere.
Four overlays are named by the central bank as being scoped: QR code, request to pay, proxy identifier and Verification of Payee. Each is a separate channel build.

The World Bank component funding the programme commits eleven institutions to invest in fast-payment infrastructure to June 2030. The goods and IT procurement tables are still empty, and open international competition is required at or above USD 1.5m ([World Bank procurement plan](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051526174517828/pdf/P507881-c295d365-73e9-4972-93a5-a4072086c160.pdf)).

A binding cyber-risk regulation, whose compliance date passed on 01/06/2026, forces a ring-fenced cybersecurity budget and four-hour incident reporting. It names cash machines as critical infrastructure ([CBK regulation](https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-sistemet-e-informacionit-1-1.pdf?lang=en)).
outlook.rationale:
The central bank finished buying this cycle. With the connectivity award published on 12/08/2026 and the advisory contract awarded on 22/07/2026, the programme moved from planning into delivery. The open question changed from whether the rail happens to when each commercial bank connects to it, and nobody has published that.

That undated bank-side gap sits between a November onboarding window and a competitor newly installed at the central bank on a five-year contract. That is why the next two quarters are the moment to engage all seven banks, rather than wait for a tender to appear.
cite_ungrounded: No commercial-bank connection date has been published anywhere, so the bank-side timetable is inferred from the November 2026 central-bank onboarding window rather than sourced.
The expectation that the connectivity contractor will sell overlay services outward to commercial banks is the analysts' assessment in the underlying signal, not a stated intention by that company.
Kosovo's SEPA application remains blocked by two laws still in constitutional review, so the wider compliance wave behind this programme has no fixed date.

outlook.scope: Supervisory action plans due by October require banks to name their end-of-life machines
outlook.summary:
This is the firmest dated trigger for technology spending in the seven supervised markets in the footprint: Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia and Slovakia. It points straight at ageing self-service estates, meaning a bank's fleet of ATMs and kiosks.

Every significant institution must file an action plan with its Joint Supervisory Team by 31/10/2026. That team is the European Central Bank team that supervises the individual bank. One of the six named focus areas is replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies ([ECB — letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)). Money for fixes therefore has to be written into a document that a supervisor then monitors.

A second named focus area, accurate identification of technology assets, is a sale of device telemetry in its own right. Device telemetry is automatic reporting from each machine. The same letter also brings supplier service-level agreements and contract terms into scope. So this is both an opportunity and a duty to review every managed-service contract Printec already holds.

Two supply-side complications fall in the same fortnight. A competitor is selling banks the opposite answer, keeping old machines alive with virtualisation software. Printec's main machine supplier is also going through a dated regulatory review that would make it part of a direct competitor.
outlook.projected:
Strong growth, and the clearest funded trigger in the whole book. The order of events is fixed.

Claudia Buch signed the letter on 07/07/2026. The same 31/10/2026 deadline was then repeated in Official Journal text. It came through the European Systemic Risk Board's formal warning of 25/06/2026, published on 16/07/2026. So it is no longer only a letter.

On 31/07/2026 the three European Supervisory Authorities extended the same governance expectation down to smaller banks supervised at national level. That is the mid-market tier where most of Printec's estate sits. The ECB's annual technology-risk questionnaire has also moved from September 2026 to February 2027, which extends the evidence window rather than closing it.

The likely next supervisory step is threat-led penetration testing. That is a controlled attack simulation run against live production systems under Articles 26 and 27 of the digital operational resilience rules. Supervisors recognise each other's tests. So one group-level exercise at Erste, RBI, OTP, NLB or UniCredit can pull Printec-operated estates in several countries into a single window. The repair work afterwards is the actual sale ([Hrvatska narodna banka — Digitalna operativna otpornost](https://www.hnb.hr/-/digitalna-operativna-otpornost)).

Two counterweights must be stated plainly. KAL is marketing a hypervisor, which is software that runs one system inside another. It runs a newer Windows on old machines, even where the hardware maker no longer supports them. It has a named Czech reference, plus a zero-licence pre-install offer that fits under any multivendor software account. The counter-argument is total cost of ownership: a fleet kept alive in software still fails mechanically, and still cannot take deposits or recycle notes.

The UK competition authority opened its Phase 1 inquiry into Brink's purchase of NCR Atleos on 26/08/2026. The statutory decision deadline is 22/10/2026, while both companies moved expected completion forward to early Q1-2027 ([UK CMA — Brink's / NCR Atleos merger inquiry](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry)). Printec's main supplier of dispense, deposit and recycling machines is about to be owned by a company that competes with Printec directly.

Where to focus: the significant institutions filing on 31/10/2026. They include Erste Group and RBI in Vienna, Bank of Cyprus, the Greek banks, the Bulgarian banks now under direct supervision since euro entry, and the Slovenian and Slovak groups. Next come the smaller nationally supervised banks caught by the 31/07/2026 extension.

Internally, the focus is the DORA register of information. Its 31/12/2026 reference date feeds national bank-level cut-offs in February and March 2027. Failing to supply clean register data is a common reason for a service to be put back out to tender.

Conclusion: sell the asset inventory and the deposit-and-recycling refresh against a filing date the customer cannot move. In parallel, put written distributor-continuity terms in place before 22/10/2026, together with change-of-control and price-protection clauses.
drivers: Every significant institution must submit an AI-cyber action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by 31/10/2026. Focus area 5 requires modernising infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies. Focus area 1 requires accurate inventories of technology assets ([ECB — letter SSM-2026-0301](https://www.bankingsupervision.europa.eu/press/letterstobanks/shared/pdf/2026/ssm.2026_letter_on_AI_enabled_cybersecurity_threats.en.pdf)).

KAL is pitching its Kalignite hypervisor across Greece, Czechia, Slovakia and Romania precisely so banks can keep ageing machines through the move to Windows 11. It returns to Banktech in Athens on 08-09/10/2026 as a guest of Mellon. This is independent confirmation that the end of life of machine operating systems is the main area of competition in 2026-27 ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

The Brink's purchase of NCR Atleos reached a dated regulatory step on 26/08/2026. A Phase 1 decision is due 22/10/2026, and completion has moved forward to early Q1-2027. Atleos held no Q2 earnings call and published no outlook, so the usual regional commentary has gone quiet for at least two quarters ([UK CMA — Brink's / NCR Atleos merger inquiry](https://www.gov.uk/cma-cases/the-brinks-company-slash-ncr-atleos-corporation-merger-inquiry)).

Diebold Nixdorf's Q2 filings of 29/07/2026 show European banking product sales down 13.0% to USD 236.6m on lower European volume. Its services base held, and it shipped a record number of teller cash recyclers. Its hardware refresh cycle has stalled, but it is now bundling branch automation, cash management and long-term service agreements ([Diebold Nixdorf Form 10-Q, quarter ended 30/06/2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/28823/000002882326000033/dbd-20260630.htm)).

The ECB has committed in writing to a separate future letter on post-quantum cryptography, which is encryption designed to survive a future large-scale quantum computer. It says adoption must start now, but gives no date. So it is an announced supervisory action, and must never be presented to a customer as a deadline ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).
outlook.rationale:
The change that matters is enforceability. A supervisory letter became Official Journal text on 16/07/2026. The expectation was pushed down to nationally supervised banks on 31/07/2026. The evidence window was extended to February 2027.

So what was guidance in July is now a dated duty with follow-up monitoring. It lands during the autumn planning round, when 2027 budgets are set. The calendar also adds commercial urgency. The competition decision on Printec's own supply chain falls on 22/10/2026. That is nine days before the banks file the plans naming the machines they intend to replace.
cite_ungrounded: Pairing the 22/10/2026 competition decision with the 31/10/2026 supervisory filing is our own juxtaposition; no source connects the two events.

The reading that the Cyber Resilience Act captures cash machines, point-of-sale terminals, kiosks, recyclers and hardware security modules — and that it places Printec in an importer or distributor role — is explicitly flagged as an interpretation that no cited source states.

That ageing machines on unsupported operating systems fall inside the ECB's 'legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies' wording is a reading of the letter's language, not a category the ECB names.
No count of how many machines in the footprint actually run unsupported software exists in any signal, so the scale of the refresh population is unquantified here.

outlook.scope: Structured payment address data becomes mandatory across all seventeen markets in November
outlook.summary:
A hard network deadline in November forces address and party data into a structured format across every market Printec operates in. Messages that do not conform are rejected.

The euro settlement platform's release goes into production on Saturday 14/11/2026. Its test window opens 25/09/2026 and closes 28/10/2026. That closing date is the real hard stop, because a bank that has not tested by then has no second chance ([Deutsche Bundesbank — T2 R2026.NOV release information](https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/994978/e841962b2370d811340b0fa5e3f61080/472B63F073F071307366337C94F8C870/t2-r2026nov-information-on-release-data.pdf)).

The scheme-side cut-off reported for 15/11/2026 at 03:30 CET could not be checked at source this cycle. It must be flagged as unverified in every customer conversation.

The settlement core itself is not Printec's lane. The layer around it is. That work covers cleaning address and party data, plus re-tuning sanctions and financial-crime screening onto the structured fields. It also covers payment repair, monitoring rejects through the cutover weekend, and the field services to run it.

The programme budget window has already closed. So the sale between now and November is emergency remediation rather than a planned migration. The largest unclaimed opportunity is in the non-EU markets, where no local regulator forces the change but correspondent flows break anyway. Correspondent flows are payments routed through partner banks.
outlook.projected:
Growth, but as a sharp, short spike rather than a lasting line, followed by a separately funded second wave.

The dated events run in order. The euro settlement release test window opens 25/09/2026 and closes 28/10/2026. Production deployment falls on Saturday 14/11/2026, alongside the annual standards-release weekend. The payment-scheme address cut-off is reported for 15/11/2026 at 03:30 CET. A second wave in November 2027 migrates seven core payment messages that stay on their 2019 version this year. So any vendor pitching a core schema migration in 2026 has the scope wrong.

Two corrections cap the honest scope. Only the structured town and country fields are needed for regulatory screening, so the data-cleaning job is narrower than it is usually sold as. But no end date has been set for the hybrid address format, so it must not be presented as permanent either.

Where to focus: banks in the ten European Union markets in the footprint that have not booked test slots in the 25/09–28/10/2026 window. There the work is data cleaning, repair and reject monitoring rather than platform change.

Next come the non-European Union markets: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo and Ukraine. No local regulator forces the change there, and correspondent traffic will reject regardless, which makes it the largest unclaimed opportunity.

The third group is any bank whose outsourced processing contract is ending. Worldline has told investors its bank-facing division carries a EUR 60m full-year drag from contract terminations and will not return to growth before the second half of 2027. That brings estates and payment operations back to market at exactly the moment they need hands-on remediation ([Worldline H1 2026 results presentation](https://investors.worldline.com/content/dam/investors-worldline-com/assets/documents/presentations/2026/20260730-worldline-h1-2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

Conclusion: sell survival of the test window and reject monitoring through October and November 2026. Keep the scope honest at town and country. Open the 2027 conversation on the second wave before the first one is finished.
drivers: The euro real-time settlement release goes into production on 14/11/2026. Testing is open from 25/09/2026 and closes 28/10/2026. Address removal reaches the core payment messages through a usage guideline rather than a schema change ([Deutsche Bundesbank — T2 R2026.NOV release information](https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/994978/e841962b2370d811340b0fa5e3f61080/472B63F073F071307366337C94F8C870/t2-r2026nov-information-on-release-data.pdf)).

Scheme guidance reported to fix the end of the unstructured address format states that its use will no longer be allowed. Rejects will follow, on the inter-bank leg and on corporate file upload alike. But the publisher's site was unreachable by every route this cycle, so this is reported, not verified ([EPC153-22 v2.1 — Provision of Addresses under the EPC Payment Schemes](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/sites/default/files/kb/file/2025-10/EPC153-22%20v2.1%20EPC%20guidance%20document%20-%20Provision%20of%20Addresses%20under%20the%20EPC%20Payment%20Schemes.pdf)).

A change request confirms that seven core payment messages stay on the 2019 version in November 2026 and are only probably migrated in November 2027. That splits the work into two separately funded waves ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The wider payments package that would extend Verification of Payee beyond instant payments has slipped. Verification of Payee is a check that the name on a transfer matches the account it is going to. The only forward date is an indicative plenary of 14/12/2026. So roadmaps must be reset, and no 2027 or 2028 compliance date should be quoted as fixed ([Council of the EU — ST 8221/26, Payment Services Regulation](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-8221-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).
outlook.rationale:
Two things make this the moment. First, the anchor date moved from vendor guidance to a central-bank release document. So the testing window of 25/09–28/10/2026 can be quoted to a customer as an operational fact, and that window opens within a month.

Second, the scoping errors can now be named. The seven core messages are not migrating this year, and only town and country are needed for screening. A bank that has not started has roughly five weeks to book testing. That is remediation work rather than programme work, and remediation is bought late, quickly and locally.
cite_ungrounded: The European Payments Council site was blocked to every route this cycle, so none of the five scheme dates carried here is verified at primary source — including the 15/11/2026 03:30 CET address cut-off and the four rulebooks it is said to span. Quote them to customers as reported-but-unverified.
The Verification-of-Payee rulebook version 1.1 becoming binding at 20/09/2026 03:30 CET is unverified this cycle for the same reason and does not appear in any cited signal.
Bulgaria's 01/01/2027 instant-payments date and the 09/01/2027 date for Czechia, Hungary and Romania are carried from briefing context and appear in none of the cited signals.
The claim of a network-level rejection mechanic at the messaging network is recorded as unverified in the underlying research and should not be asserted to a bank.
No signal quantifies how many footprint banks have yet to book a test slot, so the size of the remediation population is asserted from the shape of the deadline, not measured.

outlook.scope: Ten months to the money-laundering regulation, with the technical rulebook still unpublished
outlook.summary:
Every bank across the ten European Union markets in the footprint is now scoping financial-crime programmes against draft rules. The Anti-Money-Laundering Regulation applies directly on 10/07/2027, and the accompanying directive must be written into national law the same day.

A search of the European Union's own publications database on 27/08/2026 returned not a single binding technical text. Roughly nineteen mandates that were due on 10/07/2026 are overdue. They include the customer-due-diligence standards that say which sources may be used to verify identity ([AMLA — Regulatory Instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

That gap is the commercial argument. What banks can safely buy this autumn is a configurable rules layer that can be re-pointed when the official text lands, not a hard-coded onboarding or monitoring flow.

A second, larger programme runs alongside it and is bought centrally. The new anti-money-laundering authority is drawing up the list of cross-border groups it will supervise directly from 2028. Budget for both is committed in the 2027 planning round now open, from September to November 2026.
outlook.projected:
Growth, spread across two different buying centres.

On the per-country side, two consultations close on 03/09 and 20/09. Two more close on 27/09 and 06/10/2026. The first of them is the ongoing-monitoring guidelines, which are in effect the functional specification for transaction monitoring. A European Banking Authority reporting release also carries the new risk-assessment and eligibility taxonomy, applying to reports as of December 2026.

Transposition means writing the directive into national law, and it is uneven in a way that creates a specific window. Croatia has reported no measures against the July-2025 tranche, and Slovakia only partial ones. Infringement proceedings are pending against Croatia, Cyprus, Greece and Slovakia. So those banks get national rules late while the July-2027 date does not move. Historically, that is the pattern that produces rushed, vendor-led remediation ([European Commission — AMLD6 transposition monitoring](https://finance.ec.europa.eu/regulation-and-supervision/financial-services-legislation/enforcement-and-infringements-banking-and-finance-law/monitoring-banking-and-finance-directives/anti-money-laundering-and-terrorist-financing-directive-vi_en)).

On the group side, national supervisors filed their data by 15/08/2026. The provisional list of eligible entities is expected to be finalised at the end of September 2026. The first selection process must begin by 01/07/2027 and finish within six months, and direct supervision starts in 2028. The eligibility test is operating in at least six Member States including the home state ([AMLA — next step toward the 2027 selection of entities](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

What is really being tested there is whether customer-due-diligence and monitoring records are consistent across subsidiaries in eight to thirteen countries. That is a group-level data-lineage problem, bought centrally rather than country by country. Data lineage means tracing where each piece of data came from.

Underneath both runs the identity build. Every Member State must provide a digital identity wallet by 24/12/2026, and the register regime for the businesses that accept wallet presentations applies the same day. The bank-side duty to accept wallets is worked out, not printed, at 24/12/2027. Seven of the ten markets still had no public sandbox as of an April-2026 tracker, so those banks cannot test on their own ([European Commission — EUDI Architecture and Reference Framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

Where to focus: group compliance and data functions at the large cross-border groups, for the consistency and lineage work. Then Croatian and Slovak banks, for the late-rules remediation window.

The third target is the identity-verification build at banks in the seven markets without a sandbox. Sell it as a wallet-agnostic acceptance layer that keeps document-and-selfie proofing alongside it, because the portrait does not become mandatory wallet data until 2028 and may still be declined.

Conclusion: sell configurability and say so openly in bids. Get into the 2027 budget round before November. Treat the group-level data question as a separate and larger sale than the per-country compliance work.
drivers: Not one delegated or implementing regulation under the three anti-money-laundering instruments has reached the Official Journal. The two instruments that matter most to banks remain at 'consultation closed' with no final report. Their statutory delivery date of 10/07/2026 has been missed ([AMLA — Regulatory Instruments register](https://www.amla.europa.eu/policy/regulatory-instruments_en)).

The new authority's provisional list of eligible obliged entities is expected at end-September 2026. The first selection starts by 01/07/2027 and direct supervision runs from 2028. The eligibility test is operating in at least six Member States including the home state ([AMLA — next step toward the 2027 selection of entities](https://www.amla.europa.eu/amla-takes-next-step-toward-2027-selection-entities-direct-supervision_en)).

Member State wallet issuance and the relying-party register regime both apply from 24/12/2026. An amending implementing regulation in force from 11/08/2026 adds a biometric warning and an explicit confirmation step whenever a portrait is requested. It also adds a wallet trust mark and mandatory cryptographic mechanisms ([European Commission — EUDI Architecture and Reference Framework v3.0.0](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/releases/tag/v3.0.0)).

The crypto-asset transitional period ended on 01/07/2026. Unauthorised providers must wind down while keeping full customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and suspicious-activity reporting in place throughout. That gives two modest but real pulses of demand in identity verification and monitoring as client books move ([ESMA — public statement on the end of the MiCA transitional period](https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-06/ESMA75-113276571-1710_Public_Statement_MiCA_transitional_period_ends.pdf)).

The real artificial-intelligence compliance deadline for financial-crime analytics moved to 02/12/2027, not December 2026. That buys about a year, and means any customer being told otherwise is being mis-sold ([Official Journal — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj)).
outlook.rationale:
The reason to act now is a gap, not an event. Ten months before a directly applicable regulation, the binding detail does not exist. So every bank in the footprint is designing against drafts and knows it. That makes configurability a purchasing criterion this autumn rather than a feature claim.

At the same time, the group-level supervision list is being finalised at the end of September 2026, and the identity supply side goes live on 24/12/2026. Three separate timetables therefore meet in the same 2027 budget round, which opens now and closes in November.
cite_ungrounded: The inference that Erste, Raiffeisen Bank International, UniCredit, OTP, NLB and Intesa Sanpaolo all clear the six-Member-State eligibility test is Printec's own; the authority names no individual institution, and no group is identified as selected here for that reason.

Linking the overdue customer-due-diligence standards to the digital identity wallet is our reading: the standards are recorded as specifying the attributes electronic identification must carry, but no cited source names the EU wallet as the vehicle.
The bank-side wallet acceptance date of 24/12/2027 is derived from a 36-month clock in the legal text and is not printed anywhere; it must be presented to customers as derived.
The 'seven of ten markets without a public sandbox' figure comes from an April-2026 tracker and may have moved since.

outlook.scope: Digital euro: funded terminal work now, and no funding for cash machines
outlook.summary:
The digital euro is real and has dates. But the part of it that touches cash machines is explicitly not funded, and that distinction is the most useful thing a sales force can carry this year.

The draft scheme rulebook of 02/07/2026 does contain a full section covering cash funding, cash defunding and balance enquiry at a machine, with flows started by card and by code. The same annex states word for word that those use cases are deprioritised and will be addressed later ([ECB — draft digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91, Annex D1](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/timeline/profuse/shared/pdf/ecb.derdgpr260702_Digital_euro_scheme_rulebook_v0.91_-_Annex_D1_-_Front-end_implementation_specifications_4_Acceptance_device.en.pdf)).

What is funded is the pilot. Thirty-six payment service providers test four use cases, with no machine and no hardware terminal case. Development runs from Q3-2026, and operation runs for twelve months from the second half of 2027.

So the warm sale is terminal firmware, contactless and offline readiness, and remote update capability at the named pilot banks. The honest machine offer is a readiness assessment and a survey of gaps in code capability. Hardware should never be sold against a deadline that does not exist.

The first market discussion of rollout strategy is 13/10/2026. The sentence to watch is the deprioritisation sentence: if it changes in a later rulebook version, the whole euro-area machine estate becomes a buy signal.
outlook.projected:
Mixed by design: growth on terminals, flat on machines, with the machine side depending on one sentence in the rulebook.

The dated triggers start with the 21st Euro Retail Payments Board technical session on 13/10/2026, the first time rollout strategy is discussed with the market. The pilot development phase is already running from Q3-2026. The twelve-month operating phase starts in the second half of 2027, which obliges the named banks to have terminal readiness in place well before it begins.

Parliament confirmed its negotiating mandate on 09/07/2026 by 416 votes to 169 with 22 abstentions. The central bank is formalising a memorandum of understanding with the payments-scheme body. That body's named candidate standards include a code-based payment standard described as potentially covering machine transactions. That point is reported, but could not be checked at source this cycle.

Two related cash files sit behind it. The legal-tender file entered trilogue on 08/07/2026, with political agreement targeted around end-2026. Trilogue means three-way talks between Parliament, Council and Commission. The draft names density of cash access points relative to population as a monitoring indicator, and geographical access requirements would follow if that indicator fails.

If that survives adoption, it is the largest single machine signal anywhere in the regulatory book. But nothing is adopted, and the indicator is not verified in the mandate articles. So a gap analysis of estate density may be sold today only as scenario planning.

The euro banknote redesign has a public survey closing 21/09/2026 and a design decision expected around end-2026. The manufacturer Glory guides related equipment demand from around 2029 ([ECB — ECB reveals shortlisted designs for new banknotes](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260723~c2d43f9170.en.html)). A series change is a recurring stream of recognition-template, sensor and re-testing work rather than a machine replacement. That favours a field organisation over a pure manufacturer. The condition is that the budget lines are shaped in the 2027 and 2028 planning rounds, instead of arriving as a single manufacturer package.

Where to focus: the named pilot banks, on terminal and terminal-management readiness for the second half of 2027. They are BAWAG P.S.K. and Raiffeisen Bank International in Austria, Bank of Cyprus with JCC Payment Systems, and three Greek banks including Piraeus. The list also includes Tatra banka with the Slovak central bank, NLB in Slovenia, Raiffeisenbank Austria in Croatia and UniCredit.

Offer the same accounts a readiness assessment for the machine estate, priced as an assessment. Offer euro-area central banks and large branch networks banknote-redesign service planning for 2027-2028 budgets.

Conclusion: sell terminal readiness where the obligation is real. Do not sell machine hardware against a deprioritised use case. Watch the rulebook version for the sentence that would change that.
drivers: The pilot tests four use cases only, with no machine and no hardware terminal case. It runs from Q3-2026 into a twelve-month operating phase from the second half of 2027. Bulgaria is not among the nineteen participating central banks, despite having joined the euro on 01/01/2026 ([ECB — press release naming the 36 pilot payment service providers](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260714~8cd07d9d45.en.html)).

The rulebook's machine annex says plainly that those use cases are deprioritised and will be addressed at a later stage. Version 0.91 was still the latest when re-checked on 27/08/2026. So there is no certification duty and no trigger for capital spending on the machine estate ([ECB — draft digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91, Annex D1](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/timeline/profuse/shared/pdf/ecb.derdgpr260702_Digital_euro_scheme_rulebook_v0.91_-_Annex_D1_-_Front-end_implementation_specifications_4_Acceptance_device.en.pdf)).

Worldline is positioning itself as digital-euro infrastructure through PAYONE in Germany and Austria, as both acquirer and technical service provider. Meanwhile its bank-facing division shrank 7.1% organically in the first half of 2026 and will not return to growth before the second half of 2027 ([Worldline H1 2026 results presentation](https://investors.worldline.com/content/dam/investors-worldline-com/assets/documents/presentations/2026/20260730-worldline-h1-2026-results-presentation.pdf)).

The euro legal-tender file moved into trilogue after the plenary confirmed the mandate on 08/07/2026. The duty only bites through a Commission implementing act that defines the indicators, so the first half of 2027 is the earliest it could matter ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Accessibility rules already require self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 to be replaced or retrofitted by 28/06/2030. The pending payments package would forbid making authentication depend on owning a smartphone. Those are two independent reasons the attended and self-service estate stays in scope ([Council of the EU — ST 8221/26, Payment Services Regulation](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-8221-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).
outlook.rationale:
The reason to make this call now is protective as much as commercial. The pilot list published on 14/07/2026 created named banks with a contractual duty and a readiness date in the second half of 2027. That is a concrete terminal build to sell this autumn.

In the same fortnight the rulebook confirmed that the machine use cases are deprioritised, and a re-check on 27/08/2026 confirmed it again. Someone is likely to tell the market that the digital euro requires new machines. Separating the funded and unfunded halves before the 13/10/2026 rollout-strategy session keeps the terminal sale credible and stops the machine estate being mis-sold.
cite_ungrounded: Everything on the payments-scheme side — the memorandum of understanding with the European Payments Council and the code-based payment standard named as potentially covering machine transactions — is reported through secondary reading only, because the scheme body's site was blocked to every route this cycle and none of its dates is verified at primary.

The cash-access-point density indicator rests on a Parliament summary page last updated before the committee vote, so it describes a draft report rather than the adopted negotiating mandate, and is not verified in the mandate articles.
The banknote-redesign demand cycle from around 2029 rests on a single manufacturer's investor guidance and on one research unit; the regulation workstream filed no row on it at all.
The list of named pilot participants is assembled from several per-market rows rather than read off one published list, so treat the roster as compiled rather than authoritative.

product_outlooks.label: ATM & cash automation / recycling
product_outlooks.scope: ATM fleet conversion: dispense-only machines becoming deposit machines
product_outlooks.summary:
This line is growing, but almost none of the growth is in the number of machines. ATM fleets across Printec's markets are flat or shrinking. The spending is going into the machines that already exist. Banks are turning cash-out-only ATMs into recyclers, which are machines that re-use the notes customers have just paid in.

Two dated requirements drive the next twelve months. First, every bank directly supervised by the European Central Bank must give its supervisor a plan by 31 October 2026. That plan must name the “legacy, unsupported or end-of-life” technology the bank will replace, which covers ATMs still running unsupported operating systems ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)). Second, Hungary has passed a law under which ATMs may be replaced but never removed ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The pool of machines to convert is no longer an estimate. It is a count taken from the banks' own data feeds. Two thirds of BCR's 1,668 Romanian devices cannot take a deposit. Roughly 1,840 to 1,950 dispense-only sites sit across Bulgaria's four largest banks ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec should aim this line at those named fleets and at the two contests that are already open, in Austria and Ukraine. It should sell device telemetry, meaning remote machine monitoring, and cash-cycle software together with the hardware rather than afterwards.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, and the timing is unusually easy to date. The firmest trigger anywhere in Printec's markets is the European Central Bank's supervisory letter SSM-2026-0301, signed 7 July 2026. It tells every significant institution to send an artificial-intelligence and cyber action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by 31 October 2026. Focus area 5 requires the replacement of legacy, unsupported and end-of-life technology. Focus area 1 requires an accurate inventory of information-technology assets. On 31 July 2026 the three European supervisory authorities extended the same expectation to nationally supervised mid-market banks, which is where most of Printec's estate sits ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Hungary is the second dated force. Since 14 May 2026, Act XIV of 2026 has banned a bank from shutting down any ATM that existed when the Act came into force. It expressly allows replacement instead. The law itself expects that the replacement machine may not fit the old opening, because of its size and security requirements. That is exactly what happens when a through-the-wall dispenser is swapped for a deposit or recycling machine. Alongside it, Act XVIII still requires ATM cash withdrawal in every settlement above 500 inhabitants by 31 December 2026, across 1,039 named settlements allocated to nine banks ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Two contests are open now rather than expected later. Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m banknote and coin recycler framework was checked again on 31 August 2026 and was still unawarded. The recorded contract start is 2 November 2026, and call-off deliveries under it can reach Slovenia, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)). PrivatBank's recycler renewal closed stage-one qualification on 25 August 2026. The commercial round is the next step, on a specification written to a Diebold Nixdorf software baseline ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Croatia adds a structural deadline of 1 January 2027. By then the banks must set up a national shared ATM network, or let any consumer withdraw free twice a month at any bank ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

Where to aim: at the counted conversion populations rather than the market totals.

- Romania: BCR's 1,100 dispense-only machines, and CEC Bank's roughly 350 branches marked for operating-model redesign.
- Hungary: MBH's 1,029 cash-out-only machines, of which the 803 inherited from Takarékbank take no deposits at all, plus OTP Hungary's 1,220.
- Bulgaria: the 1,840 to 1,950 dispense-only sites across UBB, Postbank, DSK and UniCredit Bulbank.
- Croatia: Zagrebačka banka's 562, ahead of the shared-network decision.
- Serbia: AikBank's 457 of 570. The bank refits a branch roughly every two weeks to a published standard specification, so the target is the standard rather than the site.
- Czechia: the 944 cash-out-only machines in the four-bank pool, worst at MONETA and Air Bank.
- Slovakia: the retrofit tail, where cash desks have gone from only 25 of 121 VÚB branches and 16 of 47 at UniCredit.

([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

In short: run this line as a conversion programme driven by supervisory deadlines, aimed at named machine populations. Attach device telemetry, cash forecasting and multivendor ATM software to every machine.
drivers: The European Central Bank's letter SSM-2026-0301 of 7 July 2026 sets a deadline of 31 October 2026. By then every significant institution must name its legacy, unsupported and end-of-life technology in a plan that a supervisor reads. The same expectation was pushed down to nationally supervised banks on 31 July 2026. An ageing ATM on an unsupported operating system falls squarely inside that wording ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Hungary has turned a shrinking fleet into a guaranteed replacement market. Act XIV of 2026 bans the removal of any existing machine from 14 May 2026, but allows replacement. Act XVIII requires cash withdrawal in 1,039 named settlements by 31 December 2026. A hand-over of ATM operation cannot be contracted for less than five years ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

The white space is now counted rather than estimated. Croatia's central bank publishes a machine-readable national cash-point registry. It returned 6,852 records on 27 August 2026, of which 3,841 are cash-out-only ATMs. Zagrebačka banka is the weakest of the big four, with a 19.6% deposit share. The same matching-date method gives Bulgaria's four largest banks roughly 1,840 to 1,950 dispense-only sites, and BCR exactly 1,100 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Two contests are open inside the horizon. Geldservice Austria's EUR 9.1m recycler and coin framework was still unawarded on 31 August 2026. It has a 2 November 2026 contract start and delivery reach into four further Printec countries. PrivatBank's recycler renewal closed stage-one qualification on 25 August 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Branch cash desks are being removed faster than machines are being added, which pushes the cash into the lobby. Across Slovakia's five largest banks, 93 of 128 Slovenská sporiteľňa branches now have no cash desk. The same is true at 48 of 69 Tatra branches and at 47 of 120 ČSOB branches. The banks name security rules, staff training and vault equipment as the costs they are escaping ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec's main ATM supplier, NCR Atleos, is being bought by Brink's, a direct competitor in managed services. The UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a Phase 1 inquiry on 26 August 2026, with a decision deadline of 22 October 2026. Completion has been brought forward to early Q1 2027. That is a supply-channel question to settle before signing any multi-year fleet commitment.

Deposit volume is growing far faster than the fleet that carries it. Bulgaria's national fleet fell to 5,031 ATMs at end-2025 from a peak of 5,751. At the same time, ATM deposits reached 12.53m transactions worth EUR 7.2bn, up about 50% by value. Fewer machines doing much more cash-in work is the recycler business case in plain numbers ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
What changed this cycle is that the case for conversion stopped being an argument and became an inventory. In the four weeks to 31 August 2026, the banks' own ATM locator feeds and two central-bank registries were pulled on matching dates. The dispense-only population can now be addressed machine by machine and provider by provider, rather than estimated from market totals ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The supervisory calendar also became firm. An ATM running an unsupported operating system used to be quiet technical debt. The 31 October 2026 filing turns it into a fix-list item that a supervisor will read and then track. The annual information-technology risk questionnaire moving to February 2027 lengthens the evidence window rather than closing it ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The two largest single contests in the line, Austria and Ukraine, both reached their decision stage in the last weeks of August 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

By opportunity value this is the largest of Printec's six lines, at EUR 377.8m. But it is a replacement and conversion cycle inside fleets that are not growing, not an expansion. It should be planned that way.
cite_ungrounded: The NCR Atleos / Brink's transaction in its entirety — the acquisition itself, Brink's status as a managed-services competitor, the UK Competition and Markets Authority Phase 1 inquiry opened 26/08/2026, the 22/10/2026 decision deadline and the early-Q1-2027 completion date. None of it appears in any signal tagged to this line; it was supplied as briefing context and must be re-sourced before it is put in front of a customer.
The characterisation of atm_recycling as the largest of the six lines by opportunity value rests on comparing the six `m` figures supplied with this task, not on any signal.

product_outlooks.label: Self-service, kiosks & branch transformation
product_outlooks.scope: Branch counter closures and the move of counter work to lobby machines
product_outlooks.summary:
This line grows because banks are removing the teller, not the branch. Across Printec's markets, the counter is being taken out of buildings that stay open. The cash and paperwork it used to handle has to go somewhere. The usual replacements are a lobby recycler, a business cash-deposit machine, a bill-payment kiosk or a video-advisory pod.

The volumes make the case on their own. Albania's branch counters took in ALL 783.7bn of cash deposits in the first half of 2026. That is roughly eleven times what the whole national ATM estate took in ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)). In Cyprus almost nine in ten deposits already arrive at a machine ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The largest named pipelines are in Romania and at NLB. CEC Bank has marked roughly 350 Romanian branches for operating-model redesign, against only 46 that have a 24/7 zone today. NLB has committed to a group-wide cash-deposit upgrade across six markets ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec should sell a repeatable per-site package: counter recycler, deposit machine, kiosk, queueing and accessible fit-out. The aim is to win the template rather than the individual branch.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, driven by banks cutting counter staff rather than by network expansion. The branch estates being kept open matter most.

CEC Bank's 2025 audited report names an Operational Model Redesign Program covering roughly 350 rural and urban branches, built around self-service equipment and remote advice. The measured base today is only 46 of 1,011 units with a 24/7 self-service zone. Its Cash2Card launch on 4 August 2026 lets anyone deposit cash onto any Romanian bank's Visa or Mastercard debit card, on a fleet of over 270 multifunction machines. This justifies the spend, because each new deposit point now serves the whole national card base ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

In Cyprus, Eurobank Limited disclosed on 6 August 2026 that 95% of withdrawals and almost 90% of deposits now happen at machines rather than counters. It has two legacy estates to standardise before an April 2027 core-banking cutover ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

NLB has put a named group programme behind the same idea. It is an ATM and cash-deposit-system upgrade that moves cash out of branches. Branch cash transactions fell from 32% at end-2023 to 13.5% in March 2026, against a target below 10%. Three cash-light branches opened in Slovenia in the first half of 2026, and a EUR 160–200m technology budget sits behind Strategy 2030 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Two Greek programmes carry hard dates. Comments on ELTA's EUR 6m retail and delivery transformation specification close on 10 September 2026 through the ESIDIS platform. That is the only moment its scope can still be shaped. ODAP's EUR 30.0m visitor-services procurement closed for tenders on 23 July 2026, with no award published as at 27 August 2026. Its classification set explicitly includes ticket-issuing machines ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Where to aim:

- CEC Bank and BCR in Romania, where 211 of BCR's 282 branches already run with no cash desk and depend on lobby machines staying up.
- Eurobank Limited in Cyprus, before the April 2027 cutover.
- NLB group procurement in Ljubljana rather than any single subsidiary.
- Komercijalna banka in North Macedonia, which has now repeated the same modernised-branch template at five or more sites.
- VÚB and UniCredit in Slovakia, as the counter estates least converted so far.
- DSK in Bulgaria, where exactly one site in 777 has a kiosk device and coin deposit is entirely manual. That is the entry point with the least competition in that market.
- The Greek consortium routes into ELTA and ODAP, where Printec's realistic position is under a systems integrator rather than as a prime contractor.

([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md))

In short: turn one per-site package into a product and sell the branch standard. At CEC, Komercijalna and AikBank the specification is copied site by site rather than re-tendered.
drivers: Counters are being removed from branches that stay open. Across Slovakia's five largest banks the cash desk has already gone from 93 of 128 Slovenská sporiteľňa branches, 48 of 69 at Tatra and 47 of 120 at ČSOB. That leaves VÚB at 25 of 121 and UniCredit at 16 of 47 as the largest remaining refit pipelines ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

CEC Bank has published its own pipeline. Roughly 350 branches are named for operating-model redesign, against 46 of 1,011 units with a 24/7 self-service zone today. The Cash2Card national deposit service, launched 4 August 2026, is the business case ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The counter still handles the cash. Albania's central bank recorded 2,279,914 over-the-counter cash deposits worth ALL 783.7bn in the first half of 2026, against ATM deposits of ALL 68.6bn. It had 408 branches at end-2025, up from 400. So this is fit-out demand in a growing network, not closures ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Montenegro shows the same flow for businesses. Roughly EUR 2.9bn a year of company cash still arrives at a teller. CKB reopened its Podgorica Business Point on 24 July 2026 with no counter cash at all, on a transition closing around 24 January 2027. That is a dated template to quote to the other ten banks ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Two Greek public programmes are inside their decision window. ELTA's EUR 6m retail and delivery transformation is open for comments on its specification until 10 September 2026. ODAP's EUR 30.0m visitor-services award, covering ticket-issuing machines across 125 sites, was still unpublished on 27 August 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo has turned from a build market into a refit market. The commercial-bank network peaked at 237 units in August 2025 and has stayed at 234 since March 2026. So the roughly 35 units opened since 2022 are the target base for counter recyclers and kiosks ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

The kiosk layer beyond the ATM is almost untouched at the region's largest retail network. Exactly one of DSK Bank's 777 Bulgarian sites has a kiosk device, and coin deposit is 100% manual at the counter. This sits against a disclosed 22% year-on-year rise in Bulgarian operating expenses, which the bank puts partly down to information-technology costs ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
The trigger is that cutting staff has moved faster than automation. Branch counts are falling far more slowly than the people behind them. BCR now runs 211 of 282 branches with no staffed cash desk and only 71 with a teller. The lobby machines therefore carry the load rather than being a convenience ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Where branches are being kept flat or opened, as in Albania, Kosovo and at VÚB in Slovakia, the same automation is bought as fit-out instead of as closure.

What is new this cycle is that the buyers have published their own specifications. Postbank has defined exactly two Express Banking device types, a cash device and a cashless kiosk, and named network expansion among its coming initiatives ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)). Komercijalna banka has repeated one modernised-branch template across at least five sites ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)). CEC has named the branch count.

When the customer writes the requirement, the product being sold is the standard. Those standards are being set now.
cite_ungrounded: Postbank's two published Express Banking device types are cited in the rationale from the postbank-eurobank-bulgaria-postbank-next-branch-format-rebuild signal, which sits in the card_issuing slice rather than in this line's own slice; the claim is sourced but the routing key is not in cite_signals.

product_outlooks.label: POS, acquiring & terminal management
product_outlooks.scope: Legal card-acceptance mandates and the growth of terminal estates
product_outlooks.summary:
Card acceptance is the fastest-growing area Printec sells into. The growth is being ordered by law rather than chosen by merchants. Albania's terminal count rose 57.9% in eighteen months to 38,662, under a legal duty that covers the last businesses on 31 December 2026. Kosovo added roughly 9,400 terminals in a single year. Slovakia's eKasa duty to accept a cashless payment on any sale above EUR 1 has been in force since 1 May 2026 ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

At the same time, the terminal itself is becoming a commodity underneath that growth. Three things pull margin out of the hardware: tap-to-phone software terminals; hardware-abstraction specifications that make different makes interchangeable; and a Bulgarian terminal maker that now owns its own acquiring rail. An acquiring rail is the network used to process card payments.

The lasting revenue is therefore in the layer above the device. It covers terminal management, remote key injection, certification, monitoring and field logistics. Remote key injection means loading security keys onto terminals remotely. The buyers are acquirers, the banks and firms that process card payments for merchants, and they run mixed hardware-and-software estates.

Printec should aim this line at the acquirers doing the deploying rather than at the merchants. The lead argument is the complexity of running the estate.
product_outlooks.projected:
Strong growth in volume is expected, with the value moving from the terminal to the platform that runs it.

The clearest mandates are dated. Albania's Law on Tax Procedures, as amended at end-2025, requires accommodation, transport and public enterprises to have a terminal from end-May 2026. Everyone else must have one by 31 December 2026. The central bank's own series already shows 38,662 terminals at end-Q2-2026, against 24,481 at end-2024. The POSi free-terminal programme runs through five named acquirers until 31 December 2026 ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Slovakia's Act 384/2025 has been in force since 1 January 2026, with the acceptance duty applying from 1 May 2026. It carries a scale of fines rising to EUR 3,000–40,000 per further detection, and the possible loss of a trade licence. Its section 15(3) expressly allows a third party to supply the technical means that confirm a QR payment back to the cash register. That is a legal opening. The Financial Directorate had still not published its specification on 27 August 2026 ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo's acceptance estate jumped 45% to about 30,300 terminals in one year. Montenegro's reached an all-time high of 23,250 in the first quarter of 2026. That is up roughly 4,475 in five quarters, in a market of 633,000 people ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Against that, three things weaken the economics of hardware and must be priced in. North Macedonia's central bank has publicly named the cost of the acceptance device as the barrier. It is backing a national interoperable QR code, aliases and request-to-pay, while NLB ships a certified tap-on-phone application ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)). Romania's newly obliged merchants are being served largely by bank software-POS applications and shared terminals rather than by new devices ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)). And a Bulgarian terminal manufacturer had its payment-institution licence extended on 27 August 2026 to cover cash withdrawal and payment-instrument issuing, on top of an existing acquiring rail ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Where to aim: the acquirers carrying the deployment load.

- Albania: Raiffeisen, Union Bank, BKT, Credins and OTP, where Printec's own footprint is roughly 150 terminals against a national estate of 38,662.
- Bosnia and Herzegovina: UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar, the largest card-acceptance estate in the Federation at 11,131 terminals, with falling software capitalisation and two shareholder-ordered audits running.
- Romania: Raiffeisen Romania, as its 45,000-terminal book folds into the Garanti BBVA integration closing in early October 2026, and Banca Transilvania's 200,000-plus installed terminals.
- Slovakia: Penta Bank, a greenfield platform build with a new chief executive, operating officer and finance officer, where acquiring and key management are all still being chosen.

([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md))

One live public contest is worth tracking whatever the bid decision. Operátor ICT's CZK 250m Prague payment gateway was republished with a 31 August 2026 deadline, and an award is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

In short: sell one management platform across several acceptance formats, which are attended, unattended and phone-based. Take the recurring estate revenue rather than the device.
drivers: Three separate legal mandates land inside the horizon. Albania's terminal duty covers all remaining businesses on 31 December 2026, on an estate already up 23.7% in six months to 38,662. Slovakia's eKasa acceptance duty on any sale above EUR 1 has applied since 1 May 2026, with a scale of fines that can cost a merchant its trade licence. Romania's acceptance duty has been reported in force since 1 January 2026 ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

The estates are growing fast where the mandates are softer too. Kosovo's card-accepting terminals rose about 45% to 30,300 in a year, and Montenegro's to an all-time high of 23,250. The Bosnian Federation added 3,079 terminals in six months, against thirty more ATMs ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Value is moving out of the device. North Macedonia's central bank has named device cost as the barrier. It is backing a national QR code, an alias directory and request-to-pay. NLB's certified tap-on-phone application, where the merchant's own handset becomes the terminal, grew installations 46% year on year ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

A structural competitor has put the whole stack together. On 27 August 2026 the Bulgarian National Bank extended DatecsPay's licence to cover cash withdrawal, card-transaction execution, credit transfers and instrument issuing. It already holds an acquiring rail passported and agented into Romania. A terminal maker like this can bundle in a way a reseller cannot match on price ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

Whole banks have no acquiring estate at all. Seven of the thirteen banks headquartered in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina reported zero own POS terminals at 30 June 2026. So acceptance there is a build, not a fight to displace someone ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Bank-side buying teams are forming now. ČSOB in Czechia posted five concurrent international-acquiring vacancies inside four weeks in August 2026. That was a third of the whole national demand for the skill. Platform and terminal-vendor choices freeze once those architects are in post ([A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).
product_outlooks.rationale:
Two things are happening at the same time. Terminal estates are being expanded by law on fixed dates, Albania on 31 December 2026 and Slovakia since 1 May 2026. Acquirers are therefore adding thousands of devices in months, and physically cannot manage them by hand. That turns terminal management, remote key injection and deployment logistics from a nice-to-have into the operational bottleneck ([A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md), [A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

At the same time the hardware itself is being deliberately turned into a commodity. Banks specify hardware-abstraction layers so one payment application runs unchanged across makes. Regulators sponsor phone-based acceptance to cut device cost. And a manufacturer with its own acquiring licence can undercut any reseller ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A6](findings/06-vendors/2026-08-31.md)).

The timing matters for two reasons. A fleet installed in one burst starts its refresh clock at the same time. And the acquirers deciding how to run these estates are hiring the people who will choose the platform.
cite_ungrounded: DatecsPay's 27/08/2026 licence supplement and its Romanian acquiring agency, the seven Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina banks with zero own POS estate, and ČSOB Czechia's five August-2026 acquiring vacancies are all sourced, but their signal keys sit in the card_issuing and payments_instant slices rather than in this line's slice, so they are not represented in cite_signals.

Raiffeisen Romania's “nearly 45,000” POS terminals at 30/06/2026 comes from the raiffeisen-bank-romania-1-211-device-own-estate signal in the payments_instant slice, which is not among this card's cite_signals.

product_outlooks.label: Managed services / outsourcing
product_outlooks.scope: Managed services: regulatory duties on uptime, patching and telemetry
product_outlooks.summary:
Managed services grows over the next year because supervisors, not sales teams, are making the case. The European Central Bank's 31 October 2026 filing reaches into the contract terms and service levels of every information-technology supplier at a significant institution. Bosnia's Federation banks must file an external audit of their systems by 31 March 2027. Kosovo's own resilience rulebook has been binding since 1 June 2026. It names ATMs as critical infrastructure, and their make, model and firmware must be reported within four hours of an incident ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Cutting branch staff has also made uptime essential. 211 of BCR's 282 Romanian branches now run with no cash desk and depend on lobby machines staying up ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Printec should aim this line at estates where a regulator has created a reporting duty that the bank cannot meet from its own records. It should sell device telemetry, meaning remote machine monitoring, together with documented patching and auditable key management, as the evidence pack. The one thing to settle first is the supply channel, because Printec's main ATM supplier is changing owners.
product_outlooks.projected:
Growth is expected, with the buying decision moving from information-technology managers to boards, because the requirements now arrive as regulatory filings.

The European Central Bank's letter SSM-2026-0301 requires an artificial-intelligence and cyber action plan to be with the supervisor by 31 October 2026. Its focus area 1 demands accurate information-technology asset inventories, which is a device-telemetry sale. Focus area 2 pulls patching into the contract terms and service levels of any external service provider. The same letter is therefore both an opening and a duty to review every Printec managed-service agreement at a supervised bank ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina makes the same demand on a national calendar. Its binding information-technology risk decision has applied since 31 December 2025. Every one of the thirteen Federation banks must file a standalone external audit of its systems each year, next by 31 March 2027. Supervisory expectations also require penetration testing, continuous monitoring and a full register of every outsourced activity, with direct board accountability ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo's central bank went further and earlier. Its resilience regulation has bound every financial institution since 1 June 2026. It requires notification within four hours of discovering an incident, and names ATMs among the critical systems. Its most useful clause in that market requires the cybersecurity budget to be separate from the overall information-technology budget, so business projects cannot compete with it ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Two commercial triggers sit alongside the regulatory ones. Hungary's rural mandate cannot be handed over on a contract of less than five years. That turns each of the 80 settlement packages into a multi-year operating relationship rather than a supply order ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)). Ageing estates are already paying for this in the wrong budget line. NLB Komercijalna's maintenance bill for electronic-banking equipment rose 30.7% year on year to RSD 207.8m, which is the exact spend a managed contract replaces ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Where to aim:

- BCR in Romania, where three quarters of branches have no cash desk, so service levels are contractual rather than optional.
- NLB Komercijalna in Serbia, where 49 towns have a machine and no branch behind it. Remote monitoring and predictive maintenance earn their fee there without waiting for a refresh.
- The thirteen Federation banks, and the Republika Srpska banks under the parallel rule.
- Every Kosovo bank, against the four-hour reporting duty.
- The nine Hungarian banks holding settlement packages.
- The two Croatian government lots decided inside a month. One is scored on price plus response time to a service call-out, where a dense field team wins on merit ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md)).

In short: sell the regulator's own evidence requirement, which is asset inventory, patch record, incident pipeline and service levels written into the contract. Let the hardware follow.
drivers: The 31 October 2026 European Central Bank filing writes patching into “contractual terms and service level agreements when an ICT service provider is involved”, and requires accurate asset inventories. So it creates demand for device telemetry and managed patching. It also requires a review of every existing Printec service agreement at a supervised bank ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md)).

Bosnia's Federation Banking Agency requires a standalone external audit of each bank's information systems, filed by 31 March every year and next on 31 March 2027. This applies across all thirteen Federation banks. On top of that, supervisory expectations cover penetration testing, continuous monitoring and a register of every outsourced activity, with board accountability ([A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md), [A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Kosovo's resilience regulation has been binding since 1 June 2026. It requires incident notification within four hours, and names ATMs explicitly among critical systems. The report must give the affected hardware manufacturer, software developer, make and model. No bank can produce that without visibility of its estate ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Uptime is now essential rather than convenient. 211 of BCR's 282 branches are tagged cashless with no staffed cash desk, and only 71 still run a teller counter. So incident management and cash forecasting become the lead product rather than an add-on ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

The cost is already being paid in maintenance rather than in service. NLB Komercijalna's electronic-banking equipment maintenance rose 30.7% year on year to RSD 207.8m, while capital work in progress rose 15.7%. 49 of the towns it covers have a machine and no branch behind it ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

Structural events create multi-year operating work rather than one-off supply. Hungary's hand-over of rural ATM operation cannot be contracted for under five years across 80 settlement packages. Croatia must set up a shared national ATM network by 1 January 2027. That needs multivendor software, monitoring and field services rather than devices alone ([A2](findings/02-tenders/2026-08-27.md), [A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A5](findings/05-jobs/2026-08-31.md)).

Printec's main ATM supplier, NCR Atleos, is being bought by Brink's, which competes directly in managed services. The UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a Phase 1 inquiry on 26 August 2026, with a decision deadline of 22 October 2026. Completion was brought forward to early Q1 2027. A supplier becoming a competitor in this specific line is a channel question to resolve before signing long-dated service commitments.
product_outlooks.rationale:
The change is that the requirement is now filed rather than argued. Until this cycle, telemetry, documented patching and service levels were an efficiency pitch. From 31 October 2026 a significant institution has to name its unsupported technology to a supervisor. From 1 June 2026 a Kosovo bank has to report an ATM incident within four hours, with make and model. And by 31 March 2027 every Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina bank has to give a regulator an external audit of its systems ([A3](findings/03-regulation/2026-08-27.md), [A4](findings/04-statistics/2026-08-31.md)).

Each of those is a document a bank cannot produce from its own records if it does not know what is in its estate.

The operational dependency has also become real. Branch counters have been removed faster than the machines behind them were modernised. A machine that is down is now a branch that cannot serve cash ([A1](findings/01-bank-disclosures/2026-08-27.md)).

One factor pulls the other way, and it sits on the supply side rather than the demand side. The ownership of the hardware channel is changing, and this call depends on how that settles.
cite_ungrounded: The NCR Atleos / Brink's transaction in its entirety — the acquisition, Brink's position as a managed-services competitor, the UK Competition and Markets Authority Phase 1 inquiry of 26/08/2026, the 22/10/2026 decision deadline and the early-Q1-2027 completion. It was supplied as briefing context and does not trace to any signal tagged to this line.

Kosovo's Central Bank Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management — the 01/06/2026 compliance date, the four-hour incident notification, the naming of ATMs in the reporting template and the ring-fenced cybersecurity budget in Article 10 — is sourced, but its signal key sits in the payments_instant slice; the Kosovo key carried in cite_signals is the Law 08/L-304 banking-compliance row, which is a different instrument.
